slept.

Tarefa de consolidação

Crie uma tabela com pelo menos 25 verbos irregulares.

Base verb Simple Past
go went
have had
do did
eat ate
see saw
______ ______
______ ______
______ ______

Depois organize alguns por tema.

Rotina

wake → woke

get → got

eat → ate

drink → drank

sleep → slept

Movimento

go → went

come → came

leave → left

drive → drove

fly → flew

Comunicação

speak → spoke

say → said

tell → told

write → wrote

Ações comuns

have → had

do → did

make → made

take → took

buy → bought

Em seguida, escreva dez pares comparando presente e passado.

Exemplo:

I go to university every day.
I went to university yesterday.

She has breakfast at seven every day.
She had breakfast at seven yesterday.

Depois escreva uma narrativa de oito a dez frases sobre um dia no passado usando pelo menos:

  • went;
  • had;
  • ate;
  • saw;
  • took;
  • bought;
  • came;
  • did;
  • read;
  • slept.

Finalize memorizando a regra essencial:

Verbos irregulares não seguem a regra geral de -ed.

Por isso:

go → went, não goed

eat → ate, não eated

buy → bought, não buyed

take → took, não taked

make → made, não maked

A melhor forma de consolidá-los é encontrá-los repetidamente em frases, textos e atividades, e não apenas tentar memorizar uma lista isolada.

Aula 39 — Simple Past: perguntas e negativas

Objetivos

Ao final desta aula, você deverá ser capaz de:

  • formar frases negativas no Simple Past;
  • construir perguntas com did;
  • usar corretamente a forma básica do verbo depois de did e didn’t;
  • diferenciar afirmativas, negativas e interrogativas no passado;
  • formular perguntas com what, where, when, why, who e how;
  • responder perguntas com short answers;
  • reconhecer erros frequentes como didn’t went e Did she studied?;
  • compreender pequenos diálogos sobre eventos passados;
  • produzir perguntas e respostas sobre atividades concluídas;
  • aplicar Simple Past com verbos regulares e irregulares.

Desenvolvimento

Nas aulas anteriores, estudamos frases afirmativas no Simple Past.

Com verbos regulares:

I worked yesterday.

She studied last night.

Com verbos irregulares:

I went to school.

She ate breakfast.

Agora vamos estudar duas estruturas essenciais:

negative sentences

frases negativas

e:

questions

perguntas.

O auxiliar did

Para a maioria dos verbos no Simple Past, usamos:

did

como auxiliar.

Ele é usado com todos os sujeitos:

I

you

he

she

it

we

they.

Exemplo:

Did you work yesterday?

Did she study?

Did they go home?

A forma:

did

já indica passado.

Por isso, o verbo principal volta para sua forma básica.

Forma negativa

A estrutura é:

subject + did not + base verb

ou, de forma contraída:

subject + didn’t + base verb

Exemplo:

I did not work yesterday.

Forma mais comum:

I didn’t work yesterday.

Outro:

She didn’t study last night.

Outro:

They didn’t go to school.

Regra central

Depois de:

did

ou:

didn’t

use o verbo na forma básica.

Correto:

She didn’t work.

Incorreto:

She didn’t worked.

Correto:

He didn’t go.

Incorreto:

He didn’t went.

Por que isso acontece?

Compare:

Afirmativa:

She worked yesterday.

Negativa:

She didn’t work yesterday.

Na afirmativa, o passado aparece no verbo:

worked.

Na negativa, o passado aparece no auxiliar:

did.

Logo, o verbo principal volta para:

work.

Verbos regulares na negativa

Afirmativa:

I watched TV.

Negativa:

I didn’t watch TV.

Afirmativa:

She studied English.

Negativa:

She didn’t study English.

Afirmativa:

They played football.

Negativa:

They didn’t play football.

Verbos irregulares na negativa

Afirmativa:

I went home.

Negativa:

I didn’t go home.

Afirmativa:

She ate breakfast.

Negativa:

She didn’t eat breakfast.

Afirmativa:

We saw the movie.

Negativa:

We didn’t see the movie.

Observe:

went → go

ate → eat

saw → see

depois de didn’t.

Didn’t é igual para todos os sujeitos

I didn’t work.

You didn’t work.

He didn’t work.

She didn’t work.

We didn’t work.

They didn’t work.

Não existe:

doesn’t

para Simple Past.

Doesn’t pertence ao Simple Present.

Compare:

Presente:

She doesn’t work on Sunday.

Passado:

She didn’t work yesterday.

Perguntas com did

A estrutura básica é:

Did + subject + base verb + complement?

Exemplos:

Did you work yesterday?

Did she study last night?

Did they play football?

Did he go home?

O verbo continua na forma básica

Correto:

Did she study?

Incorreto:

Did she studied?

Correto:

Did he go?

Incorreto:

Did he went?

Correto:

Did they see the movie?

Incorreto:

Did they saw the movie?

Short answers

Para responder perguntas com did:

Yes, subject + did.

No, subject + didn’t.

Exemplo:

Did you study yesterday?

Yes, I did.

ou:

No, I didn’t.

Outro:

Did Maria work yesterday?

Yes, she did.

Outro:

Did they go to school?

No, they didn’t.

Não repetimos o verbo na short answer

Pergunta:

Did you work yesterday?

Resposta curta:

Yes, I did.

Não:

Yes, I did work yesterday.

Essa segunda forma pode existir em contextos específicos de ênfase, mas para respostas básicas use:

Yes, I did.

Perguntas com question words

Também podemos usar:

what

where

when

why

how.

A estrutura normalmente é:

question word + did + subject + base verb?

Exemplo:

Where did you go?

What did she study?

When did they arrive?

Why did he call?

How did you travel?

Where did you go?

Observe:

Where did you go?

Não:

Where did you went?

Como did já indica passado:

go

fica na forma básica.

What did you do?

Uma pergunta extremamente frequente:

What did you do yesterday?

Resposta:

I studied English.

Outro:

What did you do last weekend?

I visited my family.

Where did you go?

Where did you go last night?

I went to a restaurant.

A pergunta usa:

go.

A resposta afirmativa usa:

went.

When did…?

When did the class start?

It started at seven.

Pergunta:

start.

Resposta:

started.

Why did…?

Why did you stay at home?

Because I was tired.

Ou:

Because I had work to do.

How did…?

How did you go to university?

I went by bus.

Outro:

How did she travel?

She traveled by train.

What time did…?

What time did you wake up?

I woke up at seven.

A pergunta usa:

wake.

A resposta usa:

woke.

Who com did

Podemos ter:

Who did you see?

Aqui, who é o objeto da ação.

Resposta:

I saw Laura.

Outro:

Who did she call?

She called her mother.

Who como sujeito

Há também casos como:

Who called you?

Aqui, who é o próprio sujeito.

Nesse caso, normalmente não usamos:

did.

Compare:

Who did you call?

Quem você chamou?

Who called you?

Quem chamou você?

Essa diferença será aprofundada mais tarde, mas é importante reconhecê-la.

Perguntas yes/no

Essas perguntas podem ser respondidas com:

yes

ou:

no.

Exemplos:

Did you work yesterday?

Did she call you?

Did they arrive early?

Perguntas abertas

Pedem uma informação específica.

Where did you work?

When did she call?

What did they eat?

Why did he leave?

Não são respondidas apenas com:

yes/no.

Forma afirmativa, negativa e interrogativa

Compare o mesmo verbo:

Afirmativa:

She worked yesterday.

Negativa:

She didn’t work yesterday.

Pergunta:

Did she work yesterday?

Outro:

Afirmativa:

He went to school.

Negativa:

He didn’t go to school.

Pergunta:

Did he go to school?

Tabela de contraste

Tipo Estrutura Exemplo
Afirmativa subject + past verb She studied.
Negativa subject + didn’t + base verb She didn’t study.
Pergunta Did + subject + base verb? Did she study?

Present x Past

Presente:

Do you work here?

Passado:

Did you work here last year?

Presente:

Does she study English?

Passado:

Did she study English yesterday?

Presente:

He doesn’t go by bus.

Passado:

He didn’t go by bus yesterday.

Marcadores temporais

Continue observando:

yesterday

last night

last week

last month

last year

ago.

Exemplo:

Did you work yesterday?

Did she travel last month?

Where did they go last weekend?

Conversa simples

A: Did you work yesterday?
B: No, I didn’t.
A: What did you do?
B: I stayed at home and studied English.

Observe a sequência:

Did you work…?

pergunta yes/no.

No, I didn’t.

short answer.

What did you do?

pergunta aberta.

Outro diálogo

A: Did Anna go to the party?
B: Yes, she did.
A: What time did she arrive?
B: She arrived at eight.

Correção de erro frequente

Erro:

Did you went there?

Correto:

Did you go there?

Erro:

She didn’t studied.

Correto:

She didn’t study.

Erro:

Did he ate breakfast?

Correto:

Did he eat breakfast?

Erro com verbo regular

Não:

Did she worked yesterday?

Use:

Did she work yesterday?

Erro com verbo irregular

Não:

Did he saw the movie?

Use:

Did he see the movie?

Erro com negativa irregular

Não:

I didn’t went.

Use:

I didn’t go.

Erro com doesn’t

Não:

She doesn’t work yesterday.

Use:

She didn’t work yesterday.

Perguntas sobre rotina passada

Did you study yesterday?

Did you cook dinner?

Did you watch TV?

Did you go out?

Essas perguntas são úteis em diálogos cotidianos.

Perguntas sobre uma viagem

Where did you go?

How did you travel?

Where did you stay?

What did you visit?

Did you like the trip?

Perguntas sobre estudo

Did you study for the test?

What did you study?

When did you start?

Did you finish the homework?

Perguntas sobre trabalho

Did you work yesterday?

What time did you start?

What time did you finish?

Did you have a meeting?

Perguntas com verbos regulares e irregulares

Did you watch the movie?

regular.

Did you see the movie?

irregular.

Em ambos:

did + base verb.

Pequeno texto

Leia:

Last Saturday, Julia didn’t work. She stayed at home in the morning and studied English. In the afternoon, she went to the city center. She didn’t take the bus; she walked. She met her friend Anna at a café. They talked for an hour, but they didn’t eat there. Julia came home at six.

Perguntas possíveis:

Did Julia work?

No, she didn’t.

Where did she go?

She went to the city center.

Did she take the bus?

No, she didn’t.

Who did she meet?

She met Anna.

Negativas em Reading

Em Reading, didn’t pode ser uma palavra decisiva.

Compare:

He went to work.

com:

He didn’t go to work.

Uma pequena palavra muda o sentido.

Negativas em Listening

No Listening, escute a frase completa.

Exemplo:

I didn’t go to the library. I went to the café.

Se a pergunta for:

Where did the speaker go?

Resposta:

the café.

A biblioteca é um distrator.

Didn’t + base form como padrão automático

Treine como blocos:

didn’t go

didn’t eat

didn’t see

didn’t work

didn’t study

didn’t call

didn’t buy

didn’t take.

Evite traduzir e depois reconstruir a regra a cada frase.

Did + subject + base form

Também automatize:

Did you go…?

Did she eat…?

Did he work…?

Did they study…?

Did Maria call…?

Writing no passado

Para escrever sobre o que não aconteceu:

I didn’t work yesterday.

I didn’t study at night.

I didn’t go out.

Para combinar com afirmativas:

I stayed at home, but I didn’t watch TV.

Speaking no passado

Pergunta:

What did you do yesterday?

Resposta:

I studied in the morning and worked in the afternoon.

Pergunta:

Did you go out?

No, I didn’t. I stayed at home.

Essa é uma interação básica muito importante no nível A2.

Vocabulário-chave

did — auxiliar do Simple Past

didn’t / did not — não fez/não aconteceu, auxiliar negativo

yesterday — ontem

last night — ontem à noite

last week — semana passada

ago — atrás

go — ir

Did you go?

work — trabalhar

Did she work?

study — estudar

She didn’t study.

eat — comer

Did they eat?

see — ver

Who did you see?

take — pegar/levar

Did you take the bus?

buy — comprar

What did you buy?

call — ligar

Who did she call?

arrive — chegar

When did they arrive?

leave — sair/partir

What time did he leave?

Estratégia de prova

Ao ver:

did

ou:

didn’t

procure imediatamente um verbo na forma básica.

Exemplo:

Did she ___ yesterday?

  1. worked
  2. work
  3. works
  4. working

Resposta:

work.

Outro:

He didn’t ___ the bus.

  1. took
  2. takes
  3. take
  4. taking

Resposta:

take.

Use o esquema:

DID/DIDN’T = PAST

Portanto:

MAIN VERB = BASE FORM

Em questões de Reading ou Listening, preste atenção especial a:

didn’t

porque ele pode transformar uma alternativa aparentemente correta em um distrator.

B: No, I didn’t. I read a book.

O diálogo combina:

  • perguntas com did;
  • perguntas abertas;
  • negativas;
  • verbos regulares;
  • verbos irregulares.

Tarefa de consolidação

Transforme dez frases afirmativas no passado em:

  1. negativa;
  2. pergunta.

Exemplo:

She worked yesterday.

Negativa:

She didn’t work yesterday.

Pergunta:

Did she work yesterday?

Faça o mesmo com:

He studied English.

They played football.

She went to school.

He ate breakfast.

We saw a movie.

Maria bought a book.

They took the bus.

I visited my family.

She called her friend.

We watched TV.

Depois crie perguntas para estas respostas:

I went to the bank.

I went there on Monday.

I bought a new book.

I traveled by bus.

I called my sister.

Use:

Where did…?

When did…?

What did…?

How did…?

Who did…?

Finalize memorizando o contraste:

She worked.

She didn’t work.

Did she work?

E:

He went.

He didn’t go.

Did he go?

Regra central:

Did e didn’t já carregam a ideia de passado. Por isso, o verbo principal deve permanecer na forma básica.

Aula 40 — Past Continuous

Objetivos

Ao final desta aula, você deverá ser capaz de:

  • compreender a função básica do Past Continuous;
  • formar frases afirmativas, negativas e interrogativas nesse tempo verbal;
  • usar corretamente was e were;
  • reconhecer ações que estavam em andamento em um momento específico do passado;
  • diferenciar Simple Past e Past Continuous;
  • compreender o uso de when e while em contextos simples;
  • descrever ações simultâneas no passado;
  • identificar uma ação em andamento interrompida por outra;
  • interpretar pequenos textos e diálogos no passado;
  • produzir frases e pequenos relatos usando o Past Continuous.

Desenvolvimento

O Past Continuous é usado para falar de uma ação que estava acontecendo em determinado momento do passado.

Compare:

I studied English yesterday.

Isso é Simple Past.

A ação aconteceu e foi concluída.

Agora:

I was studying English at 8 p.m.

Isso é Past Continuous.

A ideia é:

às 20h, a ação de estudar estava em andamento.

Estrutura básica

A estrutura afirmativa é:

subject + was/were + verb-ing

Exemplos:

I was studying.

She was working.

They were playing.

Was e were

Usamos:

I was

he was

she was

it was

E:

you were

we were

they were.

Tabela:

Sujeito Auxiliar
I was
You were
He was
She was
It was
We were
They were

Forma afirmativa

I was reading.

She was cooking.

He was sleeping.

We were studying.

They were talking.

A estrutura sempre inclui:

was/were + verb-ing.

Ação em andamento em um horário passado

Exemplo:

At 9 p.m. last night, I was studying.

Pergunta:

What were you doing at 9 p.m.?

Resposta:

I was studying.

Outro:

At six yesterday, she was working.

A ação estava acontecendo naquele momento.

Past Continuous x Simple Past

Compare:

I watched TV last night.

Simple Past.

Ação concluída.

I was watching TV at 9 p.m.

Past Continuous.

Ação em andamento às 21h.

Outro:

She cooked dinner.

ação concluída.

She was cooking dinner at seven.

ação em progresso naquele momento.

Marcadores frequentes

O Past Continuous aparece muito com:

at 7 p.m.

at that moment

this time yesterday

while

when

Exemplo:

This time yesterday, I was working.

This time yesterday

Essa expressão significa:

a esta hora ontem.

Exemplo:

This time yesterday, we were traveling.

Formação do -ing

As regras são as mesmas do Present Continuous.

Forma básica:

work → working

study → studying

play → playing

Verbos terminados em -e

Normalmente removemos o e:

make → making

write → writing

come → coming

Exemplo:

She was making dinner.

Verbos com duplicação de consoante

Alguns verbos curtos duplicam a consoante final:

run → running

sit → sitting

swim → swimming

Exemplo:

They were running in the park.

Lie

Um caso especial:

lie → lying.

Forma negativa

A estrutura é:

subject + was not/were not + verb-ing

Contrações:

wasn’t

weren’t.

Exemplos:

I wasn’t sleeping.

She wasn’t working.

They weren’t studying.

Wasn’t

Usamos com:

I

he

she

it.

Exemplo:

He wasn’t watching TV.

Weren’t

Usamos com:

you

we

they.

Exemplo:

They weren’t playing football.

Perguntas

Estrutura:

Was/Were + subject + verb-ing?

Exemplos:

Was she studying?

Were they working?

Were you sleeping?

Short answers

Was she working?

Yes, she was.

No, she wasn’t.

Outro:

Were they studying?

Yes, they were.

No, they weren’t.

Perguntas com question words

What were you doing?

Where was she going?

Who were they talking to?

Why was he running?

What were they watching?

What were you doing?

Essa é uma das perguntas mais importantes deste conteúdo.

What were you doing at 8 p.m.?

Resposta:

I was studying.

Ação longa e ação curta

Um uso muito importante é combinar:

Past Continuous

com:

Simple Past.

Exemplo:

I was studying when the phone rang.

Temos:

was studying

ação em andamento.

rang

ação curta que interrompe.

When

When frequentemente introduz a ação que aconteceu durante outra.

Exemplo:

I was sleeping when the phone rang.

A ação de dormir estava em andamento.

O telefone tocou em determinado momento.

Outro:

She was walking home when it started to rain.

Estrutura comum

Past Continuous + when + Simple Past

Exemplo:

We were eating dinner when the lights went out.

Ordem invertida

Também podemos dizer:

When the lights went out, we were eating dinner.

O sentido principal permanece.

While

While significa:

enquanto.

É muito usado para duas ações em andamento ao mesmo tempo.

Exemplo:

I was studying while my brother was watching TV.

As duas ações estavam acontecendo simultaneamente.

Duas ações simultâneas

She was cooking while he was cleaning.

They were talking while they were walking.

I was reading while my sister was studying.

When x while

De forma básica:

when → frequentemente com ação curta que acontece durante outra.

while → frequentemente conecta ações em progresso.

Compare:

I was studying when Sarah called.

I was studying while Sarah was cooking.

Não é uma regra absoluta

No inglês real, when e while podem aparecer em outras estruturas.

Neste nível, use o padrão básico para entender e produzir frases corretamente.

Interrupção

Leia:

Tom was driving when he saw an accident.

Ação em progresso:

was driving.

Evento:

saw.

Outro:

We were having dinner when the doorbell rang.

Cenário de uma narrativa

O Past Continuous também é útil para descrever o que estava acontecendo ao redor.

Exemplo:

It was raining. People were walking quickly. Cars were moving slowly.

Esse tipo de descrição cria um cenário.

Depois, um evento pode aparecer:

Suddenly, a bus stopped.

Simple Past para evento principal

Compare:

People were walking.

contexto.

A car stopped.

evento específico.

Isso é muito comum em pequenas narrativas.

Pequeno relato

Leia:

Yesterday at 6 p.m., Julia was walking home. It was raining, and people were carrying umbrellas. Julia was listening to music when she saw her friend Anna. Anna was waiting for a bus.

Verbos no Past Continuous:

was walking

was raining

were carrying

was listening

was waiting.

Simple Past:

saw.

Past Continuous não significa ação concluída

I was reading a book.

Essa frase não informa necessariamente se o livro foi terminado.

Compare:

I read the book.

Dependendo do contexto, pode indicar a ação concluída.

Pergunta sobre um momento específico

What were you doing at midnight?

I was sleeping.

Outro:

What was Laura doing at 3 p.m.?

She was working.

Negativa em contexto

At 10 p.m., I wasn’t studying. I was watching a movie.

A primeira frase exclui uma ação.

A segunda informa a ação real.

Perguntas contrastivas

Were you sleeping at ten?

No, I wasn’t. I was reading.

Erros frequentes

Erro 1

I was study.

Correto:

I was studying.

Erro 2

They was working.

Correto:

They were working.

Erro 3

She were sleeping.

Correto:

She was sleeping.

Erro 4

Were you study?

Correto:

Were you studying?

Erro 5

I didn’t studying.

Se a intenção é Past Continuous:

I wasn’t studying.

Erro 6

I was studied.

Para ação em progresso:

I was studying.

Past Continuous x Simple Past na negativa

Compare:

I didn’t study last night.

Ação passada negada como um todo.

I wasn’t studying at 8 p.m.

Ação não estava em andamento às 20h.

Diferença de sentido

She didn’t work yesterday.

Ela não trabalhou ontem.

She wasn’t working at 3 p.m.

Às 15h, ela não estava trabalhando.

Ela pode ter trabalhado em outro horário.

Perguntas diferentes

Did you study yesterday?

Pergunta se a atividade aconteceu.

Were you studying at 8 p.m.?

Pergunta se estava acontecendo naquele momento.

Construindo uma linha do tempo mental

Imagine:

7:00 — ação começa
8:00 — ação continua
9:00 — ação termina

Se perguntarmos:

What was happening at 8:00?

Use Past Continuous.

I was studying.

Ação curta no meio

Imagine:

I was studying from 7 to 9.

Às 8:

the phone rang.

Podemos dizer:

I was studying when the phone rang.

Listening

Em Listening, procure reconhecer:

was + -ing

were + -ing.

Exemplo:

She was working.

Não confunda com:

She worked.

A segunda frase não enfatiza ação em andamento.

Reading

Em narrativas, procure separar:

background

was raining

were talking

was walking

de:

events

arrived

called

fell

saw.

Isso ajuda a compreender a estrutura do texto.

Writing

Você pode criar relatos simples:

Yesterday at eight, I was studying. My brother was watching TV. My parents were talking in the kitchen. Then the phone rang.

O Past Continuous estabelece o cenário.

O Simple Past introduz o evento.

Speaking

Pergunta:

What were you doing at 9 p.m. yesterday?

Resposta:

I was studying at home.

Pergunta:

Were you watching TV?

No, I wasn’t. I was reading.

Descrição de uma cena no passado

Imagine uma festa ontem às 20h.

Você pode dizer:

Some people were dancing. Two people were talking. A man was eating. A woman was taking photos.

Uso de while

While some people were dancing, others were talking.

Isso conecta atividades simultâneas.

Uso de when

People were dancing when the music stopped.

A dança estava acontecendo.

Depois:

the music stopped.

Mais exemplos

I was taking a shower when the phone rang.

She was studying when her friend arrived.

They were playing football when it started to rain.

We were driving when we saw the accident.

Was/were + verb-ing deve funcionar como uma unidade

Treine blocos:

was working

was studying

was sleeping

were playing

were talking

were waiting.

Isso facilita Listening e Speaking.

Vocabulário-chave

while — enquanto

I was studying while she was reading.

when — quando

I was sleeping when he called.

at that moment — naquele momento

this time yesterday — a esta hora ontem

happen — acontecer

interrupt — interromper

rain — chover

It was raining.

wait — esperar

She was waiting.

drive — dirigir

He was driving.

walk — caminhar

They were walking.

sleep — dormir

I was sleeping.

talk — conversar

We were talking.

watch — assistir

She was watching TV.

read — ler

He was reading.

cook — cozinhar

They were cooking.

Estratégia de prova

Procure três pistas principais.

1. Um momento específico no passado

at 8 p.m. yesterday

this time yesterday

Isso favorece Past Continuous.

2. Uma ação em andamento interrompida

I ___ when the phone rang.

Provável estrutura:

was/were + verb-ing.

3. Duas ações simultâneas

while

frequentemente conecta dois Past Continuous.

Exemplo:

I ___ while my brother ___ TV.

  1. studied / watched
  2. was studying / was watching
  3. am studying / watches
  4. was study / watched

Resposta:

was studying / was watching.

Antes de escolher, confira o sujeito:

I → was

she → was

they → were.

Prática

1. Complete:

I ___ studying at 8 p.m.

  1. was
  2. were
  3. did
  4. am

They ___ watching TV.

  1. was
  2. were
  3. did

  1. cook

  3. cooking
  4. cooks

  1. listen
  2. listened
  3. listening
  4. listens

5. Complete:

He ___ sleeping at midnight.

  1. were
  2. was
  3. did
  4. is

6. Transforme para a negativa:

She was working.

7. Transforme:

They were studying.

I ___ not watching TV.

  1. was
  2. were
  3. did
  4. do

9. Complete:

  1. was
  2. were

  4. does

  1. Were

  4. Does

  1. when

21. Escolha a frase correta:

22. Escolha a frase correta:

23. Corrija:

27. Leia:

Yesterday at 7 p.m., Daniel was studying in his bedroom. His sister was watching TV in the living room, and his parents were cooking dinner. Daniel was reading a text when his phone rang. It was his friend Lucas. They talked for ten minutes, and then Daniel continued studying.

  2. She was working at eight.

30. Produção

Escreva um pequeno texto de 8 a 10 frases descrevendo uma situação no passado.

Inclua:

  • um horário específico;

30.

Modelo:

Yesterday at 8 p.m., I was studying at home. My brother was watching TV, and my parents were talking in the kitchen. It was raining outside. I was reading a book when my phone rang. My friend was waiting for a bus and called me. While we were talking, the rain became stronger. We talked for a few minutes. Then I continued studying.

O texto estabelece cenário com Past Continuous e utiliza Simple Past para eventos específicos.

Tarefa de consolidação

Crie dez pares contrastando Simple Past e Past Continuous.

Exemplo:

I studied last night.
I was studying at 8 p.m.

She cooked dinner.
She was cooking dinner when I arrived.

Depois complete cinco frases com:

when

Exemplo:

I was sleeping when the phone rang.

E cinco frases com:

while

Exemplo:

I was studying while my brother was watching TV.

Em seguida, escolha um horário de ontem e responda:

What were you doing at 7 a.m.?

What were you doing at noon?

What were you doing at 3 p.m.?

What were you doing at 8 p.m.?

What were you doing at midnight?

Por fim, escreva um pequeno relato começando com:

Yesterday at 6 p.m….

Use pelo menos:

was/were + verb-ing

when + Simple Past

while + Past Continuous.

Finalize memorizando:

Simple Past = ação/evento concluído

Past Continuous = ação em andamento em determinado momento do passado

E o contraste:

I was studying when the phone rang.

While I was studying, my brother was watching TV.

Aula 41 — Simple Past vs. Past Continuous

Objetivos

Ao final desta aula, você deverá ser capaz de:

  • diferenciar Simple Past e Past Continuous;
  • reconhecer ações concluídas e ações em andamento no passado;
  • identificar o tempo verbal adequado a partir do contexto;
  • compreender a diferença entre evento principal e situação de fundo;
  • usar corretamente when e while;
  • combinar Simple Past e Past Continuous em uma mesma frase;
  • compreender interrupções e ações simultâneas;
  • interpretar pequenos textos narrativos;
  • produzir frases e relatos curtos no passado;
  • evitar erros frequentes na escolha entre os dois tempos verbais.

Desenvolvimento

Nas últimas aulas, estudamos dois tempos verbais importantes do passado:

Simple Past

e:

Past Continuous.

Agora vamos compará-los diretamente.

Simple Past

O Simple Past é usado principalmente para ações:

  • concluídas;
  • pontuais;
  • sequenciais;
  • que aconteceram em determinado momento do passado.

Exemplo:

I studied English yesterday.

A ação aconteceu e terminou.

Outro:

She arrived at eight.

Temos um evento específico.

Past Continuous

O Past Continuous é usado principalmente para ações que:

  • estavam acontecendo;
  • estavam em progresso em determinado momento;
  • formavam o cenário de uma situação passada.

Exemplo:

I was studying English at 8 p.m.

Às 20h, a atividade ainda estava acontecendo.

Comparação básica

Compare:

I watched TV last night.

Simple Past.

A informação principal é que a atividade aconteceu.

Agora:

I was watching TV at 9 p.m.

Past Continuous.

A informação principal é que, naquele momento, a atividade estava em andamento.

Estruturas

Simple Past afirmativo:

subject + past verb

Exemplo:

She worked.

Past Continuous:

subject + was/were + verb-ing

Exemplo:

She was working.

Ação concluída x ação em andamento

Compare:

Daniel studied from 7 to 9 p.m.

A frase apresenta a atividade como um evento completo.

At 8 p.m., Daniel was studying.

Aqui observamos Daniel no meio da atividade.

Uma linha do tempo

Imagine:

7:00 — Daniel começou a estudar
8:00 — Daniel ainda estava estudando
9:00 — Daniel terminou

Para falar da atividade como um todo:

Daniel studied from 7 to 9.

Para falar do que estava acontecendo às 8:

Daniel was studying at 8.

O contexto decide

Não escolha o tempo verbal apenas pelo verbo.

O mesmo verbo pode aparecer nos dois tempos.

I worked yesterday.

I was working at 3 p.m.

She cooked dinner.

She was cooking dinner when I arrived.

They played football.

They were playing football at five.

Marcadores do Simple Past

Expressões frequentes:

yesterday

last night

last week

two days ago

in 2025

Exemplo:

I visited my friend yesterday.

Marcadores do Past Continuous

Expressões frequentes:

at 8 p.m.

at that moment

this time yesterday

while

Exemplo:

This time yesterday, I was traveling.

Um marcador não resolve tudo sozinho

Leia:

Yesterday at 8 p.m., I was studying.

Temos:

yesterday

e:

at 8 p.m.

A expressão específica:

at 8 p.m.

indica uma ação em progresso naquele momento.

Por isso usamos:

was studying.

Interrupção

Um dos contrastes mais importantes é:

Past Continuous + Simple Past.

Exemplo:

I was studying when the phone rang.

Temos:

was studying

ação em progresso.

rang

evento que aconteceu durante essa ação.

Ação longa e ação curta

De forma simplificada:

Past Continuous = ação longa/em andamento

Simple Past = ação curta/evento

Exemplo:

She was walking home when it started to rain.

A caminhada já estava acontecendo.

Depois:

it started to rain.

When

When aparece com frequência para introduzir o evento que acontece durante outra ação.

I was sleeping when Maria called.

Outro:

They were having dinner when the lights went out.

Ordem da frase

Podemos inverter:

Maria called when I was sleeping.

Ou:

When Maria called, I was sleeping.

A relação temporal continua clara.

While

While normalmente destaca uma ação em andamento.

While I was studying, my brother was watching TV.

As duas ações estavam acontecendo simultaneamente.

Duas ações simultâneas

I was cooking while my sister was cleaning.

They were talking while they were walking.

Laura was reading while Daniel was studying.

Nesse tipo de construção, os dois verbos podem ficar no Past Continuous.

When x while

Padrão útil:

when + evento

while + ação em progresso

Exemplo:

I was walking when I saw Anna.

While I was walking, Anna was waiting for the bus.

Não transforme isso em regra absoluta

O inglês permite outras combinações.

Neste nível, o objetivo é dominar o padrão mais comum:

background → Past Continuous

event → Simple Past.

Background

Background significa o cenário ou situação de fundo.

Leia:

It was raining. People were walking quickly. Cars were moving slowly.

Tudo isso descreve o cenário.

Depois:

Suddenly, a bus stopped.

Agora aparece um evento.

Narrativas

O contraste entre os dois tempos é muito usado em histórias.

Exemplo:

It was raining, and people were running to the bus stop. Anna was walking home when she saw a small dog in the street.

Cenário:

was raining

were running

was walking.

Evento:

saw.

Sequência de eventos

Quando várias ações acontecem uma depois da outra, usamos normalmente Simple Past.

I woke up, took a shower, ate breakfast and left home.

Essas ações formam uma sequência.

Não é necessário Past Continuous.

Compare

I woke up and ate breakfast.

Sequência de eventos.

Agora:

I was eating breakfast when my friend called.

Uma ação estava acontecendo e outra surgiu durante ela.

Outra comparação

She opened the door, entered the room and sat down.

Sequência.

She was opening the door when the phone rang.

Ação em andamento + interrupção.

Ação contínua sem interrupção

Não é necessário haver interrupção.

At 10 p.m., I was sleeping.

Isso já justifica Past Continuous.

Ação concluída em horário específico

Compare:

The class started at 7 p.m.

Simple Past porque start é um evento pontual.

At 7:30 p.m., the students were studying.

Past Continuous porque a ação estava em andamento.

Verbos que normalmente aparecem como eventos

Exemplos frequentes:

arrive

start

stop

call

see

find

open

close.

Exemplo:

The teacher arrived while the students were talking.

Ações de fundo frequentes

study

sleep

walk

talk

watch

work

rain

wait.

Exemplo:

The students were talking when the teacher arrived.

Did x was/were

Essa diferença também aparece em perguntas.

Simple Past:

What did you do yesterday?

Pergunta sobre o que aconteceu.

Past Continuous:

What were you doing at 8 p.m.?

Pergunta sobre o que estava acontecendo naquele momento.

Perguntas contrastadas

Did you study last night?

Yes, I did.

Agora:

Were you studying at 9 p.m.?

Yes, I was.

Essas perguntas não significam exatamente a mesma coisa.

Negativas contrastadas

I didn’t work yesterday.

Significa:

eu não trabalhei ontem.

I wasn’t working at 3 p.m.

Significa:

às 15h, eu não estava trabalhando.

Talvez tenha trabalhado em outro horário.

Exemplo contextual

Julia worked yesterday, but she wasn’t working at 3 p.m. She was having lunch.

Não há contradição.

Ela trabalhou em algum momento do dia, mas não exatamente às 15h.

Ação interrompida

I was taking a shower when the phone rang.

A ação de tomar banho estava acontecendo.

O telefone tocou durante ela.

Ação simultânea

I was taking a shower while my brother was making breakfast.

Duas ações em andamento ao mesmo tempo.

Um evento dentro de duas ações

I was studying while my sister was watching TV when the electricity went out.

Temos:

was studying

was watching

ações em andamento.

went out

evento.

Pequeno texto

Leia:

Yesterday evening, Laura was studying in her bedroom. Her brother was watching TV, and her parents were cooking dinner. At 8 p.m., the phone rang. Laura answered it. It was her friend Emma. They talked for ten minutes, and then Laura continued studying.

Past Continuous:

was studying

was watching

were cooking.

Simple Past:

rang

answered

was

talked

continued.

Por que “talked” é Simple Past?

Porque:

They talked for ten minutes.

A atividade é apresentada como concluída.

Se quiséssemos focar em um ponto durante a conversa:

At 8:05, they were talking.

Diferentes perspectivas

Compare:

They talked for an hour.

foco no evento completo.

They were talking at 8 p.m.

foco na ação em andamento naquele momento.

Outro texto

Mark was driving to work when he saw an accident. Some people were standing near a car, and one man was talking on the phone. Mark stopped his car and called the police.

Past Continuous cria o cenário:

was driving

were standing

was talking.

Simple Past apresenta os eventos:

saw

stopped

called.

Erros frequentes

Erro 1

I studied when the phone was ringing.

Pode ser gramatical em um contexto específico, mas se a intenção é dizer que você estudava quando o telefone tocou, o padrão esperado é:

I was studying when the phone rang.

Erro 2

I was went home.

Correto:

I went home.

Ou, dependendo do contexto:

I was going home.

Erro 3

They were played football.

Correto:

They were playing football.

Erro 4

She did sleeping.

Correto:

She was sleeping.

Erro 5

While I studied, my brother was watching TV.

Pode ocorrer em contextos específicos, mas para duas atividades simultâneas em andamento, o padrão básico é:

While I was studying, my brother was watching TV.

Não combine did com verb-ing

Incorreto:

Did you studying?

Correto para Simple Past:

Did you study?

Correto para Past Continuous:

Were you studying?

Não combine was com passado simples

Incorreto:

She was worked.

Use:

She worked.

ou:

She was working.

Reading: procure a função da ação

Ao ler uma narrativa, pergunte:

Is this background?

ou:

Is this an event?

Isso ajuda a compreender o texto mesmo antes de traduzir tudo.

Listening

Escute a diferença entre:

worked

e:

was working.

studied

e:

was studying.

O auxiliar:

was/were

é uma pista muito importante.

Writing

Uma estrutura eficiente para pequenas narrativas:

background + event + reaction.

Exemplo:

I was walking home. It was raining. Suddenly, I saw my friend. We stopped and talked for a few minutes.

Speaking

Pergunta:

What were you doing when your friend called?

Resposta:

I was studying.

Pergunta:

What did you do after the call?

I went back to studying.

Decidindo qual tempo usar

Pergunte:

1. A ação é vista como concluída?

Simple Past.

2. A ação estava acontecendo em determinado momento?

Past Continuous.

3. Uma ação estava acontecendo quando outra aconteceu?

longa: Past Continuous

evento: Simple Past.

4. Duas ações estavam acontecendo simultaneamente?

Past Continuous + while + Past Continuous.

Vocabulário-chave

background — cenário/situação de fundo

event — evento

interrupt — interromper

while — enquanto

when — quando

suddenly — de repente

Suddenly, the phone rang.

at that moment — naquele momento

this time yesterday — a esta hora ontem

continue — continuar

happen — acontecer

ring — tocar, especialmente telefone/campainha

The phone rang.

arrive — chegar

leave — sair/partir

wait — esperar

drive — dirigir

rain — chover

talk — conversar

Estratégia de prova

Ao escolher entre Simple Past e Past Continuous, procure responder três perguntas:

Was the action finished?

Was it in progress?

Did another event interrupt it?

Exemplo:

I ___ TV when the phone ___.

  1. watched / was ringing
  2. was watching / rang
  3. was watch / rang
  4. watched / ring

A ação de assistir já estava em andamento.

O telefone tocou durante ela.

Resposta:

I was watching TV when the phone rang.

Outro:

While she , her brother .

  1. studied / slept
  2. was studying / was sleeping
  3. did study / was slept
  4. studies / sleeps

Se as duas ações estavam simultaneamente em andamento:

was studying / was sleeping.

Use:

background = Past Continuous

event = Simple Past

Prática

1. Complete:

I ___ TV when Maria called.

  1. watched
  2. was watching
  3. am watching
  4. watches

2. Complete:

I was watching TV when Maria ___.

  1. calls
  2. called
  3. was calling every day
  4. call

3. Complete:

They ___ football at 5 p.m.

  1. played
  2. were playing
  3. play
  4. did playing

4. Complete:

They ___ football yesterday and went home at six.

  1. were playing
  2. played
  3. are playing
  4. was playing

5. Complete:

She ___ dinner when the lights went out.

  1. cooked
  2. was cooking
  3. cooks
  4. did cooking

6. Complete:

While she was cooking, her husband ___ the table.

  1. was cleaning
  2. cleaned every day
  3. is cleaning
  4. cleans

7. Complete:

I ___ home when I saw Anna.

  1. was walking
  2. walked every day
  3. am walking
  4. walks

8. Complete:

We ___ dinner, watched TV and went to bed.

  1. were having
  2. had
  3. having
  4. were had

9. Escolha a frase correta:

  1. I was sleeping when the phone rang.

  2. I slept when the phone was rang.

  3. I was slept when the phone rang.

  4. I did sleeping when the phone rang.

10. Escolha a frase correta:

  1. While I studied, she were cooking.

  2. While I was studying, she was cooking.

  3. While I was study, she cooked.

  4. While I studying, she was cook.

11. Complete:

At 10 p.m. last night, I ___.

  1. slept
  2. was sleeping
  3. sleep
  4. am sleeping

12. Complete:

I ___ eight hours last night.

  1. was sleeping
  2. slept
  3. sleep
  4. was slept

13. Complete:

What ___ you doing at eight?

  1. did
  2. were
  3. was
  4. do

14. Complete:

What ___ you do yesterday?

  1. were
  2. was
  3. did
  4. are

15. Transforme usando Past Continuous:

I studied at 8 p.m.

Reescreva enfatizando que a ação estava em andamento.

16. Transforme usando Simple Past:

I was watching TV at 9 p.m.

Escreva uma frase dizendo apenas que você assistiu TV ontem.

17. Una as frases com when:

I was studying.
The phone rang.

18. Una com while:

Laura was reading.
Mark was watching TV.

19. Corrija:

I was went to school.

20. Corrija:

They were played football.

21. Corrija:

Did you studying at eight?

22. Corrija:

She was worked when I called.

23. Leia:

Yesterday at 6 p.m., Anna was walking home from work. It was raining, and many people were waiting for buses. Anna was carrying an umbrella when she saw her friend Julia. Julia was standing near a café. Anna stopped, and they talked for a few minutes. Then Anna went home.

Responda:

  1. What was Anna doing at 6 p.m.?

  2. What was the weather like?

  3. What were many people doing?

  4. What was Anna carrying?

  5. Who did she see?

  6. Where was Julia standing?

  7. What did Anna do after seeing Julia?

  8. What did Anna do after the conversation?

24. Separe os verbos do texto anterior em Simple Past e Past Continuous.

25. Classifique:

I worked yesterday.

  1. Simple Past
  2. Past Continuous

26. Classifique:

I was working at 3 p.m.

  1. Simple Past
  2. Past Continuous

27. Classifique:

She was sleeping when I arrived.

Identifique o tempo de:

  1. was sleeping

  2. arrived

28. Complete livremente:

I was studying when __________.

29. Complete:

While I was studying, __________.

30. Produção

Escreva um pequeno texto de 8 a 10 frases sobre uma situação passada.

Inclua:

  • pelo menos três ações no Past Continuous;
  • pelo menos três eventos no Simple Past;
  • uma frase com when;
  • uma frase com while;
  • uma expressão de tempo;
  • uma sequência lógica de acontecimentos.

Gabarito comentado

1. B — was watching

A ação estava em andamento quando Maria ligou.

2. B — called

called

é o evento que ocorre durante:

was watching.

3. B — were playing

O horário específico:

at 5 p.m.

indica ação em andamento naquele momento.

4. B — played

A frase apresenta uma sequência concluída:

played

went home.

5. B — was cooking

A atividade estava acontecendo quando:

the lights went out.

6. A — was cleaning

Com:

while

as duas ações são apresentadas como simultâneas e em progresso.

7. A — was walking

I was walking home when I saw Anna.

8. B — had

Temos uma sequência:

had dinner

watched TV

went to bed.

9. A

I was sleeping when the phone rang.

Padrão:

ação em andamento + evento.

10. B

While I was studying, she was cooking.

Duas ações simultâneas.

11. B — was sleeping

A pergunta implícita é sobre o que estava acontecendo às 22h.

12. B — slept

A frase apresenta a duração completa do sono:

eight hours.

13. B — were

What were you doing…?

14. C — did

What did you do yesterday?

15.

I was studying at 8 p.m.

16.

I watched TV yesterday.

17.

I was studying when the phone rang.

18.

Laura was reading while Mark was watching TV.

19.

I went to school.

Ou, se a intenção é ação em andamento:

I was going to school.

20.

They were playing football.

21.

Were you studying at eight?

Se a intenção fosse perguntar simplesmente se a pessoa estudou:

Did you study?

22.

She was working when I called.

23.

  1. She was walking home from work.

  2. It was raining.

  3. They were waiting for buses.

  4. She was carrying an umbrella.

  5. She saw Julia.

  6. She was standing near a café.

  7. She stopped and talked to Julia.

  8. She went home.

24.

Past Continuous:

was walking

was raining

were waiting

was carrying

was standing.

Simple Past:

saw

stopped

talked

went.

25. A — Simple Past

A ação é apresentada como concluída.

26. B — Past Continuous

A ação estava em andamento às 15h.

27.

  1. Past Continuous

was sleeping.

  1. Simple Past

arrived.

28.

Possível resposta:

I was studying when my friend called.

29.

Possível resposta:

While I was studying, my brother was watching TV.

30.

Modelo:

Yesterday at 7 p.m., I was studying at home. My brother was watching TV, and my parents were cooking dinner. While I was reading, it started to rain. A few minutes later, the phone rang. I answered it and talked to my friend. He was waiting for a bus when he called me. We talked for ten minutes. Then I returned to my book and continued studying.

O texto usa Past Continuous como cenário e Simple Past para acontecimentos específicos.

Tarefa de consolidação

Crie duas colunas.

Na primeira:

Simple Past

Na segunda:

Past Continuous

Classifique estas ideias:

  • ação concluída;
  • ação em andamento;
  • evento pontual;
  • cenário de uma narrativa;
  • sequência de acontecimentos;
  • ação interrompida.

Depois produza dez pares.

Exemplo:

I studied yesterday.
I was studying at 8 p.m.

She worked on Monday.
She was working when I called.

Em seguida, escreva cinco frases com:

Past Continuous + when + Simple Past

Exemplo:

I was walking home when it started to rain.

Depois escreva cinco com:

while + Past Continuous + Past Continuous

Exemplo:

While I was reading, my sister was studying.

Por fim, responda:

What did you do yesterday?

e:

What were you doing at 8 p.m. yesterday?

As respostas devem mostrar claramente a diferença:

What did you do? → evento/atividade concluída

What were you doing? → atividade em andamento naquele momento

Finalize memorizando:

Simple Past = o que aconteceu

Past Continuous = o que estava acontecendo

E o padrão central:

I was studying when the phone rang.

While I was studying, my brother was watching TV.

Aula 42 — Future with will

Objetivos

Ao final desta aula, você deverá ser capaz de:

  • compreender o uso básico de will para falar sobre o futuro;
  • formar frases afirmativas, negativas e interrogativas;
  • usar corretamente will + verbo na forma base;
  • produzir previsões simples;
  • expressar decisões tomadas no momento da fala;
  • fazer ofertas e promessas;
  • usar marcadores temporais como tomorrow, next week, later e in the future;
  • diferenciar will de estruturas já estudadas no presente e no passado;
  • compreender pequenos textos e diálogos sobre eventos futuros;
  • evitar erros frequentes como will goes, will to study e does will.

Desenvolvimento

Depois de estudar o presente e o passado, começamos agora a falar sobre o futuro.

Uma das estruturas mais importantes é:

will

Usamos will para falar sobre eventos futuros em vários contextos.

Exemplo:

I will study tomorrow.

Eu estudarei amanhã.

Outro:

She will call you later.

Ela ligará para você mais tarde.

Estrutura afirmativa

A estrutura é:

subject + will + base verb

Exemplos:

I will work tomorrow.

She will study tonight.

They will travel next week.

Will não muda com o sujeito

Usamos a mesma forma com:

I

you

he

she

it

we

they.

Exemplos:

I will go.

You will go.

He will go.

She will go.

We will go.

They will go.

Não existe:

wills

para a terceira pessoa.

Verbo na forma básica

Depois de will, usamos o verbo sem:

  • -s;
  • -ed;
  • -ing;
  • to.

Correto:

She will work.

Incorreto:

She will works.

Correto:

I will go.

Incorreto:

I will to go.

Correto:

They will study.

Incorreto:

They will studying.

Forma contraída

Em contextos informais, will pode ser contraído.

I will → I’ll

you will → you’ll

he will → he’ll

she will → she’ll

we will → we’ll

they will → they’ll

Exemplos:

I’ll call you later.

She’ll study tomorrow.

We’ll see you next week.

Forma negativa

A estrutura é:

subject + will not + base verb

Forma contraída:

won’t

Exemplos:

I will not go.

I won’t go.

She won’t work tomorrow.

They won’t come tonight.

Won’t

Won’t significa:

will not.

Exemplo:

I won’t be late.

Outro:

He won’t study tonight.

Perguntas

A estrutura é:

Will + subject + base verb?

Exemplos:

Will you work tomorrow?

Will she come?

Will they study?

Short answers

Will you go?

Yes, I will.

No, I won’t.

Outro:

Will Maria come?

Yes, she will.

No, she won’t.

Não usamos do/does/did

Erro:

Does she will come?

Correto:

Will she come?

Erro:

Do they will study?

Correto:

Will they study?

Will já funciona como auxiliar.

Perguntas com question words

Estrutura:

question word + will + subject + base verb?

Exemplos:

What will you do tomorrow?

Where will she go?

When will they arrive?

Who will you call?

How will you travel?

What will you do?

Pergunta muito frequente:

What will you do tomorrow?

Resposta:

I will study.

ou:

I’ll study.

Marcadores de futuro

Palavras e expressões comuns:

tomorrow

amanhã.

tomorrow morning

amanhã de manhã.

tomorrow night

amanhã à noite.

next week

semana que vem.

next month

mês que vem.

next year

ano que vem.

later

mais tarde.

soon

em breve.

in the future

no futuro.

Tomorrow

Exemplo:

I will work tomorrow.

Next week

We will travel next week.

Later

I’ll call you later.

Soon

The class will start soon.

Previsões

Um uso muito comum de will é fazer previsões.

Exemplo:

It will rain tomorrow.

Outro:

The test will be difficult.

Outro:

People will use more technology in the future.

A ideia é:

acreditamos que algo acontecerá.

I think + will

Uma estrutura muito comum:

I think + subject + will + verb

Exemplo:

I think it will rain.

I think she will pass the test.

I think they will arrive early.

Probably

Também podemos usar:

probably

provavelmente.

Exemplo:

She will probably come later.

It will probably rain tomorrow.

Maybe

Outra forma simples:

Maybe he will call.

Maybe they will travel next month.

Decisões tomadas no momento

Will também é usado quando decidimos algo no momento da fala.

Exemplo:

A: The phone is ringing.
B: I’ll answer it.

A decisão de atender é tomada naquele momento.

Outro:

A: I’m thirsty.
B: I’ll get you some water.

Exemplo de decisão espontânea

A: We don’t have milk.
B: I’ll buy some.

A pessoa decide comprar naquele instante.

Ofertas

Will também aparece em ofertas.

I’ll help you.

I’ll carry your bag.

I’ll open the door.

Exemplo:

A: This box is heavy.
B: I’ll help you.

Promessas

Outro uso importante:

I will call you.

I won’t forget.

I’ll help you tomorrow.

Exemplo:

Don’t worry. I’ll be there.

Isso pode funcionar como promessa.

Will para concordar em fazer algo

A: Can you send me the document?
B: Yes, I’ll send it tonight.

Will e be

O verbo be também fica na forma base.

I will be at home.

She will be happy.

They will be busy.

Não:

She will is happy.

Correto:

She will be happy.

There will be

Para dizer que algo existirá:

There will be a meeting tomorrow.

There will be many people at the event.

There will be a test next week.

Comparando presente e futuro

Presente:

I study every day.

Futuro:

I will study tomorrow.

Presente:

She works at a hospital.

Futuro:

She will work tomorrow.

Comparando passado e futuro

Passado:

I worked yesterday.

Futuro:

I will work tomorrow.

Passado:

She went to school.

Futuro:

She will go to school.

Observe que depois de will usamos:

go

não:

went.

Forma base até com verbos irregulares

Os verbos irregulares só mudam no passado.

Depois de will, voltam para a forma base.

go → will go

eat → will eat

see → will see

take → will take

buy → will buy

write → will write.

Exemplo:

I will go tomorrow.

Não:

I will went tomorrow.

Frases afirmativas

I will study tonight.

She will visit her family next week.

He will take the bus tomorrow.

We will watch a movie later.

Negativas

I won’t study tonight.

She won’t work tomorrow.

They won’t travel next month.

Perguntas

Will you study tonight?

Will she work tomorrow?

Will they travel next month?

Short answers

Will you study?

Yes, I will.

No, I won’t.

Previsão do tempo

Exemplos:

It will be hot tomorrow.

It will rain in the afternoon.

It won’t be cold.

Essas estruturas são comuns em Reading e Listening.

Previsões pessoais

I think I will pass the exam.

I think I will learn more English.

I think I will work in another city in the future.

Promessas

I will study more.

I won’t forget the meeting.

I’ll call you tomorrow.

Ofertas

I’ll help you.

I’ll carry that.

I’ll make some coffee.

Decisão rápida

A: We need bread.
B: I’ll go to the supermarket.

Perguntas sobre o futuro

What will you do tomorrow?

Where will you go?

Who will you meet?

What time will you arrive?

Will you work?

Pequeno diálogo

A: What will you do tomorrow?
B: I’ll study in the morning.
A: Will you work in the afternoon?
B: No, I won’t. I’ll stay at home.

Outro diálogo

A: The room is very hot.
B: I’ll open the window.

Aqui will expressa uma decisão no momento.

Texto simples

Leia:

Tomorrow, Laura will have a busy day. She will wake up at seven and will go to university in the morning. She will have lunch with a friend. In the afternoon, she will study for an exam. She won’t work tomorrow. In the evening, she will watch a movie at home.

Ações futuras:

will wake up

will go

will have

will study

won’t work

will watch.

Repetição de will

Em inglês, podemos repetir will:

She will wake up and will go to university.

Mas, quando o sujeito é o mesmo, também é comum:

She will wake up and go to university.

A segunda forma é mais enxuta.

Erros frequentes

Erro 1

She will works tomorrow.

Correto:

She will work tomorrow.

Erro 2

I will to study.

Correto:

I will study.

Erro 3

He will went home.

Correto:

He will go home.

Erro 4

They won’t studied.

Correto:

They won’t study.

Erro 5

Does she will come?

Correto:

Will she come?

Erro 6

Will she comes?

Correto:

Will she come?

Will x Simple Present

Simple Present:

I work every Monday.

rotina.

Future with will:

I will work tomorrow.

evento futuro.

Will x Present Continuous

Present Continuous:

I am studying now.

ação atual.

Future:

I will study later.

ação futura.

Contexto é essencial

Compare:

I study English every day.

rotina.

I studied English yesterday.

passado.

I am studying English now.

ação atual.

I will study English tomorrow.

futuro.

Linha do tempo

yesterday → I studied

now → I am studying

tomorrow → I will study.

Essa comparação ajuda a consolidar os tempos verbais.

Reading

Em textos futuros, procure:

will

won’t

tomorrow

next…

soon

later.

Essas pistas ajudam a reconhecer o período temporal.

Listening

Em fala rápida, I’ll, he’ll, she’ll, we’ll e they’ll podem ser difíceis de perceber inicialmente.

Treine como unidades:

I’ll call.

She’ll come.

We’ll see.

Won’t x want

Em Listening, estudantes podem confundir:

won’t

com:

want.

Compare:

I won’t go.

I want to go.

O contexto e a estrutura ajudam.

Após:

won’t

vem verbo base:

won’t go.

Após:

want

normalmente aparece:

want to go.

Writing

Para escrever sobre futuro:

Tomorrow, I will study in the morning. I will have lunch at home. In the afternoon, I will work. At night, I will watch TV.

Speaking

Pergunta:

What will you do next weekend?

Resposta:

I’ll stay at home and study.

Pergunta:

Will you work?

No, I won’t.

Uma observação importante

Will não é a única maneira de falar sobre futuro em inglês.

Há outras estruturas, como:

be going to

que será estudada separadamente.

Nesta aula, concentre-se nos usos fundamentais de will.

Vocabulário-chave

future — futuro

tomorrow — amanhã

later — mais tarde

soon — em breve

next week — semana que vem

next month — mês que vem

next year — ano que vem

in the future — no futuro

prediction — previsão

promise — promessa

offer — oferta

decision — decisão

probably — provavelmente

maybe — talvez

think — pensar/achar

I think it will rain.

help — ajudar

I’ll help you.

call — ligar

I’ll call you later.

arrive — chegar

They will arrive at eight.

stay — ficar

We will stay at home.

Estratégia de prova

Ao encontrar uma lacuna com will, elimine qualquer alternativa que não esteja na forma básica.

Exemplo:

She will ___ tomorrow.

  1. works
  2. worked
  3. work
  4. working

Resposta:

work.

Use:

will + base verb

won’t + base verb

Will + subject + base verb?

Procure também marcadores de futuro:

tomorrow

next week

later

soon.

Em questões de uso, observe o contexto.

Se a decisão acontece no momento:

I’ll help you.

Se é uma previsão:

I think it will rain.

Se é uma promessa:

I won’t forget.

Use pelo menos:

Modelo:

Tomorrow, Julia will wake up at seven. She will have breakfast at home. She will go to university in the morning. She will study for an exam in the afternoon. She won’t work tomorrow. Tarefa de consolidação

Transforme dez verbos em frases futuras usando:

will + base verb.

Use:

work

study

go

eat

see

take

buy

call

travel

stay.

Depois transforme cinco dessas frases em negativas.

Exemplo:

I will work tomorrow.

I won’t work tomorrow.

Transforme outras cinco em perguntas:

Will you work tomorrow?

Em seguida, escreva três exemplos de cada uso:

Previsão

I think…

Decisão no momento

I’ll…

Oferta

I’ll help…

Promessa

I won’t…

Por fim, compare:

I studied yesterday.

I am studying now.

I will study tomorrow.

Faça o mesmo com:

work

go

eat

watch

call.

Finalize memorizando:

will + base verb

won’t + base verb

Will + subject + base verb?

E:

prediction → I think it will…

instant decision → I’ll…

offer → I’ll help…

promise → I will / I won’t…

Aula 43 — Be going to

Objetivos

Ao final desta aula, você deverá ser capaz de:

  • compreender a estrutura be going to;
  • formar frases afirmativas, negativas e interrogativas;
  • usar corretamente am/is/are going to + verbo na forma base;
  • falar sobre planos e intenções futuras;
  • expressar previsões baseadas em evidências presentes;
  • diferenciar, em nível básico, will e be going to;
  • formular perguntas sobre planos futuros;
  • compreender pequenos textos e diálogos sobre intenções;
  • produzir frases sobre seus próprios planos;
  • evitar erros como I going to, she is going to studies e do you going to…?

Desenvolvimento

Na aula anterior, estudamos:

will

Agora veremos outra estrutura muito importante para falar sobre o futuro:

be going to

Essa estrutura é muito usada para:

  • planos;
  • intenções;
  • decisões já tomadas;
  • previsões baseadas em sinais visíveis ou evidências presentes.

Exemplo:

I am going to study tonight.

Eu vou estudar hoje à noite.

A ideia é que esse estudo já faz parte de um plano ou intenção.

Estrutura afirmativa

A estrutura é:

subject + am/is/are + going to + base verb

Exemplos:

I am going to study.

She is going to travel.

They are going to work.

O verbo to be muda com o sujeito

Usamos:

I am

you are

he is

she is

it is

we are

they are.

Depois:

going to + verbo base.

Exemplos completos

I am going to visit my grandmother tomorrow.

She is going to buy a new computer.

We are going to study for the exam.

They are going to travel next month.

Forma contraída

Na fala e na escrita informal:

I am → I’m

you are → you’re

he is → he’s

she is → she’s

we are → we’re

they are → they’re.

Exemplos:

I’m going to study tonight.

She’s going to travel tomorrow.

We’re going to cook dinner.

Verbo principal na forma base

Depois de:

going to

usamos o verbo na forma básica.

Correto:

She is going to study.

Incorreto:

She is going to studies.

Correto:

They are going to go.

Incorreto:

They are going to went.

Correto:

I am going to buy a book.

Incorreto:

I am going to buying a book.

Uso 1: planos

Um dos principais usos é falar sobre planos já existentes.

Exemplo:

I’m going to study this evening.

A pessoa já pretende estudar.

Outro:

We’re going to visit our friends on Saturday.

Isso indica um plano.

Uso 2: intenções

Também usamos be going to para intenções.

I am going to learn Spanish.

She is going to exercise more.

They are going to save money.

Essas ações ainda não aconteceram, mas existe intenção.

Plano x decisão instantânea

Compare:

I’m going to buy a new phone next month.

Isso sugere planejamento prévio.

Agora:

The phone is ringing. I’ll answer it.

Aqui a decisão acontece no momento da fala.

Esse é um contraste importante entre:

be going to

e:

will.

Will x going to: ideia básica

Use be going to frequentemente para:

plano já pensado.

Use will frequentemente para:

decisão tomada no momento.

Compare:

I’m going to cook dinner tonight.

Plano.

A: I’m hungry.
B: I’ll make you a sandwich.

Decisão espontânea/oferta.

Não é uma divisão absoluta

Na língua real, os usos podem se sobrepor.

Neste nível, use esse contraste como guia:

plan → going to

instant decision → will

Previsão com evidência

Outro uso importante:

be going to

pode expressar uma previsão baseada em algo que vemos ou percebemos agora.

Exemplo:

Look at those dark clouds. It’s going to rain.

As nuvens escuras são evidência.

Outro:

Be careful! You’re going to fall.

A pessoa parece estar em risco de cair.

Will para previsão mais neutra

Compare:

I think it will rain tomorrow.

É uma opinião/previsão.

Look at those clouds. It’s going to rain.

Existe uma evidência presente.

Forma negativa

A estrutura é:

subject + am/is/are + not + going to + base verb

Exemplos:

I am not going to work tomorrow.

She isn’t going to travel.

They aren’t going to study tonight.

Contrações negativas

is not → isn’t

are not → aren’t.

Com I am:

I’m not going to…

Exemplo:

I’m not going to go out tonight.

Perguntas

A estrutura é:

Am/Is/Are + subject + going to + base verb?

Exemplos:

Are you going to study tonight?

Is she going to travel?

Are they going to work tomorrow?

Short answers

Are you going to study?

Yes, I am.

No, I’m not.

Outro:

Is Laura going to travel?

Yes, she is.

No, she isn’t.

Outro:

Are they going to come?

Yes, they are.

No, they aren’t.

Não repetimos going to na resposta curta

Pergunta:

Are you going to study?

Resposta:

Yes, I am.

Não é necessário:

Yes, I am going to.

Perguntas com question words

What are you going to do tomorrow?

Where is she going to go?

When are they going to travel?

Who are you going to visit?

How are you going to get there?

What are you going to do?

Pergunta central:

What are you going to do this weekend?

Resposta:

I’m going to study.

Ou:

I’m going to visit my family.

Where are you going to go?

Where are you going to go on vacation?

I’m going to go to Recife.

Em fala natural, também podemos simplesmente dizer:

I’m going to Recife.

Mas, para praticar a estrutura futura:

I’m going to go to Recife.

Going to go

A sequência:

going to go

pode parecer repetitiva, mas é gramatical.

I’m going to go home.

Primeiro:

going to

marca o futuro.

Segundo:

go

é o verbo principal.

Going to have

We’re going to have a test next week.

Aqui:

have

fica na forma base.

Going to be

She is going to be a doctor.

The test is going to be difficult.

Depois de going to, usamos:

be

e não:

is/are.

Não:

It is going to is difficult.

Correto:

It is going to be difficult.

Expressões de tempo

Comuns:

tomorrow

tonight

this afternoon

this evening

this weekend

next week

next month

next year

soon.

Exemplo:

I’m going to study tonight.

We’re going to travel next month.

Planos de estudo

I’m going to study English tonight.

I’m going to review grammar tomorrow.

We’re going to have a test next week.

Planos de trabalho

She’s going to start a new job next month.

They’re going to have a meeting tomorrow.

Planos pessoais

I’m going to visit my family.

I’m going to clean my room.

I’m going to buy some books.

I’m going to cook dinner.

Férias e viagens

We’re going to travel in July.

We’re going to stay at a hotel.

We’re going to visit museums.

We’re going to take the bus.

Pequeno diálogo

A: What are you going to do this weekend?
B: I’m going to visit my parents.
A: Are you going to stay there all weekend?
B: No, I’m not. I’m going to come home on Sunday afternoon.

Outro diálogo

A: Look at those clouds.
B: Yes. It’s going to rain.

Aqui temos previsão baseada em evidência.

Going to em Reading

Procure a estrutura completa:

am/is/are + going to + verb.

Exemplo:

Laura is going to travel next week.

Isso indica futuro.

Going to em Listening

Na fala natural:

going to

pode soar de maneira reduzida.

Em registros informais, você pode ouvir algo semelhante a:

gonna.

Mas, em escrita padrão, especialmente em provas, use:

going to.

Não escreva gonna em tarefas formais.

Plano já decidido

Leia:

I bought a plane ticket yesterday. I’m going to travel next week.

A compra da passagem reforça que existe um plano.

Previsão por evidência

The glass is near the edge of the table. It’s going to fall.

A posição do copo é a evidência.

Will e going to lado a lado

Situação:

A: What are your plans for Saturday?
B: I’m going to study in the morning.

Plano.

Agora:

A: I can’t carry these books.
B: I’ll help you.

Decisão/oferta no momento.

Previsões

Opinião:

I think our team will win.

Evidência presente:

They’re playing very well. They’re going to win.

No nível A2, essa distinção é suficiente.

Não usamos do/does

Erro:

Do you going to study?

Correto:

Are you going to study?

Erro:

Does she going to travel?

Correto:

Is she going to travel?

O auxiliar da estrutura é o próprio:

am/is/are.

Não omita o verb to be

Erro:

I going to study.

Correto:

I am going to study.

Erro:

They going to travel.

Correto:

They are going to travel.

Não use -s no verbo principal

Erro:

She is going to studies.

Correto:

She is going to study.

Não coloque to novamente

Erro:

I’m going to to study.

Correto:

I’m going to study.

Não use passado depois de going to

Erro:

We’re going to went home.

Correto:

We’re going to go home.

Comparando quatro tempos/estruturas

Rotina:

I study English every day.

Ação atual:

I am studying English now.

Passado:

I studied English yesterday.

Plano futuro:

I am going to study English tomorrow.

Will no mesmo contraste

I will study English tomorrow.

Também é futuro, mas pode expressar uma decisão, previsão ou promessa dependendo do contexto.

Contexto é mais importante que tradução

As duas frases:

I will study tomorrow.

I am going to study tomorrow.

podem ser traduzidas de maneira semelhante em português.

A diferença aparece no contexto e na intenção comunicativa.

Exemplo contextual 1

A: What are your plans for tomorrow?
B: I’m going to study.

Como a pergunta é sobre:

plans

going to é muito natural.

Exemplo contextual 2

A: We have a test tomorrow!
B: Really? I’ll study tonight.

A decisão pode estar sendo tomada naquele momento.

Exemplo contextual 3

Look at the child! He’s going to fall!

Previsão baseada em evidência.

Texto curto

Leia:

Julia has a busy weekend planned. On Saturday morning, she’s going to clean her apartment. In the afternoon, she’s going to meet two friends at a café. They are going to watch a movie in the evening. On Sunday, Julia isn’t going to go out. She’s going to stay at home and study for an exam.

Planos:

is going to clean

is going to meet

are going to watch

isn’t going to go out

is going to stay

study.

Um único going to para dois verbos

Podemos dizer:

She’s going to stay at home and study.

O segundo verbo:

study

continua ligado a:

going to.

Não precisamos repetir:

she’s going to.

Perguntando sobre planos

Are you going to study tonight?

What are you going to eat?

Where are you going to stay?

Who are you going to meet?

When are you going to leave?

How are you going to travel?

Essas estruturas são muito úteis em Speaking.

Vocabulário-chave

plan — plano

What’s your plan?

intention — intenção

future — futuro

tonight — hoje à noite

this weekend — neste fim de semana

next week — semana que vem

planned — planejado

visit — visitar

travel — viajar

stay — ficar/hospedar-se

meet — encontrar

study — estudar

work — trabalhar

buy — comprar

start — começar

rain — chover

It’s going to rain.

fall — cair

He’s going to fall.

evidence — evidência

cloud — nuvem

dark clouds.

Estratégia de prova

Primeiro identifique se o contexto apresenta:

a plan/intention

ou:

present evidence.

Esses contextos favorecem:

be going to.

Depois confira a estrutura:

am/is/are + going to + base verb

Exemplo:

She ___ travel next month.

  1. is going to
  2. going to
  3. will going
  4. is going to travels

Resposta:

is going to.

Para perguntas:

___ they going to study?

  1. Do
  2. Did
  3. Are
  4. Will

Resposta:

Are.

Para diferenciar de will, pergunte:

Was this planned before?

Se sim, going to costuma ser uma boa escolha.

Is the decision happening now?

Se sim, will pode ser mais adequado.
