  4. did

30. Produção

Escreva oito a dez frases sobre seus planos para um fim de semana fictício.

Use:

  • pelo menos cinco formas afirmativas com going to;
  • duas negativas;
  • uma pergunta;
  • uma previsão baseada em evidência;
  • pelo menos três expressões de tempo futuro.

Gabarito comentado

1. A — am

I am going to…

2. B — is

She is going to…

3. C — are

They are going to…

4. C — buy

Depois de:

going to

usamos o verbo base.

5. B — study

Não usamos:

studies

depois de going to.

6. B

I am going to work tomorrow.

A estrutura precisa incluir:

am + going to + work.

7.

She isn’t going to travel.

ou:

She is not going to travel.

8.

They aren’t going to study tonight.

9. A — am not

I am not going to go out tonight.

10.

Is she going to buy a computer?

11.

Are they going to visit London?

12. B — Are

Are you going to work tomorrow?

13. C — Is

Is Maria going to travel?

14.

Yes, I am.

15.

No, he isn’t.

16. B — are

What are you going to do…?

17. C — go

going to + base verb.

18. B — have

We are going to have a test.

19. A — is going to

A frase apresenta evidência presente:

The sky is very dark.

Logo:

It’s going to rain.

20. B — I’ll

A decisão/oferta é feita no momento:

I’ll help you.

21. A — am going to

A pergunta é sobre:

plans.

Logo:

I’m going to visit my grandparents.

22.

I am going to study tomorrow.

Faltava:

am.

23.

She is going to study English.

Depois de going to, usamos:

study.

24.

Are you going to work?

Não usamos do nessa estrutura.

25.

They are going to go home.

Depois de:

going to

usamos:

go.

26.

  1. His sister.

  2. By train.

  3. On Saturday morning.

  4. His sister.

  5. At a restaurant.

  6. They are going to visit a museum.

  7. No, he isn’t.

  8. On Sunday evening.

27.

As formas são:

is going to visit

is going to take

is going to meet

are going to have

[are going to] visit

isn’t going to stay

is going to come.

28. A — are going to

A compra dos ingressos mostra que o plano já existe.

29. B — will

I’ll open it.

A decisão acontece no momento da fala.

30.

Modelo:

This weekend, I’m going to stay at home on Saturday morning. I’m going to study English and clean my room. In the afternoon, I’m going to meet two friends. We’re going to have coffee together. I’m not going to work on Saturday. I’m not going to stay out late. On Sunday, I’m going to visit my family. Are we going to have lunch together? Yes, we are. The sky is very dark, so I think it’s going to rain on Sunday afternoon.

Tarefa de consolidação

Escreva dez frases sobre planos usando:

am/is/are going to + base verb

Use estes verbos:

study

work

travel

visit

buy

meet

cook

watch

go

have.

Depois transforme cinco frases em negativas.

Exemplo:

I’m going to work tomorrow.

I’m not going to work tomorrow.

Transforme outras cinco em perguntas:

Are you going to work tomorrow?

Depois produza três exemplos de:

Planos

I’m going to…

Intenções

I’m going to…

Previsões com evidência

Look… It’s going to…

Por fim, compare:

A: What are your plans for tonight?
B: I’m going to study.

com:

A: I need help with this exercise.
B: I’ll help you.

E:

I think it will rain tomorrow.

com:

Look at those dark clouds. It’s going to rain.

Finalize memorizando:

plan/intention → be going to

present evidence → be going to

instant decision → will

offer/promise → will

E a estrutura central:

I am going to study.

She isn’t going to travel.

Are they going to work?

Aula 44 — Present Continuous para planos futuros

Objetivos

Ao final desta aula, você deverá ser capaz de:

  • reconhecer o uso do Present Continuous para falar de compromissos e planos futuros já organizados;
  • diferenciar o Present Continuous com sentido de presente e com sentido de futuro;
  • formar frases afirmativas, negativas e interrogativas sobre planos futuros;
  • usar corretamente am/is/are + verb-ing;
  • reconhecer marcadores como tomorrow, tonight, this weekend, next Monday;
  • distinguir, em nível básico, will, be going to e Present Continuous;
  • compreender pequenos diálogos sobre compromissos marcados;
  • falar sobre agenda, encontros e atividades futuras;
  • interpretar mensagens e calendários simples;
  • evitar erros como I am meet, she is go tomorrow e do you meeting…?

Desenvolvimento

Até agora, você já estudou três formas importantes de falar sobre o futuro:

will

be going to

e agora:

Present Continuous

O Present Continuous não serve apenas para falar sobre o que está acontecendo agora.

Ele também pode ser usado para falar de:

planos futuros já combinados ou organizados.

Exemplo:

I am meeting Laura tomorrow.

Eu vou encontrar Laura amanhã.

A ideia é que esse encontro já está combinado.

Estrutura

A estrutura é a mesma do Present Continuous que você já conhece:

subject + am/is/are + verb-ing

Exemplo:

I am studying now.

ação acontecendo neste momento.

Agora:

I am studying with Julia tomorrow.

plano futuro já organizado.

A estrutura é igual.

O contexto mostra o sentido.

Marcador temporal é essencial

Compare:

I am working.

Sem contexto, pensamos principalmente no presente.

Agora:

I am working tomorrow.

A palavra:

tomorrow

indica futuro.

Outro:

She is meeting the doctor at 3 p.m. tomorrow.

A ação ainda não está acontecendo, mas já está programada.

Uso principal: arrangement

Um conceito importante é:

arrangement

Um arrangement é um compromisso ou plano organizado.

Pode envolver:

  • horário marcado;
  • local definido;
  • outra pessoa;
  • reserva;
  • compromisso profissional;
  • consulta;
  • viagem organizada.

Exemplo:

I’m meeting my teacher at 4 p.m.

Isso parece mais organizado do que uma intenção vaga.

Plano concreto

Compare:

I’m going to visit my friend someday.

Essa frase pode expressar intenção.

Agora:

I’m visiting my friend on Saturday at 3 p.m.

Há:

  • dia;
  • horário;
  • compromisso mais definido.

Por isso, o Present Continuous é muito natural.

Exemplos

I’m having lunch with Anna tomorrow.

We’re traveling to São Paulo next Friday.

She is seeing the dentist at 10 a.m.

They are playing football on Saturday.

My parents are visiting us this weekend.

Forma afirmativa

I am meeting Peter tomorrow.

She is working tonight.

We are having dinner together on Friday.

They are leaving next Monday.

Contrações

I am → I’m

you are → you’re

he is → he’s

she is → she’s

we are → we’re

they are → they’re

Exemplos:

I’m meeting Carlos at six.

She’s traveling tomorrow.

We’re having a class on Saturday.

Forma negativa

A estrutura:

subject + am/is/are + not + verb-ing

Exemplos:

I’m not working tomorrow.

She isn’t coming tonight.

They aren’t traveling this weekend.

Perguntas

Am/Is/Are + subject + verb-ing?

Exemplos:

Are you working tomorrow?

Is Laura coming tonight?

Are they traveling next week?

Short answers

Are you working tomorrow?

Yes, I am.

No, I’m not.

Outro:

Is Maria coming?

Yes, she is.

No, she isn’t.

Perguntas com question words

What are you doing tomorrow?

Where are you going tonight?

Who are you meeting?

When are you leaving?

What time are you arriving?

Essas perguntas são muito úteis em Speaking.

What are you doing tomorrow?

Dependendo do contexto, essa pergunta não quer saber o que você está fazendo agora.

Ela significa:

quais são seus planos para amanhã?

Resposta:

I’m studying in the morning and meeting a friend in the afternoon.

Going

O verbo:

go

fica:

going.

Exemplo:

I’m going to the bank tomorrow.

Aqui temos Present Continuous do verbo go.

A frase significa:

Eu vou ao banco amanhã.

Atenção: going to x be going to

Compare:

I’m going to the bank tomorrow.

Aqui:

going

é o verbo go no Present Continuous.

Agora:

I’m going to study tomorrow.

Aqui:

be going to

é uma estrutura de futuro.

Como diferenciar?

Observe o que vem depois de:

going to.

Se vem um lugar ou substantivo:

I’m going to the bank.

Temos o verbo go.

Se vem outro verbo:

I’m going to study.

Temos:

be going to + verb.

Present Continuous para viagem

We’re flying to Madrid next week.

We’re leaving on Monday.

We’re staying at a hotel.

Essas frases soam como planos já organizados.

Verbos frequentes nesse uso

Alguns verbos aparecem muito com futuro programado:

meet

come

go

leave

arrive

travel

fly

stay

have

work

study

play

see.

Meet

I’m meeting my professor tomorrow.

Isso sugere compromisso marcado.

See

Em certos contextos:

I’m seeing the doctor tomorrow.

Significa:

tenho consulta marcada com o médico.

Have

We’re having a meeting at 2 p.m.

I’m having dinner with my family tonight.

Leave e arrive

The team is leaving tomorrow morning.

My friend is arriving at eight.

Esses verbos são comuns em planos de viagem.

Present Continuous x rotina

Compare:

I work on Mondays.

Simple Present: rotina.

I’m working next Monday.

Present Continuous: compromisso específico futuro.

Present Continuous x ação atual

I’m working now.

ação atual.

I’m working tomorrow.

plano futuro.

A única diferença está no contexto temporal.

Present Continuous x going to

Compare:

I’m going to study tonight.

intenção/plano.

I’m studying with Julia at 7 tonight.

plano mais específico e organizado.

Ambas podem estar corretas.

A diferença é principalmente de perspectiva.

Going to: intenção

I’m going to exercise more.

Isso pode ser apenas uma intenção.

Present Continuous: compromisso organizado

I’m exercising with my trainer at 6 tomorrow.

Há detalhes concretos.

Will x Present Continuous

Compare:

I’ll call Sarah.

A decisão pode ter sido tomada agora.

I’m calling Sarah at 8 tonight.

O telefonema já está programado.

Três formas futuras

Will

I’ll help you.

decisão espontânea/oferta.

Be going to

I’m going to study more.

intenção/plano.

Present Continuous

I’m studying with Laura at 7 tomorrow.

compromisso organizado.

Não transforme a distinção em regra absoluta

Na língua real, essas estruturas podem se sobrepor.

Exemplo:

I’m going to visit my parents this weekend.

e:

I’m visiting my parents this weekend.

As duas podem ser naturais.

A segunda costuma destacar mais o plano como já definido.

Agenda

Imagine:

Monday 9 a.m. — dentist
Tuesday 2 p.m. — meeting
Friday 7 p.m. — dinner with Sarah

Podemos dizer:

I’m seeing the dentist on Monday at nine.

I’m having a meeting on Tuesday at two.

I’m having dinner with Sarah on Friday at seven.

Datas e horários

O Present Continuous com futuro frequentemente aparece com informações específicas.

We’re meeting at 5 p.m.

She’s leaving on Friday.

They’re arriving on June 12.

In, on e at

Continue usando corretamente as preposições:

at + horário

at 7 p.m.

on + dia/data

on Monday

on June 10

in + mês

in July.

Exemplo:

We’re traveling in July.

Tonight

I’m working tonight.

Isso pode significar que o turno já está definido.

This weekend

We’re visiting our grandparents this weekend.

Next week

I’m starting a new course next week.

Pequeno diálogo

A: What are you doing tomorrow?
B: I’m working in the morning.
A: Are you free in the afternoon?
B: No, I’m meeting my teacher at three.

Aqui, o diálogo é sobre agenda futura.

Outro diálogo

A: Are you coming to the party tonight?
B: No, I’m not. I’m studying for a test.

A atividade está planejada para aquela noite.

Mensagem curta

Hi Tom,
I’m meeting Julia at the café at 4 p.m. tomorrow. Are you coming too?
Anna

Informações:

  • pessoa: Julia;
  • local: café;
  • horário: 4 p.m.;
  • dia: tomorrow.

Reading

Em Reading, uma forma am/is/are + -ing não significa automaticamente “agora”.

Leia o marcador temporal.

Exemplo:

Sarah is traveling next week.

Não está viajando agora.

É futuro.

Listening

Pergunta:

What is Sarah doing tomorrow?

Áudio:

She’s meeting her manager at ten.

A resposta é:

meeting her manager.

O calendário ajuda a prever o sentido

Se um exercício apresenta:

  • agenda;
  • timetable;
  • calendar;
  • appointments;

o Present Continuous pode estar sendo usado para planos futuros.

Futuro negativo

I’m not going out tonight.

She isn’t working tomorrow.

We’re not meeting on Friday.

Essas frases indicam que determinado plano não acontecerá.

Mudança de plano

I’m not meeting Tom tomorrow. I’m meeting him on Friday.

A primeira parte cancela um compromisso.

A segunda apresenta o novo.

Perguntando disponibilidade

Are you working tomorrow?

Are you doing anything tonight?

Are you meeting anyone after class?

Are you doing anything…?

Essa é uma pergunta comum para verificar planos.

Are you doing anything this weekend?

Resposta:

Yes. I’m visiting my family.

Ou:

No, I’m not.

Making arrangements

O Present Continuous é muito útil para combinar compromissos.

A: Are you free tomorrow?
B: Yes.
A: I’m having lunch at the café at one. Do you want to come?
B: Sure.

Going to com verbo go

Uma estrutura visualmente confusa:

I’m going to go to the library.

Isso é:

be going to + go.

Significa:

pretendo ir à biblioteca.

Agora:

I’m going to the library.

É:

Present Continuous do verbo go.

Em muitos contextos, ambas falam do futuro.

Comparação

I’m going to go to the library tomorrow.

ênfase na intenção.

I’m going to the library tomorrow.

mais natural como compromisso/plano definido em muitos contextos.

Erros frequentes

Erro 1

I meeting my teacher tomorrow.

Correto:

I’m meeting my teacher tomorrow.

Faltava:

am.

Erro 2

She is meet Laura tonight.

Correto:

She is meeting Laura tonight.

Erro 3

They are travel next week.

Correto:

They are traveling next week.

Erro 4

Do you meeting Peter tomorrow?

Correto:

Are you meeting Peter tomorrow?

Erro 5

She doesn’t coming tonight.

Correto:

She isn’t coming tonight.

Pergunta no presente x pergunta sobre futuro

What are you doing?

Sem contexto, normalmente:

o que você está fazendo agora?

What are you doing tomorrow?

Agora significa:

o que você fará amanhã?

Comparando linha temporal

I studied yesterday.

passado.

I’m studying now.

presente.

I’m studying with Anna tomorrow.

futuro programado.

Plano pessoal

Exemplo:

Tomorrow, I’m waking up early. I’m meeting my professor at nine. I’m having lunch with two classmates at noon. In the afternoon, I’m studying at the library. I’m coming home at six.

Esse tipo de texto descreve uma agenda futura.

Um cuidado com wake up

Em muitos contextos, para um plano pessoal, também é natural usar:

I’m going to wake up early.

Nem toda atividade futura precisa necessariamente ser apresentada no Present Continuous.

Ele é particularmente útil quando há organização concreta.

Vocabulário-chave

arrangement — compromisso/plano organizado

appointment — compromisso/consulta marcada

schedule — agenda/cronograma

calendar — calendário

meeting — reunião/encontro

plan — plano

tonight — hoje à noite

tomorrow — amanhã

this weekend — neste fim de semana

next week — semana que vem

meet — encontrar

I’m meeting Anna tomorrow.

leave — partir

We’re leaving on Friday.

arrive — chegar

She’s arriving at eight.

visit — visitar

We’re visiting our family.

stay — ficar/hospedar-se

fly — viajar de avião/voar

They’re flying tomorrow.

appointment — compromisso agendado

I have an appointment tomorrow.

Estratégia de prova

Ao ver:

am/is/are + verb-ing

não responda automaticamente:

present action.

Procure o marcador temporal.

Se houver:

now

right now

at the moment

provavelmente é ação presente.

Se houver:

tomorrow

tonight

next week

on Friday

pode ser um plano futuro.

Exemplo:

She ___ her doctor tomorrow at ten.

  1. sees every day
  2. is seeing
  3. saw
  4. was seeing

Como existe um compromisso futuro específico:

is seeing

é uma opção natural.

Para diferenciar:

will → spontaneous decision/prediction

going to → intention/plan

Present Continuous → arranged future plan

Prática

1. Complete:

I ___ meeting Anna tomorrow.

  1. am
  2. is
  3. are
  4. do

2. Complete:

She ___ working tonight.

  1. am
  2. is
  3. are
  4. does

3. Complete:

They ___ traveling next week.

  1. is
  2. am
  3. are
  4. do

4. Complete:

We are ___ dinner with Laura tonight.

  1. have
  2. had
  3. having
  4. has

5. Complete:

He is ___ tomorrow morning.

  1. leave
  2. leaving
  3. left
  4. leaves

6. Escolha a frase correta.

  1. I meeting my professor tomorrow.
  2. I am meeting my professor tomorrow.
  3. I am meet my professor tomorrow.
  4. I do meeting my professor tomorrow.

7. Transforme para a negativa:

She is working tomorrow.

8. Transforme:

They are traveling this weekend.

9. Complete:

I ___ going out tonight.

  1. am not
  2. don’t
  3. didn’t
  4. wasn’t

10. Transforme em pergunta:

Laura is coming tonight.

11. Transforme:

They are meeting at six.

12. Complete:

___ you working tomorrow?

  1. Do
  2. Are
  3. Did
  4. Will do

13. Complete:

___ Daniel meeting us tonight?

  1. Does
  2. Is
  3. Did
  4. Do

14. Responda afirmativamente:

Are you studying tomorrow morning?

15. Responda negativamente:

Is Maria coming tonight?

16. Complete:

What ___ you doing tomorrow?

  1. do
  2. are
  3. did
  4. will be do

17. Complete:

Who is she ___ tonight?

  1. meet
  2. met
  3. meeting
  4. meets

18. Complete:

What time are they ___?

  1. arrive
  2. arriving
  3. arrived
  4. arrives

19. Identifique o sentido:

I’m studying now.

  1. passado
  2. ação atual
  3. futuro programado
  4. hábito

20. Identifique:

I’m studying with Peter tomorrow.

  1. passado
  2. rotina
  3. futuro programado
  4. ação concluída

21. Escolha a opção mais adequada:

A: The phone is ringing.
B: I ___ answer it.

  1. am answering tomorrow
  2. will
  3. was
  4. did

22. Escolha a opção mais adequada:

I have an appointment at 10 tomorrow. I ___ the dentist.

  1. am seeing
  2. saw
  3. see every day
  4. did see

23. Corrija:

I meeting Julia tomorrow.

24. Corrija:

She is meet the doctor at three.

25. Corrija:

Do you working tomorrow?

26. Corrija:

They doesn’t coming tonight.

27. Leia:

Laura has a busy Friday. She is meeting her manager at 9 a.m. At noon, she is having lunch with a client. In the afternoon, she is visiting a new office. She isn’t working in the evening. She is meeting two friends at a restaurant at 7:30.

Responda:

  1. Who is Laura meeting at 9 a.m.?

  2. What is she doing at noon?

  3. Who is she having lunch with?

  4. What is she doing in the afternoon?

  5. Is she working in the evening?

  6. Who is she meeting at night?

  7. What time are they meeting?

28. Identifique todas as formas de Present Continuous no texto anterior.

29. Escolha entre will, going to ou Present Continuous:

  1. The phone is ringing. I ___ answer it.

  2. I already decided to study more. I ___ study every evening.

  3. I have a meeting with my professor at 3 tomorrow. I ___ my professor at 3.

30. Produção

Crie uma agenda fictícia para um dia e escreva de oito a dez frases usando Present Continuous com sentido futuro.

Inclua:

  • pelo menos quatro horários;
  • duas pessoas;
  • dois lugares;
  • uma negativa;
  • uma pergunta;
  • expressões como tomorrow, in the morning, in the afternoon, tonight.

Gabarito comentado

1. A — am

I am meeting…

2. B — is

She is working…

3. C — are

They are traveling…

4. C — having

are having dinner.

5. B — leaving

is leaving.

6. B

I am meeting my professor tomorrow.

7.

She isn’t working tomorrow.

ou:

She is not working tomorrow.

8.

They aren’t traveling this weekend.

9. A — am not

I am not going out tonight.

10.

Is Laura coming tonight?

11.

Are they meeting at six?

12. B — Are

Are you working tomorrow?

13. B — Is

Is Daniel meeting us tonight?

14.

Yes, I am.

15.

No, she isn’t.

16. B — are

What are you doing tomorrow?

17. C — meeting

Who is she meeting tonight?

18. B — arriving

What time are they arriving?

19. B — ação atual

O marcador:

now

indica presente.

20. C — futuro programado

tomorrow

muda a referência temporal.

21. B — will

A decisão ocorre no momento em que o telefone toca.

I’ll answer it.

22. A — am seeing

A consulta já está marcada.

23.

I am meeting Julia tomorrow.

24.

She is meeting the doctor at three.

25.

Are you working tomorrow?

26.

They aren’t coming tonight.

27.

  1. Her manager.

  2. She is having lunch.

  3. A client.

  4. She is visiting a new office.

  5. No, she isn’t.

  6. Two friends.

  7. At 7:30.

28.

As formas são:

is meeting

is having

is visiting

isn’t working

is meeting.

29.

  1. will

I’ll answer it.

Decisão espontânea.

  1. am going to

I’m going to study every evening.

Intenção já decidida.

  1. am meeting

I’m meeting my professor at 3.

Compromisso marcado.

30.

Modelo:

Tomorrow, I’m meeting my teacher at 8 a.m. At 9:30, I’m studying at the library. I’m having lunch with Carla at a café at noon. In the afternoon, I’m visiting my grandmother. At 4 p.m., I’m meeting Daniel at the university. I’m not working tomorrow evening. I’m having dinner at home at seven. Are my friends coming tonight? Yes, they are. We’re watching a movie at eight.

Tarefa de consolidação

Crie uma agenda para amanhã com pelo menos seis compromissos.

Exemplo:

8:00 — class

10:30 — meeting with Anna

12:00 — lunch with Paulo

15:00 — library

18:00 — gym

20:00 — dinner.

Transforme a agenda em frases:

I’m having class at eight.

I’m meeting Anna at ten thirty.

Depois transforme três frases em negativas:

I’m not going to the gym at six.

E três em perguntas:

Are you meeting Anna at ten thirty?

Em seguida, escreva pares comparativos:

I’m studying now.
I’m studying with Laura tomorrow.

They’re traveling now.
They’re traveling next week.

Depois compare os três futuros:

I’ll help you.
decisão espontânea.

I’m going to study tonight.
intenção/plano.

I’m studying with Julia at 7 tonight.
compromisso organizado.

Finalize memorizando:

Present Continuous + future time expression = plano futuro organizado

E:

I’m working now. → presente

I’m working tomorrow. → futuro programado

A estrutura não muda. O marcador temporal e o contexto determinam o sentido.

Aula 45 — Comparatives

Objetivos

Ao final desta aula, você deverá ser capaz de:

  • compreender a função dos comparatives;
  • comparar duas pessoas, objetos, lugares ou situações;
  • formar comparativos com adjetivos curtos;
  • usar -er than corretamente;
  • formar comparativos com adjetivos terminados em -y;
  • reconhecer casos de duplicação de consoante;
  • usar more + adjective + than com adjetivos mais longos;
  • utilizar comparativos irregulares como better e worse;
  • evitar erros como more taller e beautifuller;
  • compreender comparações em Reading, Listening, Writing e Speaking.

Desenvolvimento

Os comparatives são usados para comparar duas coisas.

Exemplo:

Anna is taller than Maria.

Anna é mais alta que Maria.

Outro:

This book is cheaper than that book.

Este livro é mais barato que aquele.

A palavra:

than

é extremamente importante.

Ela corresponde, em muitos contextos, a:

do que.

Estrutura básica

Com muitos adjetivos curtos:

subject + be + adjective-er + than + comparison

Exemplo:

Tom is taller than Peter.

Temos:

Tom = primeiro elemento

taller = comparativo

than

Peter = segundo elemento.

Adjetivos curtos

Muitos adjetivos de uma sílaba recebem:

-er.

Exemplos:

tall → taller

small → smaller

old → older

young → younger

fast → faster

slow → slower

cheap → cheaper

long → longer

short → shorter.

Tall → taller

My brother is taller than me.

Outro:

Building A is taller than Building B.

Small → smaller

My room is smaller than my sister’s room.

Old → older

My father is older than my mother.

Young → younger

Julia is younger than Ana.

Fast → faster

A car is faster than a bicycle.

Cheap → cheaper

This phone is cheaper than that one.

Adjetivos terminados em -e

Quando o adjetivo já termina em:

e

acrescentamos apenas:

-r.

Exemplos:

large → larger

nice → nicer

safe → safer.

Exemplo:

This house is larger than that apartment.

Consoante + y

Quando um adjetivo termina em:

consoante + y

mudamos:

y → i

e acrescentamos:

-er.

Exemplos:

easy → easier

busy → busier

happy → happier

heavy → heavier.

Easy → easier

This exercise is easier than the last one.

Não:

easyer.

Happy → happier

She is happier today than yesterday.

Busy → busier

The city center is busier on Friday than on Sunday.

Duplicação da consoante final

Alguns adjetivos curtos terminados em:

consoante + vogal + consoante

duplicam a última consoante.

Exemplos:

big → bigger

hot → hotter

thin → thinner.

Big → bigger

São Paulo is bigger than many Brazilian cities.

Não:

biger.

Hot → hotter

Today is hotter than yesterday.

Thin → thinner

This book is thinner than that one.

Adjetivos mais longos

Com muitos adjetivos de duas ou mais sílabas, usamos:

more + adjective + than.

Exemplos:

expensive → more expensive

beautiful → more beautiful

difficult → more difficult

interesting → more interesting

comfortable → more comfortable.

Expensive

This computer is more expensive than that one.

Não:

expensiver.

Beautiful

This park is more beautiful than the other park.

Não:

beautifuller.

Difficult

Exercise 10 is more difficult than Exercise 5.

Interesting

This book is more interesting than the film.

Comfortable

This chair is more comfortable than that chair.

Than

Depois do comparativo, usamos frequentemente:

than.

Exemplo:

Laura is taller than Emma.

This car is faster than that car.

English is easier than I expected.

Sem than

Nem sempre precisamos dizer o segundo elemento.

Exemplo:

This computer is expensive, but that one is cheaper.

O contexto já informa o que está sendo comparado.

One e ones

Para evitar repetição de substantivos:

This phone is cheaper than that one.

One substitui:

phone.

Plural:

These shoes are more comfortable than those ones.

Na prática, também é muito comum dizer apenas:

These shoes are more comfortable than those.

Comparativos irregulares

Alguns adjetivos não seguem as regras normais.

Os principais são:

good → better

bad → worse

far → farther/further.

Good → better

This book is better than that one.

Não:

gooder.

Bad → worse

The weather today is worse than yesterday.

Não:

badder.

Far → farther/further

My new school is farther from home than my old school.

Farther é frequentemente associado a distância física.

Further também pode indicar distância e é muito usado em sentidos mais abstratos.

No nível A2, o mais importante é reconhecer ambas as formas.

Much / a lot + comparative

Podemos intensificar um comparativo.

Exemplo:

This test is much easier than the last one.

My new apartment is much bigger than my old apartment.

Também:

a lot better

a lot more expensive.

A little + comparative

Para uma pequena diferença:

This book is a little cheaper than that one.

Anna is a little taller than Maria.

Very não funciona da mesma maneira

Não usamos normalmente:

very taller.

Para intensificar comparativo:

much taller

a lot taller

a little taller.

Comparando idade

Peter is 30. John is 25.

Podemos dizer:

Peter is older than John.

Ou:

John is younger than Peter.

Comparando preço

Phone A: $500
Phone B: $700

Phone A is cheaper than Phone B.

Phone B is more expensive than Phone A.

Comparando tamanho

House A is bigger than House B.

House B is smaller than House A.

Comparando velocidade

A plane is faster than a car.

Comparando dificuldade

Mathematics is more difficult than this exercise.

Ou, dependendo da opinião:

This exercise is easier than mathematics.

Comparando lugares

The city center is busier than my neighborhood.

My neighborhood is quieter than the city center.

Comparando clima

Today is hotter than yesterday.

July is colder than January in some countries.

Comparative + noun context

Exemplo:

I need a bigger bag.

Aqui não usamos than, porque o contexto não apresenta explicitamente o segundo elemento.

Outro:

We need a cheaper hotel.

Comparatives em perguntas

Which city is bigger?

Which book is more interesting?

Who is older, Peter or Paul?

Which is better?

Pergunta frequente:

Which is better, the bus or the train?

Resposta:

The train is better.

Ou:

The train is faster and more comfortable.

How much…?

Também podemos comparar preços:

Which one is cheaper?

How much cheaper is it?

A segunda pergunta é mais avançada, mas é útil reconhecê-la.

Erros frequentes

Erro 1

Maria is more tall than Anna.

Correto:

Maria is taller than Anna.

Erro 2

This car is fast than that car.

Correto:

This car is faster than that car.

Erro 3

This exercise is difficulter.

Correto:

This exercise is more difficult.

Erro 4

My house is more bigger.

Correto:

My house is bigger.

Não usamos dois marcadores de comparativo ao mesmo tempo.

Erro 5

This book is gooder.

Correto:

This book is better.

Erro 6

Today is badder than yesterday.

Correto:

Today is worse than yesterday.

Regra: -er ou more, não os dois

Correto:

taller

Não:

more taller.

Correto:

more beautiful

Não:

beautifuller.

Algumas palavras de duas sílabas

Alguns adjetivos de duas sílabas podem aparecer com -er, especialmente:

easy → easier

happy → happier

narrow → narrower

simple → simpler.

Outros preferem:

more + adjective.

No nível A2, memorize principalmente as formas mais frequentes em vez de tentar criar uma regra perfeita para todos os adjetivos.

Comparatives e verb to be

Muitas frases usam:

be + comparative.

Exemplo:

Anna is taller than Maria.

This hotel is cheaper than that one.

Mas comparativos também podem aparecer com outros verbos.

This car runs faster than mine.

No nível A2, o padrão com be é o mais importante.

Comparando duas rotinas

Laura starts work at seven. Maria starts work at nine.

Podemos dizer:

Laura starts work earlier than Maria.

Aqui temos:

early → earlier.

Late → later

John arrived later than Peter.

Adjetivo x advérbio

No nível A2, você encontrará comparações como:

He runs faster than me.

Aqui faster modifica:

runs.

Mas o mesmo formato:

faster

também pode funcionar como comparativo de fast em outras estruturas.

Comparando dados

Leia:

Hotel A: $80 per night
Hotel B: $120 per night

Podemos concluir:

Hotel A is cheaper than Hotel B.

Hotel B is more expensive than Hotel A.

Reading

Em textos comparativos, procure pares de informação.

Exemplo:

The blue apartment has two bedrooms and costs $700. The green apartment has three bedrooms and costs $900.

Pergunta:

Which apartment is cheaper?

Resposta:

The blue apartment.

Pergunta:

Which apartment is bigger?

Se o texto usar número de quartos como referência de tamanho, talvez haja uma inferência possível, mas em provas de informação explícita é melhor depender do que o texto realmente informa.

Listening

Em Listening, reconheça terminações como:

bigger

cheaper

faster

e estruturas:

more expensive

more comfortable.

Uma palavra como:

than

também ajuda a detectar uma comparação.

Writing

Uma pequena comparação pode ter várias frases.

Exemplo:

My old phone was small and slow. My new phone is bigger and faster. It is also more expensive, but the camera is better.

Speaking

Perguntas frequentes:

Which is better, studying at home or at the library?

Resposta simples:

The library is better for me because it is quieter.

Outra:

Which is faster, a bus or a bicycle?

A bus is usually faster than a bicycle.

Comparações pessoais simples

My brother is taller than me.

My city is bigger than my hometown.

Mathematics is more difficult than English for me.

Nem toda comparação é objetiva

This movie is better than that one.

Isso é uma opinião.

Já:

Building A is taller than Building B.

pode ser uma comparação objetiva baseada em altura.

Comparative em anúncios

Exemplo:

Faster internet. Lower prices.

Anúncios frequentemente usam comparativos mesmo sem:

than.

O segundo elemento pode estar implícito:

mais rápido do que antes / do que concorrentes.

Lower e higher

Palavras úteis:

low → lower

high → higher.

Exemplo:

This price is lower than last year’s price.

Building A is higher than Building B.

Para altura de pessoas, normalmente usamos:

taller

não:

higher.

More e less

Também podemos expressar:

mais

e:

menos.

more expensive

mais caro.

less expensive

menos caro.

Exemplo:

This hotel is less expensive than that one.

Less

Less + adjective pode ser usado com adjetivos longos.

This exercise is less difficult than the previous one.

Isso significa:

menos difícil.

Comparação equivalente por sentido

This book is easier than that book.

Também podemos dizer:

That book is more difficult than this one.

A relação é apresentada de outra perspectiva.

Texto curto

Leia:

Julia and Emma are sisters. Julia is 24 and Emma is 20. Julia is taller than Emma, but Emma is more athletic. Julia’s car is older and cheaper than Emma’s car. Emma’s car is newer, faster and more comfortable.

Comparações:

Julia is older than Emma.

Julia is taller than Emma.

Emma is more athletic.

Julia’s car is older.

Julia’s car is cheaper.

Emma’s car is newer.

Emma’s car is faster.

Emma’s car is more comfortable.

Vocabulário-chave

compare — comparar

comparison — comparação

than — do que

tall / taller — alto / mais alto

short / shorter — baixo/curto / mais baixo/curto

big / bigger — grande / maior

small / smaller — pequeno / menor

old / older — velho/mais velho

young / younger — jovem/mais jovem

fast / faster — rápido / mais rápido

slow / slower — lento / mais lento

cheap / cheaper — barato / mais barato

expensive / more expensive — caro / mais caro

easy / easier — fácil / mais fácil

difficult / more difficult — difícil / mais difícil

beautiful / more beautiful — bonito / mais bonito

comfortable / more comfortable — confortável / mais confortável

good / better — bom / melhor

bad / worse — ruim / pior

far / farther/further — longe / mais longe

Estratégia de prova

Ao encontrar uma questão de comparação, identifique primeiro o adjetivo.

Pergunte:

Is it short?

Se for um adjetivo curto, procure normalmente:

adjective + -er.

Exemplo:

tall → taller.

Se for um adjetivo mais longo:

more + adjective.

Exemplo:

expensive → more expensive.

Depois confira se há:

than.

Exemplo:

This hotel is ___ than that one.

  1. cheap
  2. cheaper
  3. more cheap
  4. cheapest

Resposta:

cheaper.

Também memorize os irregulares:

good → better

bad → worse

Nunca combine:

more + -er.

Prática

Peter: 30 years old
John: 25 years old

  2. older
  3. more old
  4. oldest

  2. hotter

13. Corrija:

14. Corrija:

This test is difficulter than the last one.

15. Corrija:

This phone is more cheaper than that one.

16. Corrija:

Today is hoter than yesterday.

17. Corrija:

English is easyer than I expected.

18. Transforme em comparativo:

small → ______

large → ______

busy → ______

19. Leia:

Phone A costs $300 and Phone B costs $500.

Complete:

20. No mesmo exemplo:

Complete:

Maria is ______ than Ana.

30. Produção

Escreva de oito a dez frases comparando dois lugares, duas pessoas, dois produtos ou duas opções fictícias.

Use pelo menos:

  • dois comparativos com -er;
  • dois com more;
  • better;

Gabarito comentado

1. B — older

hoter.
