Modelo:

City A is bigger than City B. City B is quieter than City A. Public transportation in City A is better than in City B. However, traffic is worse in City A. Apartments in City A are more expensive than apartments in City B. City B is more comfortable for people who prefer quiet places. The city center in City A is much busier. City B is a little cheaper overall. For me, City B is better because it is calmer.

Tarefa de consolidação

Crie uma tabela com três colunas:

Adjective Comparative Example
tall taller Anna is taller than Julia.
big bigger This house is bigger.
easy easier This exercise is easier.
expensive more expensive This phone is more expensive.
good better This book is better.

Inclua pelo menos 20 adjetivos.

Separe-os em quatro grupos:

+ -er

tall → taller

consonant + y

easy → easier

double consonant

big → bigger

more + adjective

expensive → more expensive

Depois crie cinco pares opostos:

older / younger

bigger / smaller

faster / slower

cheaper / more expensive

better / worse.

Em seguida, compare:

  • dois telefones;
  • duas cidades;
  • dois meios de transporte;
  • duas disciplinas;
  • duas casas.

Use pelo menos uma frase com:

much

e uma com:

a little.

Finalize memorizando:

short adjective → -er + than

tall → taller than

long adjective → more + adjective + than

expensive → more expensive than

good → better

bad → worse

E nunca:

more taller

more cheaper

gooder

badder.

Aula 46 — Superlatives

Objetivos

Ao final desta aula, você deverá ser capaz de:

  • compreender a função dos superlatives;
  • identificar quando uma pessoa, objeto, lugar ou situação se destaca dentro de um grupo;
  • formar superlativos com adjetivos curtos usando the + adjective-est;
  • formar superlativos com adjetivos longos usando the most + adjective;
  • reconhecer mudanças ortográficas como big → biggest e easy → easiest;
  • utilizar formas irregulares como best e worst;
  • diferenciar comparatives e superlatives;
  • compreender perguntas como Which is the biggest…? e Who is the oldest…?;
  • usar superlativos em Reading, Writing, Listening e Speaking;
  • evitar erros como the most tallest, the goodest e the beautifullest.

Desenvolvimento

Na aula anterior, estudamos os comparatives.

Eles servem para comparar duas coisas.

Exemplo:

Anna is taller than Maria.

Agora vamos estudar os superlatives.

Superlativos são usados quando queremos dizer que algo possui uma característica no grau mais alto ou mais baixo dentro de um grupo.

Exemplo:

Anna is the tallest student in the class.

Anna é a aluna mais alta da turma.

Aqui não estamos comparando apenas Anna e Maria.

Estamos comparando Anna com todos os estudantes da turma.

Comparative x Superlative

Compare:

Anna is taller than Maria.

Comparative.

Agora:

Anna is the tallest student in the class.

Superlative.

A diferença central é:

comparative → compara duas coisas

superlative → destaca uma entre três ou mais, ou dentro de um grupo.

Estrutura com adjetivos curtos

A estrutura básica é:

subject + be + the + adjective-est

Exemplo:

Tom is the tallest.

Outro:

This is the cheapest phone.

The

O artigo:

the

é muito importante com superlativos.

Exemplo:

the tallest

the biggest

the fastest

the cheapest.

Não diga normalmente:

Tom is tallest student.

Use:

Tom is the tallest student.

Adjetivos curtos

Muitos adjetivos de uma sílaba recebem:

-est.

Exemplos:

tall → tallest

small → smallest

old → oldest

young → youngest

fast → fastest

slow → slowest

cheap → cheapest

long → longest

short → shortest.

Tall → tallest

Peter is the tallest person in the group.

Small → smallest

This is the smallest room in the house.

Old → oldest

My grandfather is the oldest person in my family.

Young → youngest

Julia is the youngest student in the class.

Fast → fastest

The plane is the fastest option.

Cheap → cheapest

Hotel A is the cheapest hotel in this area.

Adjetivos terminados em -e

Quando o adjetivo já termina em:

e

acrescentamos apenas:

-st.

Exemplos:

large → largest

nice → nicest

safe → safest.

Exemplo:

This is the largest room in the building.

Consoante + y

Quando o adjetivo termina em:

consoante + y

mudamos:

y → i

e acrescentamos:

-est.

Exemplos:

easy → easiest

happy → happiest

busy → busiest

heavy → heaviest.

Easy → easiest

This is the easiest exercise in the book.

Não:

easyest.

Happy → happiest

She was the happiest person at the party.

Busy → busiest

Friday is the busiest day of the week here.

Duplicação de consoante

Alguns adjetivos curtos duplicam a consoante final.

Exemplos:

big → biggest

hot → hottest

thin → thinnest.

Big → biggest

This is the biggest building in the city.

Não:

bigest.

Hot → hottest

July is the hottest month in some countries.

Adjetivos longos

Com muitos adjetivos de duas ou mais sílabas, usamos:

the most + adjective.

Exemplos:

expensive → the most expensive

beautiful → the most beautiful

difficult → the most difficult

interesting → the most interesting

comfortable → the most comfortable.

Expensive

This is the most expensive restaurant in the city.

Não:

the expensivest.

Beautiful

This is the most beautiful park in the city.

Não:

the beautifullest.

Difficult

This is the most difficult exercise in the test.

Interesting

This is the most interesting book in the course.

Comfortable

This is the most comfortable chair in the room.

Formas irregulares

Alguns superlativos são irregulares.

Os principais são:

good → better → best

bad → worse → worst

far → farther/further → farthest/furthest.

Good → best

This is the best option.

Não:

the goodest.

Bad → worst

This is the worst day of the week for traffic.

Não:

the baddest

quando queremos o superlativo normal de bad.

Far → farthest/furthest

That is the farthest station from my house.

Comparative e superlative juntos

Observe:

tall → taller → tallest

big → bigger → biggest

easy → easier → easiest

expensive → more expensive → most expensive

good → better → best

bad → worse → worst.

A forma com the

Compare:

This house is bigger than that one.

This is the biggest house in the neighborhood.

No comparativo:

bigger than.

No superlativo:

the biggest.

In + lugar ou grupo

Usamos frequentemente:

in

para indicar o grupo ou lugar.

Exemplo:

She is the tallest student in the class.

This is the biggest building in the city.

It is the most expensive hotel in the area.

Of + grupo específico

Também podemos usar:

of.

Exemplo:

She is the youngest of the three sisters.

This is the cheapest of the four options.

In x of

Como regra prática:

in + lugar ou grupo geral

of + conjunto específico.

Exemplo:

the tallest person in the room

the tallest of the three people.

The oldest in my family

My grandfather is the oldest person in my family.

The youngest of three children

Anna is the youngest of the three children.

Perguntas com superlativos

Who is the oldest person in your family?

What is the biggest city in your country?

Which is the cheapest option?

What is the most difficult subject for you?

Which is the best?

Pergunta muito frequente:

Which is the best option?

Resposta:

Option B is the best.

Who is the tallest?

Who is the tallest student in the class?

Daniel is the tallest.

What is the most expensive?

What is the most expensive item in the store?

The laptop is the most expensive item.

Superlative + noun

Muitas vezes o substantivo aparece depois do superlativo.

the biggest house

the fastest car

the most interesting book

the best student.

Sem substantivo

Quando o contexto já está claro:

Which phone is the cheapest?

The blue one is the cheapest.

Não é necessário repetir:

phone.

One

Exemplo:

The red phone is the most expensive one.

One evita repetição do substantivo.

Datas, preços e números

Superlativos aparecem muito em questões baseadas em dados.

Exemplo:

Hotel A: $80
Hotel B: $110
Hotel C: $150

Podemos dizer:

Hotel A is the cheapest.

Hotel C is the most expensive.

Comparando idades

Ana: 20
Bruno: 25
Carlos: 32

Carlos is the oldest.

Ana is the youngest.

Comparando velocidade

Bus: 80 km/h
Train: 160 km/h
Plane: 800 km/h

The plane is the fastest.

The bus is the slowest.

Comparando tamanho

Room A: 10 m²
Room B: 18 m²
Room C: 25 m²

Room C is the biggest.

Room A is the smallest.

The least

Além de:

the most

podemos usar:

the least.

The least significa:

o menos.

Exemplo:

This is the least expensive option.

Isso significa:

a opção menos cara.

Cheapest x least expensive

Podemos dizer:

This is the cheapest hotel.

Ou:

This is the least expensive hotel.

As duas expressões podem transmitir praticamente a mesma ideia.

Most não significa sempre superlativo

A palavra:

most

pode ter outros usos.

Mas nesta aula, o foco é:

the most + adjective.

Exemplo:

the most beautiful

the most difficult.

Não use more no superlativo

Erro:

This is the more expensive hotel.

Se estamos comparando todos dentro de um grupo:

This is the most expensive hotel.

Não misture most e -est

Erro:

the most tallest

Correto:

the tallest.

Erro:

the most cheapest

Correto:

the cheapest.

Comparatives x Superlatives

Compare:

Car A is faster than Car B.

Comparative.

Car A is the fastest car in the group.

Superlative.

Outro:

This exam is more difficult than the previous exam.

Comparative.

This is the most difficult exam of the course.

Superlative.

Três elementos

Quando há três ou mais opções, superlativos são muito naturais.

Exemplo:

Phone A is cheap.
Phone B is cheaper than Phone C.
Phone A is the cheapest of the three.

Exemplo com família

Julia is 30.
Mark is 25.
Emma is 19.

Podemos dizer:

Julia is older than Mark.

Comparative.

E:

Julia is the oldest.

Superlative.

Também:

Emma is the youngest.

Lugares

City A is bigger than City B.

Mas:

City C is the biggest city in the region.

Clima

Today is hotter than yesterday.

Mas:

August was the hottest month of the year.

Good, better, best

Compare:

This book is good.

This book is better than that one.

This is the best book in the series.

Bad, worse, worst

This restaurant is bad.

It is worse than the café.

It is the worst restaurant in the area.

Erros frequentes

Erro 1

She is tallest student.

Correto:

She is the tallest student.

Erro 2

This is the most cheapest phone.

Correto:

This is the cheapest phone.

Erro 3

This is the beautifullest place.

Correto:

This is the most beautiful place.

Erro 4

This is the goodest option.

Correto:

This is the best option.

Erro 5

Today is the baddest day.

Correto, no sentido geral de bad:

Today is the worst day.

Erro 6

This exercise is the easyest.

Correto:

This exercise is the easiest.

Adjetivos de duas sílabas

Assim como nos comparativos, alguns adjetivos de duas sílabas aceitam -est.

Exemplos importantes:

easy → easiest

happy → happiest

simple → simplest

narrow → narrowest.

Outros usam naturalmente:

the most + adjective.

No nível A2, memorize as formas mais frequentes.

Uso em Reading

Em Reading, superlativos ajudam a localizar extremos.

Palavras importantes:

biggest

smallest

cheapest

most expensive

oldest

youngest

fastest

slowest

best

worst.

Se a pergunta diz:

Which is the cheapest hotel?

procure os preços e identifique o menor.

Uso em Listening

Em Listening, não confunda:

bigger

com:

biggest.

Compare:

bigger than

comparativo.

the biggest

superlativo.

A presença de:

than

favorece comparativo.

A presença de:

the

pode ajudar a reconhecer o superlativo.

Writing

Exemplo:

I compared three hotels. Hotel A is the cheapest, but Hotel B is the most comfortable. Hotel C is the most expensive. For me, Hotel B is the best option.

Speaking

Pergunta:

What is the most interesting subject for you?

Resposta:

Mathematics is the most interesting subject for me.

Outro:

What is the busiest day of your week?

Monday is the busiest day of my week.

Superlativos e opiniões

Nem todos os superlativos apresentam fatos objetivos.

This is the best movie.

pode ser opinião.

This is the tallest building.

pode ser informação objetiva.

Ever

Uma construção muito comum em níveis posteriores é:

the best … ever.

Exemplo:

This is the best movie ever.

No A2, basta reconhecer:

ever

como uma forma de ampliar a ideia para “de todos os tempos/que já…”, dependendo do contexto.

Texto curto

Leia:

There are three hotels near the station. The Green Hotel costs $70 per night. The Blue Hotel costs $95 and has very comfortable rooms. The Grand Hotel costs $140 and has the largest rooms. The Green Hotel is the cheapest, the Grand Hotel is the most expensive, and many visitors say that the Blue Hotel is the most comfortable.

Informações:

Green Hotel → cheapest

Grand Hotel → most expensive

Grand Hotel → largest rooms

Blue Hotel → most comfortable.

Vocabulário-chave

superlative — superlativo

the tallest — o mais alto

the shortest — o mais baixo/curto

the biggest — o maior

the smallest — o menor

the oldest — o mais velho

the youngest — o mais jovem

the fastest — o mais rápido

the slowest — o mais lento

the cheapest — o mais barato

the most expensive — o mais caro

the easiest — o mais fácil

the most difficult — o mais difícil

the most interesting — o mais interessante

the most comfortable — o mais confortável

the best — o melhor

the worst — o pior

the least expensive — o menos caro

of the three — dos três

in the group — no grupo

Estratégia de prova

Primeiro, determine quantos elementos estão sendo comparados.

Se houver apenas dois:

comparative

costuma ser mais natural.

Se a questão pede o extremo dentro de um grupo:

superlative.

Exemplo:

Of the three hotels, Hotel A is ___.

  1. cheaper
  2. cheapest
  3. the cheapest
  4. more cheap

Como estamos escolhendo um entre três:

the cheapest.

Depois observe o tamanho do adjetivo.

Adjetivo curto:

the + adjective-est

tall → the tallest.

Adjetivo longo:

the most + adjective

expensive → the most expensive.

Irregulares:

good → the best

bad → the worst

Evite formas duplas:

the most tallest

the most cheapest.

Prática

1. Complete:

Peter is ___ student in the class.

  1. taller
  2. the tallest
  3. the most tall
  4. tallest than

2. Complete:

This is ___ room in the house.

  1. the smallest
  2. smaller
  3. the most small
  4. smallest than

3. Complete:

This is ___ building in the city.

  1. bigger
  2. the biggest
  3. the most biggest
  4. bigest

4. Complete:

Today is ___ day of the week.

  1. hotter
  2. the hottest
  3. the most hotter
  4. hotest

5. Complete:

This is ___ exercise in the book.

  1. easier
  2. the easiest
  3. the most easiest
  4. easyest

6. Complete:

This is ___ restaurant in the area.

  1. the most expensive
  2. the expensivest
  3. more expensive
  4. the more expensive

7. Complete:

This is ___ park in the city.

  1. the most beautiful
  2. beautifullest
  3. more beautiful
  4. the more beautiful

8. Complete:

This is ___ book in the course.

  1. goodest
  2. the best
  3. better
  4. the most good

9. Complete:

That was ___ day of the trip.

  1. the worse
  2. the worst
  3. the baddest
  4. worse than

10. Transforme:

tall → ______

big → ______

easy → ______

expensive → ______

good → ______

bad → ______

11. Corrija:

She is tallest person in the group.

12. Corrija:

This is the most biggest house.

13. Corrija:

This is the beautifullest place here.

14. Corrija:

This is the goodest restaurant.

15. Corrija:

Monday is the busyest day.

16. Leia:

Anna is 18. Julia is 25. Maria is 31.

Quem é:

  1. the oldest?

  2. the youngest?

17. Leia:

Car A: 120 km/h
Car B: 180 km/h
Car C: 210 km/h

Complete:

Car C is ______.

Car A is ______.

18. Leia:

Hotel A: $60
Hotel B: $90
Hotel C: $130

Complete:

Hotel A is ______.

Hotel C is ______.

19. Leia:

Book A has 100 pages.
Book B has 250 pages.
Book C has 400 pages.

Which book is the longest?

20. Complete:

This is ___ interesting film of the three.

  1. more
  2. the most
  3. most than
  4. the more

21. Complete:

She is ___ of the three sisters.

  1. younger
  2. the youngest
  3. the more young
  4. youngest than

22. Complete:

This exercise is ___ in the test.

  1. difficultest
  2. the most difficult
  3. more difficult
  4. the more difficult

23. Comparative ou superlative?

Maria is taller than Ana.

24. Comparative ou superlative?

Maria is the tallest student in the class.

25. Complete:

My new computer is ___ one in the office.

  1. faster
  2. the fastest
  3. more faster
  4. fastest than

26. Leia:

There are three apartments. Apartment A has one bedroom and costs $500. Apartment B has two bedrooms and costs $700. Apartment C has three bedrooms and costs $1,000.

Responda:

  1. Which apartment is the cheapest?

  2. Which is the most expensive?

  3. Which has the most bedrooms?

  4. Which has the fewest bedrooms?

27. Leia:

Sarah got 70 points. Mark got 85. Julia got 95.

Complete:

Julia got ______ score.

Sarah got ______ score.

28. Escreva uma frase usando:

good → best

29. Escreva uma frase usando:

comfortable → most comfortable

30. Produção

Compare três produtos, cidades, hotéis, cursos ou pessoas fictícias em um texto de oito a dez frases.

Use pelo menos:

  • the biggest;
  • the smallest;
  • the most expensive;
  • the cheapest;
  • the best;
  • the worst;
  • the most interesting;
  • uma comparação com of the three ou in the group.

Gabarito comentado

1. B — the tallest

Estamos destacando um estudante dentro de toda a turma.

2. A — the smallest

small → smallest.

3. B — the biggest

big → biggest.

A consoante é duplicada.

4. B — the hottest

hot → hottest.

5. B — the easiest

easy → easiest.

6. A — the most expensive

Com expensive, usamos:

the most + adjective.

7. A — the most beautiful

8. B — the best

good → better → best.

9. B — the worst

bad → worse → worst.

10.

tall → the tallest

big → the biggest

easy → the easiest

expensive → the most expensive

good → the best

bad → the worst

11.

She is the tallest person in the group.

Faltava:

the.

12.

This is the biggest house.

Não combinamos:

most + biggest.

13.

This is the most beautiful place here.

14.

This is the best restaurant.

15.

Monday is the busiest day.

busy → busiest.

16.

  1. Maria is the oldest.

  2. Anna is the youngest.

17.

Car C is the fastest.

Car A is the slowest.

18.

Hotel A is the cheapest.

Hotel C is the most expensive.

19.

Book C is the longest.

20. B — the most

the most interesting.

21. B — the youngest

22. B — the most difficult

23.

Comparative

A pista é:

taller than.

24.

Superlative

A pista é:

the tallest … in the class.

25. B — the fastest

Estamos comparando o computador com todos os computadores do escritório.

26.

  1. Apartment A.

  2. Apartment C.

  3. Apartment C.

  4. Apartment A.

Fewest significa:

menor quantidade

com substantivos contáveis.

27.

Julia got the highest score.

Sarah got the lowest score.

28.

Modelo:

This is the best book in the course.

29.

Modelo:

This chair is the most comfortable chair in the room.

30.

Modelo:

There are three hotels in the city center. Hotel A is the smallest, but it is also the cheapest. Hotel B is bigger and has the most interesting location. Hotel C is the biggest and the most expensive. Hotel C has the most comfortable rooms. Hotel A has the smallest rooms. For me, Hotel B is the best of the three because it has a good price and location. Hotel C is the worst option for someone with a small budget.

Tarefa de consolidação

Crie uma tabela com três colunas:

Adjective Comparative Superlative
tall taller the tallest
big bigger the biggest
easy easier the easiest
expensive more expensive the most expensive
good better the best
bad worse the worst

Adicione pelo menos 20 adjetivos.

Depois separe os superlativos em:

-est

tall → the tallest

-iest

easy → the easiest

consoante duplicada + -est

big → the biggest

the most + adjective

expensive → the most expensive

irregulares

good → the best

bad → the worst.

Depois compare três elementos em cada grupo:

  • três cidades;
  • três meios de transporte;
  • três disciplinas;
  • três hotéis;
  • três produtos.

Produza frases como:

A bus is faster than a bicycle, but a plane is the fastest of the three.

Hotel A is cheaper than Hotel B, but Hotel C is the most expensive.

Finalize memorizando:

comparative = two things

superlative = one thing inside a group

E:

tall → taller → the tallest

big → bigger → the biggest

easy → easier → the easiest

expensive → more expensive → the most expensive

good → better → the best

bad → worse → the worst.

Aula 47 — Must, have to e should

Objetivos

Ao final desta aula, você deverá ser capaz de:

  • compreender a diferença básica entre must, have to e should;
  • expressar obrigação, necessidade e recomendação;
  • formar frases afirmativas, negativas e interrogativas;
  • usar must + verbo na forma base;
  • usar corretamente have to / has to;
  • compreender a diferença entre mustn’t e don’t have to;
  • usar should / shouldn’t para dar conselhos;
  • reconhecer essas estruturas em avisos, regras, instruções e diálogos;
  • evitar erros como must to, she have to e should studies;
  • aplicar as três estruturas em Reading, Listening, Writing e Speaking.

Desenvolvimento

Nesta aula, vamos estudar três estruturas muito importantes:

must

have to

should.

Todas podem estar relacionadas a regras, necessidade ou orientação, mas não significam exatamente a mesma coisa.

A diferença principal, em nível A2, pode ser resumida assim:

must → obrigação forte

have to → necessidade/obrigação

should → conselho/recomendação

Must

Must é um verbo modal.

Ele é usado para expressar obrigação forte, regra ou necessidade percebida como importante.

Exemplo:

You must wear a seat belt.

Você deve usar cinto de segurança.

Outro:

Students must arrive on time.

Os estudantes devem chegar no horário.

Estrutura com must

A estrutura é:

subject + must + base verb

Exemplos:

I must study.

You must wait.

She must leave.

They must follow the rules.

O verbo não muda

Depois de must, usamos sempre a forma básica.

Correto:

She must study.

Incorreto:

She must studies.

Correto:

He must go.

Incorreto:

He must goes.

Não usamos to

Erro:

You must to study.

Correto:

You must study.

Assim como com can e will, o verbo vem diretamente depois do modal.

Must com todos os sujeitos

A forma é igual:

I must

you must

he must

she must

we must

they must.

Não existe:

musts.

Must em regras

Exemplo:

Visitors must show ID.

Outro:

You must turn off your phone during the exam.

Outro:

Employees must wear a uniform.

Must em instruções importantes

You must read the instructions carefully.

You must answer all questions.

Must para obrigação pessoal

Também pode aparecer em falas como:

I must study tonight.

Aqui o falante apresenta a ação como muito necessária.

Outro:

I must call my mother.

Must not / mustn’t

A forma negativa é:

must not

ou:

mustn’t.

Ela normalmente expressa:

proibição.

Exemplo:

You mustn’t smoke here.

Significa:

é proibido fumar aqui.

Outro:

Students mustn’t use phones during the test.

Mustn’t é forte

Compare:

You mustn’t enter.

Isso não significa simplesmente:

não é necessário entrar.

Significa:

você não pode entrar / é proibido entrar.

Have to

Have to também expressa necessidade ou obrigação.

Exemplo:

I have to work tomorrow.

Eu tenho que trabalhar amanhã.

Outro:

She has to wear a uniform.

Ela tem que usar uniforme.

Have to muda com o sujeito

No presente:

I have to

you have to

we have to

they have to

Mas:

he has to

she has to

it has to.

Exemplos

I have to study.

They have to leave early.

He has to work on Saturday.

Maria has to take the bus.

Have to + base verb

Depois de:

have to / has to

usamos a forma básica.

She has to study.

Não:

She has to studies.

Must x have to

Em muitos contextos, os dois podem expressar obrigação.

Compare:

You must wear a helmet.

You have to wear a helmet.

As duas frases podem indicar obrigação.

No nível A2, uma distinção útil é:

must frequentemente apresenta uma regra forte ou obrigação percebida pelo falante.

have to frequentemente destaca uma necessidade causada por regra, circunstância ou situação.

Exemplo de regra

At this school, students have to wear a uniform.

A regra da escola cria a obrigação.

Exemplo de obrigação pessoal forte

I must study more.

O falante apresenta isso como uma necessidade muito importante.

Não transforme a diferença em regra absoluta

Na língua real, must e have to podem se sobrepor bastante.

Em muitos contextos:

You must be careful.

e:

You have to be careful.

podem ter sentidos muito próximos.

Have to no passado

Uma vantagem de have to é poder mudar de tempo verbal.

No passado:

had to.

Exemplo:

I had to work yesterday.

She had to leave early.

Não usamos normalmente must como passado simples de obrigação dessa maneira.

Have to no futuro

Podemos dizer:

I will have to work tomorrow.

She will have to study more.

Esse uso será aprofundado mais adiante.

Forma negativa de have to

No presente:

don’t have to

doesn’t have to.

Exemplo:

I don’t have to work today.

She doesn’t have to come tomorrow.

Don’t have to significa ausência de necessidade

Isso é extremamente importante.

You don’t have to come.

Significa:

você não precisa vir.

Não significa:

você não pode vir.

A pessoa pode vir se quiser.

Mustn’t x don’t have to

Compare:

You mustn’t park here.

É proibido estacionar.

Agora:

You don’t have to drive.

Você não precisa dirigir.

Talvez possa ir de ônibus.

Contraste essencial

mustn’t = prohibition

don’t have to = no necessity

Esse é um dos contrastes mais importantes da aula.

Exemplo

You mustn’t bring food into the laboratory.

Proibido.

You don’t have to bring a laptop. We have computers here.

Não é necessário.

Perguntas com have to

Usamos:

do/does.

Exemplo:

Do you have to work tomorrow?

Does she have to wear a uniform?

Depois de does: have

Correto:

Does she have to study?

Não:

Does she has to study?

Como já estudamos no Simple Present:

does + base form.

Short answers

Do you have to work tomorrow?

Yes, I do.

No, I don’t.

Outro:

Does Maria have to come?

Yes, she does.

No, she doesn’t.

Perguntas com must

Perguntas com must são possíveis:

Must I finish this today?

Must we leave now?

Elas podem soar mais formais ou menos frequentes em algumas situações cotidianas.

Em conversas comuns, muitas vezes usamos:

Do I have to…?

Exemplo:

Do I have to finish this today?

Should

Should é usado principalmente para:

  • conselho;
  • recomendação;
  • sugestão;
  • dizer o que seria uma boa ideia.

Exemplo:

You should study more.

Você deveria estudar mais.

Outro:

You should drink more water.

Estrutura com should

subject + should + base verb

Exemplos:

I should study.

She should rest.

They should arrive early.

Sem -s

Correto:

He should work.

Não:

He should works.

Sem to

Correto:

You should sleep.

Não:

You should to sleep.

Should not / shouldn’t

Forma negativa:

should not

ou:

shouldn’t.

Exemplo:

You shouldn’t stay up late.

He shouldn’t drive when he is tired.

We shouldn’t be late.

Should não é obrigação forte

Compare:

You must wear a seat belt.

obrigação/regra.

You should sleep eight hours.

recomendação.

Exemplo simples

You have an exam tomorrow.

Conselho:

You should study tonight.

Obrigação:

You must bring your ID to the exam.

Necessidade externa:

You have to arrive before 8 a.m.

Perguntas com should

Should I study more?

Should we leave now?

Should she call the doctor?

Short answers com should

Should I go?

Yes, you should.

No, you shouldn’t.

What should I do?

Pergunta extremamente útil:

What should I do?

Significa:

O que eu deveria fazer?

Exemplo:

A: I have a test tomorrow and I haven’t studied. What should I do?
B: You should study tonight.

Conselho com problema cotidiano

I’m tired.

You should rest.

I have a headache.

You should drink water and rest.

I’m always late.

You should leave home earlier.

Should com saúde cotidiana

Em contextos simples:

You should sleep more.

You should eat healthy food.

You shouldn’t drink too much coffee.

Esses exemplos são orientações gerais, não substituem avaliação profissional quando há questões médicas reais.

Must em sinalização

Você pode encontrar:

You must wear protective equipment.

Ou:

Passengers must show their tickets.

Mustn’t em placas

You mustn’t smoke.

You mustn’t touch the equipment.

Em avisos reais, também é comum encontrar formas mais curtas:

NO SMOKING

DO NOT ENTER.

Have to em rotina

I have to wake up at six because I start work at seven.

A situação de trabalho cria a necessidade.

Has to

My sister has to take two buses to work.

Daniel has to study tonight.

Don’t have to

It’s Sunday. I don’t have to work.

The homework is optional. You don’t have to do it.

Doesn’t have to

Maria doesn’t have to come early tomorrow.

Should em recomendações de estudo

You should read the questions first.

You should check your answers.

You shouldn’t spend too much time on one question.

Essas recomendações também se conectam às estratégias de prova estudadas anteriormente.

Três graus diferentes

Imagine uma prova.

Regra obrigatória:

You must show your ID.

Necessidade por circunstância:

You have to arrive before the doors close.

Recomendação:

You should arrive early.

As três frases não possuem a mesma força.

Comparação visual

Estrutura Ideia principal Exemplo
must obrigação forte/regra You must wear a seat belt.
have to necessidade/obrigação I have to work tomorrow.
should conselho You should rest.

Negativas

Estrutura Significado
mustn’t é proibido
don’t/doesn’t have to não é necessário
shouldn’t não é recomendável

Exemplo completo

You mustn’t use your phone during the exam.

Proibição.

You don’t have to bring paper because the school provides it.

Ausência de necessidade.

You shouldn’t spend twenty minutes on one question.

Conselho.

Erro frequente: confundir mustn’t e don’t have to

Situação:

The museum is free.

Você:

You don’t have to pay.

Correto.

Não diga:

You mustn’t pay.

Isso poderia sugerir:

é proibido pagar.

Erro com terceira pessoa

Errado:

She have to work.

Correto:

She has to work.

Erro em pergunta

Errado:

Does she has to work?

Correto:

Does she have to work?

Erro com modal

Errado:

He must to go.

Correto:

He must go.

Erro com should

Errado:

She should studies.

Correto:

She should study.

Erro com negativas

Errado:

He doesn’t has to work.

Correto:

He doesn’t have to work.

Reading

Em Reading, identifique a força da expressão.

Exemplo:

Visitors must leave their bags at reception.

Pergunta:

Is leaving the bag optional?

Resposta:

No.

É obrigação.

Agora:

Visitors don’t have to pay.

Isso indica:

pagamento não é necessário.

Listening

Preste atenção especialmente a:

must

mustn’t

have to

don’t have to

should

shouldn’t.

As negativas podem alterar totalmente a informação.

Listening: must x mustn’t

Em fala rápida, o final de mustn’t pode ser difícil.

Use o contexto.

You mustn’t enter this room.

Se o contexto é uma regra de segurança, a negativa é decisiva.

Writing

Você pode escrever regras:

Students must arrive on time.

They mustn’t use phones in class.

Ou recomendações:

Students should study every day.

They shouldn’t study only before the test.

Speaking

Pergunta:

What should I do to improve my English?

Resposta:

You should practice every day. You should read short texts and listen to English.

Pergunta:

Do you have to study English for your course?

Resposta:

Yes, I do.

Situação 1: escola

Students must respect the teacher.

They have to complete their assignments.

They should review before tests.

Situação 2: trabalho

Employees must follow safety rules.

They have to arrive before 8 a.m.

They should communicate clearly with coworkers.

Situação 3: viagem

Passengers must show their passports.

They have to arrive early for international flights.

They should check their documents before leaving home.

Situação 4: biblioteca

You mustn’t make a lot of noise.

You don’t have to buy the books.

You should return borrowed books on time.

Advice versus rule

Compare:

You should turn off your phone during the movie.

Pode ser recomendação dependendo do contexto.

You must turn off your phone during the exam.

É apresentada como regra obrigatória.

Contexto decide

A mesma ação pode receber estruturas diferentes dependendo da situação.

You should wear comfortable shoes.

recomendação.

Workers must wear safety shoes.

regra.

Must e have to no uso real

Em várias situações, falantes podem escolher must ou have to com diferenças pequenas de nuance.

Exemplo:

I must leave now.

I have to leave now.

Ambas podem comunicar uma necessidade forte.

No nível A2, mais importante do que tentar separar todos os casos é dominar:

  • a estrutura;
  • as negativas;
  • o contraste com should.

Vocabulário-chave

obligation — obrigação

necessity — necessidade

advice — conselho

rule — regra

recommendation — recomendação

must — deve/precisa, obrigação forte

mustn’t — não deve/não pode, proibição

have to — ter que

has to — tem que

don’t have to — não precisar

doesn’t have to — não precisar

should — deveria

shouldn’t — não deveria

wear — usar/vestir

You must wear a uniform.

follow — seguir

Follow the rules.

bring — trazer

show — mostrar

arrive — chegar

leave — sair

wait — esperar

rest — descansar

careful — cuidadoso

You should be careful.

Estratégia de prova

Primeiro, identifique a intenção da frase.

Se for:

strong rule / obligation

pense em:

must

ou:

have to.

Se for:

advice

pense em:

should.

Depois observe a negativa.

mustn’t = prohibited

don’t have to = optional / not necessary

shouldn’t = bad idea / advice not to do something

Exemplo:

The entrance is free. You ___ pay.

  1. mustn’t
  2. don’t have to
  3. should
  4. must

Resposta:

don’t have to.

Porque não pagar é ausência de necessidade, não proibição.

Outro:

You ___ smoke in this hospital.

  1. don’t have to
  2. should
  3. mustn’t
  4. have to

Resposta:

mustn’t.

Prática

1. Complete:

You ___ wear a seat belt.

  1. must
  2. should to
  3. must to
  4. has to

2. Complete:

She ___ wear a uniform at work.

  1. have to
  2. has to
  3. has
  4. having to

3. Complete:

They ___ arrive before eight.

  1. have to
  2. has to
  3. musts
  4. should to

4. Complete:

You ___ study more if you want to improve.

  1. should
  2. should to
  3. mustn’t
  4. don’t have

5. Complete:

You must ___ your ID.

  1. brings
  2. bringing
  3. bring
  4. brought

6. Complete:

She should ___ earlier.

  1. sleeps
  2. sleeping
  3. sleep
  4. slept

7. Complete:

He has to ___ tomorrow.

  1. works
  2. work
  3. worked
  4. working

8. Escolha a frase correta.

  1. She must to study.
  2. She must studies.
  3. She must study.
  4. She does must study.

9. Transforme para a negativa com must:

You must enter this room.

Agora diga que é proibido entrar.

10. Complete:

You ___ use your phone during the exam.

  1. mustn’t
  2. don’t have to
  3. should
  4. have to not

11. Complete:

The museum is free. You ___ pay.

  1. mustn’t
  2. don’t have to
  3. shouldn’t pay because it is dangerous
  4. must

12. Complete:

It’s optional. She ___ come.

  1. mustn’t
  2. doesn’t have to
  3. has to
  4. must

13. Complete:

You look tired. You ___ rest.

  1. mustn’t
  2. should
  3. don’t have to
  4. should to

14. Complete:

You ___ stay up all night before the exam.

  1. should
  2. shouldn’t
  3. have to
  4. must

15. Transforme em pergunta:

You have to work tomorrow.

16. Transforme em pergunta:

Maria has to wear a uniform.

17. Complete:

Does she ___ work on Saturday?

  1. has to
  2. have to
  3. had to
  4. having to

18. Responda afirmativamente:

Do you have to study tonight?

19. Responda negativamente:

Does she have to come early?

20. Complete:

What ___ I do?

  1. should
  2. should to
  3. do should
  4. am should

21. Situação:

You have a headache after a long day and need general rest advice.

Qual frase funciona como conselho?

  1. You should rest.
  2. You mustn’t rest.
  3. You don’t have to rest because rest is prohibited.
  4. You should to rest.

22. Situação:

A sign says “NO ENTRY”.

Qual frase corresponde melhor?

  1. You don’t have to enter.
  2. You mustn’t enter.
  3. You should enter.
  4. You have to enter.

23. Situação:

Students may bring a laptop, but it is optional.

  1. Students mustn’t bring a laptop.
  2. Students don’t have to bring a laptop.
  3. Students have to bring a laptop.
  4. Students must bring a laptop.

24. Corrija:

She have to study tonight.

25. Corrija:

Does he has to work tomorrow?

26. Corrija:

You must to show your passport.

27. Corrija:

He should studies more.

28. Leia:

LIBRARY RULES
Visitors must be quiet. They mustn’t eat or drink near the computers. Students have to show their library cards when they borrow books. They don’t have to pay to use the computers. Visitors should return books on time.

Responda:

  1. Must visitors be quiet?

  2. Can visitors eat near the computers?

  3. What do students have to show?

  4. Do they have to pay to use the computers?

  5. What should visitors do with borrowed books?

29. Classifique cada frase como obrigação, proibição, ausência de necessidade ou conselho:

  1. You must wear a helmet.

  2. You mustn’t park here.

  3. You don’t have to come tomorrow.

  4. You should study more.

  5. She shouldn’t go to bed so late.

30. Produção

Escreva de oito a dez frases com regras e recomendações para um dos seguintes contextos:

  • escola;
  • biblioteca;
  • trabalho;
  • viagem;
  • curso.

Use pelo menos:

  • duas frases com must;
  • uma com mustn’t;
  • duas com have to/has to;
  • uma com don’t/doesn’t have to;
  • duas com should/shouldn’t.

Gabarito comentado

1. A — must

You must wear a seat belt.

Depois de must, não usamos to.

2. B — has to

Com:

she

usamos:

has to.

3. A — have to

Com:

they

usamos:

have to.

4. A — should

É uma recomendação.

5. C — bring

must + base verb.

6. C — sleep

should + base verb.

7. B — work

has to + base verb.

8. C

She must study.

9.

You mustn’t enter this room.

Agora temos uma proibição.

10. A — mustn’t

O contexto é uma proibição durante a prova.

11. B — don’t have to

Se é gratuito, pagar não é necessário.

Não significa que pagar seja proibido.

12. B — doesn’t have to

optional

indica ausência de obrigação.

13. B — should

É um conselho.

14. B — shouldn’t

A frase apresenta uma recomendação negativa.

15.

Do you have to work tomorrow?

16.

Does Maria have to wear a uniform?

17. B — have to

Depois de does:

have.

18.

Yes, I do.

19.

No, she doesn’t.

20. A — should

What should I do?

21. A

You should rest.

A estrutura expressa conselho.

22. B

You mustn’t enter.

No entry indica proibição.

23. B

Students don’t have to bring a laptop.

Isso significa que o laptop é opcional.

24.

She has to study tonight.

25.

Does he have to work tomorrow?

26.

You must show your passport.

27.

He should study more.

28.

  1. Yes, they must.

  2. No. They mustn’t eat near the computers.

  3. Their library cards.

  4. No, they don’t.

  5. They should return the books on time.

29.

  1. obrigação

must.

  1. proibição

mustn’t.

  1. ausência de necessidade

don’t have to.

  1. conselho

should.

  1. conselho/recomendação negativa

shouldn’t.

30.

Modelo:

Students must arrive on time. They must respect the classroom rules. They mustn’t use phones during tests. Students have to complete their assignments. A student has to bring a notebook to class. They don’t have to bring a laptop because the school has computers. Students should review their notes every day. They shouldn’t wait until the night before the test to study.

Tarefa de consolidação

Crie quatro grupos de frases.

Obligation

Use:

must

have to

has to.

Exemplo:

I have to work tomorrow.

Prohibition

Use:

mustn’t.

Exemplo:

You mustn’t enter.

No necessity

Use:

don’t have to

doesn’t have to.

Exemplo:

You don’t have to pay.

Advice

Use:

should

shouldn’t.

Exemplo:

You should study more.

Depois transforme cinco frases com have to em perguntas.

Exemplo:

She has to work.

Does she have to work?

Em seguida, escreva o significado de cada contraste:

You mustn’t go.

You don’t have to go.

You shouldn’t go.

Explique:

mustn’t → não pode

don’t have to → não precisa

shouldn’t → não deveria

Depois crie um pequeno conjunto de regras para uma prova de inglês.

Use exemplos como:

You must bring your ID.

You mustn’t use your phone.

You don’t have to bring paper if the exam center provides it.

You should arrive early.

Finalize memorizando:

must + base verb

have/has to + base verb

should + base verb

E, principalmente:

mustn’t = prohibition

don’t have to = no necessity

shouldn’t = advice not to do something

Aula 48 — Could e may

Objetivos

Ao final desta aula, você deverá ser capaz de:

  • compreender os usos básicos de could;
  • compreender os usos básicos de may;
  • usar could para falar de habilidade no passado;
  • usar could para pedidos mais polidos;
  • usar could para possibilidade;
  • usar may para possibilidade;
  • usar may em pedidos de permissão mais formais;
  • diferenciar can, could e may em contextos simples;
  • formar frases afirmativas, negativas e interrogativas;
  • evitar erros como could to go, may goes e did could.

Desenvolvimento

Nesta aula, estudaremos dois verbos modais:

could

may

Como outros modais já estudados, como:

can

must

should

will

eles são seguidos pela forma básica do verbo.

Exemplo:

She could swim.

It may rain.

Não usamos:

to

nem acrescentamos:

-s

ao verbo principal.

Estrutura com could

A estrutura básica é:

subject + could + base verb

Exemplos:

I could swim.

She could speak English.

They could come later.

Could não muda com o sujeito

Usamos:

I could

you could

he could

she could

we could

they could.

Não existe:

coulds.

Uso 1: habilidade no passado

Um dos usos mais importantes de could é expressar habilidade geral no passado.

Compare:

I can swim.

Eu sei/consigo nadar agora.

I could swim when I was five.

Eu sabia/conseguia nadar quando tinha cinco anos.

Can x could

Presente:

She can speak French.

Passado:

She could speak French when she was a child.

Outro:

I can use this computer now.

I could use computers when I was ten.

Habilidade geral

Could funciona muito bem para habilidades gerais no passado.

Exemplo:

My grandfather could run very fast when he was young.

She could read when she was four.

We could play outside for hours when we were children.

Forma negativa

A negativa é:

could not

ou:

couldn’t.

Exemplos:

I couldn’t swim when I was three.

She couldn’t understand the lesson.

They couldn’t come yesterday.

Couldn’t

couldn’t

significa:

não conseguia / não podia

dependendo do contexto.

Exemplo:

I couldn’t open the door.

Perguntas com could

Could + subject + base verb?

Exemplos:

Could you swim when you were five?

Could she read at that age?

Short answers

Could you swim?

Yes, I could.

No, I couldn’t.

Outro:

Could Maria speak English?

Yes, she could.

Uso 2: pedidos polidos

Could também é muito usado para fazer pedidos de forma mais polida.

Compare:

Can you help me?

correto e comum.

Could you help me?

mais polido.

Outro:

Could you open the window, please?

Could you repeat that, please?

Could you speak more slowly, please?

Could you…?

Essa estrutura é extremamente útil em situações de Speaking.

Could you help me?

Could you say that again?

Could you wait a moment?

Respostas a pedidos

Could you help me?

Possíveis respostas:

Yes, of course.

Sure.

Certainly.

Sorry, I can’t right now.

Em pedidos, normalmente não respondemos apenas:

Yes, I could.

porque a pergunta não está realmente perguntando sobre habilidade passada.

Uso 3: possibilidade

Could também pode indicar que algo é possível.

Exemplo:

It could rain later.

Pode chover mais tarde.

Outro:

She could be at home.

Talvez ela esteja em casa.

Outro:

This could be the answer.

Essa pode ser a resposta.

Could como possibilidade menos certa

Em muitos contextos:

could

apresenta uma possibilidade.

Exemplo:

We could have a problem.

The bus could be late.

No nível A2, basta compreender:

could = pode ser possível.

May

May também é um verbo modal.

Estrutura:

subject + may + base verb

Exemplos:

It may rain.

She may come later.

They may be busy.

May não muda com o sujeito

I may

you may

he may

she may

we may

they may.

Não:

she mays.

Uso 1: possibilidade

O uso mais importante de may neste nível é expressar possibilidade.

Exemplo:

It may rain tomorrow.

Talvez chova amanhã.

Outro:

Maria may come to the party.

Maria talvez venha à festa.

Outro:

The test may be difficult.

A prova talvez seja difícil.

May + be

She may be tired.

He may be at work.

They may be late.

Não:

She may is tired.

Correto:

She may be tired.

May e could para possibilidade

Compare:

It may rain tonight.

It could rain tonight.

As duas frases expressam possibilidade.

No nível A2, não é necessário estabelecer uma diferença rígida de probabilidade entre elas.

Ambas podem ser entendidas como:

talvez aconteça.

Uso 2: permissão

May também pode ser usado para pedir permissão, especialmente em registro mais formal.

Exemplo:

May I come in?

Posso entrar?

Outro:

May I use your phone?

May I ask a question?

May I…?

Essa estrutura é mais formal do que:

Can I…?

Compare:

Can I come in?

comum e cotidiano.

May I come in?

mais formal/polido.

Pedindo permissão

May I sit here?

May I open the window?

May I leave early today?

Respondendo a May I…?

May I come in?

Resposta:

Yes, you may.

Ou, mais naturalmente em muitos contextos:

Yes, of course.

Negativa formal:

No, you may not.

May not

A negativa de may é:

may not.

Exemplo:

She may not come tonight.

Dependendo do contexto, significa:

talvez ela não venha.

Atenção ao significado de may not

Compare:

She may not come.

Possibilidade de ela não vir.

Agora:

You may not enter.

Em contexto formal de regra, pode significar:

você não tem permissão para entrar.

O contexto determina.

Could para permissão

Também podemos usar could em pedidos:

Could I use your phone?

Essa forma é muito polida.

Compare:

Can I use your phone?

Could I use your phone?

May I use your phone?

As três podem aparecer para pedir permissão, com diferenças de registro e polidez.

Can, could e may

Uma simplificação útil:

can → habilidade atual / pedido comum / permissão informal

could → habilidade passada / pedido mais polido / possibilidade

may → possibilidade / permissão mais formal

Exemplos contrastivos

Habilidade atual:

I can swim.

Habilidade passada:

I could swim when I was six.

Pedido:

Could you help me?

Permissão formal:

May I come in?

Possibilidade:

It may rain.

It could rain.

Modal + base verb

Essa regra aparece novamente.

Depois de:

can

could

may

must

should

will

usamos:

verbo base.

Correto:

She could go.

She may go.

Não:

She could goes.

She may goes.

Não usamos to depois de could ou may

Errado:

I could to help.

Correto:

I could help.

Errado:

She may to come.

Correto:

She may come.

Não usamos do/does/did em perguntas com could

Errado:

Did you could swim?

Correto:

Could you swim?

Errado:

Do you could help?

Correto:

Could you help?

Não usamos do/does com may

Errado:

Does she may come?

Correto:

May she come?

Embora perguntas desse tipo sejam menos comuns em conversação cotidiana.

Could no passado: cuidado com eventos específicos

Para habilidade geral passada:

I could swim when I was young.

Mas, para uma realização específica em determinado momento, o inglês frequentemente prefere estruturas como:

was able to.

Exemplo:

After several attempts, I was able to open the door.

Essa distinção é mais avançada.

No nível A2, concentre-se principalmente em could para habilidade geral passada.

Could em sugestões

Could também pode aparecer em sugestões.

Exemplo:

We could go to the cinema.

You could try this restaurant.

Aqui o sentido é:

poderíamos…

ou:

você poderia…

Esse uso é útil reconhecer, mesmo que o foco principal da aula seja habilidade, pedido e possibilidade.

Sugestão simples

A: What can we do tonight?
B: We could watch a movie.

Outro:

You could take the bus.

May em previsões

The weather may change later.

The teacher may give us a test.

Prices may increase next year.

Could em previsões

The train could be late.

This could take a long time.

Diferença de certeza

Compare:

It will rain.

O falante apresenta a previsão com mais certeza.

It may rain.

Existe possibilidade.

It could rain.

Existe possibilidade.

Portanto:

will

e:

may/could

não têm a mesma força.

Will x may

She will come tomorrow.

apresenta o futuro como esperado/afirmado.

She may come tomorrow.

não sabemos se ela virá.

Going to x may

She’s going to travel next week.

há um plano.

She may travel next week.

a viagem é apenas uma possibilidade.

Pequeno diálogo sobre habilidade

A: Could you swim when you were a child?
B: Yes, I could. I learned when I was six.
A: Could your brother swim too?
B: No, he couldn’t.

Pequeno diálogo com pedido

A: Excuse me. Could you help me?
B: Of course. What do you need?
A: Could you tell me where the station is?

Pequeno diálogo com permissão

A: May I come in?
B: Yes, of course.
A: May I sit here?
B: Certainly.

Pequeno diálogo sobre possibilidade

A: Are you going to the park tomorrow?
B: I’m not sure. It may rain.

Not sure

A expressão:

I’m not sure.

combina frequentemente com:

may

could.

Exemplo:

I’m not sure. She may be at work.

Perhaps e maybe

Também expressam possibilidade.

Maybe she will come.

Perhaps she is busy.

Com modal:

She may be busy.

Reading

Em Reading, reconheça:

could

como potencialmente relacionado a:

  • habilidade passada;
  • possibilidade;
  • pedido;
  • sugestão.

O contexto decide.

Exemplo de Reading

When Laura was ten, she could speak two languages.

Aqui:

could = habilidade passada.

Agora:

Laura could come tomorrow.

Aqui:

could = possibilidade.

Listening

No Listening, a posição de could é importante.

Could you help me?

pedido.

I could swim.

habilidade.

It could rain.

possibilidade.

Writing

Você pode usar could em uma narrativa sobre infância:

When I was ten, I could ride a bike, but I couldn’t swim.

Para possibilidade:

The weather may be bad tomorrow, so the event could be canceled.

No nível A2, mantenha as frases simples.

Speaking

Perguntas úteis:

What could you do when you were ten?

Could you ride a bike?

Could you swim?

May I ask a question?

Could you repeat that, please?

Habilidade passada x habilidade atual

When I was five, I couldn’t read.

Now I can read.

Outro:

I could run faster when I was younger.

Possibilidade negativa

She may not come.

They may not have enough time.

Com could:

It could be difficult.

Forma negativa:

It couldn’t be true.

Dependendo do contexto, isso pode significar:

não poderia ser verdade / é impossível que seja verdade.

Esse uso é mais complexo. No A2, concentre-se principalmente em frases afirmativas de possibilidade com could.

Erros frequentes

Erro 1

She could to swim.

Correto:

She could swim.

Erro 2

He could swims.

Correto:

He could swim.

Erro 3

Did you could read?

Correto:

Could you read?

Erro 4

It may rains.

Correto:

It may rain.

Erro 5

She may is late.

Correto:

She may be late.

Erro 6

May I to come in?

Correto:

May I come in?

Comparando os modais estudados

can → capacidade atual

could → capacidade passada

must → obrigação

should → conselho

may → possibilidade/permissão

will → futuro/previsão/decisão.

Todos compartilham uma característica importante:

modal + base verb.

Exemplo integrado

I can drive now, but I couldn’t drive when I was sixteen. I may buy a new car next year, but I’m not sure. I should save some money first. I must also pay my bills. Maybe I will buy the car later.

Nesse pequeno texto, cada modal exerce uma função diferente.

Vocabulário-chave

could — podia/conseguia/poderia

couldn’t — não podia/não conseguia

may — pode/talvez

may not — talvez não/pode não

ability — habilidade/capacidade

possibility — possibilidade

permission — permissão

request — pedido

polite — educado/polido

formal — formal

perhaps — talvez

maybe — talvez

sure — certo

I’m not sure.

help — ajudar

Could you help me?

repeat — repetir

Could you repeat that?

come in — entrar

May I come in?

possible — possível

impossible — impossível

Estratégia de prova

Ao encontrar could, pergunte:

Is this about past ability?

Is this a polite request?

Is this a possibility?

Exemplo:

When he was six, he ___ read very well.

  1. may
  2. could
  3. should
  4. will

A referência ao passado e à habilidade leva a:

could.

Agora:

___ you help me, please?

  1. Could
  2. Did
  3. Mustn’t
  4. Was

Resposta:

Could.

Para may, procure:

uncertainty

possibility

ou um pedido formal de permissão.

Exemplo:

It ___ rain tomorrow.

  1. may
  2. did
  3. has to
  4. was

Resposta:

may.

E lembre sempre:

modal + base verb

Prática

1. Complete:

I ___ swim when I was six.

  1. could
  2. may
  3. will
  4. should to

2. Complete:

She ___ read before she started school.

  1. could
  2. does
  3. may to
  4. coulds

3. Complete:

When I was three, I ___ ride a bike.

  1. couldn’t
  2. don’t
  3. may not yesterday
  4. wasn’t ride

4. Complete:

Could you ___ me?

  1. helps
  2. helped
  3. help
  4. helping

5. Complete:

Could you ___ the window, please?

  1. open
  2. opened
  3. opens
  4. opening

6. Escolha a frase correta.

  1. She could to speak English.
  2. She could speaks English.
  3. She could speak English.
  4. She did could speak English.

7. Transforme para a negativa:

I could swim when I was five.

8. Transforme em pergunta:

Maria could read when she was four.

9. Responda afirmativamente:

Could you ride a bike when you were ten?

10. Responda negativamente:

Could Peter swim when he was six?

11. Complete:

It ___ rain later.

  1. may
  2. did
  3. must to
  4. was

12. Complete:

Maria ___ come to the party.

  1. may
  2. may comes
  3. may to come
  4. mays come

13. Complete:

He may ___ at home.

  1. is
  2. be
  3. being
  4. was

14. Complete:

They may ___ late.

  1. arrive
  2. arrives
  3. arrived
  4. arriving

15. Complete:

___ I come in?

  1. Did
  2. May
  3. Was
  4. Have

16. Complete:

May I ___ a question?

  1. asks
  2. asked
  3. ask
  4. asking

17. Qual frase expressa possibilidade?

  1. It may rain tomorrow.
  2. I worked yesterday.
  3. She must wear a uniform.
  4. They are studying now.

18. Qual frase expressa habilidade passada?

  1. I can swim.
  2. I could swim when I was six.
  3. I may swim tomorrow.
  4. I should swim.

19. Qual frase é um pedido polido?

  1. Could you help me, please?
  2. You must help me.
  3. I helped you yesterday.
  4. She may be busy.

20. Qual frase pede permissão de modo formal?

  1. May I sit here?
  2. I sit here.
  3. I could sit yesterday.
  4. You should sit here.

21. Corrija:

He could to run fast.

22. Corrija:

Could she played the piano?

23. Corrija:

It may rains tonight.

24. Corrija:

She may is tired.

25. Corrija:

May I to use your phone?

26. Escolha entre can e could:

Today, I ___ use this program very well.

When I was ten, I ___ use a computer, but not very well.

27. Escolha entre will e may:

I’m certain she ___ come tomorrow.

I’m not sure. She ___ come tomorrow.

28. Leia:

When Daniel was eight, he could swim and ride a bike, but he couldn’t cook. Now he can cook very well. Tomorrow, his family may visit him. Daniel isn’t sure because the weather may be bad. His sister could also come, but she hasn’t decided yet.

Responda:

  1. What could Daniel do when he was eight?

  2. What couldn’t he do?

  3. What can he do now?

  4. Who may visit him tomorrow?

  5. Why isn’t the visit certain?

  6. Who could also come?

29. Classifique o uso de could:

  1. I could read when I was five.

  2. Could you help me?

  3. It could rain later.

  4. We could go to the cinema.

Use:

  • past ability;
  • polite request;
  • possibility;
  • suggestion.

30. Produção

Escreva um pequeno texto de oito a dez frases usando:

  • duas frases com could para habilidade passada;
  • uma com couldn’t;
  • uma pergunta polida com Could you…?;
  • duas frases com may para possibilidade;
  • uma pergunta com May I…?;
  • pelo menos uma comparação entre can e could.

Gabarito comentado

1. A — could

A frase descreve uma habilidade passada.

2. A — could

She could read…

Depois de could, usamos a forma base.

3. A — couldn’t

A frase fala de uma incapacidade no passado.

4. C — help

could + base verb.

5. A — open

Could you open…?

6. C

She could speak English.

Não usamos:

to

nem:

-s.

7.

I couldn’t swim when I was five.

8.

Could Maria read when she was four?

9.

Yes, I could.

10.

No, he couldn’t.

11. A — may

It may rain later.

Expressa possibilidade.

12. A — may

Maria may come…

13. B — be

Depois de may, usamos a forma base:

be.

14. A — arrive

may arrive.

15. B — May

May I come in?

16. C — ask

May I ask a question?

17. A

It may rain tomorrow.

18. B

I could swim when I was six.

Could indica habilidade no passado.

19. A

Could you help me, please?

20. A

May I sit here?

É uma forma tradicionalmente mais formal de pedir permissão.

21.

He could run fast.

22.

Could she play the piano?

Depois de could, usamos:

play.

23.

It may rain tonight.

24.

She may be tired.

25.

May I use your phone?

26.

Today, I can use this program very well.

When I was ten, I could use a computer, but not very well.

27.

I’m certain she will come tomorrow.

I’m not sure. She may come tomorrow.

Will apresenta o evento com mais certeza no contexto fornecido.

May preserva a incerteza.

28.

  1. He could swim and ride a bike.

  2. He couldn’t cook.

  3. He can cook very well.

  4. His family may visit him.

  5. Because the weather may be bad.

  6. His sister.

29.

  1. past ability

  2. polite request

  3. possibility

  4. suggestion

30.

Modelo:

When I was seven, I could ride a bike. I could also read simple books, but I couldn’t swim. Now I can swim very well. Could you help me with this exercise, please? It may be difficult, but I can try. My teacher may give us another exercise tomorrow. May I use your dictionary? When I was younger, I couldn’t understand much English, but now I can understand simple conversations.

Tarefa de consolidação

Crie quatro grupos.

Past ability

Escreva cinco frases com:

could

couldn’t.

Exemplo:

When I was six, I could read.

Polite requests

Escreva cinco perguntas com:

Could you…?

Exemplo:

Could you repeat that, please?

Possibility

Escreva cinco frases com:

may

e cinco com:

could.

Exemplo:

It may rain.

The bus could be late.

Permission

Escreva cinco perguntas com:

May I…?

Exemplo:

May I come in?

Depois compare:

I can swim now.

I could swim when I was ten.

It may rain tomorrow.

It will rain tomorrow.

Could you help me?

May I come in?

Finalize memorizando:

can = capacidade atual

could = capacidade passada / pedido polido / possibilidade

may = possibilidade / permissão formal

E a regra estrutural:

could + base verb

may + base verb

Nunca:

could to go

could goes

may to come

may comes.

Aula 49 — Infinitive e gerund: introdução

Objetivos

Ao final desta aula, você deverá ser capaz de:

  • compreender o que são infinitive e gerund;
  • reconhecer a estrutura to + verbo;
  • reconhecer a estrutura verbo + -ing;
  • entender que certos verbos são normalmente seguidos por infinitive e outros por gerund;
  • usar estruturas frequentes como want to, need to, decide to, enjoy -ing, like -ing;
  • distinguir o gerund do Present Continuous;
  • formar frases simples com infinitive e gerund;
  • compreender essas estruturas em pequenos textos e diálogos;
  • evitar erros como want studying, enjoy to read e decide going;
  • desenvolver estratégias para memorizar padrões verbais frequentes.

Desenvolvimento

Em inglês, muitas vezes encontramos dois verbos na mesma frase.

Exemplo:

I want to study English.

Temos:

want

e:

study.

Outro exemplo:

I enjoy studying English.

Temos:

enjoy

e:

studying.

Observe que o segundo verbo aparece de duas maneiras diferentes:

to study

ou:

studying.

Essas estruturas são chamadas, respectivamente, de:

infinitive

e:

gerund.

O que é o infinitive?

Nesta introdução, trabalharemos principalmente com o infinitivo formado por:

to + base verb

Exemplos:

to study

to work

to travel

to eat

to sleep

to read.

Em uma frase:

I want to study.

She needs to work.

They decided to travel.

Estrutura básica

Um padrão frequente é:

verb + to + base verb

Exemplo:

want to study

need to work

decide to travel.

O primeiro verbo determina a forma do segundo.

Want to

Um dos padrões mais importantes:

want + to + verb.

Exemplos:

I want to learn English.

She wants to travel.

They want to buy a house.

Observe:

She wants to travel.

O -s aparece em:

wants

porque esse é o verbo principal no Simple Present.

Mas depois de to:

travel

continua na forma base.

Não:

She wants to travels.

Need to

need + to + verb.

Exemplos:

I need to study.

We need to leave now.

She needs to buy some food.

Decide to

decide + to + verb.

Exemplos:

I decided to stay at home.

She decided to study medicine.

They decided to travel by bus.

Como:

decided

está no passado, a decisão aconteceu no passado.

Mas:

to stay

to study

to travel

continuam na estrutura infinitiva.

Plan to

plan + to + verb.

Exemplos:

We plan to visit London.

I plan to study tomorrow.

She plans to start a new course.

Hope to

hope + to + verb.

Exemplos:

I hope to travel next year.

She hopes to pass the exam.

We hope to see you soon.

Would like to

Outra estrutura muito frequente:

would like to + verb.

Exemplo:

I would like to order some coffee.

She would like to study abroad.

We’d like to visit the museum.

Ela pode expressar desejo de forma mais polida.

Compare:

I want to speak to the manager.

e:

I would like to speak to the manager.

A segunda costuma soar mais polida.

O que é o gerund?

O gerund é formado com:

verb + -ing.

Exemplos:

studying

working

reading

traveling

swimming.

Em determinadas estruturas, essa forma funciona como complemento de outro verbo.

Exemplo:

I enjoy reading.

Aqui:

reading

não significa necessariamente que a pessoa está lendo neste momento.

A frase significa:

eu gosto de ler / eu aprecio a atividade de leitura.

Enjoy + -ing

Depois de:

enjoy

usamos normalmente:

verb-ing.

Exemplos:

I enjoy reading.

She enjoys cooking.

They enjoy traveling.

Não:

I enjoy to read.

No padrão básico estudado aqui:

enjoy + gerund.

Like + -ing

Também é muito comum:

like + verb-ing.

Exemplos:

I like studying English.

She likes listening to music.

We like watching movies.

Love + -ing

I love reading.

He loves playing football.

They love traveling.

Hate + -ing

I hate waiting.

She hates waking up early.

He hates driving in heavy traffic.

Gerund não é sempre Present Continuous

Observe:

I am reading now.

Aqui:

am reading

é Present Continuous.

Agora:

I enjoy reading.

Aqui:

reading

é gerund.

A forma:

reading

é visualmente igual, mas exerce funções diferentes.

Como distinguir?

Present Continuous:

subject + am/is/are + verb-ing.

Exemplo:

She is cooking now.

Gerund após outro verbo:

verb + verb-ing.

Exemplo:

She enjoys cooking.

Na segunda frase, não existe a ideia obrigatória de ação acontecendo agora.

Compare

I am studying English now.

Estou estudando neste momento.

I like studying English.

Gosto de estudar inglês.

They are swimming now.

Eles estão nadando agora.

They enjoy swimming.

Eles gostam de nadar.

Alguns verbos frequentes seguidos de infinitive

Nesta introdução, memorize principalmente:

want to

need to

decide to

plan to

hope to

would like to.

Exemplos:

I want to go.

I need to study.

I decided to stay.

I plan to travel.

I hope to pass.

I would like to order.

Alguns verbos frequentes seguidos de gerund

Memorize:

enjoy + -ing

like + -ing

love + -ing

hate + -ing.

Exemplos:

enjoy reading

like cooking

love traveling

hate waiting.

Não traduza palavra por palavra

Em português, podemos dizer:

Eu gosto de estudar.

Em inglês:

I like studying.

Uma tradução palavra por palavra poderia levar o estudante a construir:

I like to study.

Essa forma também é possível com like em muitos contextos, mas nesta introdução o padrão:

like + -ing

é especialmente importante.

Já com:

enjoy

o padrão é:

enjoy + -ing.

Verb patterns

Essas combinações são frequentemente chamadas de:

verb patterns.

Ou seja, padrões que mostram qual forma costuma seguir determinado verbo.

Exemplo:

want → to + verb

enjoy → verb-ing.

Uma estratégia eficaz é não memorizar apenas:

want = querer.

Memorize:

want to do something.

Da mesma forma, não memorize apenas:

enjoy = gostar/apreciar.

Memorize:

enjoy doing something.

Mudanças ortográficas no gerund

As mesmas regras do -ing estudadas anteriormente continuam válidas.

Forma simples:

work → working

read → reading

study → studying.

Verbos terminados em -e:

make → making

write → writing

take → taking.

Alguns verbos curtos duplicam a consoante:

run → running

swim → swimming

sit → sitting.

Exemplos

I enjoy swimming.

She likes running.

They hate sitting for a long time.

Negativa com infinitive

Podemos negar o verbo principal:

I don’t want to go.

She doesn’t need to come.

They didn’t decide to leave.

Observe:

don’t want to

doesn’t need to

didn’t decide to.

A estrutura infinitiva continua:

to go

to come

to leave.

Negativa com gerund

Também negamos normalmente o verbo principal:

I don’t enjoy waiting.

She doesn’t like cooking.

They don’t like working at night.

Perguntas com infinitive

Do you want to go?

Does she need to study?

Did they decide to stay?

O verbo após to permanece na forma base.

Perguntas com gerund

Do you enjoy reading?

Does she like cooking?

Do they love traveling?

What do you like doing?

Pergunta muito útil:

What do you like doing in your free time?

Resposta:

I like reading.

I like watching movies.

I enjoy listening to music.

What do you want to do?

Compare:

What do you want to do this weekend?

Resposta:

I want to visit my family.

Aqui usamos:

want to + base verb.

Duas perguntas, dois padrões

What do you like doing?

preferências e atividades de que a pessoa gosta.

What do you want to do?

desejo ou intenção.

Exemplo de diálogo

A: What do you like doing on weekends?
B: I enjoy reading and watching movies.
A: What do you want to do this weekend?
B: I want to visit my grandparents.

Observe:

enjoy reading

e:

want to visit.

Outro diálogo

A: Do you like cooking?
B: Yes, I do. I love making pasta.
A: Would you like to cook tonight?
B: Yes, I’d like to try a new recipe.

Aqui temos:

like cooking

love making

would like to cook

would like to try.

Would like x like

Compare:

I like drinking coffee.

Gosto de beber café.

I would like to drink some coffee.

Eu gostaria de beber café agora ou em determinada situação.

Essa diferença é importante.

Like + atividade geral

I like traveling.

Preferência geral.

Would like to + desejo específico

I’d like to travel to Italy next year.

Desejo específico.

Infinitive com finalidade: introdução

O infinitive também pode indicar finalidade.

Exemplo:

I went to the supermarket to buy some food.

Por que fui ao supermercado?

to buy some food.

Outro:

She called me to ask a question.

Esse uso será aprofundado posteriormente, mas já é importante reconhecê-lo.

Exemplo de finalidade

I study English to communicate with more people.

Aqui:

to communicate

expressa objetivo.

Gerund como atividade

O gerund pode nomear uma atividade.

Exemplo:

Reading is important.

Swimming is good exercise.

Learning English takes time.

Aqui, o gerund aparece como sujeito da frase.

Nesta aula, basta reconhecer esse padrão.

Reading is useful

Compare:

I am reading.

verbo no Present Continuous.

I enjoy reading.

gerund como complemento.

Reading is useful.

gerund como nome de uma atividade.

A forma é igual:

reading.

A função muda.

Erros frequentes

Erro:

I want studying English.

Correto:

I want to study English.

Erro:

She enjoys to cook.

Correto:

She enjoys cooking.

Erro:

They decided going home.

Correto:

They decided to go home.

Erro:

He needs studying.

Correto:

He needs to study.

Erro:

I enjoy read.

Correto:

I enjoy reading.

Erro:

She plans traveling next month.

No padrão básico:

She plans to travel next month.

Cuidado com modais

Depois de modais como:

can

could

should

must

may

will

não usamos to.

Compare:

I want to go.

Mas:

I can go.

Não:

I can to go.

Outro:

She needs to study.

Mas:

She should study.

Isso ajuda a diferenciar estruturas.

Infinitive depois de certos verbos

I hope to see you.

We decided to stay.

She plans to start tomorrow.

Gerund depois de certos verbos

I enjoy studying.

We like traveling.

She hates waiting.

O ponto principal é:

o primeiro verbo influencia a forma do segundo.

Reading

Leia:

Laura loves traveling. Every year, she plans to visit a new place. This year, she wants to go to Chile. She enjoys learning about different cultures and likes taking photos. She hopes to stay there for two weeks.

Formas com gerund:

traveling

learning

taking.

Formas com infinitive:

to visit

to go

to stay.

Por que isso importa em provas?

Uma questão pode testar exatamente qual forma vem após determinado verbo.

Exemplo:

She enjoys ___ books.

  1. read
  2. to read
  3. reading
  4. reads

Resposta:

reading.

Outra:

She wants ___ a new book.

  1. buy
  2. buying
  3. to buy
  4. buys

Resposta:

to buy.

Memorize em blocos

Mais eficiente:

want to travel

do que:

want + regra.

Mais eficiente:

enjoy traveling

do que:

enjoy + regra.

Assim, seu cérebro começa a reconhecer combinações naturais.

Vocabulário-chave

infinitive — infinitivo

gerund — gerúndio/forma em -ing usada como nome ou complemento

verb pattern — padrão verbal

want to — querer

I want to travel.

need to — precisar

I need to study.

decide to — decidir

We decided to stay.

plan to — planejar

They plan to travel.

hope to — esperar ter a oportunidade de

I hope to see you.

would like to — gostaria de

I’d like to order.

enjoy — gostar/apreciar

I enjoy reading.

like — gostar

I like cooking.

love — adorar

She loves traveling.

hate — odiar/não gostar muito

He hates waiting.

activity — atividade

purpose — finalidade/objetivo

free time — tempo livre

Estratégia de prova

Em questões com dois verbos, não escolha a forma do segundo verbo apenas pela tradução.

Primeiro, identifique o primeiro verbo.

Se encontrar:

want

need

decide

plan

hope

procure normalmente:

to + base verb

Exemplo:

I decided ___ home.

  1. going
  2. to go
  3. went
  4. goes

Resposta:

to go.

Se encontrar:

enjoy

procure:

verb-ing

Exemplo:

They enjoy ___.

  1. travel
  2. to travel
  3. traveling
  4. traveled

Resposta:

traveling.

Memorize especialmente:

want to do

need to do

decide to do

enjoy doing

Também verifique se o -ing pertence ao Present Continuous:

She is reading.

ou se funciona como gerund:

She enjoys reading.

Prática

1. Complete:

I want ___ English.

  1. studying
  2. to study
  3. studied
  4. studies

2. Complete:

She needs ___ tomorrow.

  1. work
  2. working
  3. to work
  4. worked

3. Complete:

They decided ___ home.

  1. to go
  2. going
  3. went
  4. goes

4. Complete:

We plan ___ next year.

  1. traveling
  2. traveled
  3. to travel
  4. travels

5. Complete:

I hope ___ you soon.

  1. seeing
  2. to see
  3. saw
  4. sees

6. Complete:

I enjoy ___ books.

  1. read
  2. to read
  3. reading
  4. reads

7. Complete:

She likes ___ music.

  1. listening to
  2. to listening
  3. listened
  4. listens

8. Complete:

They love ___.

  1. travel
  2. traveling
  3. traveled
  4. travels

9. Complete:

He hates ___ in long lines.

  1. wait
  2. waiting
  3. to waiting
  4. waited yesterday

10. Escolha a frase correta.

  1. She wants studying English.
  2. She wants to study English.
  3. She wants to studying English.
  4. She want studies English.

11. Escolha a frase correta.

  1. I enjoy to read.
  2. I enjoy reading.
  3. I enjoy read.
  4. I enjoying reading.

12. Transforme usando want:

I / travel next year

13. Transforme usando enjoy:

she / cook

14. Transforme usando plan:

we / visit the museum

15. Transforme usando love:

they / swim

16. Complete:

Would you like ___ some coffee?

  1. drink
  2. drinking
  3. to drink
  4. drank

17. Complete:

I would like ___ a question.

  1. ask
  2. asking
  3. to ask
  4. asked

18. Identifique: infinitive ou gerund?

to study

19. Identifique: infinitive ou gerund?

studying

20. Identifique a função de reading:

I am reading now.

  1. gerund após verbo
  2. Present Continuous
  3. infinitive
  4. Simple Past

21. Identifique a função:

I enjoy reading.

  1. Present Continuous
  2. gerund após verbo
  3. Simple Past
  4. infinitive

22. Identifique:

Reading is useful.

  1. gerund funcionando como nome de atividade
  2. Past Continuous
  3. infinitive
  4. Simple Present de read

23. Corrija:

I want going home.

24. Corrija:

She enjoys to swim.

25. Corrija:

They decided traveling by bus.

26. Corrija:

He hopes seeing you tomorrow.

27. Leia:

Daniel loves learning languages. He enjoys watching films in English and likes listening to podcasts. Next year, he plans to travel to Canada. He wants to practice English every day before the trip. He also hopes to meet new people there.

Responda:

  1. What does Daniel love doing?

  2. What does he enjoy watching?

  3. What does he like listening to?

  4. Where does he plan to travel?

  5. What does he want to practice?

  6. Who does he hope to meet?

28. Separe as estruturas do texto anterior em duas categorias: infinitive e gerund.

29. Complete com a forma correta do verbo entre parênteses:

  1. I enjoy ______ books. (read)

  2. She wants ______ home. (go)

  3. They decided ______. (stay)

  4. We love ______. (travel)

  5. He needs ______. (study)

  6. Maria hates ______. (wait)

30. Produção

Laura loves learning new things. She enjoys reading books and likes watching documentaries. She hates waiting for opportunities, so she makes plans carefully. She wants to study abroad next year.
