While we were having lunch, it suddenly started to rain, so we went to a café nearby. We stayed there for about an hour and talked. Finally, the rain stopped and we went home. I was tired, but I really enjoyed the day.

Por que esse texto funciona?

Ele informa:

when

where

who

sequence

unexpected event

result

opinion.

Também usa:

Simple Past

Past Continuous

because

so

finally.

Começo eficiente

Evite introduções excessivamente gerais.

Fraco:

There are many experiences in life and people have experiences every day.

Melhor:

Last month, I visited a science museum with my classmates.

Entre diretamente na experiência.

Final eficiente

Evite terminar abruptamente:

Then I went home.

Melhor:

Finally, I went home. I was tired, but it was one of the most interesting days of the semester.

Não invente complexidade

Você não precisa usar palavras sofisticadas como:

nevertheless

notwithstanding

subsequently

para produzir um bom texto A2.

Use estruturas que domina:

but

because

so

then

after that.

Word count

Se a tarefa pede:

80–100 words

planeje algo como:

  • 1–2 frases de introdução;
  • 5–7 frases de acontecimentos;
  • 1–2 frases finais.

Isso normalmente produz tamanho adequado.

Revisão de tempos verbais

Faça uma leitura apenas procurando verbos.

Exemplo:

Yesterday I go to the park and saw my friend.

Você percebe:

go

está incorreto.

Correção:

Yesterday I went to the park and saw my friend.

Revisão de verbos irregulares

Verifique especialmente:

go → went

see → saw

buy → bought

take → took

get → got

have → had

eat → ate

come → came

leave → left

feel → felt.

Did e verbo base

Se usar negativa:

I didn’t go.

Não:

I didn’t went.

Pergunta:

Did you enjoy the trip?

Não:

Did you enjoyed…?

Was / were

I was tired.

She was happy.

We were late.

They were excited.

Past Continuous

I was walking.

They were waiting.

Não:

I was walk.

Erros comuns

Errado:

Last year I go to another city.

Correto:

Last year I went to another city.

Errado:

We didn’t arrived on time.

Correto:

We didn’t arrive on time.

Errado:

I was very exciting.

Se você quer dizer que ficou animado:

I was very excited.

Excited x exciting

excited → como a pessoa se sente.

exciting → como algo é.

Compare:

I was excited.

The trip was exciting.

Bored x boring

I was bored.

The lecture was boring.

Tired x tiring

I was tired.

The journey was tiring.

Essa distinção é útil em relatos.

Vocabulário-chave

Experience — experiência

event — evento/acontecimento

memorable — memorável

trip — viagem

journey — trajeto/jornada

arrive — chegar

leave — sair/partir

happen — acontecer

decide — decidir

enjoy — gostar/aproveitar

feel — sentir

felt — sentiu/senti

excited — animado

nervous — nervoso

worried — preocupado

surprised — surpreso

disappointed — decepcionado

tired — cansado

interesting — interessante

exciting — empolgante

first — primeiro

then — depois

after that — depois disso

later — mais tarde

finally — finalmente

suddenly — de repente

luckily — felizmente

unfortunately — infelizmente

Estratégia de prova

Ao receber uma tarefa de relato, transforme o comando em quatro perguntas:

When and where?

Who?

What happened?

How did you feel?

Depois monte uma linha temporal curta:

arrival → activity → problem/event → solution → ending.

Use o Simple Past como tempo principal.

Se precisar apresentar uma ação em andamento:

was/were + -ing.

Antes de entregar, verifique:

□ Há um início claro?

□ Os acontecimentos estão em ordem?

□ Usei passado corretamente?

□ Expliquei causa ou consequência quando necessário?

□ Dei uma opinião ou sentimento?

□ Respondi todos os pontos do comando?

Prática

1. Escolha a melhor abertura para um relato de experiência:

  1. Experiences are things and people have many things.
  2. Last Saturday, I visited a science museum with my friends.
  3. Dear Sir or Madam, how much is the course?
  4. English is a language.

2. Complete:

Last weekend, we ___ to the beach.

  1. go
  2. went
  3. going
  4. goes

3. Complete:

We ___ lunch at a small restaurant.

  1. have
  2. has
  3. had
  4. having

4. Complete:

I ___ very tired after the journey.

  1. feel
  2. felt
  3. feeling
  4. feeled

5. Complete:

First, we visited the museum. ___, we went to a café.

  1. Then
  2. Because
  3. Who
  4. Where

6. Complete:

The weather was bad, ___ we stayed inside.

  1. because
  2. so
  3. who
  4. before of

7. Complete:

We stayed inside ___ the weather was bad.

  1. so
  2. because
  3. finally
  4. where

8. Complete:

While we ___ in the park, it started to rain.

  1. walked every day
  2. were walking
  3. are walking
  4. will walk

9. Escolha a frase correta:

  1. I didn’t went to the museum.
  2. I didn’t go to the museum.
  3. I don’t went to the museum.
  4. I didn’t going to the museum.

10. Escolha:

  1. I was exciting about the trip.
  2. I was excited about the trip.
  3. I excited about the trip.
  4. I was excite about the trip.

11. Corrija:

Yesterday, I go shopping with my sister.

12. Corrija:

We didn’t arrived early.

13. Corrija:

The trip was very excited.

14. Corrija:

Because the train was late, so we took a taxi.

15. Organize:

  1. Finally, we returned to the hotel.
  2. First, we visited the old town.
  3. After that, we had dinner.
  4. Then, we went to a museum.

16. Combine com because:

I was tired.
I walked for five hours.

17. Combine com so:

The restaurant was full.
We went to another place.

18. Combine com when:

I arrived home.
I called my friend.

19. Combine usando Past Continuous + when:

I waited for the bus.
I saw my teacher.

20. Escolha o melhor encerramento:

  1. Finally, we went home. I was tired, but I had a great day.
  2. Finally.
  3. Experience end.
  4. Yesterday is good.

21. Identifique o erro de coerência:

First, I arrived at the restaurant. Finally, I ordered dinner. Then I left home to go to the restaurant.

Explique qual ação está fora de ordem.

22. Reescreva evitando repetição:

Maria went to the museum. Maria bought a ticket. Maria visited three exhibitions. Maria enjoyed the museum.

23. Complete com uma palavra adequada:

The trip was very ______, so I was ______.

Use uma combinação correta entre:

exciting / excited.

24. Complete:

The journey was very ______, and at the end I was ______.

Use:

tiring / tired.

25. Planejamento

Para o comando:

Write about a school event. Say where it happened, who was with you, what happened and how you felt.

Crie quatro notas curtas antes de escrever.

26. Produção — viagem

Escreva de 70 a 90 palavras sobre uma viagem fictícia.

Inclua:

  • destino;
  • companhia;
  • transporte;
  • duas atividades;
  • um problema;
  • opinião final.

27. Produção — experiência acadêmica

Escreva de 70 a 90 palavras sobre uma prova, apresentação ou evento escolar.

Use:

  • Simple Past;
  • um marcador de sequência;
  • because ou so;
  • pelo menos um sentimento.

28. Produção — problema cotidiano

Escreva de 70 a 90 palavras sobre um dia em que algo deu errado.

Estrutura:

situação inicial → problema → tentativa de solução → resultado.

29. Revisão

Corrija o texto:

Last friday I went to a concert with my friend. We take the bus at seven and arrive at the concert hall at eight. While we waited outside, it start to rain. We didn’t had an umbrella, so we was completely wet. Finally, the doors opened and we go inside. I was tired, but the concert was very excited.

30. Produção completa

Escreva um relato de aproximadamente 90–110 palavras sobre:

A day you will remember

Inclua:

  • quando aconteceu;
  • onde aconteceu;
  • quem estava com você;
  • pelo menos quatro acontecimentos;
  • um problema ou surpresa;
  • como terminou;
  • como você se sentiu.

Gabarito comentado

1. B

Last Saturday, I visited a science museum with my friends.

A frase inicia diretamente a experiência e fornece tempo, lugar e participantes.

2. B — went

go → went.

3. C — had

have → had.

4. B — felt

O passado de:

feel

é:

felt.

5. A — Then

Indica sequência.

6. B — so

A primeira oração apresenta a causa:

bad weather.

Depois vem o resultado:

stayed inside.

7. B — because

Aqui a causa aparece depois de:

because.

8. B — were walking

A caminhada estava em andamento quando começou a chover.

9. B

I didn’t go to the museum.

Depois de:

didn’t

usamos verbo base.

10. B

I was excited about the trip.

Excited descreve o sentimento da pessoa.

11.

Yesterday, I went shopping with my sister.

12.

We didn’t arrive early.

13.

Se a viagem causou animação:

The trip was very exciting.

Se o objetivo fosse falar da pessoa:

I was very excited.

14.

Duas possibilidades:

Because the train was late, we took a taxi.

Ou:

The train was late, so we took a taxi.

15.

Ordem:

  1. First, we visited the old town.
  1. Then, we went to a museum.
  1. After that, we had dinner.
  1. Finally, we returned to the hotel.

16.

I was tired because I walked for five hours.

17.

The restaurant was full, so we went to another place.

18.

When I arrived home, I called my friend.

Ou:

I called my friend when I arrived home.

19.

I was waiting for the bus when I saw my teacher.

20. A

O texto termina com:

ação final + sentimento/opinião.

21.

A ação:

Then I left home to go to the restaurant.

deveria acontecer antes de:

arrived at the restaurant.

Uma sequência coerente seria:

First, I left home. Then I arrived at the restaurant. After that, I ordered dinner.

22.

Maria went to the museum and bought a ticket. She visited three exhibitions and really enjoyed the museum.

23.

The trip was very exciting, so I was excited.

A experiência é:

exciting.

A pessoa fica:

excited.

24.

The journey was very tiring, and at the end I was tired.

25.

Modelo de planejamento:

where → school gym

who → classmates + teachers

what → science fair + presentation

feeling → nervous, then happy.

Essas notas já fornecem a base do texto.

26.

Modelo:

Last month, I traveled to a small town with two friends. We went there by bus and stayed for two nights. On the first day, we visited a museum and walked around the historic center. Later, we had dinner at a local restaurant. Unfortunately, it started to rain and we didn’t have umbrellas, so we returned to the hotel early. The next morning, the weather was better. I really enjoyed the trip because the town was beautiful and quiet.

27.

Modelo:

Last week, I gave a presentation in my English class. I was very nervous because I don’t usually enjoy speaking in front of people. First, my classmate introduced our topic. Then I explained the main part of the project. I forgot one word, but my teacher helped me, so I continued. At the end, our classmates asked some questions. I felt tired after the presentation, but I was also happy because everything went well.

28.

Modelo:

Yesterday, I had a difficult morning. I left home at seven because I had an important class. When I arrived at the bus stop, I realized that I had forgotten my wallet. I went back home to get it, so I missed my usual bus. Then the next bus arrived late. I finally reached school twenty minutes after the class started. I was embarrassed, but the teacher allowed me to enter. It was a stressful morning.

29.

Versão corrigida:

Last Friday, I went to a concert with my friend. We took the bus at seven and arrived at the concert hall at eight. While we were waiting outside, it started to rain. We didn’t have an umbrella, so we were completely wet. Finally, the doors opened and we went inside. I was tired, but the concert was very exciting.

Correções principais:

friday → Friday

take → took

arrive → arrived

waited → were waiting

start → started

didn’t had → didn’t have

we was → we were

go → went

excited → exciting.

30.

Modelo:

Last year, I spent a memorable day with some friends at a cultural festival. We arrived in the morning and first visited several exhibitions. Then we watched a music performance and tried different foods. In the afternoon, we were walking through the festival when it suddenly started to rain heavily. We didn’t have umbrellas, so we ran into a small café. Luckily, the rain stopped after thirty minutes. Finally, we watched the last performance and went home. I was extremely tired, but I felt happy because the day was different, surprising and very enjoyable.

Tarefa de consolidação

Escreva três relatos diferentes.

Relato 1 — Experiência positiva

Tema:

a good weekend.

Use:

first

then

finally

because.

Relato 2 — Problema

Tema:

something went wrong.

Inclua:

cause

problem

solution

result.

Relato 3 — Experiência acadêmica

Tema:

exam, course, presentation or project.

Inclua:

feelings before

what happened

feelings after.

Depois destaque todos os verbos no passado e confira se estão corretos.

Faça uma lista separada com os irregulares utilizados:

go → went

see → saw

have → had

take → took

feel → felt.

Em seguida, encontre no seu próprio texto:

um marcador de sequência;

uma causa;

uma consequência;

um sentimento;

uma opinião final.

Finalize usando esta estrutura mental sempre que precisar escrever um relato:

Contexto → sequência → acontecimento principal → resultado → sentimento/opinião

E lembre-se:

Simple Past conta o que aconteceu.

Past Continuous apresenta uma ação que estava acontecendo.

First / then / after that / finally organizam a sequência.

Because explica a causa.

So apresenta a consequência.

Uma boa conclusão mostra como a experiência terminou e o que você pensou ou sentiu sobre ela.

Aula 62 — Speaking A2: preferências, planos e experiências

Objetivos

Ao final desta aula, você deverá ser capaz de:

  • falar sobre preferências pessoais em inglês;
  • explicar do que gosta e do que não gosta;
  • comparar opções simples;
  • falar sobre planos futuros;
  • usar estruturas como going to, Present Continuous e will em respostas orais;
  • relatar experiências passadas de forma simples;
  • utilizar o Simple Past para contar acontecimentos;
  • responder perguntas de Speaking com mais de uma frase;
  • justificar respostas usando because;
  • organizar uma fala curta com começo, desenvolvimento e conclusão;
  • pedir esclarecimento ou repetição quando necessário;
  • ganhar tempo para pensar sem interromper completamente a comunicação;
  • desenvolver respostas adequadas a tarefas de Speaking de nível A2.

Desenvolvimento

No nível A2, uma prova de Speaking normalmente exige que você consiga falar sobre assuntos cotidianos e pessoais de forma compreensível.

Três temas extremamente comuns são:

preferences

preferências.

plans

planos.

experiences

experiências.

Você pode receber perguntas como:

What do you like doing in your free time?

Which do you prefer, studying at home or in a library?

What are you going to do next weekend?

Have you got any plans for your holidays?

What did you do last weekend?

Tell me about a trip you enjoyed.

O objetivo não é produzir discursos longos ou perfeitos.

Você precisa mostrar que consegue:

  • compreender a pergunta;
  • responder diretamente;
  • acrescentar detalhes;
  • justificar sua resposta;
  • manter a comunicação.

Respostas muito curtas

Pergunta:

Do you like traveling?

Resposta:

Yes.

Gramaticalmente, isso pode estar correto, mas demonstra muito pouco.

Melhor:

Yes, I do. I really like traveling because I enjoy visiting new places and trying different food.

Você respondeu:

yes

e desenvolveu:

reason + detail.

Estrutura simples para desenvolver respostas

Uma técnica útil é:

answer + reason + example/detail

Pergunta:

Do you like reading?

Resposta:

Yes, I do. I like reading because it helps me relax. I usually read at night before I go to bed.

Temos:

answer → Yes, I do.

reason → because it helps me relax.

detail → I usually read at night.

Essa estrutura funciona para muitas perguntas A2.

Preferências

Para falar sobre aquilo de que você gosta:

I like…

I really like…

I love…

I enjoy…

Exemplos:

I like listening to music.

I really like studying languages.

I love traveling.

I enjoy watching films.

Lembre-se dos padrões estudados:

like + -ing

love + -ing

enjoy + -ing.

Não gostar

I don’t like…

I don’t really like…

I dislike…

I hate…

Exemplos:

I don’t like waiting in long lines.

I don’t really like crowded places.

I hate waking up very early.

No nível A2, formas simples como:

I don’t like…

são suficientes.

Perguntas sobre preferências

What do you like doing in your free time?

What kind of music do you like?

Do you like cooking?

What’s your favorite type of film?

Which sports do you enjoy?

What do you like doing…?

Resposta curta:

I like reading.

Resposta melhor:

I like reading, especially science fiction. I usually read in the evening because it’s quiet then.

Favorite

What’s your favorite subject?

My favorite subject is mathematics because I enjoy solving problems.

Outro:

What’s your favorite place in your city?

My favorite place is the public library because it’s quiet and comfortable.

Prefer

Uma estrutura importante:

prefer.

Exemplo:

I prefer tea to coffee.

Outro:

I prefer studying at home.

Pergunta:

Do you prefer studying alone or with other people?

Resposta:

I prefer studying alone because I can concentrate better.

Prefer A to B

I prefer trains to buses.

I prefer online classes to early morning classes.

Which do you prefer…?

Perguntas frequentes:

Which do you prefer, summer or winter?

Which do you prefer, books or films?

Do you prefer traveling by bus or by plane?

Uma resposta bem desenvolvida:

I prefer traveling by plane because it’s faster. However, buses are usually cheaper.

Aqui você compara duas opções.

Comparatives em Speaking

Você pode utilizar:

cheaper

faster

easier

quieter

more comfortable

more interesting.

Exemplo:

I prefer trains because they’re more comfortable than buses.

Outro:

I prefer studying in the morning because it’s quieter.

Superlatives

Também pode dizer:

It’s my favorite…

It’s the best…

It’s the most interesting…

Exemplo:

Saturday is my favorite day because I usually have more free time.

Giving reasons

A palavra mais importante para expandir respostas é:

because.

Pergunta:

Why do you prefer studying at home?

Resposta:

Because it’s quieter.

Melhor:

I prefer studying at home because it’s quieter and I have all my books there.

Because of

Pode aparecer:

I prefer the morning because of the quiet atmosphere.

No nível A2, because + oração costuma ser mais simples.

And, but e so

Use conectores simples.

I like the café because it’s cheap and comfortable.

I like traveling, but I don’t like airports.

I was tired, so I stayed home.

Esses conectores deixam sua fala mais natural.

Expressando opinião

Estruturas úteis:

I think…

I don’t think…

In my opinion…

For me…

Exemplo:

I think public transport is useful because it’s cheaper than taking a taxi.

Outro:

In my opinion, studying every day is better than studying only before a test.

No A2, não é necessário usar expressões argumentativas complexas.

Planos futuros

Outro tema frequente é:

plans.

Perguntas:

What are you doing this weekend?

What are you going to do during your holiday?

Do you have any plans for next year?

Where are you going to travel?

What will you do after the course?

Be going to

Use para intenção e plano.

I’m going to study this weekend.

I’m going to visit my family next month.

We’re going to travel in July.

Pergunta:

What are you going to do next weekend?

Resposta:

I’m going to stay at home on Saturday morning because I need to study. In the evening, I’m going to meet some friends.

Present Continuous para arranjos

I’m meeting my friend at six.

We’re having dinner with my family on Sunday.

I’m traveling to São Paulo next week.

Essa estrutura é útil quando existe um arranjo mais definido.

Will

Pode ser usado para previsões ou decisões.

I think I’ll stay home.

Maybe I’ll travel next year.

I think technology will become even more important.

Para planos já definidos, muitas vezes:

going to

ou:

Present Continuous

são mais adequados.

Expressões temporais

Use:

tomorrow

tonight

this weekend

next week

next month

next year

during the holidays

in the future.

Exemplo:

Next year, I’m going to take another English course.

Planos incertos

Nem todo plano está decidido.

Você pode dizer:

I’m not sure yet.

Maybe I’ll…

I might…

Mesmo que might seja um pouco além do núcleo desta aula, pode aparecer em conversação simples.

Como já estudamos may:

I may travel next month.

Também é possível.

Não sei ainda

Uma resposta perfeitamente válida:

I’m not sure yet, but I think I’ll stay home and relax.

Isso é muito melhor do que simplesmente:

I don’t know.

First Conditional ao falar de planos

Você também pode usar:

If the weather is good, I’ll go to the beach.

If I have enough time, I’ll visit my friends.

If I finish my work early, I’ll watch a film.

Isso ajuda a falar sobre possibilidades futuras.

Relatos de experiência

O terceiro grande tema é:

experiences.

Perguntas comuns:

What did you do last weekend?

Tell me about your last holiday.

Did you go anywhere interesting last year?

Tell me about a good day you remember.

What was your last trip like?

Aqui, o tempo principal normalmente é:

Simple Past.

Resposta simples

Pergunta:

What did you do last weekend?

I stayed at home.

Melhor:

I stayed at home on Saturday because I had some work to finish. On Sunday, I met a friend and we had lunch together.

Organizando experiências

Use:

first

then

after that

later

finally.

Exemplo:

Last Saturday, I went to the city center. First, I visited a bookstore. Then I had lunch at a café. After that, I met some friends. Finally, I went home at about seven.

Sentimentos

Inclua:

I was happy.

I was tired.

I was nervous.

I was excited.

I felt relaxed.

I really enjoyed it.

Exemplo:

I was tired at the end of the day, but I really enjoyed it.

Perguntas sobre viagem

Where did you go?

Who did you go with?

How did you travel?

Where did you stay?

What did you do?

Did you enjoy it?

Uma resposta pode integrar tudo:

Last year, I went to a small town with my family. We traveled by car and stayed in a hotel near the center. We visited a museum and tried some local food. I really enjoyed the trip because the town was quiet and beautiful.

Past Continuous em Speaking

Você pode usar:

I was walking home when it started to rain.

We were having dinner when the lights went out.

Não é obrigatório, mas ajuda a enriquecer relatos.

Experiência positiva

Pergunta:

Tell me about a day you enjoyed.

Resposta:

Last month, I went to a music festival with two friends. We arrived in the afternoon and watched several performances. The weather was good, and the atmosphere was very friendly. I was tired when I got home, but I had a great time.

Experiência problemática

Tell me about a difficult journey.

Resposta:

Last year, I took a bus to another city. The bus left late because there was a technical problem. Then there was heavy traffic, so we arrived almost two hours late. I was tired and frustrated, but eventually everything was fine.

Speaking não precisa ser perfeito

Se você cometer um pequeno erro, continue.

Evite parar por muito tempo para corrigir toda frase.

Por exemplo:

Yesterday I go—sorry, I went to the museum with my friend.

Uma autocorreção simples é suficiente.

Self-correction

Expressões naturais:

Sorry, I mean…

Sorry, I meant…

Let me say that again.

Exemplo:

I went there on Friday—sorry, I mean Saturday.

Pedindo repetição

Se não entender a pergunta:

Could you repeat the question, please?

Could you say that again, please?

Sorry, could you repeat that?

Essas expressões são melhores do que fingir que entendeu.

Pedindo esclarecimento

What do you mean by…?

Do you mean…?

Exemplo:

Do you mean my last holiday?

Isso pode ajudar quando a pergunta é ambígua.

Ganhar tempo para pensar

Em Speaking, pequenos marcadores ajudam.

Well…

Let me think…

I think…

That’s an interesting question.

I’m not sure, but…

Use com moderação.

Não transforme toda resposta em:

Well… um… well… um…

Evite silêncio longo

Se precisa pensar:

Let me think. I think I’d choose the train because it’s more comfortable.

Isso mantém a interação.

Não memorize discursos completos

Uma resposta decorada pode parecer artificial e pode não se adaptar à pergunta.

Melhor memorizar:

estruturas.

Exemplo:

I prefer ___ because ___.

Last weekend, I ___ with ___.

Next month, I’m going to ___.

Assim você cria respostas novas.

Expandindo uma resposta em três passos

Pergunta:

What’s your favorite way to travel?

Passo 1:

I prefer traveling by train.

Passo 2:

I prefer traveling by train because it’s comfortable.

Passo 3:

I prefer traveling by train because it’s comfortable, and I can read or relax during the journey.

Essa técnica é excelente para A2.

Resposta com contraste

I like traveling by plane because it’s fast, but I don’t enjoy waiting at airports.

Resposta com comparação

I prefer trains to buses because trains are usually faster and more comfortable.

Resposta com exemplo

I enjoy visiting museums. For example, last month I visited a science museum and spent almost three hours there.

Mesmo que for example seja simples, ajuda bastante.

Falar sobre frequência

Use:

always

usually

often

sometimes

rarely

never.

Exemplo:

I usually spend my weekends at home, but sometimes I meet friends.

Falar sobre rotina e preferência

I usually study at night because it’s quieter.

I often watch films on weekends.

I rarely go shopping during the week.

Speaking com perguntas de seguimento

O examinador pode perguntar:

Why?

Who with?

How often?

Where?

When?

Prepare-se para ampliar.

Pergunta inicial:

Do you like cooking?

Yes, I do.

Seguimento:

What do you usually cook?

I usually make simple meals, especially pasta and rice dishes.

Seguimento:

When do you cook?

Usually in the evening or at weekends.

Respostas coerentes

Evite contradições.

Exemplo ruim:

I never travel. Last month I traveled to three cities, and I travel every weekend.

Se corrigir:

I don’t travel very often, but last month I visited three cities.

Fica coerente.

Pronúncia e inteligibilidade

Em A2, o principal é:

ser compreendido.

Não é necessário imitar um sotaque específico.

Concentre-se em:

  • ritmo claro;
  • palavras principais;
  • finais importantes;
  • negativas.

Compare:

can

e:

can’t.

Uma negativa mal pronunciada pode mudar o sentido.

Números e datas no Speaking

Pratique dizer claramente:

13

30

15

Datas:

My birthday is on May fifth.

Horários:

My class starts at six thirty.

Essas informações podem aparecer em perguntas pessoais básicas.

Não responda algo diferente da pergunta

Pergunta:

What are you going to do next weekend?

Resposta inadequada:

Last weekend I went to the beach.

Você mudou de futuro para passado.

Identifique a palavra temporal antes de responder.

Sinais de tempo

usually → rotina

yesterday → passado

last weekend → passado

tomorrow → futuro

next year → futuro

now → presente.

Escute o auxiliar

Pergunta:

Do you…?

Resposta:

Yes, I do.

Pergunta:

Did you…?

Resposta:

Yes, I did.

Pergunta:

Can you…?

Resposta:

Yes, I can.

Pergunta:

Are you going to…?

Resposta:

Yes, I am.

Reconhecer o auxiliar ajuda a formar rapidamente a resposta.

Mini diálogo — preferências

A: What do you like doing in your free time?
B: I enjoy reading and watching films.
A: Which do you prefer?
B: I prefer reading because it’s more relaxing.

Mini diálogo — planos

A: What are you doing this weekend?
B: I’m meeting some friends on Saturday.
A: What are you going to do?
B: We’re going to have lunch and probably watch a film.

Mini diálogo — experiência

A: What did you do last Sunday?
B: I went to a park with my family.
A: Did you enjoy it?
B: Yes. The weather was good, and we had a picnic.

Vocabulário-chave

preferences

prefer — preferir

favorite — favorito

enjoy — gostar/apreciar

like — gostar

dislike — não gostar

reason — motivo

choice — escolha

plans

plan — plano/planejar

next — próximo

future — futuro

arrange — combinar/organizar

decide — decidir

maybe — talvez

probably — provavelmente

definitely — definitivamente/com certeza

experiences

experience — experiência

happen — acontecer

trip — viagem

event — evento

enjoy — aproveitar/gostar

feel — sentir

felt — sentiu/senti

memorable — memorável

exciting — empolgante

excited — animado

tiring — cansativo

tired — cansado

Speaking

repeat — repetir

explain — explicar

mean — significar

answer — responder/resposta

question — pergunta

opinion — opinião

example — exemplo

Estratégia de prova

Antes de responder, identifique a categoria da pergunta.

Se for sobre:

preference

use:

I prefer…

I like…

My favorite…

e explique:

because…

Se for sobre:

future plan

use:

I’m going to…

I’m …ing…

I think I’ll…

Se for sobre:

past experience

use:

Simple Past

e organize:

first → then → finally.

Uma estrutura segura para respostas curtas é:

Direct answer + reason + detail/example

Exemplo:

What do you like doing at weekends?

I like reading because it helps me relax. I usually read for an hour on Sunday afternoon.

Se não compreender:

Could you repeat the question, please?

Não responda aleatoriamente.

Prática

1. Responda de forma expandida:

Do you like traveling?

Use:

answer + because + detail.

2. Responda:

What do you like doing in your free time?

Use pelo menos duas atividades.

3. Complete:

I prefer trains ___ buses.

  1. than
  2. to
  3. of
  4. from

4. Complete:

I enjoy ___ films.

  1. watch
  2. watching
  3. to watching
  4. watched

5. Escolha a melhor resposta:

Which do you prefer, studying alone or studying with friends?

  1. Yesterday.
  2. I prefer studying alone because I can concentrate better.
  3. Yes, I did.
  4. At seven.

6. Responda usando comparative:

Do you prefer buses or trains?

Inclua:

more comfortable

ou:

cheaper.

7. Responda:

What’s your favorite place to study?

Inclua uma razão.

8. Complete:

Next weekend, I’m going to ___ my family.

  1. visited
  2. visit
  3. visiting after to
  4. visits

9. Responda:

What are you going to do next weekend?

Use pelo menos duas frases.

10. Responda com Present Continuous para futuro:

What are you doing on Saturday evening?

11. Complete:

If the weather is good, I ___ go to the park.

  1. will
  2. am yesterday
  3. did
  4. was

12. Responda:

What will you do if it rains this weekend?

13. Escolha a resposta coerente:

What did you do last weekend?

  1. I’m going to study.
  2. I went to a museum with my friends.
  3. I usually study.
  4. I will go tomorrow.

14. Responda:

Tell me about your last weekend.

Use:

first

then

finally.

15. Responda:

Tell me about a trip you enjoyed.

Inclua:

  • lugar;
  • companhia;
  • atividade;
  • opinião.

16. Corrija:

Last Saturday I go to the park.

17. Corrija:

I prefer bus than train.

18. Corrija:

I enjoy to watch films.

19. Corrija:

Tomorrow I went to visit my friend.

20. Escolha a melhor expressão para pedir repetição:

  1. Repeat!
  2. What?
  3. Could you repeat the question, please?
  4. Again question.

21. Escolha uma expressão para ganhar tempo:

  1. Let me think.
  2. I no answer.
  3. Stop question.
  4. Yesterday tomorrow.

22. Responda:

Which is better for you, studying in the morning or at night?

Use:

I think…

because…

23. Responda:

What kind of films do you like?

Inclua um exemplo.

24. Responda:

Do you have any plans for next year?

Use:

going to

e:

hope to.

25. Responda:

Tell me about a difficult day you remember.

Use:

because

so

e um sentimento.

26. Desenvolva esta resposta:

Question: Do you like technology?
Answer: Yes.

Transforme-a em três frases.

27. Desenvolva:

Question: What are you doing this weekend?
Answer: I’m studying.

Acrescente:

  • quando;
  • por quê;
  • outra atividade.

28. Desenvolva:

Question: What did you do yesterday?
Answer: I stayed home.

Acrescente:

  • duas atividades;
  • sentimento/opinião.

29. Simulação de entrevista

Responda oralmente às cinco perguntas:

  1. What do you usually do at weekends?

  2. Which do you prefer, reading or watching films? Why?

  3. What are you going to do next month?

  4. Tell me about a good experience you had recently.

  5. What will you do if you have free time tomorrow?

30. Produção oral longa

Prepare uma fala de aproximadamente um a dois minutos sobre:

My preferences, my plans and a memorable experience

Inclua:

  • uma preferência e sua justificativa;
  • um plano para o futuro;
  • uma experiência passada;
  • pelo menos um comparative;
  • because;
  • um marcador de sequência;
  • uma frase final de opinião.

Gabarito comentado

1.

Modelo:

Yes, I do. I like traveling because I enjoy visiting new places. I especially like short trips to quiet places.

A resposta possui:

posição + razão + detalhe.

2.

Modelo:

I enjoy reading and listening to music in my free time. I usually read in the evening and listen to music when I’m traveling.

3. B — to

A estrutura é:

prefer A to B.

4. B — watching

Um padrão muito comum:

enjoy + -ing.

5. B

A resposta aborda diretamente a preferência e oferece uma justificativa.

6.

Modelo:

I prefer trains because they’re usually more comfortable than buses. However, buses are sometimes cheaper.

7.

Modelo:

My favorite place to study is the library because it’s quiet and there are fewer distractions.

8. B — visit

going to + base verb.

9.

Modelo:

Next weekend, I’m going to study on Saturday morning. In the afternoon, I’m going to meet a friend and have lunch.

10.

Modelo:

I’m meeting some friends on Saturday evening.

O Present Continuous pode indicar arranjo futuro.

11. A — will

First Conditional:

If + Simple Present, will + base verb.

12.

Modelo:

If it rains this weekend, I’ll stay home and watch a film.

13. B

A pergunta está no passado:

did.

A resposta adequada também relata passado:

went.

14.

Modelo:

Last weekend, I stayed in the city. First, I went shopping in the morning. Then I had lunch with a friend. Finally, I went home and watched a film.

15.

Modelo:

Last year, I went to a small town with my family. We traveled by car and stayed there for three days. We visited a museum and tried some local food. I really enjoyed the trip because the town was peaceful and beautiful.

16.

Last Saturday, I went to the park.

17.

I prefer buses to trains.

Ou, dependendo da preferência:

I prefer trains to buses.

18.

I enjoy watching films.

19.

Para futuro:

Tomorrow, I’m going to visit my friend.

Também:

I’m visiting my friend tomorrow.

20. C

Could you repeat the question, please?

É uma forma educada e clara.

21. A

Let me think.

Permite ganhar alguns segundos sem interromper a comunicação.

22.

Modelo:

I think studying at night is better for me because it’s quieter and I can concentrate more easily.

23.

Modelo:

I like science-fiction films because they’re interesting. For example, I enjoy films about space and technology.

24.

Modelo:

Next year, I’m going to continue studying English. I also hope to travel and use English during the trip.

25.

Modelo:

Last month, I had a very difficult day because my bus was late. I had an important appointment, so I took a taxi. I arrived just in time, but I felt very stressed.

26.

Modelo:

Yes, I do. I like technology because it makes many everyday activities easier. I especially enjoy using computers for studying and communication.

27.

Modelo:

I’m studying on Saturday morning because I have an exam next week. In the afternoon, I’m meeting a friend for coffee.

28.

Modelo:

I stayed home yesterday. I studied for two hours and then watched a film. It was a quiet day, and I felt relaxed.

29.

Modelos possíveis:

I usually study, read and rest at weekends. Sometimes I meet friends on Saturday evening.

I prefer reading because it’s more relaxing than watching films. I also like learning new things from books.

Next month, I’m going to start a new course and visit some relatives.

Recently, I went to a cultural event with some friends. We watched a presentation and tried different foods. I really enjoyed it.

If I have free time tomorrow, I’ll read or watch a film.

30.

Modelo:

I really enjoy reading, especially books about science and technology. I prefer reading to watching television because I can study at my own pace, and books are often more detailed. Next month, I’m going to start a new course, so I plan to organize my study schedule before it begins. A memorable experience I had was a visit to a science museum last year. First, I visited an exhibition about space. Then I watched a short presentation about technology. I was tired at the end of the day, but I was very happy because the visit was interesting and educational. I would definitely like to go there again.

Tarefa de consolidação

Grave ou pratique oralmente respostas para quinze perguntas divididas em três grupos.

Preferências

What do you like doing in your free time?

What kind of music do you like?

Do you prefer studying alone or with other people?

What’s your favorite place in your city?

Which do you prefer, traveling by bus or by plane?

Para cada resposta, use:

answer + reason + detail.

Planos

Responda:

What are you doing this weekend?

What are you going to do next month?

Do you have any plans for your next holiday?

What do you hope to do next year?

What will you do if you have more free time?

Use:

going to

Present Continuous

will

quando adequados.

Experiências

Responda:

What did you do last weekend?

Tell me about your last trip.

Tell me about a good day you remember.

Tell me about a difficult experience.

Tell me about a place you visited.

Tente incluir:

when

where

who

what happened

how you felt.

Depois ouça sua própria resposta e verifique:

□ Respondi diretamente à pergunta?

□ Dei uma razão ou detalhe?

□ Usei o tempo verbal adequado?

□ Minha resposta teve começo e fim?

□ Falei de forma compreensível?

□ Evitei pausas excessivamente longas?

Finalize memorizando estas estruturas de apoio:

**I prefer ___ because ___.**

**I really enjoy ___ because ___.**

**I’m going to ___ next ___.**

**I’m ___ing on Saturday.**

If , I’ll .

Last , I went to .

**First , then , and finally ___.**

**I really enjoyed it because ___.**

Could you repeat the question, please?

Let me think.

No Speaking A2, uma resposta simples, relevante e bem desenvolvida costuma ser muito mais eficaz do que uma resposta excessivamente complexa que você não consegue sustentar com clareza.

Aula 63 — Skimming e scanning: introdução

Objetivos

Ao final desta aula, você deverá ser capaz de:

  • compreender o que é skimming;
  • compreender o que é scanning;
  • diferenciar leitura global de busca por informação específica;
  • escolher a estratégia adequada de acordo com a pergunta;
  • localizar rapidamente nomes, números, datas, horários e palavras-chave;
  • identificar a ideia principal de textos curtos;
  • evitar a leitura palavra por palavra quando ela não for necessária;
  • usar títulos, subtítulos e organização visual como pistas;
  • combinar skimming e scanning em tarefas de Reading;
  • aplicar essas estratégias em textos A2 como anúncios, e-mails, narrativas e textos informativos;
  • administrar melhor o tempo durante provas de proficiência.

Desenvolvimento

Em uma prova de proficiência, nem toda questão exige que você leia um texto da mesma maneira.

Às vezes, você precisa entender:

sobre o que o texto fala.

Em outros momentos, precisa apenas encontrar:

um horário;

um preço;

uma data;

um nome;

uma informação específica.

Duas estratégias fundamentais para isso são:

skimming

e:

scanning.

Essas duas técnicas ajudam a ler com mais rapidez e eficiência.

O que é skimming?

Skimming é uma leitura rápida para compreender:

o assunto geral;

a ideia principal;

o objetivo do texto;

a organização geral.

Quando você faz skimming, não precisa entender cada palavra.

Você procura responder perguntas como:

What is the text mainly about?

What is the main idea?

What is the purpose of the text?

What kind of text is this?

Exemplo

Leia rapidamente:

CITY LANGUAGE SCHOOL
English classes for adults
Morning and evening groups
Courses from beginner to advanced level
Small classes and experienced teachers
Registration open until September 10

Mesmo sem analisar cada detalhe, podemos dizer que o texto é principalmente sobre:

English courses at a language school.

Isso é skimming.

O objetivo do skimming

A meta não é encontrar todos os detalhes.

É construir um mapa mental rápido do texto.

Pergunte:

Who or what is this text about?

Why was this text written?

What is the general message?

O que observar primeiro

Ao fazer skimming, observe:

title

headings

first sentence

repeated words

final sentence

visual organization.

Esses elementos frequentemente revelam o tópico.

Título

Título:

Healthy Habits for Students

Antes mesmo de ler, esperamos um texto relacionado a:

saúde;

hábitos;

estudantes.

Palavras repetidas

Se aparecem várias vezes:

exercise

sleep

food

water

provavelmente o tópico envolve:

healthy lifestyle.

Primeira frase

Muitos textos informativos apresentam o tema logo no início.

Exemplo:

Online learning has become an important part of modern education.

Isso já fornece o assunto central.

Última frase

A conclusão também pode reforçar a ideia principal.

Exemplo:

For these reasons, many students choose online courses because they are flexible and convenient.

Podemos inferir que o texto apresenta vantagens ou características do ensino online.

Skimming não é leitura descuidada

Ler rapidamente não significa:

ler sem atenção.

Você está procurando informações específicas de nível global.

Uma leitura lenta de todas as palavras pode até prejudicar se a questão pergunta apenas:

What is the text mainly about?

Exemplo de skimming

Texto:

Many people use smartphones every day for communication, work and entertainment. Smartphones allow users to send messages, access the internet, take photos and use different applications. However, spending too much time on a phone can also create problems. For this reason, it is important to use technology in a balanced way.

Ideia principal:

smartphones are useful, but should be used in a balanced way.

Não é apenas:

phones take photos.

Esse é um detalhe.

Main idea x detail

Compare:

Main idea: the text discusses smartphone use and balance.

Detalhes:

send messages;

take photos;

use applications.

Uma questão de skimming pede o primeiro tipo de informação.

O que é scanning?

Scanning é procurar rapidamente uma informação específica dentro do texto.

Você não precisa compreender tudo.

Você já sabe o que está procurando.

Por exemplo:

What time does the museum close?

Seu alvo é:

horário de fechamento.

Então, em vez de reler todo o texto, procure:

close

closing

horário.

Exemplo

CITY MUSEUM
Monday–Friday: 9 a.m.–6 p.m.
Saturday: 10 a.m.–5 p.m.
Sunday: Closed
Adult ticket: $12
Student ticket: $8

Pergunta:

How much does a student pay?

Use scanning.

Procure:

student ticket.

Resposta:

$8.

Você não precisa analisar primeiro os horários.

Scanning é busca direcionada

Antes de procurar, transforme a pergunta em uma palavra-chave.

Pergunta:

When does the course start?

Alvos:

course

start

date.

Pergunta:

Which room is the exam in?

Alvos:

room

exam.

Pergunta:

How much does it cost?

Alvos:

price

cost

currency symbol.

Informações fáceis de localizar

Scanning funciona especialmente bem para:

numbers

prices

dates

times

names

places

capital letters

percentages.

Essas informações têm formato visual distinto.

Números

Se pergunta:

How many students can join the course?

procure números relacionados a:

students

class size

maximum.

Datas

Procure:

Monday

Friday

May

September

12/08

ou outros formatos.

Preços

Procure:

$

£

€

e números próximos.

Nomes

Nomes próprios normalmente aparecem com letra inicial maiúscula.

Exemplo:

Laura

Daniel

London

Oxford.

Scanning com palavras equivalentes

A pergunta nem sempre usa a mesma palavra do texto.

Pergunta:

When does the shop close?

Texto:

Opening hours: 9 a.m.–7 p.m.

Você precisa compreender que:

closing time

corresponde ao final do período.

Outro:

Pergunta:

What is the price?

Texto:

Tickets cost $15.

price

e:

cost

estão relacionados.

Skimming e scanning são diferentes

Resumo:

skimming → general meaning

scanning → specific information

Pergunta:

What is this article mainly about?

Use:

skimming.

Pergunta:

How much is the ticket?

Use:

scanning.

As duas estratégias podem ser usadas no mesmo texto

Isso é muito comum.

Primeiro:

skim the text

para entender o tema.

Depois:

scan the text

para responder perguntas específicas.

Sequência eficiente

Uma estratégia possível:

1. Read the title.

2. Skim the text.

3. Read the question.

4. Identify keywords.

5. Scan for the answer.

6. Read the relevant sentence carefully.

Esse último passo é importante.

Scanning localiza a área.

Depois você deve ler aquela parte com atenção.

Não responda só porque encontrou a mesma palavra

Exemplo:

Texto:

The train originally left from platform 4, but it now leaves from platform 7.

Pergunta:

Which platform should passengers use?

Se você procura apenas:

platform

encontrará:

4

e:

É preciso ler a frase completa.

Resposta:

platform 7.

Palavras de contraste

Tenha cuidado com:

but

however

instead

now

actually.

Elas podem mudar a informação.

Negativas

Texto:

The library is not open on Sundays.

Pergunta:

Is the library open every day?

Resposta:

No.

Se você apenas identificar:

library

open

pode errar se ignorar:

not.

Condições

Texto:

Students can enter free if they show a valid student ID.

Pergunta:

Can all students enter free automatically?

Não necessariamente.

Existe uma condição:

show a valid student ID.

Scanning encontra:

free

mas leitura cuidadosa identifica a condição.

Skimming em narrativas

Também podemos usar skimming em histórias.

Texto:

Last weekend, Julia traveled to another city for a music festival. She went with two friends, stayed in a small hotel and attended several concerts. Although the weather was rainy, they enjoyed the trip.

Ideia geral:

Julia’s trip to a music festival.

Não:

the weather was rainy.

Scanning em narrativas

Pergunta:

Who traveled with Julia?

Procure:

with.

Resposta:

two friends.

Pergunta:

What was the weather like?

Procure:

weather.

Resposta:

rainy.

Skimming em e-mails

Leia:

Hi Tom,
Thanks for your message. I’m writing because our plans for Saturday have changed. The museum is closed, so let’s meet at the café near the station instead. How about 3 p.m.?
See you,
Anna

Skimming:

change of Saturday plans.

Scanning:

Where will they meet?

café near the station.

What time?

3 p.m.

Skimming em anúncios

Anúncio:

SUMMER ENGLISH COURSE
Four-week intensive course
Classes Monday to Friday
Morning sessions
Course materials included
Registration closes June 20

Tópico:

summer English course.

Detalhes:

four weeks;

Monday to Friday;

morning;

June 20.

Texto informativo mais longo

Leia:

Cycling is becoming more popular in many cities. It is inexpensive, does not produce pollution and can help people stay active. Some cities are building more cycle paths to make cycling safer. However, cyclists still need to follow traffic rules and use appropriate safety equipment.

Skimming:

benefits and safety of cycling in cities.

Scanning:

Pergunta:

What are cities building?

Resposta:

cycle paths.

Previewing

Antes de skimming, faça uma inspeção visual.

Observe:

title

pictures, if available

headings

bold words

bullet points

text length.

Isso é frequentemente chamado de:

previewing.

No Reading de prova, essa inspeção pode economizar tempo.

Predicting

Com base no título, você pode prever o vocabulário.

Título:

Problems at the Airport

Você pode esperar:

flight

delay

luggage

gate

passport.

Isso facilita o reconhecimento durante a leitura.

Pergunta antes ou texto antes?

Depende da prova.

Para textos curtos, você pode:

ler as perguntas primeiro.

Isso define o alvo de scanning.

Para um texto maior, pode ser útil fazer:

título + skimming rápido

antes.

Não existe uma única sequência obrigatória para todos os exames.

Não faça leitura palavra por palavra sempre

Imagine um texto de 500 palavras com pergunta:

What time does the event begin?

Ler todas as 500 palavras lentamente é ineficiente.

Use scanning para localizar:

event

begins

time.

Quando leitura detalhada é necessária

Skimming e scanning não substituem completamente:

careful reading.

Se a pergunta exige:

  • inferência;
  • causa e efeito;
  • comparação;
  • significado contextual;

talvez você precise ler um trecho com mais atenção.

A estratégia correta é:

localizar rapidamente → ler profundamente apenas a área relevante.

Scanning e paráfrase

Pergunta:

Why was the event postponed?

Texto:

Because of heavy rain, the organizers moved the event to the following week.

A palavra:

postponed

não aparece.

Mas:

moved the event to the following week

é a informação equivalente.

Skimming e tópico

Cuidado com alternativas estreitas.

Texto fala sobre:

  • transporte;
  • hospedagem;
  • atividades;
  • comida

durante uma viagem.

Tópico provavelmente:

a holiday/trip.

Não:

restaurant food.

Alternativa ampla demais

Se o texto fala exclusivamente sobre:

problems with online classes

uma alternativa:

technology in modern life

pode ser ampla demais.

Procure a opção com melhor correspondência ao foco real.

Técnica do primeiro e último parágrafo

Em textos informativos maiores:

  • primeiro parágrafo frequentemente apresenta o tema;
  • último pode resumir ou concluir.

Isso pode ajudar no skimming.

Mas não é uma regra absoluta.

Tópicos de parágrafo

Você também pode fazer skimming por parágrafo.

Pergunte:

What is paragraph 1 about?

What is paragraph 2 about?

Isso cria um mapa do texto.

Exemplo:

Paragraph 1 → problem

Paragraph 2 → causes

Paragraph 3 → solutions.

Depois, quando uma questão perguntar sobre solução, você sabe onde procurar.

Marcadores visuais

Em textos reais, informações podem aparecer em:

tables

lists

schedules

menus

forms.

Scanning é especialmente útil nesses formatos.

Tabela

Course Day Time Price
English Monday 18:00 $40
Spanish Wednesday 19:00 $35
French Friday 17:30 $45

Pergunta:

Which course is the cheapest?

Scanning nos preços:

$40

$35

$45.

Resposta:

Spanish.

Scanning vertical

Em tabelas, leia a coluna relevante.

Se pergunta preço:

price column.

Se pergunta dia:

day column.

Não leia necessariamente todas as células.

Cronogramas

Exemplo:

09:00 Registration
09:30 Welcome talk
10:00 Workshop 1
12:00 Lunch
13:30 Workshop 2

Pergunta:

What happens after the welcome talk?

Resposta:

Workshop 1.

Aqui scanning e sequência trabalham juntos.

Dicionário não deve substituir estratégia

Mesmo com dicionário permitido, procurar cada palavra:

  • consome tempo;
  • quebra a compreensão;
  • aumenta dependência.

Primeiro tente:

skimming

scanning

inferência contextual.

Velocidade não significa pressa

O objetivo é:

leitura seletiva.

Você lê rapidamente onde basta e devagar onde é necessário.

Erros frequentes

Erro 1: ler tudo lentamente antes de olhar a pergunta

Nem sempre é necessário.

Erro 2: confundir skimming com adivinhação

Você deve usar evidências do texto.

Erro 3: procurar apenas palavras idênticas

Espere paráfrases.

Erro 4: parar em palavra desconhecida

Talvez ela seja irrelevante para a questão.

Erro 5: encontrar um número e marcar imediatamente

Verifique a que esse número se refere.

Exemplo completo

Texto:

COMMUNITY SPORTS DAY
Saturday, August 12
Riverside Park
Activities begin at 9:30 a.m.
Registration from 8:45 a.m.
Football, tennis, running and cycling events
Entry is free, but participants must register before August 10.

Skimming:

community sports event.

Scanning:

Date? → August 12.

Place? → Riverside Park.

Activities start? → 9:30.

Registration on event day? → 8:45.

Cost? → free.

Important condition? → register before August 10.

Vocabulário-chave

skimming — leitura rápida para captar ideia geral

scanning — busca rápida por informação específica

main idea — ideia principal

topic — tópico

purpose — propósito

detail — detalhe

keyword — palavra-chave

heading — subtítulo/cabeçalho

title — título

paragraph — parágrafo

preview — examinar previamente

predict — prever

specific information — informação específica

careful reading — leitura cuidadosa

locate — localizar

search — procurar

relevant — relevante

irrelevant — irrelevante

schedule — programação/cronograma

table — tabela

Estratégia de prova

Quando a pergunta pedir:

main idea

topic

purpose

use:

SKIMMING

Observe:

título;

início;

palavras repetidas;

organização;

conclusão.

Quando a pergunta pedir:

time

date

price

name

place

number

use:

SCANNING

Identifique primeiro o alvo e depois procure-o visualmente.

Após localizar a informação:

leia a frase ou linha completa.

Isso evita cair em:

negativas;

mudanças;

condições;

distratores.

Prática

Texto 1

PARKSIDE CAFÉ
Open Monday to Saturday
7:30 a.m.–6:00 p.m.
Breakfast served until 11 a.m.
Free Wi-Fi for customers
Closed on Sundays

1. Usando skimming, qual é o tópico principal?

  1. Uma escola
  2. Informações sobre um café

1. B — Informações sobre um café
