O objetivo deste simulado não é apenas obter uma pontuação. Ele deve mostrar quais estruturas já estão automatizadas e quais ainda exigem prática, para que a transição do A2 para o B1 seja feita sobre uma base sólida.

Aula 68 — Present Perfect

Objetivos

Ao final desta aula, você deverá ser capaz de:

  • compreender a formação do Present Perfect;
  • reconhecer o uso de have e has como auxiliares;
  • utilizar o particípio passado dos verbos;
  • distinguir verbos regulares e irregulares no Present Perfect;
  • falar sobre experiências de vida sem indicar um momento passado específico;
  • usar o Present Perfect para situações iniciadas no passado que continuam no presente;
  • utilizar ever, never, already, yet, just, for e since;
  • formular frases afirmativas, negativas e interrogativas;
  • diferenciar usos básicos de Present Perfect e Simple Past;
  • reconhecer marcadores temporais incompatíveis com o Present Perfect em seu uso básico;
  • compreender perguntas e respostas frequentes em provas de proficiência;
  • aplicar o tempo verbal em Reading, Listening, Writing e Speaking.

Desenvolvimento

O Present Perfect é formado por:

have / has + past participle

Exemplos:

I have visited London.

She has finished her homework.

They have seen this film.

Esse tempo verbal cria uma ligação entre:

past

e:

present.

Por isso, ele não deve ser entendido simplesmente como “mais um passado”.

O Present Perfect pode falar de algo que aconteceu antes de agora, mas que ainda possui alguma relação com o presente.

Formação básica

Com:

I

you

we

they

usamos:

have.

Exemplos:

I have finished.

You have studied.

We have arrived.

They have traveled.

Com:

he

she

it

usamos:

has.

Exemplos:

He has finished.

She has studied.

It has stopped.

Contrações

Na fala e em textos informais:

I have → I’ve

you have → you’ve

we have → we’ve

they have → they’ve

he has → he’s

she has → she’s

it has → it’s.

Exemplos:

I’ve finished my work.

She’s already left.

Atenção:

she’s

pode significar:

she is

ou:

she has.

O contexto mostra qual é o caso.

Compare:

She’s tired.

Aqui:

she is.

She’s finished the report.

Aqui:

she has.

O que é past participle?

O terceiro elemento do Present Perfect é:

past participle.

Em verbos regulares, normalmente o particípio é igual ao Simple Past.

Exemplos:

work → worked → worked

visit → visited → visited

study → studied → studied

finish → finished → finished.

Portanto:

I have worked.

She has visited Rome.

We have studied this topic.

Verbos irregulares

Nos verbos irregulares, precisamos aprender a terceira forma.

Alguns exemplos importantes:

Base form Simple Past Past Participle
be was/were been
go went gone
see saw seen
do did done
eat ate eaten
write wrote written
take took taken
give gave given
speak spoke spoken
know knew known
come came come
become became become
buy bought bought
have had had
make made made
find found found
read read read
leave left left
meet met met
lose lost lost

Exemplos:

I have seen this film.

She has written three emails.

They have gone home.

We have eaten already.

Afirmativa

Estrutura:

subject + have/has + past participle.

Exemplos:

I have visited Portugal.

He has finished the course.

We have seen that movie.

Maria has bought a new laptop.

Negativa

Estrutura:

subject + have not / has not + past participle.

Contrações:

have not → haven’t

has not → hasn’t.

Exemplos:

I haven’t finished yet.

She hasn’t called me.

They haven’t arrived.

He hasn’t seen the message.

Perguntas

Estrutura:

Have/Has + subject + past participle?

Exemplos:

Have you finished?

Has she arrived?

Have they seen the film?

Has he completed the assignment?

Respostas curtas

Have you finished?

Yes, I have.

No, I haven’t.

Has she called?

Yes, she has.

No, she hasn’t.

Não responda:

Yes, I did.

quando a pergunta usa:

Have you…?

O auxiliar deve ser mantido.

Uso 1 — experiências de vida

Um dos usos mais importantes do Present Perfect é falar sobre experiências em algum momento da vida, sem dizer exatamente quando.

Exemplo:

I have visited Argentina.

Significa:

em algum momento da minha vida, visitei a Argentina.

O momento específico não foi informado.

Outro:

She has seen snow.

They have traveled abroad.

He has tried Japanese food.

Sem tempo passado específico

Com experiências, normalmente não usamos:

yesterday

last year

in 2024

se quisermos manter o Present Perfect.

Compare:

I have visited London.

Experiência geral.

I visited London in 2025.

Momento específico.

Essa segunda frase usa:

Simple Past.

Ever

ever

significa:

alguma vez.

Muito comum em perguntas sobre experiências.

Estrutura:

Have you ever + past participle…?

Exemplos:

Have you ever visited another country?

Have you ever eaten sushi?

Have you ever traveled by plane?

Has she ever studied French?

Resposta:

Yes, I have.

Depois você pode acrescentar:

I visited Chile two years ago.

Observe a mudança:

Have you ever…? → Present Perfect.

Depois:

two years ago → Simple Past.

Never

never

significa:

nunca.

Exemplos:

I have never been to Canada.

She has never traveled by plane.

We have never tried that restaurant.

Como:

never

já é negativo em sentido, não use:

haven’t never.

Errado:

I haven’t never seen it.

Correto:

I have never seen it.

Ou:

I haven’t ever seen it.

Mas:

have never

é muito comum.

Been x gone

Compare:

She has gone to the supermarket.

Isso normalmente significa:

ela foi ao supermercado e ainda está lá ou está a caminho.

Agora:

She has been to the supermarket.

Pode indicar:

ela foi e voltou.

Em experiências:

I have been to France.

Significa:

eu já estive na França.

Não:

I have gone to France

se você está falando de uma experiência passada e já retornou.

Have been to

Muito comum para viagens e lugares.

Have you ever been to London?

I’ve been to São Paulo several times.

She’s never been abroad.

Uso 2 — passado com resultado no presente

O Present Perfect também pode falar de uma ação passada cujo resultado é importante agora.

Exemplo:

I’ve lost my keys.

Resultado presente:

não tenho minhas chaves agora.

Compare:

I lost my keys yesterday, but I found them later.

Aqui o evento está totalmente localizado e concluído no passado.

Outro:

She has broken her phone.

O telefone está quebrado agora.

The bus has arrived.

O ônibus chegou e essa informação é relevante agora.

Just

just

indica algo que aconteceu há pouco tempo.

Estrutura frequente:

have/has + just + past participle.

Exemplos:

I’ve just finished my homework.

She has just arrived.

They have just left.

The train has just arrived.

Already

already

significa:

já.

É frequente em frases afirmativas.

Estrutura:

have/has + already + past participle.

Exemplos:

I’ve already eaten.

She has already finished the assignment.

We have already booked the hotel.

Pode indicar que algo ocorreu antes do esperado ou simplesmente que já está concluído.

Yet

yet

é muito usado em:

questions

e:

negative sentences.

Geralmente aparece no final.

Pergunta:

Have you finished yet?

Negativa:

I haven’t finished yet.

Outro:

Has the bus arrived yet?

No, it hasn’t arrived yet.

Already x yet

Compare:

I’ve already finished.

Afirmativa.

Have you finished yet?

Pergunta.

I haven’t finished yet.

Negativa.

Just x already x yet

She has just arrived.

há pouco.

She has already arrived.

já chegou.

Has she arrived yet?

já chegou?

She hasn’t arrived yet.

ainda não chegou.

Uso 3 — situações que começaram no passado e continuam

O Present Perfect também é usado para falar de situações que começaram no passado e continuam no presente.

Exemplo:

I have lived here for five years.

A ideia é:

comecei a morar aqui há cinco anos e continuo morando aqui.

Outro:

She has worked at the school since 2023.

Ela começou em 2023 e ainda trabalha lá.

For

for

indica duração.

Exemplos:

for two hours

for three days

for a week

for six months

for ten years.

Frase:

I have studied English for three years.

Since

since

indica o ponto inicial.

Exemplos:

since Monday

since 2024

since January

since I started university.

Frase:

I have studied English since 2024.

For x since

Compare:

for three years

duração.

since 2023

ponto inicial.

Pergunte:

How long?

Resposta:

for three years.

Pergunte:

Since when?

Resposta:

since 2023.

How long…?

Perguntas comuns:

How long have you lived here?

How long has she worked there?

How long have they known each other?

Respostas:

For five years.

Since 2021.

Verbos de estado

O Present Perfect aparece frequentemente com verbos como:

know

live

work

have

quando uma situação continua.

Exemplos:

I’ve known Anna for ten years.

We’ve lived here since 2022.

He has had this laptop for two years.

Present Perfect x Simple Past

Essa distinção é central.

Present Perfect

Use quando:

  • o tempo exato não é importante ou não é mencionado;
  • fala de experiência;
  • há ligação com o presente;
  • a situação continua;
  • usamos just/already/yet;
  • usamos for/since em situações continuadas.

Exemplo:

I have seen this film.

Simple Past

Use quando:

  • a ação aconteceu em um momento passado específico;
  • o período está terminado.

Exemplo:

I saw this film last Saturday.

Marcadores de Simple Past

Palavras que normalmente pedem Simple Past:

yesterday

last night

last week

last year

two days ago

in 2022.

Exemplos:

I visited Rome last year.

Não, no uso básico:

I have visited Rome last year.

Compare

Have you ever visited Rome?

Experiência.

Yes. I visited Rome in 2024.

Momento específico.

Outro:

I’ve seen that film.

Experiência.

I saw it yesterday.

Tempo definido.

Today, this week e this year

Períodos ainda não concluídos podem aparecer com Present Perfect.

Exemplo:

I’ve had three classes today.

Se:

today

ainda não terminou.

Outro:

I’ve read two books this month.

Isso depende de o período ainda estar aberto.

No nível inicial de Present Perfect, concentre-se primeiro em:

experiência;

just/already/yet;

for/since.

Frequência sem momento específico

Podemos usar:

once

twice

three times

many times

several times.

Exemplos:

I’ve visited that museum twice.

She’s watched the film three times.

We’ve been there several times.

The first time

Uma estrutura útil:

This is the first time I have…

Exemplo:

This is the first time I have traveled alone.

É uma estrutura mais avançada dentro deste tópico, mas útil para reconhecimento.

Present Perfect em viagens

Exemplos:

Have you ever traveled abroad?

I’ve never been to Europe.

We’ve already booked our tickets.

The flight hasn’t left yet.

Present Perfect em educação

I’ve finished my assignment.

She hasn’t submitted her project yet.

Have you ever taken an online course?

I’ve studied English for four years.

Present Perfect em tecnologia

I’ve forgotten my password.

She has just updated the app.

Have you downloaded the file yet?

The computer has stopped working.

Present Perfect em saúde

I’ve had a headache since this morning.

She has felt tired for two days.

Have you taken your medicine yet?

Em situações reais, o conteúdo linguístico não substitui orientação médica; aqui o foco é apenas a estrutura da língua.

Present Perfect em Speaking

Pergunta:

Have you ever traveled by plane?

Resposta simples:

Yes, I have.

Melhor:

Yes, I have. I traveled by plane for the first time three years ago.

Primeira frase:

Present Perfect

para experiência.

Segunda:

Simple Past

porque informa:

three years ago.

Speaking: never

Have you ever tried Indian food?

No, I’ve never tried it.

Outra:

No, I haven’t, but I’d like to.

Follow-up question

Pergunta:

Have you ever visited another country?

Yes, I have.

Seguimento:

Where did you go?

Observe:

Have you ever…? → Present Perfect.

Where did you go? → Simple Past.

Isso é extremamente frequente em tarefas de Speaking.

Present Perfect em Writing

Em um e-mail:

I’ve just arrived at the hotel. The journey was long, but everything went well.

Primeiro:

have just arrived

resultado recente.

Depois:

was / went

para contar a viagem.

Outro:

I’ve already visited the museum, but I haven’t seen the old town yet.

Present Perfect em Reading

Texto:

Emma has worked at Green School for six years. She started there in 2020.

Primeira frase:

Present Perfect

porque a situação continua.

Segunda:

Simple Past

porque informa o momento inicial específico.

Perguntas de interpretação

Texto:

Daniel has lived in London since 2023.

Podemos concluir:

he moved there in 2023 and still lives there.

No contexto básico do Present Perfect contínuo em sentido temporal, essa é a leitura esperada.

Been x lived

I’ve been in London for three days.

Pode indicar que estou em Londres há três dias.

I’ve lived in London for three years.

Indica residência.

Erro: auxiliar errado

Errado:

She have finished.

Correto:

She has finished.

Erro: particípio errado

Errado:

I have went.

Correto:

I have gone.

Errado:

She has saw.

Correto:

She has seen.

Erro: Simple Past depois de have

Errado:

We have ate.

Correto:

We have eaten.

Erro: usar did com Present Perfect

Errado:

Did you ever been to London?

No modelo básico de experiência:

Have you ever been to London?

Erro: tempo específico

Evite:

I have seen him yesterday.

Use:

I saw him yesterday.

Erro com for e since

Errado:

I’ve lived here since five years.

Correto:

I’ve lived here for five years.

Errado:

I’ve lived here for 2022.

Correto:

I’ve lived here since 2022.

Erro com yet

Mais natural:

I haven’t finished yet.

Não:

I yet haven’t finished.

Erro com already

Forma comum:

I’ve already finished.

Não:

I already have finish.

Erro com never

Errado:

I haven’t never traveled abroad.

Correto:

I’ve never traveled abroad.

Linha temporal

Imagine:

2022 ───────────── NOW

Frase:

I have lived here since 2022.

A situação começa em 2022 e continua até agora.

Agora:

I lived there from 2022 to 2024.

Esse período terminou.

Por isso:

Simple Past.

Comparação final

Situação Exemplo
experiência I’ve visited Chile.
momento específico I visited Chile in 2024.
ação recém-concluída I’ve just finished.
já aconteceu I’ve already finished.
ainda não aconteceu I haven’t finished yet.
duração I’ve lived here for five years.
ponto inicial I’ve lived here since 2021.

Vocabulário-chave

Present Perfect — tempo verbal que relaciona passado e presente

past participle — particípio passado

experience — experiência

ever — alguma vez

never — nunca

already — já

yet — já/ainda, conforme o contexto

just — há pouco/acabar de

for — por/durante, indicando duração

since — desde, indicando ponto inicial

been — particípio de be

gone — particípio de go

seen — particípio de see

done — particípio de do

written — particípio de write

known — particípio de know

finished — terminado/concluído

recently — recentemente

experience — experiência

result — resultado

duration — duração

Estratégia de prova

Ao encontrar uma questão com Present Perfect, procure primeiro os marcadores.

Se houver:

ever

never

pense em:

experiência.

Se houver:

just

already

yet

pense em:

ação recente ou estado atual.

Se houver:

for

since

pergunte:

a situação continua até agora?

Se houver:

yesterday

last year

two days ago

prefira:

Simple Past.

Outra estratégia:

identifique se a questão pede:

Have/Has + past participle

e não deixe um verbo no Simple Past depois do auxiliar.

Exemplo:

has ___

Se as opções são:

  1. went
  2. gone
  3. go
  4. going

Resposta:

gone.

sem mencionar quando.

1. B — have

Com:

I

Ou:

Tarefa de consolidação

Crie uma tabela pessoal de verbos irregulares com pelo menos 30 itens:

Base form Simple Past Past Participle
go went gone
see saw seen
write wrote written
eat ate eaten
take took taken

Depois faça três grupos de frases.

Experiences

Escreva dez perguntas com:

Have you ever…?

Exemplos:

Have you ever traveled alone?

Have you ever eaten foreign food?

Responda usando:

Yes, I have.

ou:

No, I’ve never…

Recent actions

Escreva frases usando:

just

already

yet.

Por exemplo:

I’ve just arrived.

I’ve already finished.

I haven’t finished yet.

Duration

Escreva dez frases usando:

for

e:

since.

Exemplos:

I’ve studied English for two years.

I’ve lived here since 2024.

Depois transforme cinco experiências gerais em acontecimentos específicos.

Exemplo:

I’ve been to Rio de Janeiro.

Transforme:

I went to Rio de Janeiro in 2025.

Outro:

I’ve seen that film.

Transforme:

I saw that film last Friday.

Finalize memorizando o contraste central:

Present Perfect → experiência, resultado presente, período ainda conectado ao presente.

Simple Past → acontecimento localizado em um momento passado específico e concluído.

E revise as estruturas:

have/has + past participle

Have you ever…?

I have never…

I’ve just…

I’ve already…

I haven’t… yet.

for + duration

since + starting point

O Present Perfect é uma das estruturas mais importantes na transição do A2 para o B1 porque permite deixar de falar apenas sobre acontecimentos passados isolados e começar a relacionar experiências anteriores ao momento presente.

Aula 69 — Present Perfect vs. Simple Past

Objetivos

Ao final desta aula, você deverá ser capaz de:

  • diferenciar Present Perfect e Simple Past;
  • reconhecer quando o tempo passado está definido ou indefinido;
  • identificar situações em que o Present Perfect conecta passado e presente;
  • usar o Simple Past para eventos concluídos em um momento específico;
  • escolher corretamente entre have/has + past participle e o passado simples;
  • usar marcadores como ever, never, already, yet, just, for e since;
  • reconhecer marcadores típicos do Simple Past, como yesterday, last week, ago e datas específicas;
  • alternar corretamente entre Present Perfect e Simple Past em uma mesma conversa;
  • evitar combinações inadequadas, como Present Perfect com yesterday;
  • aplicar essa distinção em Reading, Listening, Writing e Speaking.

Desenvolvimento

O contraste entre Present Perfect e Simple Past é um dos pontos mais importantes na passagem do A2 para o B1.

Os dois tempos podem falar sobre acontecimentos anteriores ao momento presente.

A diferença principal está em como o falante organiza essa informação.

Compare:

I have visited London.

e:

I visited London in 2024.

As duas frases falam de uma visita a Londres.

Mas não comunicam exatamente a mesma coisa.

Na primeira:

I have visited London.

o foco é a experiência.

Não dizemos exatamente quando.

Na segunda:

I visited London in 2024.

o acontecimento está ligado a um momento passado específico.

Regra central

Uma distinção inicial muito útil é:

Present Perfect → passado conectado ao presente, sem tempo passado específico concluído.

Simple Past → acontecimento concluído em um tempo passado específico ou claramente terminado.

Essa regra não explica todos os usos possíveis do inglês, mas cobre grande parte do contraste necessário neste nível.

Revisão do Present Perfect

Estrutura:

have/has + past participle.

Exemplos:

I have finished.

She has arrived.

We have seen that film.

They have visited the museum.

Negativa:

I haven’t finished.

She hasn’t arrived.

Pergunta:

Have you finished?

Has she arrived?

Revisão do Simple Past

Afirmativa:

subject + past form.

Exemplos:

I finished yesterday.

She arrived at eight.

We saw that film last week.

Negativa:

didn’t + base verb.

I didn’t finish yesterday.

Pergunta:

Did + subject + base verb?

Did she arrive on time?

Experiência geral x momento específico

Compare:

Have you ever been to Italy?

A pergunta significa:

em algum momento da sua vida?

Não perguntamos quando.

Resposta:

Yes, I have.

Depois, podemos perguntar:

When did you go?

Agora precisamos de Simple Past porque estamos pedindo:

um momento específico.

Resposta:

I went there in 2025.

Portanto:

Have you ever been to Italy?

Yes, I have.

When did you go?

I went there in 2025.

Esse padrão é extremamente comum.

Present Perfect primeiro, Simple Past depois

Observe:

A: Have you ever visited a science museum?
B: Yes, I have.
A: Which museum did you visit?
B: I visited the National Science Museum last year.

Primeiro:

experiência geral → Present Perfect.

Depois:

detalhes de um evento concluído → Simple Past.

Tempo passado específico

Use Simple Past com expressões como:

yesterday

last night

last week

last month

last year

two hours ago

three days ago

in 2023

on Monday

when I was a child.

Exemplos:

I saw Maria yesterday.

We traveled last month.

He finished the course in 2025.

She called me two hours ago.

Evite Present Perfect com tempo passado concluído

Inadequado no uso padrão básico:

I have seen Maria yesterday.

Correto:

I saw Maria yesterday.

Inadequado:

We have visited the museum last Saturday.

Correto:

We visited the museum last Saturday.

Tempo não especificado

Present Perfect:

I have read this book.

Não sabemos exatamente quando.

She has visited Portugal.

Não sabemos quando.

We have tried that restaurant.

O foco está na experiência ou no resultado atual.

Ever

Have you ever seen snow?

Aqui não há momento específico.

Por isso:

Present Perfect.

Se a resposta acrescenta um momento:

Yes. I saw snow when I visited Argentina in 2024.

Passamos para:

Simple Past.

Never

I’ve never traveled by ship.

Experiência acumulada até o momento presente.

Compare:

I never traveled by ship when I lived there.

Aqui estamos falando de um período passado concluído:

when I lived there.

O Simple Past pode aparecer.

Just

I’ve just finished my assignment.

A ação aconteceu há pouco e é relevante agora.

Compare:

I finished my assignment ten minutes ago.

Como temos:

ten minutes ago

usamos Simple Past.

Already

I’ve already eaten.

A informação relevante é:

a refeição já aconteceu.

Sem momento passado específico.

Compare:

I ate at 12:30.

Agora o momento é especificado.

Yet

Have you finished yet?

I haven’t finished yet.

A ação é vista em relação ao presente.

Today

Algumas expressões exigem atenção.

Compare:

I’ve had two classes today.

Se:

today

ainda está em andamento.

Mas:

I had two classes yesterday.

Ontem terminou.

This week

Se a semana ainda está em andamento:

I’ve had three exams this week.

Se falamos de uma semana concluída:

I had three exams last week.

This year

I’ve read ten books this year.

O ano ainda está em andamento.

I read twelve books last year.

O ano passado terminou.

Período aberto x período fechado

Essa ideia ajuda bastante.

Período aberto

today

this week

this month

this year

quando ainda não terminaram.

Pode favorecer Present Perfect.

Período fechado

yesterday

last week

last month

last year.

Normalmente:

Simple Past.

Resultado presente

Compare:

I’ve lost my keys.

Isso geralmente significa:

não sei onde elas estão agora.

Resultado presente importante.

Agora:

I lost my keys yesterday, but I found them later.

O problema pertence ao passado e foi resolvido.

Outro exemplo

She has broken her phone.

O telefone está quebrado agora.

Compare:

She broke her phone last month, but she bought a new one.

O evento pertence a um período passado concluído.

Situação que continua x situação concluída

Present Perfect:

I have lived here for five years.

Significado:

ainda moro aqui.

Simple Past:

I lived there for five years.

Significado:

morei lá durante cinco anos, mas esse período terminou.

Essa diferença é muito importante.

Compare

She has worked at the hospital since 2022.

Ela ainda trabalha lá.

She worked at the hospital from 2022 to 2025.

O período terminou em 2025.

For com Present Perfect e Simple Past

Present Perfect

I’ve studied English for three years.

Se ainda estudo.

Simple Past

I studied French for three years when I was at school.

O período terminou.

Portanto, for não pertence exclusivamente ao Present Perfect.

O contexto é que determina.

Since

Quando uma situação começou no passado e continua:

I’ve lived here since 2021.

She has known him since university.

No uso básico, since aparece muito com Present Perfect.

How long…?

Pergunta sobre situação que continua:

How long have you worked here?

Resposta:

I’ve worked here for four years.

Mas se o trabalho terminou:

How long did you work there?

Resposta:

I worked there for four years.

Compare as perguntas

How long have you lived in Belton?

Implica normalmente:

ainda mora lá.

How long did you live in Belton?

Implica:

não mora mais lá ou fala de um período encerrado.

Been x went

I’ve been to Japan.

Significa:

já estive no Japão e voltei.

I went to Japan last year.

Fala de uma viagem específica.

Compare:

Have you ever been to Japan?

Yes, I have. I went there in 2025.

Gone x went

Maria has gone to the bank.

Ela foi e ainda não voltou, em muitos contextos.

Maria went to the bank at 10.

Relatamos o evento passado.

Notícias recentes

Present Perfect pode aparecer para apresentar uma notícia recente:

The company has opened a new store.

Depois, os detalhes podem vir no Simple Past:

It opened yesterday morning.

Primeira frase:

notícia relevante agora.

Segunda:

momento específico.

Narrativas

Para contar uma sequência de eventos passados, o Simple Past é normalmente o principal tempo.

Exemplo:

Last Saturday, I went to the city center. I met a friend, had lunch and bought a new book.

Não usamos normalmente Present Perfect para cada passo de uma narrativa passada com tempo definido.

Relatos de experiência

Podemos começar com Present Perfect:

I’ve had some interesting travel experiences.

Depois contar uma:

Last year, I traveled to Chile with two friends. We stayed there for a week and visited several places.

Assim:

Present Perfect → experiência geral.

Simple Past → narrativa específica.

Present Perfect em perguntas de entrevista

Have you ever worked with children?

Have you ever used this software?

Have you ever studied another language?

Se a resposta for positiva, podem vir detalhes no passado:

Yes, I have. I worked at a school in 2024.

Reading

Texto:

Laura has traveled abroad several times. Last year, she went to Spain with her sister. They stayed in Madrid for five days and visited several museums.

Primeira frase:

experiência acumulada.

Depois:

experiência específica do ano passado.

Listening

Você pode ouvir:

I’ve been to that restaurant before.

E depois:

I went there last month.

A primeira fala:

experiência.

A segunda:

momento específico.

Marcadores do Present Perfect

Fique atento a:

ever

never

already

yet

just

recently

so far

for

since.

So far

so far

significa:

até agora.

Exemplo:

I’ve read five chapters so far.

O período ainda está em andamento.

Outro:

So far, we haven’t had any problems.

Recently

Pode aparecer com Present Perfect:

I’ve recently started a new course.

Também pode ocorrer com outros tempos dependendo do contexto, mas aqui o foco é reconhecer sua associação frequente com acontecimentos recentes.

Marcadores do Simple Past

yesterday

last…

…ago

in + ano passado específico

on + dia/data passada específica.

Exemplos:

last Friday

two weeks ago

in 2024

on July 10.

Cuidado com “when”

Perguntas com:

When…?

normalmente procuram um tempo passado específico.

Por isso, geralmente usamos Simple Past:

When did you arrive?

Não:

When have you arrived?

no uso básico estudado aqui.

Have you ever…? x When did…?

Memorize como par:

Have you ever visited New York?

When did you visit New York?

A primeira:

experiência.

A segunda:

data/momento.

Have you…? x Did you…?

Compare:

Have you finished your assignment?

Foco:

está concluído agora?

Did you finish your assignment yesterday?

Foco:

o que aconteceu ontem?

Have you eaten? x Did you eat?

Have you eaten?

Normalmente pergunta se a pessoa já comeu até agora.

Did you eat at the restaurant?

Pergunta sobre uma situação passada específica.

Erro frequente 1

I have gone there last year.

Correção:

I went there last year.

Erro frequente 2

Did you ever been to France?

Correção:

Have you ever been to France?

Erro frequente 3

I have seen him two days ago.

Correção:

I saw him two days ago.

Erro frequente 4

I lived here since 2022.

Se ainda mora:

I have lived here since 2022.

Se não mora mais, seria necessário reconstruir a frase com um período passado concluído.

Erro frequente 5

Have you finished yesterday?

Correção:

Did you finish yesterday?

Ou, sem momento específico:

Have you finished?

Erro frequente 6

She has worked there from 2020 to 2023.

Como o período explicitamente terminou em 2023:

She worked there from 2020 to 2023.

Linha temporal — Present Perfect

PAST ─────────────── NOW

I have lived here for five years.

A situação atravessa a linha até agora.

Linha temporal — Simple Past

PAST [event] ───────── NOW

I visited London in 2024.

O evento está localizado e concluído.

Teste mental rápido

Antes de escolher o tempo, pergunte:

Is the time specified and finished?

Se:

yes

pense em:

Simple Past.

Pergunte:

Is it an experience, recent result, or unfinished situation connected to now?

Se:

yes

pense em:

Present Perfect.

Comparação em tabela

Situação Present Perfect Simple Past
experiência sem quando I’ve visited Rome. —
evento em data específica — I visited Rome in 2024.
resultado atual I’ve lost my keys. —
evento passado resolvido — I lost my keys yesterday and found them later.
situação continua I’ve worked here for five years. —
situação terminou — I worked there for five years.
ever/never Have you ever…? —
yesterday/last/ago — I went yesterday.
just/already/yet I’ve just finished. —
sequência narrativa passada — We arrived, ate and left.

Vocabulário-chave

specific time — tempo específico

unspecified time — tempo não especificado

finished period — período concluído

unfinished period — período ainda em andamento

experience — experiência

present result — resultado presente

duration — duração

starting point — ponto inicial

ever — alguma vez

never — nunca

already — já

yet — já/ainda

just — há pouco

for — por/durante

since — desde

ago — atrás/há

so far — até agora

recently — recentemente

Estratégia de prova

Procure primeiro os marcadores temporais.

Se houver:

yesterday

last week

two years ago

in 2023

pense:

Simple Past.

Se houver:

ever

never

just

already

yet

so far

pense:

Present Perfect.

Se houver:

for

ou:

since

pergunte:

a situação continua?

Se continuar:

Present Perfect.

Se terminou:

Simple Past pode ser necessário.

Outra estratégia importante:

quando uma conversa começa com:

Have you ever…?

espere que uma pergunta de seguimento sobre detalhes use:

did.

Exemplo:

Have you ever traveled abroad?

Where did you go?

Prática

1. Complete:

I ___ this film three times.

  1. saw yesterday
  2. have seen
  3. have saw
  4. did seen

2. Complete:

I ___ this film last night.

  1. have seen
  2. saw
  3. have saw
  4. seen

3. Complete:

  1. has gone
  2. went
  3. has been
  4. go

4. Complete:

She ___ to Portugal several times.

  1. went yesterday
  2. has been
  3. did been
  4. was been

5. Complete:

Have you ever ___ sushi?

  1. ate
  2. eaten
  3. eat
  4. eating

6. Complete:

Yes. I ___ sushi for the first time last year.

  1. have eaten
  2. ate
  3. have ate
  4. eaten

7. Complete:

I ___ my keys. I can’t find them.

  1. lost yesterday and found
  2. have lost
  3. did lose last year
  4. have lose

8. Complete:

I ___ my keys yesterday, but I found them later.

  1. have lost
  2. lost
  3. have lose
  4. has lost

9. Complete:

  1. lived and left
  2. have lived
  3. did live yesterday
  4. have live

10. Complete:

We ___ there from 2018 to 2022.

  1. have lived
  2. lived
  3. have live
  4. living

11. Complete:

She ___ at this school for six years, and she still works here.

  1. worked
  2. has worked
  3. did worked
  4. has work

12. Complete:

She ___ at that school for six years before moving to another city.

  1. has worked
  2. worked
  3. has work
  4. works

13. Escolha:

I ___ three cups of coffee today.

  1. have had
  2. had last year
  3. have have
  4. did had

Considere que o dia ainda não terminou.

14. Escolha:

I ___ three cups of coffee yesterday.

  1. have had
  2. had
  3. have drink
  4. have had yesterday

15. Complete:

Have you finished the report ___?

  1. yesterday
  2. yet
  3. ago
  4. last

16. Complete:

I ___ the report two hours ago.

  1. have finished
  2. finished
  3. have finish
  4. has finished

17. Complete:

I’ve ___ finished the report.

  1. yesterday
  2. just
  3. ago
  4. last Friday

18. Escolha a frase correta:

  1. I have visited Paris last year.
  2. I visited Paris last year.
  3. I have visit Paris last year.
  4. I did visited Paris last year.

19. Escolha a frase correta:

  1. Have you ever been to Paris?
  2. Did you ever been to Paris?
  3. Have you ever went to Paris?
  4. Has you ever been to Paris?

20. Complete o diálogo:

A: Have you ever been to Mexico?
B: Yes, I .
A: When you go?
B: I ___ there in 2024.

21. Escolha:

How long ___ you lived here?

  1. did
  2. have
  3. has
  4. are

Considere que a pessoa ainda mora no local.

22. Escolha:

How long ___ you live there?

  1. have
  2. did
  3. has
  4. have did

Considere que a pessoa não mora mais lá.

23. Corrija:

I’ve seen her yesterday.

24. Corrija:

Did you ever been to London?

25. Corrija:

I have lived there from 2020 to 2023.

Considere que a pessoa saiu de lá em 2023.

26. Corrija:

27. Escolha o tempo correto e explique brevemente:

I ______ English for four years.

Considere:

  1. ainda estudo inglês;

  2. parei de estudar no ano passado.

28. Complete o texto:

Emma ___ (travel) abroad several times. Last year, she ___ (go) to Spain. She ___ (stay) there for ten days and ___ (visit) Madrid and Barcelona. She ___ never ___ (be) to Portugal, but she would like to go.

29. Complete:

30. Produção

Escreva um pequeno diálogo de 8 a 10 falas contendo:

  • uma pergunta com Have you ever…?;
  • uma resposta com Present Perfect;
  • uma pergunta de seguimento com When did…? ou Where did…?;
  • duas respostas em Simple Past;
  • uma frase com never;
  • uma frase com already ou yet.

Gabarito comentado

1. B — have seen

three times

sem momento específico indica experiência acumulada.

2. B — saw

last night

é um período passado concluído.

3. B — went

in 2025

define o momento passado.

4. B — has been

several times

sem especificar quando.

5. B — eaten

Present Perfect exige particípio:

eat → ate → eaten.

6. B — ate

last year

pede Simple Past.

7. B — have lost

O resultado é importante agora:

I can’t find them.

8. B — lost

yesterday

indica momento passado específico.

Além disso, o problema já foi resolvido:

I found them later.

9. B — have lived

since 2022

e a situação continua.

10. B — lived

from 2018 to 2022

é um período encerrado.

11. B — has worked

A frase informa:

she still works here.

Portanto, há continuidade até o presente.

12. B — worked

O trabalho naquele local terminou.

13. A — have had

O período:

today

ainda está aberto no contexto proposto.

14. B — had

yesterday

é período fechado.

15. B — yet

Have you finished the report yet?

16. B — finished

two hours ago

pede Simple Past.

17. B — just

I’ve just finished the report.

18. B

I visited Paris last year.

19. A

Have you ever been to Paris?

Experiência geral.

20.

A: Have you ever been to Mexico?
B: Yes, I have.
A: When did you go?
B: I went there in 2024.

A primeira pergunta trata de experiência.

Depois, o diálogo muda para um evento específico.

21. B — have

How long have you lived here?

A situação continua.

22. B — did

How long did you live there?

O período já terminou.

23.

I saw her yesterday.

Yesterday exige Simple Past no uso estudado.

24.

Have you ever been to London?

Use:

have + past participle.

25.

I lived there from 2020 to 2023.

O intervalo está completamente encerrado.

26.

She finished the course last month.

Last month indica período passado terminado.

27.

  1. Ainda estuda:

I have studied English for four years.

A situação começou no passado e continua.

  1. Parou no ano passado:

I studied English for four years.

A duração pertence a uma situação concluída.

28.

Emma has traveled abroad several times. Last year, she went to Spain. She stayed there for ten days and visited Madrid and Barcelona. She has never been to Portugal, but she would like to go.

Justificativa:

several times → experiência acumulada;

last year → Simple Past;

stayed/visited → narrativa daquela viagem específica;

never been → experiência de vida até agora.

29.

Daniel has worked at this company since 2023. Before that, he worked at a small shop for two years. He started his current job in March 2023.

has worked → ainda trabalha;

worked → emprego anterior concluído;

started → momento específico do início.

30.

Modelo:

A: Have you ever traveled abroad?
B: Yes, I have. I’ve visited Argentina and Chile.
A: When did you go to Chile?
B: I went there two years ago.
A: Who did you travel with?
B: I traveled with two friends.
A: Have you ever been to Peru?
B: No, I’ve never been there.
A: Have you already planned your next trip?
B: No, I haven’t planned it yet.

Tarefa de consolidação

Divida uma folha em duas colunas.

Na primeira:

Present Perfect

Na segunda:

Simple Past

Coloque os seguintes marcadores:

Present Perfect

ever

never

already

yet

just

so far

for

since.

Simple Past

yesterday

last week

last year

two days ago

in 2024

on Monday.

Depois crie dez pares contrastivos.

Exemplo:

I’ve visited London.

I visited London in 2025.

Outro:

I’ve seen that film three times.

I saw that film last Saturday.

Outro:

I’ve worked here for five years.

I worked there for five years.

Para cada par, explique em uma frase:

por que o Present Perfect está conectado ao presente;

ou:

por que o Simple Past representa um evento/período concluído.

Em seguida, crie cinco mini diálogos no formato:

Have you ever…?

Yes, I have.

When did…?

I … last…

Por fim, revise estes contrastes essenciais:

I’ve been there. → experiência

I went there last year. → evento específico

I’ve lost my keys. → problema relevante agora

I lost my keys yesterday, but I found them. → evento concluído

I’ve lived here for five years. → ainda moro aqui

I lived there for five years. → não moro mais lá

Have you ever…? → experiência

When did…? → momento específico

Use como pergunta final antes de escolher o tempo verbal:

Estou falando da experiência/conexão com o presente ou estou contando quando algo aconteceu?

Essa distinção resolve grande parte dos casos básicos de Present Perfect vs. Simple Past.

Aula 70 — Present Perfect Continuous

Objetivos

Ao final desta aula, você deverá ser capaz de:

  • compreender a formação do Present Perfect Continuous;
  • reconhecer a estrutura have/has been + verb-ing;
  • usar esse tempo para ações iniciadas no passado e ainda em andamento;
  • usar o Present Perfect Continuous para atividades recentes com resultado perceptível no presente;
  • empregar corretamente for e since;
  • formular frases afirmativas, negativas e interrogativas;
  • responder perguntas com How long…?;
  • diferenciar Present Perfect Continuous, Present Perfect Simple e Simple Past em situações básicas;
  • reconhecer verbos que normalmente não aparecem na forma contínua;
  • compreender o uso do tempo verbal em Reading, Listening, Writing e Speaking;
  • evitar erros frequentes de formação e escolha verbal.

Desenvolvimento

O Present Perfect Continuous é usado para conectar:

past

com:

present

dando ênfase principalmente à:

duração;

continuidade;

atividade.

A estrutura básica é:

have/has + been + verb-ing.

Exemplos:

I have been studying English.

She has been working all morning.

They have been waiting for an hour.

Observe os três elementos:

have/has

been

verb-ing.

Formação

Com:

I

you

we

they

usamos:

have been.

Exemplos:

I have been reading.

You have been studying.

We have been working.

They have been waiting.

Com:

he

she

it

usamos:

has been.

Exemplos:

He has been sleeping.

She has been studying.

It has been raining.

Contrações

I have → I’ve

you have → you’ve

we have → we’ve

they have → they’ve

he has → he’s

she has → she’s

Exemplos:

I’ve been studying all afternoon.

She’s been working since eight.

They’ve been waiting for thirty minutes.

Afirmativa

Estrutura:

subject + have/has been + verb-ing.

Exemplos:

I have been studying for two hours.

She has been working since 9 a.m.

We have been practicing English all week.

It has been raining since this morning.

Negativa

Estrutura:

subject + have/has not been + verb-ing.

Contrações:

haven’t been

hasn’t been.

Exemplos:

I haven’t been sleeping well.

She hasn’t been studying recently.

They haven’t been using the computer.

It hasn’t been raining today.

Perguntas

Estrutura:

Have/Has + subject + been + verb-ing?

Exemplos:

Have you been studying?

Has she been working?

Have they been waiting long?

Has it been raining?

Respostas curtas

Have you been studying?

Yes, I have.

No, I haven’t.

Has she been working?

Yes, she has.

No, she hasn’t.

Na resposta curta, não precisamos repetir:

been studying.

Uso 1 — ação iniciada no passado e ainda em andamento

Esse é o uso central.

Exemplo:

I have been studying for two hours.

Significa:

comecei há duas horas e continuo estudando agora.

Linha temporal:

PAST ─────────────── NOW
studying → studying → studying

Outro:

She has been living here since 2024.

A ideia é:

começou em 2024 e continua.

Duração

O Present Perfect Continuous combina muito bem com:

for

e:

since.

For

for

indica duração.

Exemplos:

for ten minutes

for two hours

for three days

for six months

for several years.

Frases:

I’ve been studying for three hours.

They’ve been traveling for two weeks.

He has been working here for six months.

Since

since

indica o ponto inicial.

Exemplos:

since Monday

since 8 a.m.

since January

since 2025

since I arrived.

Frases:

I’ve been waiting since 7:30.

She has been working here since January.

It has been raining since this morning.

For x since

Compare:

I’ve been studying for three hours.

Duração:

three hours.

I’ve been studying since 2 p.m.

Ponto inicial:

2 p.m.

How long…?

Uma pergunta extremamente comum:

How long have you been studying English?

Resposta:

I’ve been studying English for three years.

Outra:

How long has she been waiting?

She’s been waiting for forty minutes.

Outro:

How long have they been living there?

They’ve been living there since 2022.

Uso 2 — atividade recente com resultado no presente

O Present Perfect Continuous também pode falar de uma atividade que aconteceu recentemente e deixou um resultado visível agora.

Exemplo:

You look tired. Have you been working?

A atividade:

working

explica o estado atual:

tired.

Outro:

The ground is wet. It has been raining.

Talvez a chuva tenha acabado há pouco.

Mas vemos o resultado:

ground is wet.

Outro:

Your hands are dirty. Have you been fixing the car?

A atividade recente explica:

dirty hands.

A ação pode ter acabado

Esse ponto é importante.

Na frase:

I’ve been running.

não é obrigatório que eu esteja correndo exatamente neste segundo.

Pode significar:

corri recentemente e há um resultado agora.

Talvez eu esteja:

tired

hot

out of breath.

Present Perfect Continuous e recently

Exemplo:

I’ve been feeling tired recently.

Outro:

She has been working a lot recently.

Outro:

We’ve been studying this topic recently.

All day / all morning / all week

Expressões comuns:

all day

all morning

all afternoon

all week.

Exemplos:

I’ve been working all day.

She has been studying all morning.

It has been raining all afternoon.

Present Perfect Continuous x Present Continuous

Compare:

I am studying now.

Present Continuous:

atividade acontecendo neste momento.

Agora:

I have been studying for two hours.

Present Perfect Continuous:

atividade começou no passado e continua até agora.

Present Continuous

I’m reading now.

Foco:

agora.

Present Perfect Continuous

I’ve been reading for an hour.

Foco:

duração até agora.

Present Perfect Continuous x Simple Past

Compare:

I studied for three hours yesterday.

A atividade terminou ontem.

I’ve been studying for three hours.

A atividade começou há três horas e continua agora, ou acabou há pouquíssimo tempo com relevância presente.

Período concluído

She worked all morning yesterday.

Simple Past.

yesterday

é período concluído.

Período ligado ao presente

She has been working all morning.

Se a manhã ainda está em andamento ou a atividade é recente e relevante.

Present Perfect Continuous x Present Perfect Simple

Esse contraste é muito importante.

Compare:

I have read three chapters.

Present Perfect Simple.

Foco:

resultado / quantidade concluída.

Agora:

I have been reading for two hours.

Present Perfect Continuous.

Foco:

atividade / duração.

Resultado x duração

I’ve written five emails.

Foco:

five emails.

Quantidade concluída.

I’ve been writing emails all morning.

Foco:

duração da atividade.

Outro exemplo

She has painted three rooms.

Resultado:

três quartos concluídos.

She has been painting the house all day.

Atividade:

pintar

e duração:

all day.

Quantidade normalmente favorece Present Perfect Simple

Exemplo:

I’ve read four books this month.

Quantidade:

four books.

I’ve answered twenty emails today.

Quantidade:

twenty emails.

O foco é no resultado.

Duração normalmente favorece Present Perfect Continuous

I’ve been reading for three hours.

I’ve been answering emails all morning.

O foco está na atividade.

Pergunta: How many…?

Frequentemente:

Present Perfect Simple.

How many books have you read this month?

Resposta:

I’ve read four.

Pergunta: How long…?

Frequentemente:

Present Perfect Continuous.

How long have you been reading?

Resposta:

For two hours.

Atividade concluída x incompleta

Compare:

I’ve cleaned the kitchen.

Isso sugere:

tarefa concluída.

Agora:

I’ve been cleaning the kitchen.

Pode sugerir:

atividade em andamento

ou:

atividade recente, talvez ainda não completamente terminada.

Exemplo importante

I’ve written the report.

Provavelmente:

report finished.

I’ve been writing the report.

Provavelmente:

trabalhei no relatório, talvez ainda não esteja pronto.

Verbos de estado

Nem todos os verbos costumam aparecer naturalmente em tempos contínuos.

Verbos como:

know

believe

understand

want

need

own

belong

normalmente preferem formas simples em seus sentidos mais comuns.

Por isso:

I’ve known her for ten years.

Não normalmente:

I’ve been knowing her for ten years.

Know

Correto:

I’ve known him since 2020.

Believe

Mais comum:

I’ve believed this for a long time.

Embora o contexto real possa permitir usos especiais, para este nível mantenha a forma simples.

Want

Mais comum:

I’ve wanted to visit Japan for years.

Não:

I’ve been wanting…

como regra inicial, embora essa forma exista em certos contextos reais.

Para a aprendizagem básica, priorize:

Present Perfect Simple com state verbs.

Have

O verbo:

have

precisa de atenção.

Quando significa posse:

I’ve had this laptop for three years.

Não normalmente:

I’ve been having this laptop…

Mas quando faz parte de uma atividade:

I’ve been having problems with my computer.

Aqui:

having problems

é possível porque não indica simplesmente posse.

Live e work

Alguns verbos aceitam tanto Present Perfect Simple quanto Continuous com pouca diferença em certos contextos.

I’ve lived here for five years.

I’ve been living here for five years.

Ambas podem indicar:

comecei há cinco anos e ainda moro aqui.

A forma contínua enfatiza mais:

duração/atividade em andamento.

Work

I’ve worked here since 2023.

I’ve been working here since 2023.

As duas podem ser corretas.

A segunda destaca mais:

continuidade.

Study

I’ve studied English for three years.

I’ve been studying English for three years.

Ambas podem ocorrer.

No contexto de aprendizado contínuo, a forma:

have been studying

destaca a atividade ao longo do tempo.

Wait

Com ações claramente contínuas:

I’ve been waiting for an hour.

É muito natural.

Rain

It has been raining all morning.

Muito comum.

Sleep

I’ve been sleeping badly recently.

Atividade repetida ou condição recente.

Work

She has been working too much lately.

Lately

lately

significa:

ultimamente.

É comum com Present Perfect e Present Perfect Continuous.

Exemplo:

I’ve been studying a lot lately.

Have you been sleeping well lately?

Recently x lately

Ambas podem indicar período recente.

I’ve been exercising recently.

I’ve been exercising a lot lately.

Questions about recent activity

Perguntas comuns:

What have you been doing?

Have you been studying?

Have you been working a lot?

Have you been sleeping well?

What have you been doing?

Pode significar:

O que você tem feito?

Exemplo:

A: What have you been doing lately?
B: I’ve been studying for my exams.

Present Perfect Continuous em educação

I’ve been studying for the exam all week.

She has been preparing her presentation since Monday.

We’ve been practicing English every day.

How long have you been taking this course?

Em tecnologia

I’ve been trying to connect to the Wi-Fi for twenty minutes.

The computer has been running slowly lately.

We’ve been using this software since January.

Em trabalho

I’ve been working on this project for three months.

She has been answering emails all morning.

They’ve been preparing the report since yesterday.

Em viagens

We’ve been traveling for three weeks.

They’ve been waiting at the airport for two hours.

How long have you been staying at this hotel?

Em saúde e bem-estar

No sentido puramente linguístico:

I’ve been feeling tired lately.

She has been coughing all morning.

Have you been sleeping well?

Essas construções descrevem duração ou repetição recente.

Present Perfect Continuous no Reading

Texto:

Anna has been studying for her final exam since Monday. She has already completed four practice tests, but she still wants to review two more chapters.

Observe:

has been studying → atividade/duração.

has completed → resultado/quantidade.

Esse contraste pode aparecer em questões.

Pergunta possível

What has Anna been doing since Monday?

Resposta:

Studying for her final exam.

Pergunta:

How many practice tests has she completed?

Resposta:

Four.

Present Perfect Continuous no Listening

Áudio:

I’ve been waiting for the bus for forty minutes, and it still hasn’t arrived.

Informações:

atividade → waiting

duração → forty minutes

resultado atual → bus still absent.

Present Perfect Continuous no Speaking

Pergunta:

What have you been doing lately?

Resposta:

I’ve been studying English and preparing for my exams.

Pergunta:

How long have you been learning English?

Resposta:

I’ve been learning English for two years.

Writing

Exemplo de e-mail:

Hi Emma,

I’ve been studying a lot recently because I have an important exam next week. I’ve already completed most of my revision, but I’ve been practicing Listening every evening because I still find it difficult.

Observe:

have been studying → atividade contínua.

have completed → resultado.

have been practicing → atividade repetida.

Simple x Continuous em um mesmo texto

I’ve been reading all morning, and I’ve finished two chapters.

Primeira parte:

duração.

Segunda:

resultado.

Outro:

She has been writing emails for two hours and has sent fifteen messages.

Atividade:

writing.

Resultado:

fifteen sent.

Estrutura negativa com duração

I haven’t been sleeping well for the last few days.

She hasn’t been attending classes regularly.

We haven’t been using that computer lately.

Pergunta negativa

Haven’t you been studying?

Existe, mas para este nível concentre-se primeiro em perguntas afirmativas comuns:

Have you been studying?

Ever e Present Perfect Continuous

Ever é muito mais característico do Present Perfect Simple para experiências:

Have you ever visited London?

Não normalmente:

Have you ever been visiting London?

Para experiência de vida concluída:

Present Perfect Simple.

Never

Da mesma forma:

I’ve never traveled abroad.

Não use o Continuous apenas porque a ação durou algum tempo.

Experiência completa:

Present Perfect Simple.

Already e yet

São mais comuns com o Present Perfect Simple quando o foco é conclusão:

I’ve already finished.

I haven’t finished yet.

Com Continuous, a lógica costuma ser duração/atividade:

I’ve been working on it for two hours.

Just

Para uma ação concluída recentemente:

I’ve just finished.

Para atividade recente que explica um resultado:

I’ve been running.

Não é necessário colocar:

just

em toda atividade recente.

Erro frequente 1 — esquecer been

Errado:

I have studying for two hours.

Correto:

I have been studying for two hours.

Erro frequente 2 — usar particípio em vez de -ing

Errado:

She has been worked all day.

Correto:

She has been working all day.

Erro frequente 3 — usar has com I

Errado:

I has been studying.

Correto:

I have been studying.

Erro frequente 4 — usar have com she

Errado:

She have been waiting.

Correto:

She has been waiting.

Erro frequente 5 — for x since

Errado:

I’ve been studying since three hours.

Correto:

I’ve been studying for three hours.

Errado:

I’ve been studying for Monday.

Correto:

I’ve been studying since Monday.

Erro frequente 6 — state verb

Evite:

I’ve been knowing him for years.

Use:

I’ve known him for years.

Erro frequente 7 — quantidade concluída

Se o foco é:

three books

prefira:

I’ve read three books.

Não necessariamente:

I’ve been reading three books.

Essa segunda frase pode ter outro sentido e não expressa claramente que os três foram concluídos.

Erro frequente 8 — tempo passado concluído

Errado:

I’ve been studying yesterday.

Se toda a atividade aconteceu ontem:

I studied yesterday.

Ou:

I was studying yesterday at 8 p.m.

dependendo do sentido.

Comparação resumida

Situação Tempo mais natural
ação em andamento desde o passado Present Perfect Continuous
duração da atividade Present Perfect Continuous
resultado visível de atividade recente Present Perfect Continuous
quantidade concluída Present Perfect Simple
experiência de vida Present Perfect Simple
state verb geralmente Present Perfect Simple
evento em tempo passado concluído Simple Past

Compare os três tempos

I studied English yesterday.

Simple Past:

atividade concluída ontem.

I have studied English for three years.

Present Perfect Simple:

período iniciado no passado e conectado ao presente.

I have been studying English for three years.

Present Perfect Continuous:

mesma continuidade, com maior ênfase na atividade/duração.

Outro contraste

She wrote five emails yesterday.

Simple Past.

She has written five emails today.

Present Perfect Simple — quantidade/resultados em período ainda relevante.

She has been writing emails all morning.

Present Perfect Continuous — duração/atividade.

Vocabulário-chave

continuous — contínuo

duration — duração

activity — atividade

result — resultado

ongoing — em andamento

recent — recente

recently — recentemente

lately — ultimamente

all day — o dia todo

all morning — a manhã toda

for — por/durante

since — desde

How long…? — há quanto tempo…?

state verb — verbo de estado

quantity — quantidade

completed — concluído

unfinished — não concluído/em andamento

Estratégia de prova

Para escolher entre Present Perfect Simple e Continuous, faça duas perguntas.

Primeira:

O foco é duração/atividade?

Se sim:

Present Perfect Continuous.

Exemplo:

for three hours

all morning

since 8 a.m.

lately.

Segunda:

O foco é resultado, quantidade ou conclusão?

Se sim:

Present Perfect Simple.

Exemplo:

three emails

four books

finished

completed.

Compare:

I’ve been reading for two hours.

Duração.

I’ve read 50 pages.

Resultado.

Outra pista:

How long…?

frequentemente pede Continuous.

How many…?

frequentemente pede Simple.

Mas sempre confirme o significado da frase.

Prática

1. Complete:

I ___ been studying for two hours.

  1. have
  2. has
  3. am
  4. did

2. Complete:

She ___ been working since eight.

  1. have
  2. has
  3. is
  4. did

3. Complete:

They have been ___ for the bus.

  1. wait
  2. waited
  3. waiting
  4. waits

4. Complete:

It has been ___ all morning.

  1. rain
  2. rained
  3. raining
  4. rains

5. Complete:

How long have you been ___ English?

  1. study
  2. studied
  3. studying
  4. studies

6. Complete:

I’ve been waiting ___ forty minutes.

  1. since
  2. for
  3. ago
  4. last

7. Complete:

I’ve been waiting ___ 9 a.m.

  1. for
  2. since
  3. ago
  4. during three hours

8. Complete:

She has been working here ___ January.

  1. since
  2. for
  3. ago
  4. yesterday

9. Complete:

We have been traveling ___ two weeks.

  1. since
  2. for
  3. last
  4. ago

10. Escolha:

Look at the ground. It ___.

  1. has been raining
  2. rained last year
  3. has rain
  4. has been rained

11. Escolha:

You look tired. ___ you been working?

  1. Did
  2. Have
  3. Are
  4. Has

12. Escolha:

Maria ___ all morning.

  1. has been studying
  2. has studying
  3. was study since today
  4. has been studied

13. Escolha o melhor tempo:

I ___ three chapters today.

  1. have read
  2. have been read
  3. have been reading three chapters complete
  4. read yesterday

O foco é a quantidade concluída.

14. Escolha:

I ___ for three hours.

  1. have read three books
  2. have been reading
  3. did reading
  4. has been reading

15. Escolha:

She ___ ten emails so far.

  1. has written
  2. has been written
  3. has been writing ten complete emails
  4. wrote tomorrow

16. Escolha:

She ___ emails all morning.

  1. has been writing
  2. has wrote
  3. has been written
  4. did writing

17. Complete:

I’ve ___ him for ten years.

  1. been knowing
  2. known
  3. knowing
  4. knew yesterday

18. Complete:

I’ve ___ this laptop since 2024.

  1. been having
  2. had
  3. have
  4. having

Considere o sentido de posse.

19. Escolha:

How many books ___ you ___ this month?

  1. have / read
  2. have / been reading for
  3. did / read tomorrow
  4. has / read

20. Escolha:

How long ___ you been reading?

  1. did
  2. have
  3. has
  4. are

21. Corrija:

I have studying all afternoon.

22. Corrija:

She has been worked here for six months.

23. Corrija:

They have been waiting since two hours.

24. Corrija:

I’ve been knowing Laura since 2020.

25. Escolha a melhor opção:

The kitchen is clean now. I ___ it.

  1. have cleaned
  2. have been cleaning, se o foco é necessariamente conclusão total
  3. cleaned tomorrow
  4. have been cleaned

Considere que o foco é o resultado concluído.

26. Escolha:

My clothes are dirty because I ___ the garage.

  1. have been cleaning
  2. have clean
  3. cleaned next week
  4. has been cleaning

Considere que o foco é a atividade recente que explica o resultado visível.

27. Complete o texto:

Daniel ___ (work) on a new project for three weeks. He ___ already ___ (complete) the first two sections, but he ___ (prepare) the final section since Monday.

28. Complete:

Sarah ___ (study) all morning. She ___ (finish) three chapters so far and she still has two more to review.

29. Compare e explique:

  1. I’ve written five pages.

  2. I’ve been writing for two hours.

O que cada frase enfatiza?

30. Produção

Escreva oito frases:

  • duas com for;
  • duas com since;
  • uma com all morning/all day;
  • uma sobre atividade recente com resultado visível;
  • uma com Present Perfect Simple mostrando quantidade concluída;
  • uma contrastando Simple e Continuous.

Gabarito comentado

1. A — have

I have been studying.

2. B — has

She has been working.

3. C — waiting

A estrutura exige:

been + verb-ing.

4. C — raining

It has been raining.

5. C — studying

How long have you been studying English?

6. B — for

forty minutes

é duração.

7. B — since

9 a.m.

é ponto inicial.

8. A — since

since January.

9. B — for

for two weeks.

10. A — has been raining

O solo molhado é um resultado presente de uma atividade recente.

11. B — Have

Have you been working?

12. A — has been studying

Forma correta:

has + been + studying.

13. A — have read

O foco está em:

three chapters.

Quantidade concluída.

14. B — have been reading

O foco:

for three hours.

Duração da atividade.

15. A — has written

ten emails

é quantidade/resultados.

16. A — has been writing

all morning

enfatiza duração da atividade.

17. B — known

know

é um state verb e normalmente não aparece no Continuous nesse sentido.

I’ve known him for ten years.

18. B — had

Posse:

I’ve had this laptop since 2024.

19. A — have / read

How many…?

Foco em quantidade concluída.

20. B — have

How long have you been reading?

21.

Errado:

I have studying all afternoon.

Correto:

I have been studying all afternoon.

Faltava:

been.

22.

She has been working here for six months.

Depois de:

been

usamos:

working.

23.

They have been waiting for two hours.

two hours

é duração.

24.

I’ve known Laura since 2020.

Com:

know

preferimos Present Perfect Simple.

25. A — have cleaned

O foco é:

resultado concluído.

A cozinha está limpa.

26. A — have been cleaning

O foco é a atividade recente que explica:

dirty clothes.

27.

Daniel has been working on a new project for three weeks. He has already completed the first two sections, but he has been preparing the final section since Monday.

Análise:

has been working → duração.

has completed → resultado.

has been preparing → atividade em andamento.

28.

Sarah has been studying all morning. She has finished three chapters so far and she still has two more to review.

all morning → atividade/duração.

three chapters → quantidade concluída.

29.

I’ve written five pages.

Ênfase:

resultado/quantidade.

Sabemos exatamente quanto foi produzido.

I’ve been writing for two hours.

Ênfase:

duração da atividade.

Não sabemos necessariamente quantas páginas foram concluídas.

30.

Modelos:

I’ve been studying for two hours.

They’ve been waiting for thirty minutes.

She has been working here since 2024.

It has been raining since this morning.

I’ve been answering emails all morning.

Your shoes are wet. Have you been walking in the rain?

I’ve answered twelve emails today.

I’ve been reading for an hour, and I’ve finished two chapters.

Tarefa de consolidação

Crie uma tabela com três colunas:

Situação Present Perfect Simple Present Perfect Continuous
leitura I’ve read 3 chapters. I’ve been reading for 2 hours.
escrita I’ve written 5 emails. I’ve been writing emails all morning.
estudo I’ve completed 4 exercises. I’ve been studying since 8 a.m.

Adicione pelo menos dez pares.

Depois pratique perguntas em pares:

How long have you been…?

e:

How many … have you…?

Exemplo:

How long have you been reading?

How many pages have you read?

Outro:

How long have you been studying?

How many exercises have you completed?

Em seguida, produza cinco frases com resultado visível:

The ground is wet because it has been raining.

I’m tired because I’ve been working all day.

Depois revise os principais state verbs:

know

believe

understand

need

want

own

belong.

Para esses verbos, priorize formas simples quando exprimirem estado:

I’ve known her for years.

I’ve had this phone since 2024.

Por fim, memorize o contraste:

Present Perfect Simple → resultado, conclusão, quantidade.

Present Perfect Continuous → atividade, duração, continuidade, efeito recente da atividade.

Pergunte antes de escolher:

Quero destacar quanto foi concluído ou por quanto tempo a atividade vem acontecendo?

Se o foco for:

How many? → geralmente Simple.

Se o foco for:

How long? → geralmente Continuous.

Essa distinção será cada vez mais importante no nível B1, porque permite falar com mais precisão sobre experiências, progresso, trabalho, estudo e atividades em andamento.

Aula 71 — Past Perfect: introdução

Objetivos

Ao final desta aula, você deverá ser capaz de:

  • compreender a formação do Past Perfect;
  • reconhecer a estrutura had + past participle;
  • usar o Past Perfect para indicar uma ação que aconteceu antes de outra ação passada;
  • diferenciar Past Perfect e Simple Past;
  • utilizar marcadores como before, after, already, just, never e by the time;
  • organizar acontecimentos em ordem cronológica;
  • identificar qual evento ocorreu primeiro em uma narrativa;
  • formular frases afirmativas, negativas e interrogativas no Past Perfect;
  • compreender o uso do tempo verbal em Reading e Listening;
  • empregar o Past Perfect em relatos escritos e orais;
  • evitar erros comuns de formação;
  • reconhecer situações em que o Simple Past continua suficiente e o Past Perfect não é necessário.

Desenvolvimento

O Past Perfect é usado principalmente para falar de uma ação que aconteceu:

antes de outra ação passada.

Estrutura:

had + past participle.

Exemplos:

I had finished my homework before my friend called.

She had left when I arrived.

They had already eaten before the meeting started.

Em todos esses casos, temos dois momentos no passado.

O Past Perfect mostra qual aconteceu primeiro.

Estrutura básica

A grande vantagem do Past Perfect é que:

had

é usado com todas as pessoas.

Exemplos:

I had finished.

You had finished.

He had finished.

She had finished.

We had finished.

They had finished.

Não há:

has

ou:

have

no Past Perfect.

Past participle

Depois de:

had

usamos o:

past participle.

Com verbos regulares:

work → worked

study → studied

finish → finished

arrive → arrived.

Exemplos:

had worked

had studied

had finished

had arrived.

Verbos irregulares

Precisamos usar a terceira forma.

Base form Simple Past Past Participle
go went gone
see saw seen
eat ate eaten
take took taken
write wrote written
do did done
come came come
leave left left
buy bought bought
make made made
find found found
lose lost lost
speak spoke spoken
know knew known
be was/were been

Exemplos:

had gone

had seen

had eaten

had written.

Afirmativa

Estrutura:

subject + had + past participle.

Exemplos:

I had finished the report.

She had left the office.

We had seen that film before.

They had bought the tickets.

Contração

had

pode aparecer como:

’d.

Exemplos:

I’d finished.

She’d left.

We’d already eaten.

Atenção:

’d

também pode representar:

would.

Compare:

I’d finished before six.

Aqui:

I had finished.

I’d like some coffee.

Aqui:

I would like.

O contexto mostra o significado.

Negativa

Estrutura:

subject + had not + past participle.

Contração:

hadn’t.

Exemplos:

I hadn’t finished the assignment.

She hadn’t seen the message.

They hadn’t arrived yet.

We hadn’t eaten before the trip.

Perguntas

Estrutura:

Had + subject + past participle?

Exemplos:

Had you finished before the class started?

Had she left before you arrived?

Had they already eaten?

Respostas curtas

Had you finished?

Yes, I had.

No, I hadn’t.

Had she arrived?

Yes, she had.

No, she hadn’t.

A ideia central: passado antes do passado

Observe:

When I arrived at the station, the train had left.

Temos dois acontecimentos:

  1. the train left;
  2. I arrived.

Ambos estão no passado.

Mas o trem saiu primeiro.

Então usamos:

had left

para marcar a ação anterior.

Linha temporal

Imagine:

TRAIN LEFT ───── I ARRIVED ───── NOW

Primeiro:

the train had left.

Depois:

I arrived.

Frase:

The train had left before I arrived.

Outro exemplo

She had finished dinner before her friend called.

Sequência:

finished dinner → friend called.

Ação anterior:

had finished.

Ação posterior:

called.

Past Perfect + Simple Past

Essa é a combinação mais comum.

Past Perfect → ação anterior.

Simple Past → ação posterior.

Exemplo:

We had booked the hotel before we traveled.

Primeiro:

booked.

Depois:

traveled.

Outro:

He had studied a lot, so he passed the exam.

Primeiro:

studied.

Depois:

passed.

Compare com Simple Past

Frase:

When I arrived, Maria left.

Isso pode sugerir:

eu cheguei e então Maria saiu.

Agora:

When I arrived, Maria had left.

Isso significa:

Maria já havia saído antes da minha chegada.

A diferença é importante.

Before

before

significa:

antes.

Exemplo:

She had finished the report before the meeting started.

Primeiro:

finished report.

Depois:

meeting started.

After

after

significa:

depois.

Exemplo:

After she had finished the report, she sent it to her manager.

Primeiro:

finished.

Depois:

sent.

Past Perfect antes ou depois na frase

A ordem das palavras não precisa ser igual à ordem dos acontecimentos.

Exemplo:

After Daniel had eaten breakfast, he left home.

Primeiro:

ate breakfast.

Depois:

left home.

Agora:

Daniel left home after he had eaten breakfast.

A sequência temporal é a mesma.

By the time

Uma expressão importante:

by the time

significa aproximadamente:

quando / até o momento em que.

Exemplo:

By the time I arrived, the meeting had started.

Significa:

quando cheguei, a reunião já tinha começado.

Outro:

By the time we reached the airport, the plane had left.

Already

already

é muito comum com Past Perfect.

Exemplo:

She had already left when I called.

They had already eaten before we arrived.

Estrutura:

had + already + past participle.

Just

just

pode indicar algo que tinha acabado de acontecer.

Exemplo:

The train had just left when we reached the station.

Outro:

I had just finished dinner when the phone rang.

Never

never

pode indicar que algo nunca tinha acontecido até aquele momento passado.

Exemplo:

I had never seen snow before I visited Canada.

Primeiro período da vida:

never seen snow.

Depois:

visited Canada.

Outro:

She had never traveled by plane before that trip.

Yet

Também pode aparecer:

He hadn’t finished yet when the teacher arrived.

Aqui:

até aquele momento passado, ele ainda não tinha terminado.

First time e experiência passada anterior

Exemplo:

It was the first time I had traveled alone.

Essa estrutura indica:

até aquele momento do passado, eu nunca tinha viajado sozinho.

Outro:

It was the first time she had spoken in public.

Causa no passado

Past Perfect pode explicar uma situação passada.

Exemplo:

Anna was tired because she had worked all night.

Situação posterior:

was tired.

Causa anterior:

had worked all night.

Outro:

The streets were wet because it had rained.

Resultado no passado

He couldn’t enter the house because he had lost his keys.

Primeiro:

lost keys.

Depois:

couldn’t enter.

Narrativas

O Past Perfect é muito útil quando uma história começa em um ponto passado e depois menciona algo que aconteceu antes.

Exemplo:

Daniel arrived at the airport at 8 a.m. He was nervous because he had forgotten his passport at home.

Momento principal da narrativa:

arrived at airport.

Evento anterior:

had forgotten passport.

Flashback

O Past Perfect pode funcionar como um pequeno “retorno” na linha temporal.

Exemplo:

Maria looked at the old photograph. She remembered the trip she had taken ten years earlier.

Momento narrativo:

looked / remembered.

Experiência anterior:

had taken.

Reading

Leia:

When Emma arrived at work, she realized that she had left her laptop at home.

Pergunta:

What happened first?

Resposta:

She left her laptop at home.

O Past Perfect ajuda a identificar isso.

Listening

Áudio:

I got to the station at nine, but the train had already left.

Informações:

train left first

speaker arrived later.

Uma questão pode perguntar:

Why did the speaker miss the train?

Resposta:

Because it had already left before the speaker arrived.

Past Perfect x Present Perfect

Compare:

I have finished my homework.

Present Perfect:

ligação entre passado e presente.

Agora:

I had finished my homework before my friend arrived.

Past Perfect:

ligação entre dois momentos passados.

Linha temporal

Present Perfect

PAST ───────── NOW

I have finished.

Past Perfect

EARLIER PAST ─── LATER PAST ─── NOW

I had finished before she arrived.

Past Perfect x Simple Past

Simple Past:

I ate dinner at seven.

Acontecimento passado.

Past Perfect:

I had eaten dinner before the guests arrived.

Acontecimento anterior a outro passado.

Não use Past Perfect para tudo no passado

Errado ou desnecessário:

Yesterday, I had gone to the supermarket and had bought milk and had returned home.

Se estamos apenas contando uma sequência normal:

Yesterday, I went to the supermarket, bought milk and returned home.

Use Simple Past.

O Past Perfect é especialmente útil quando precisamos:

mostrar que uma ação ocorreu antes de outro ponto passado.

Quando a ordem já está clara

Com:

before

e:

after

o Simple Past também pode ser suficiente em muitos contextos.

Exemplo:

I ate breakfast before I left home.

Está claro.

Também podemos dizer:

I had eaten breakfast before I left home.

O Past Perfect enfatiza mais que a primeira ação estava concluída antes da segunda.

No nível atual, aprenda primeiro a reconhecer ambos e use o Past Perfect quando a ordem temporal precisar ficar clara.

Compare

After I finished the exam, I went home.

Perfeitamente natural.

After I had finished the exam, I went home.

Também correto, com maior ênfase na conclusão anterior.

Portanto:

Past Perfect não é obrigatório em toda frase com two past actions.

Ponto de referência passado

Pergunte:

Qual é o momento passado principal?

Depois:

algo já tinha acontecido antes dele?

Se sim, o Past Perfect pode ser adequado.

Exemplo:

Momento principal:

I arrived at the hotel.

Antes:

someone canceled my reservation.

Frase:

When I arrived at the hotel, I discovered that someone had canceled my reservation.

Perguntas com why

Exemplo:

Why was Peter tired?

Because he had worked all night.

Aqui o Past Perfect explica a causa anterior.

Situação acadêmica

The student was nervous because he hadn’t studied enough.

By the time the exam started, Maria had reviewed all her notes.

She had already submitted the assignment before the deadline.

Viagens

The flight had already left when we arrived.

We couldn’t enter the hotel because we had forgotten the booking confirmation.

By the time the bus arrived, we had waited for over an hour.

A última frase introduz uma estrutura de duração anterior a um ponto passado, que posteriormente pode ser aprofundada com Past Perfect Continuous.

Tecnologia

I couldn’t open the document because I had forgotten the password.

The computer stopped working after I had installed the update.

She realized that she had deleted the wrong file.

Compras

When I returned to the store, the sale had ended.

The customer had lost the receipt, so he couldn’t return the product.

Past Perfect com perguntas

Had you ever visited London before that trip?

Aqui perguntamos:

antes daquele momento passado, essa experiência já tinha acontecido?

Resposta:

Yes, I had.

Ou:

No, I hadn’t.

Present Perfect x Past Perfect com ever

Presente:

Have you ever traveled abroad?

Até agora.

Passado:

Had you ever traveled abroad before 2024?

Até aquele ponto passado.

Never

Presente:

I’ve never traveled abroad.

Até agora.

Passado:

I had never traveled abroad before that trip.

Até aquele momento passado.

Already

Presente:

I’ve already finished.

Até agora.

Passado:

I had already finished when she arrived.

Antes daquele momento passado.

Just

Presente:

I’ve just finished.

Acontecimento recente em relação ao presente.

Passado:

I had just finished when she called.

Acontecimento recente em relação a outro momento passado.

Formação: atenção ao particípio

Errado:

She had went home.

Correto:

She had gone home.

Errado:

I had saw the message.

Correto:

I had seen the message.

Errado:

They had ate dinner.

Correto:

They had eaten dinner.

Erro com did

Errado:

Did she had finished before you arrived?

Correto:

Had she finished before you arrived?

O auxiliar:

had

já forma a pergunta.

Erro na negativa

Errado:

She didn’t had finished.

Correto:

She hadn’t finished.

Ou, se for simplesmente Simple Past:

She didn’t finish.

Mas o significado pode ser diferente dependendo do contexto.

Erro com dois auxiliares

Errado:

She had didn’t finish.

Correto:

She hadn’t finished.

Erro com verbo base

Errado:

He had leave before I arrived.

Correto:

He had left before I arrived.

Erro de sequência

Frase:

When I arrived, the train had left.

Significa:

train first, arrival second.

Não interprete como:

arrival first, train second.

Marcadores úteis

before

antes.

after

depois.

by the time

até o momento em que/quando.

already

já.

just

acabado de.

never

nunca.

yet

ainda/já, dependendo do contexto.

when

quando.

Relação com sequence

Aula anterior:

first → then → finally.

Agora o Past Perfect permite contar acontecimentos fora da ordem cronológica.

Exemplo:

I arrived at the café at six. My friend had already left.

Ordem da narrativa:

  1. I arrived.
  2. informação sobre friend.

Ordem real:

  1. friend left.
  2. I arrived.

Essa capacidade é muito importante em Reading.

Exemplo completo

Last Monday, Julia arrived at university and opened her bag. She suddenly realized that she had left her assignment at home. She called her brother, but he had already gone to work. Julia explained the problem to her teacher. Fortunately, she had uploaded a copy of the assignment to the online platform the night before, so the teacher accepted it.

Linha temporal:

  1. Julia uploaded the assignment the night before.
  2. Julia left the physical assignment at home.
  3. brother went to work.
  4. Julia arrived at university.
  5. Julia realized the problem.
  6. she called.
  7. she explained.

O Past Perfect marca eventos que ocorreram antes do ponto principal da narrativa.

Vocabulário-chave

Past Perfect — passado perfeito

past participle — particípio passado

earlier — mais cedo/anterior

previous — anterior

before — antes

after — depois

by the time — até o momento em que

already — já

just — acabado de

never — nunca

yet — ainda

sequence — sequência

previous action — ação anterior

later action — ação posterior

timeline — linha temporal

realize — perceber

discover — descobrir

forget — esquecer

forgotten — esquecido

leave — sair/deixar

left — saiu/deixou

Estratégia de prova

Quando houver duas ações no passado, pergunte:

Which happened first?

A ação mais antiga pode aparecer no:

Past Perfect.

A posterior normalmente aparece no:

Simple Past.

Exemplo:

When I got home, my family had already eaten.

Primeiro:

family ate.

Depois:

I got home.

Outra estratégia:

procure:

before

after

by the time

already.

Essas palavras frequentemente ajudam a localizar a sequência.

Em Reading, desenhe mentalmente:

earlier event → later event.

Não siga apenas a ordem em que as frases aparecem.

Prática

1. Complete:

When I arrived, the train ___ already ___.

  1. had / left
  2. did / leave
  3. has / left
  4. had / leave

2. Complete:

She ___ finished the report before the meeting started.

  1. has
  2. had
  3. did
  4. was

3. Complete:

They had ___ before we arrived.

  1. eat
  2. ate
  3. eaten
  4. eating

4. Complete:

I had never ___ snow before that trip.

  1. saw
  2. seen
  3. see
  4. seeing

5. Complete:

By the time we reached the airport, the plane ___.

  1. leaves
  2. had left
  3. has left
  4. did leave before

6. Complete:

He was tired because he ___ all night.

  1. worked tomorrow
  2. had worked
  3. has worked now
  4. working

7. Complete:

She couldn’t enter the house because she ___ her keys.

  1. had lost
  2. has lost now
  3. lose
  4. had lose

8. Complete:

After they ___ dinner, they went for a walk.

  1. had finished
  2. have finished
  3. finishing
  4. had finish

9. Complete:
