Possibilidade futura realista.

Second:

If it snowed here tomorrow, I would be surprised.

A situação é vista como improvável ou imaginária.

Outro contraste

First:

If I finish early, I’ll call you.

Possibilidade real.

Second:

If I finished work at noon every day, I would have much more free time.

Situação hipotética.

Estrutura comparativa

Conditional Estrutura Uso
First if + Present, will + verb possibilidade futura realista
Second if + Past, would + verb situação hipotética/improvável

O Simple Past não indica necessariamente passado

Esse é um ponto importante.

Na frase:

If I had more money, I would travel.

had

tem forma de passado.

Mas a frase pode se referir:

ao presente ou futuro.

Aqui o Simple Past marca:

distância da realidade.

Não necessariamente tempo passado.

Have no Second Conditional

If I had more time…

Não significa:

se eu tive mais tempo.

Significa:

se eu tivesse mais tempo.

Be no Second Conditional

Com o verbo be, podemos encontrar:

If I were…

If he were…

If she were…

Em linguagem mais formal ou tradicional, were pode ser usado para todas as pessoas em situações hipotéticas.

Exemplo clássico:

If I were you, I would talk to the teacher.

If I were you

Essa expressão é muito importante para dar conselho.

If I were you, I’d study a little every day.

If I were you, I’d ask for help.

If I were you, I wouldn’t buy that laptop.

Significado:

No seu lugar, eu…

Was x were

Em inglês informal, você pode ouvir:

If I was you…

Mas em provas e em uso mais cuidadoso, prefira:

If I were you…

Especialmente para conselho e hipóteses irreais.

Would na consequência

Estrutura:

would + base verb.

Correto:

would go

would study

would buy.

Errado:

would to go

would went

would goes.

Negativa

would not → wouldn’t.

Exemplos:

If I were tired, I wouldn’t go out.

If the hotel were too expensive, we wouldn’t stay there.

If she had more time, she wouldn’t feel so stressed.

Perguntas

Uma estrutura muito comum:

What would you do if…?

Exemplo:

What would you do if you lost your phone?

Resposta:

I would call it from another phone.

Outro:

What would you do if you missed an important exam?

I’d contact the teacher immediately.

Where would you…?

Where would you live if you could choose any city?

I’d live somewhere near the sea.

Who would you…?

Who would you call if you needed help?

I’d call a friend.

Would you… if…?

Would you travel alone if you had the opportunity?

Yes, I would.

No, I wouldn’t.

Could no Second Conditional

Podemos usar:

could

na consequência.

Exemplo:

If I had more free time, I could learn another language.

Aqui:

could

indica possibilidade ou capacidade hipotética.

Outro:

If we lived closer to the university, we could walk there.

Could na oração com if

Também pode aparecer:

If I could choose any country, I would visit Japan.

If she could work from home, she would move to another city.

Aqui:

could

representa capacidade ou possibilidade hipotética.

Might

Também podemos usar:

might

na consequência para uma possibilidade menos certa.

Exemplo:

If I had a free month, I might travel.

Outro:

If the course were cheaper, I might enroll.

Would x could x might

Compare:

If I had more time, I would study French.

Resultado hipotético visto como decisão.

If I had more time, I could study French.

Seria possível.

If I had more time, I might study French.

Talvez eu estudasse.

Advice

Second Conditional é muito usado para conselho:

If I were you, I’d rest.

If I were you, I’d save the file before restarting the computer.

If I were you, I wouldn’t wait until the last day.

Situações de estudo

If I had more time, I would review every chapter.

If I understood this topic better, I would feel more confident.

If I were you, I’d practice Listening every day.

Tecnologia

If I had a better laptop, I could run this program faster.

If the internet were more stable, I would attend more online classes.

If I lost an important file, I would check the backup first.

Trabalho

If I worked from home, I would save time.

If I had a flexible schedule, I could study in the morning.

If I were the manager, I would organize shorter meetings.

Viagens

If I could travel anywhere, I would visit Japan.

If flights were cheaper, I would travel more often.

If I had a month off, I might travel around Europe.

Moradia

If I lived closer to work, I would walk there.

If I had a larger apartment, I would have a study room.

Sonhos e possibilidades

If I wrote a book, it would probably be about technology.

If I started a company, I would focus on education.

If I could change one thing about my city, I would improve public transport.

Second Conditional e probabilidade

Não existe uma porcentagem fixa.

A estrutura apenas mostra que o falante vê a situação como:

more hypothetical

less likely

ou:

contrary to reality.

Compare intenção do falante

If I get the job, I’ll move.

O falante considera:

possibilidade real.

If I got that job, I would move.

O falante apresenta a situação de forma mais hipotética.

Second Conditional e presente

If I knew the answer, I would tell you.

Isso sugere:

I don’t know the answer.

Outro:

If she were here, she would help us.

Sugere:

she isn’t here.

Inferência implícita

Frase:

If I had a car, I’d drive to university.

Podemos inferir:

the speaker probably doesn’t have a car.

Frase:

If he spoke Spanish, he could apply for the position.

Podemos inferir:

he probably doesn’t speak Spanish.

Esse tipo de inferência pode aparecer em Reading.

Reading

Texto:

Emma lives far from her office and spends almost two hours commuting every day. If she lived closer, she would walk to work.

Pergunta:

Does Emma currently live close to her office?

Resposta:

No.

A conditional indica uma situação contrária à realidade atual.

Listening

Áudio:

If I had more money, I’d buy the more expensive laptop, but I can’t afford it.

Pergunta:

Why isn’t the speaker buying the expensive laptop?

Resposta:

Because the speaker doesn’t have enough money.

Speaking

Pergunta:

What would you do if you had a month of free time?

Resposta:

If I had a month of free time, I’d probably travel and study something new. I might also spend more time reading.

Speaking — desenvolver resposta

Pergunta:

Where would you live if you could live anywhere?

Resposta curta:

Japan.

Melhor:

If I could live anywhere, I’d probably live in Japan because I’d like to experience the culture and learn the language.

Writing

O Second Conditional é útil em textos de opinião.

Exemplo:

If cities had better public transport, fewer people would use cars.

Outro:

If schools offered more technology courses, students could develop useful digital skills.

Hipótese + consequência

Estrutura conceitual:

imagined condition → imagined result.

Exemplo:

If the course were free, more students would enroll.

Condição:

course free.

Resultado:

more students enroll.

Ambos são hipotéticos.

Because e Second Conditional

I would travel more if flights were cheaper because I enjoy visiting new places.

Podemos combinar estruturas.

So

If I had more money, I would travel more, so I would probably visit several countries.

Relative clauses

If I had a job that allowed remote work, I would travel more.

Isso combina Second Conditional com relative clause.

Comparatives

If this laptop were cheaper, it would be a better option.

If the bus were faster, I would use it more often.

Present Perfect e Second Conditional

Compare:

I’ve never been to Canada.

Experiência real até agora.

If I had the opportunity, I would visit Canada.

Situação hipotética futura.

Past Perfect não é Second Conditional

Compare:

If I had more time, I would study.

Second Conditional:

had = Simple Past de have.

Agora:

I had finished before she arrived.

Past Perfect:

had + finished.

A estrutura é completamente diferente.

Não use would na oração com if

Erro comum:

If I would have more time, I would study.

Correto:

If I had more time, I would study.

No padrão básico:

if + Simple Past

e não:

if + would.

Exceções reais

Existem contextos em que would pode aparecer depois de if, especialmente relacionados a vontade, insistência ou pedidos.

Mas isso está fora do foco desta aula.

Para Second Conditional básico:

não use would na if-clause.

Erro frequente 1

Errado:

If I would have money, I would travel.

Correto:

If I had money, I would travel.

Erro frequente 2

Errado:

If she studied, she will pass.

Essa mistura pode estar inadequada para o sentido hipotético.

Second Conditional:

If she studied more, she would pass.

Erro frequente 3

Errado:

I would traveled.

Correto:

I would travel.

Erro frequente 4

Errado:

I would to buy it.

Correto:

I would buy it.

Erro frequente 5

Errado:

If he have more time, he would study.

Correto:

If he had more time, he would study.

Erro frequente 6

Errado:

If I was you, I will talk to her.

Forma recomendada:

If I were you, I would talk to her.

Erro frequente 7

Confundir realidade com hipótese.

If I have time tonight, I’ll study.

First Conditional.

If I had more free time in general, I’d study more.

Second Conditional.

First x Second com a mesma ideia

First

If I save enough money this year, I’ll buy a new computer.

Possibilidade real.

Second

If I had enough money now, I’d buy a new computer.

Situação hipotética atual.

Outro par

First

If she studies tonight, she’ll do well tomorrow.

Second

If she studied more regularly, she would get better grades.

O primeiro fala de uma situação específica.

O segundo fala de um cenário hipotético mais geral.

Zero, First e Second Conditional

Tipo Estrutura Ideia
Zero if + Present, Present fato/hábito geral
First if + Present, will + verb futuro possível
Second if + Past, would + verb hipótese/improbabilidade

Compare os três

If I drink coffee late, I don’t sleep well.

Zero:

padrão geral.

If I drink coffee tonight, I won’t sleep well.

First:

situação futura possível.

If I drank coffee every night, I would probably sleep badly.

Second:

situação imaginária/hipotética.

Unless no Second Conditional

Também é possível:

I wouldn’t buy it unless it were cheaper.

Significa:

eu não compraria a menos que fosse mais barato.

Mas use com atenção.

Para consolidar o Second Conditional, priorize primeiro estruturas com:

if.

Wish — reconhecimento

O Second Conditional se relaciona conceitualmente com hipóteses e desejos.

Você pode encontrar futuramente estruturas como:

I wish I had more time.

Isso será estudado separadamente.

Vocabulário-chave

hypothetical — hipotético

imaginary — imaginário

unlikely — improvável

realistic — realista

condition — condição

result — resultado

would — auxiliar usado em resultados hipotéticos

could — poderia/seria capaz

might — talvez/poderia

opportunity — oportunidade

choice — escolha

advice — conselho

reality — realidade

imagine — imaginar

suppose — supor

afford — ter condições financeiras de pagar

Estratégia de prova

Ao encontrar uma conditional, faça três perguntas.

É um fato ou hábito geral?

Se sim:

Zero Conditional.

É uma situação futura realista?

Se sim:

First Conditional.

É uma situação hipotética, improvável ou contrária à realidade?

Se sim:

Second Conditional.

Observe também a estrutura:

if + Past → would + verb.

E procure pistas como:

If I were you…

If I had more money…

If I could…

What would you do if…?

Essas construções frequentemente indicam Second Conditional.

Prática

1. Complete:

If I ___ more money, I would travel more.

  1. have
  2. had
  3. will have
  4. would have

2. Complete:

If she lived closer, we ___ her more often.

  1. see
  2. will see
  3. would see
  4. would saw

3. Complete:

If I ___ you, I would talk to the teacher.

  1. am
  2. was/were, com preferência por were
  3. will be
  4. would be

4. Complete:

If he ___ more, he would get better grades.

  1. studies
  2. studied
  3. will study
  4. would study

5. Complete:

I would buy that laptop if it ___ cheaper.

  1. is
  2. were
  3. will be
  4. would be

6. Complete:

If I had more free time, I ___ learn another language.

  1. could
  2. could to
  3. did
  4. will yesterday

7. Complete:

If flights were cheaper, we ___ travel more often.

  1. would
  2. will
  3. are
  4. have

8. Complete:

If I won the lottery, I ___ around the world.

  1. travel
  2. would travel
  3. traveled yesterday
  4. will definitely traveled

9. Escolha a frase correta:

  1. If I would have time, I would study.
  2. If I had time, I would study.
  3. If I had time, I would studied.
  4. If I have time, I would studying.

10. Escolha:

  1. If she were here, she would help us.
  2. If she would be here, she helped us.
  3. If she were here, she will helped us.
  4. If she here, she would to help us.

11. Escolha o Second Conditional:

  1. If water freezes, it becomes ice.
  2. If I have time tonight, I’ll call you.
  3. If I had more free time, I’d read more.
  4. If I wake up early, I drink coffee.

12. Escolha o First Conditional:

  1. If I won a million dollars, I’d travel.
  2. If it rains tomorrow, we’ll stay home.
  3. If I were you, I’d wait.
  4. If I lived near the sea, I’d swim every day.

13. Escolha o Zero Conditional:

  1. If I feel tired, I usually rest.
  2. If I felt tired, I would rest.
  3. If I feel tired tonight, I’ll rest.
  4. If I were tired, I’d go home.

14. Complete:

What ___ you do if you lost your phone?

  1. will
  2. would
  3. did
  4. are

15. Complete:

Where would you live if you ___ choose any country?

  1. can
  2. could
  3. will
  4. would can

16. Complete:

If I had a month off, I ___ travel, but I’m not sure.

  1. might
  2. must
  3. did
  4. had to

17. Corrija:

If I would have a car, I would drive to work.

18. Corrija:

If she studied more, she will get better grades.

Considere que a frase é hipotética.

19. Corrija:

I would to visit Japan if I had the opportunity.

20. Corrija:

If I was you, I will ask the teacher.

Use a forma recomendada em provas.

21. Transforme para Second Conditional:

Situação realista:

If I have enough money, I’ll buy the computer.

Agora imagine que você não tem dinheiro suficiente atualmente.

22. Transforme em conselho:

You should talk to your teacher.

Use:

If I were you…

23. Complete:

If I ___ (live) closer to university, I ___ (walk) there every day.

24. Complete:

If Maria ___ (have) a better computer, she ___ (can/run) the program faster.

25. Complete:

If we ___ (not/have) classes tomorrow, I ___ (might/stay) home.

Considere a situação como hipotética.

26. Leia:

Tom spends almost three hours traveling to work every day. If he lived closer to his office, he would have much more free time.

Podemos inferir que:

  1. Tom currently lives close to his office.
  2. Tom probably does not live close to his office.
  3. Tom doesn’t work.
  4. Tom works from home.

27. Leia:

Sarah says, “If I had enough money, I’d buy the new laptop.”

Por que ela provavelmente não comprará o laptop agora?

28. Responda:

What would you do if you had a free month?

Use pelo menos três frases.

29. Responda:

If you could change one thing about your city, what would you change?

Use:

If I could…, I would…

30. Produção

Escreva um texto de 100 a 120 palavras sobre:

If I could change my daily routine…

Inclua:

  • pelo menos quatro Second Conditionals;
  • uma frase com If I were…;
  • uma com could;
  • uma com might;
  • uma justificativa com because;
  • uma comparação com sua realidade atual.

Gabarito comentado

1. B — had

Second Conditional:

if + Simple Past.

2. C — would see

Resultado hipotético:

would + base verb.

3. B

Forma recomendada:

If I were you…

4. B — studied

If he studied more, he would get better grades.

5. B — were

if it were cheaper.

Em situações hipotéticas, were é comum, especialmente em registro mais cuidadoso.

6. A — could

could + base verb.

Não:

could to learn.

7. A — would

would travel.

8. B — would travel

Ganhar na loteria é uma situação hipotética/improvável.

9. B

If I had time, I would study.

10. A

Estrutura correta:

If + Past, would + base verb.

11. C

If I had more free time, I’d read more.

Hipótese.

12. B

tomorrow

e uma situação futura realista indicam First Conditional.

13. A

É um hábito geral.

14. B — would

What would you do if…?

15. B — could

if you could choose.

16. A — might

Expressa possibilidade hipotética.

17.

If I had a car, I would drive to work.

Não usamos would na oração com if no padrão básico.

18.

If she studied more, she would get better grades.

19.

I would visit Japan if I had the opportunity.

Depois de:

would

use verbo base.

20.

If I were you, I would ask the teacher.

Ou:

If I were you, I’d ask the teacher.

21.

If I had enough money, I would buy the computer.

A mudança de:

have/will

para:

had/would

torna a situação mais hipotética.

22.

If I were you, I would talk to your teacher.

23.

If I lived closer to university, I would walk there every day.

24.

If Maria had a better computer, she could run the program faster.

25.

If we didn’t have classes tomorrow, I might stay home.

Como o exercício define a situação como hipotética, usamos:

didn’t have.

26. B

A frase hipotética sugere que atualmente Tom:

não mora perto do escritório.

27.

Porque:

she probably doesn’t have enough money.

A frase:

If I had enough money…

sugere que a condição não é verdadeira atualmente.

28.

Modelo:

If I had a free month, I would probably travel to another country. I would also spend more time reading and learning something new. If I had enough money, I might stay in two or three different cities during the trip.

29.

Modelo:

If I could change one thing about my city, I would improve public transport. If buses were more frequent and reliable, people would spend less time traveling.

30.

Modelo:

If I could change my daily routine, I would organize my mornings differently. At the moment, I usually have many things to do later in the day, so I sometimes feel that my schedule is too concentrated. If I had more free time in the morning, I would study earlier because I find it easier to concentrate then. If I lived closer to the places I visit regularly, I could spend less time traveling. I might also exercise more often if my schedule were more flexible. If I were able to change one thing immediately, I would create longer periods without interruptions. My current routine works, but a more flexible one would be more comfortable.

Tarefa de consolidação

Crie uma tabela comparando os três conditionals estudados:

Tipo Estrutura Uso Exemplo
Zero if + Present, Present fato/hábito If I’m tired, I rest.
First if + Present, will + verb futuro possível If I’m tired tonight, I’ll rest.
Second if + Past, would + verb hipótese If I had more time, I’d rest more.

Depois produza dez conjuntos de três frases sobre o mesmo tema.

Exemplo — dinheiro:

If I have extra money, I save it.

If I have extra money this month, I’ll buy a book.

If I had a lot more money, I’d travel more.

Outro — estudo:

If I study regularly, I remember more.

If I study tonight, I’ll finish the chapter.

If I had more free time, I’d study another language.

Depois responda oralmente:

What would you do if you won a large amount of money?

Where would you live if you could choose anywhere?

What would you study if you had more free time?

What would you change if you were the director of a school?

What would you do if you lost your phone?

Crie também cinco conselhos usando:

If I were you, I’d…

Finalize memorizando:

Zero Conditional → realidade geral

First Conditional → possibilidade futura realista

Second Conditional → hipótese, imaginação ou situação improvável

E a estrutura principal:

If + Simple Past, would + base verb

Use a pergunta:

Isso é uma possibilidade concreta ou estou imaginando uma realidade diferente?

Se você está imaginando uma situação menos provável, irreal ou contrária à realidade atual, o Second Conditional é uma das principais estruturas para expressá-la.

Aula 76 — Modal verbs: obrigação, possibilidade e conselho

Objetivos

Ao final desta aula, você deverá ser capaz de:

  • revisar os principais modal verbs relacionados a obrigação, possibilidade e conselho;
  • diferenciar must, have to, should, may, might, could e can;
  • compreender diferenças entre obrigação, necessidade, recomendação, permissão e possibilidade;
  • usar corretamente a estrutura modal + base verb;
  • distinguir mustn’t de don’t have to;
  • reconhecer diferentes graus de certeza;
  • formular frases afirmativas, negativas e interrogativas;
  • empregar modais em situações cotidianas, acadêmicas, profissionais e de viagem;
  • reconhecer os modais em Reading e Listening;
  • usá-los de forma adequada em Writing e Speaking;
  • evitar erros frequentes de estrutura e interpretação.

Desenvolvimento

Os modal verbs são verbos auxiliares usados para acrescentar ideias como:

obligation

possibility

advice

permission

ability.

Nesta aula, o foco principal será:

obrigação;

possibilidade;

conselho.

Os modais mais importantes serão:

must

should

can

could

may

might.

Também revisaremos:

have to

embora tecnicamente não funcione exatamente como um modal puro.

Estrutura geral dos modais

Depois de um modal, usamos:

base verb.

Exemplos:

You must study.

She should rest.

We may travel.

He could help.

They can enter.

Não usamos:

to

depois dos modais básicos.

Errado:

You must to study.

Correto:

You must study.

Errado:

She should to rest.

Correto:

She should rest.

Sem -s na terceira pessoa

Modais não recebem:

-s

com:

he / she / it.

Correto:

She can swim.

Não:

She cans swim.

Correto:

He must leave.

Não:

He musts leave.

Must — obrigação forte

Must expressa:

obrigação forte;

regra;

necessidade considerada importante pelo falante.

Exemplos:

You must wear a seat belt.

Students must show their ID.

I must finish this report today.

Must em regras

Visitors must leave their bags outside.

Candidates must arrive before 9 a.m.

Employees must follow the safety rules.

Must em obrigação pessoal

I must remember to call Anna.

I must study more this week.

Aqui, a obrigação pode vir do próprio falante.

Have to — obrigação ou necessidade

Have to também expressa obrigação.

Exemplos:

I have to work tomorrow.

She has to wear a uniform.

We have to submit the assignment by Friday.

Have to muda com a pessoa

I have to…

you have to…

we have to…

they have to…

Mas:

he has to…

she has to…

it has to….

Exemplo:

She has to leave early.

Must x have to

Em muitos contextos, os dois são muito próximos.

You must show ID.

You have to show ID.

As duas frases indicam obrigação.

Uma diferença frequente é:

must → obrigação mais diretamente apresentada pelo falante ou regra formal.

have to → obrigação causada por circunstância ou exigência externa.

Exemplo:

I must call my mother.

O falante sente a necessidade.

I have to wear a uniform at work.

A regra vem do trabalho.

No uso cotidiano, essa diferença nem sempre é rígida.

Negativa de must

must not

ou:

mustn’t.

Significa:

proibição.

Exemplo:

You mustn’t smoke here.

Isso significa:

smoking is prohibited.

Outro:

Students mustn’t use phones during the exam.

Negativa de have to

don’t have to

doesn’t have to.

Significa:

não é necessário.

Exemplo:

You don’t have to bring a laptop.

Isso significa:

bringing a laptop is optional.

Outro:

She doesn’t have to work tomorrow.

Mustn’t x don’t have to

Essa é uma das diferenças mais importantes.

You mustn’t enter.

Significa:

você não pode entrar.

Proibição.

You don’t have to enter.

Significa:

você não precisa entrar.

Ausência de obrigação.

Compare

You mustn’t pay.

Pagamento proibido.

You don’t have to pay.

Pagamento não é necessário.

Em uma prova, confundir as duas pode mudar completamente o sentido.

Perguntas com have to

Como have to não funciona exatamente como modal puro, usamos:

do / does.

Exemplos:

Do you have to work tomorrow?

Does she have to wear a uniform?

Respostas:

Yes, I do.

No, she doesn’t.

Must em perguntas

É possível usar:

Must I…?

Exemplo:

Must I complete this form now?

É mais formal.

No cotidiano, frequentemente usamos:

Do I have to complete this form now?

Should — conselho

Should expressa:

recommendation

advice

what is a good idea.

Exemplos:

You should study every day.

You should arrive early.

She should talk to her teacher.

Should não é must

Compare:

You should study.

É recomendação.

You must study.

É obrigação forte.

Should not

shouldn’t.

Expressa:

conselho negativo.

Exemplos:

You shouldn’t stay up too late.

You shouldn’t leave your password in a public place.

He shouldn’t drive if he’s extremely tired.

Perguntas com should

Should I call her?

Should we take the bus?

What should I do?

Muito comum para pedir conselho.

What should I do?

Exemplo:

A: I have an exam tomorrow and I haven’t studied enough. What should I do?
B: You should review the main topics first.

Should em orientações

You should read the instructions carefully.

You should check your answers before submitting the test.

Can — possibilidade, capacidade e permissão

Can tem vários usos.

Nesta aula, interessa especialmente:

possibilidade prática;

permissão.

Exemplo:

You can use this computer.

Pode significar:

você tem permissão para usar.

Outro:

We can take the train.

Pode significar:

essa opção é possível.

Can para permissão

Can I sit here?

Can I use your charger?

You can leave after the test.

Can para possibilidade prática

We can meet tomorrow.

You can buy tickets online.

Could — possibilidade e conselho/sugestão

Could pode indicar:

  • possibilidade;
  • sugestão;
  • pedido educado;
  • habilidade passada.

Aqui o foco será:

possibilidade

e:

sugestão.

Exemplo:

We could go by train.

Isso significa:

essa seria uma possibilidade.

Outro:

You could ask the teacher.

É uma sugestão mais suave.

Could x should

Compare:

You should talk to the teacher.

É uma recomendação mais direta.

You could talk to the teacher.

É uma opção possível.

Could para pedidos

Could you help me?

Could I use your phone?

Mais polido que:

Can you help me?

May — possibilidade

May é usado para indicar possibilidade.

Exemplos:

It may rain later.

She may come to the meeting.

We may travel next month.

May para permissão formal

May I come in?

You may leave now.

Esse uso é mais formal.

Might — possibilidade

Might também expressa possibilidade.

Exemplos:

It might rain later.

I might stay home tonight.

They might arrive late.

May x might

No nível atual, ambos podem ser entendidos como:

talvez;

pode ser que.

Exemplos:

She may come.

She might come.

Em muitos contextos, might pode soar um pouco menos certo, mas não use isso como uma regra matemática rígida.

Grau de certeza

Compare:

She will come.

Previsão relativamente forte.

She may come.

Possibilidade.

She might come.

Possibilidade, muitas vezes percebida como mais incerta.

Probably x may/might

She’ll probably come.

O falante considera provável.

She may come.

É possível.

She might come.

Também é possível, com menor compromisso.

Modal + be

Exemplos:

It may be difficult.

She might be late.

You should be careful.

They must be tired.

Observe:

modal + be.

Modal + have — reconhecimento

Você pode encontrar estruturas mais avançadas como:

must have

might have

could have

para falar de hipóteses sobre o passado.

Essas formas serão estudadas posteriormente.

Nesta aula, concentre-se em:

modal + base verb

para presente e futuro.

Obrigação em contextos acadêmicos

Students must submit the assignment by Friday.

You have to bring your student ID.

You mustn’t use your phone during the exam.

You don’t have to print the document; you can upload it online.

Conselho em estudos

You should review your notes.

You shouldn’t study only the night before the exam.

You could practice with old tests.

Possibilidade em estudos

The teacher may change the deadline.

The test might include a Writing section.

We could study together.

Viagens — obrigação

Passengers must show their boarding pass.

You have to arrive before boarding closes.

You mustn’t carry prohibited items.

Viagens — possibilidade

The flight may be delayed.

We might take the train instead.

You could book a hotel near the station.

Tecnologia — obrigação e conselho

You must create a strong password.

You shouldn’t share your password.

You may need to restart the computer.

You could update the software.

Trabalho

Employees must follow the company rules.

Staff have to wear identification badges.

You should arrive on time.

The meeting may finish early.

Saúde e rotina

No contexto puramente linguístico:

You should rest.

You shouldn’t work all night.

You may feel tired after a long journey.

O foco aqui é a gramática e o uso linguístico.

Permission x obligation

Compare:

You can leave now.

Permissão.

You must leave now.

Obrigação.

You should leave now.

Conselho.

You may leave now.

Permissão formal.

Possibilidade x obrigação

You may take the train.

Pode significar:

essa opção é possível.

You must take the train.

Significa:

é obrigatório.

Conselho x possibilidade

You should call her.

Recomendação.

You could call her.

Sugestão/opção.

Modais e perguntas

Must

Must we leave now?

Should

Should I call?

Can

Can I enter?

Could

Could you help me?

May

May I come in?

Might

Perguntas diretas com might são menos comuns no nível básico.

Perguntas de possibilidade

Em vez de:

Might it rain?

que é possível, mas menos frequente no uso cotidiano básico, você encontrará muito:

Do you think it might rain?

Respostas curtas com can

Can you help me?

Yes, I can.

No, I can’t.

Should em respostas

Should I study tonight?

Yes, you should.

No, you shouldn’t.

Must em respostas

Must I bring my passport?

Yes, you must.

Mas em negativa, atenção:

No, you don’t have to.

Isso significa:

não é necessário.

No, you mustn’t.

significaria:

é proibido trazer.

Exemplo importante

Pergunta:

Do I have to wear a jacket?

Resposta:

No, you don’t have to.

Significa:

opcional.

Necessidade no passado

Must não possui uma forma passada regular para obrigação equivalente.

Normalmente usamos:

had to.

Exemplo:

I had to work yesterday.

She had to leave early.

Negativa no passado

didn’t have to.

Exemplo:

We didn’t have to pay.

Isso significa:

não foi necessário pagar.

Proibição no passado

Para proibição passada, dependemos do contexto e de outras construções.

Exemplo:

We weren’t allowed to enter.

Isso significa:

não tínhamos permissão para entrar.

Futuro com have to

I’ll have to work tomorrow.

She’ll have to complete the form.

Must também pode se referir ao futuro em alguns contextos, mas will have to é muito útil quando expressamos necessidade futura.

Ability — breve revisão de can/could

Embora não seja o foco principal:

can → capacidade presente.

could → capacidade geral passada.

Exemplo:

I can swim.

I could swim when I was six.

Possibilidade contextual de can

It can get very cold here in winter.

Isso expressa:

possibilidade geral.

Compare:

It may get cold tonight.

Possibilidade específica.

Can x may em possibilidade

This road can be dangerous in winter.

Possibilidade geral/característica.

This road may be dangerous tonight because of the ice.

Possibilidade específica.

Certainty scale — visão prática

Podemos pensar de forma aproximada:

must → obrigação, não grau de possibilidade neste foco

will probably → provável

may → possível

might → possível/mais incerto

could → possibilidade/opção.

Mas os significados dependem do contexto.

Modalidade

O termo:

modality

refere-se à forma como o falante apresenta uma situação:

  • obrigatória;
  • possível;
  • aconselhável;
  • permitida;
  • provável.

Os modais ajudam justamente a expressar essas diferenças.

Reading

Texto:

Visitors must show identification at reception. They may leave bags in the lockers near the entrance. Large bags mustn’t be taken into the exhibition area.

Perguntas possíveis:

What is required?

Showing identification.

What is permitted?

Leaving bags in the lockers.

What is prohibited?

Taking large bags into the exhibition area.

Listening

Áudio:

You don’t have to bring a laptop because the school has computers, but you should bring headphones. You may also want to bring a notebook.

Questões podem testar:

required?

recommended?

optional?

É importante distinguir.

Required x recommended x optional

Required

must / have to.

Recommended

should.

Optional

can / may

ou:

don’t have to.

Writing

Exemplo:

Students should prepare before the course starts. They must bring identification on the first day, but they don’t have to bring a computer because laptops are available in the classroom.

Speaking

Pergunta:

What should people do before an important exam?

Resposta:

They should review the main topics and sleep well. They shouldn’t wait until the last minute to study.

Pergunta:

What might you do next weekend?

Resposta:

I might stay home and study, but I may meet some friends if I have time.

Advice ladder

Compare:

You could talk to your teacher.

Sugestão.

You should talk to your teacher.

Recomendação mais direta.

You must talk to your teacher.

Obrigação forte.

A diferença de força é importante.

Permission ladder

Can I leave?

comum.

Could I leave?

mais polido/indireto.

May I leave?

mais formal.

Prohibition

You can’t enter.

Pode indicar:

sem permissão

ou:

impossibilidade.

You mustn’t enter.

Indica claramente:

proibição.

No necessity

You don’t need to come.

Muito próximo de:

You don’t have to come.

Ambas significam:

não é necessário.

Need to

need to

também expressa necessidade.

Exemplo:

I need to finish this today.

Não é um modal puro nesse uso, mas semanticamente está relacionado.

Must x need to

You must submit the form.

Obrigação forte.

You need to submit the form.

Necessidade.

Em alguns contextos, são muito próximos.

Regras de prova

Leia com cuidado palavras como:

required

optional

recommended

allowed

prohibited

possible.

Elas podem corresponder aos modais.

Paraphrases

must = have to / be required to

em muitos contextos.

don’t have to = don’t need to / not necessary.

mustn’t = not allowed / prohibited.

should = it’s a good idea to.

may/might = perhaps / maybe.

can = be allowed to / be able to / possible, dependendo do contexto.

Exemplos de paráfrase

You must show ID.

You are required to show ID.

You don’t have to pay.

Payment isn’t necessary.

You mustn’t enter.

You aren’t allowed to enter.

You should arrive early.

It’s a good idea to arrive early.

It may rain.

Perhaps it will rain.

Erro frequente 1 — to depois de modal

Errado:

You should to study.

Correto:

You should study.

Erro frequente 2 — -s após modal

Errado:

She cans drive.

Correto:

She can drive.

Erro frequente 3 — mustn’t x don’t have to

Errado interpretar:

You don’t have to pay

como:

You mustn’t pay.

A primeira significa:

não é necessário.

A segunda:

proibido.

Erro frequente 4 — has to

Errado:

She have to work.

Correto:

She has to work.

Erro frequente 5 — pergunta com have to

Errado:

Have you to work tomorrow?

No inglês moderno cotidiano:

Do you have to work tomorrow?

Erro frequente 6 — did + had to

Errado:

Did you had to work?

Correto:

Did you have to work?

Depois de:

did

use forma base:

have.

Erro frequente 7 — should para obrigação absoluta

Se uma regra diz:

obrigatório,

não escolha automaticamente:

should.

Use:

must / have to.

Erro frequente 8 — may para certeza

She may arrive at eight.

Não significa:

ela certamente chegará às oito.

Significa:

existe possibilidade.

Quadro geral

Forma Função principal Exemplo
must obrigação forte You must show ID.
have to obrigação/necessidade I have to work.
mustn’t proibição You mustn’t enter.
don’t have to ausência de necessidade You don’t have to pay.
should conselho You should rest.
shouldn’t conselho negativo You shouldn’t wait.
can permissão/possibilidade/capacidade You can use this computer.
could possibilidade/sugestão/pedido We could go by train.
may possibilidade/permissão formal It may rain.
might possibilidade She might come.

Vocabulário-chave

obligation — obrigação

necessity — necessidade

prohibition — proibição

advice — conselho

recommendation — recomendação

possibility — possibilidade

permission — permissão

required — obrigatório

optional — opcional

recommended — recomendado

allowed — permitido

prohibited — proibido

necessary — necessário

unnecessary — desnecessário

perhaps — talvez

maybe — talvez

rule — regra

warning — aviso

Estratégia de prova

Quando encontrar um modal, não analise apenas a gramática.

Pergunte:

Qual é a função?

Se o texto diz:

required

procure:

must / have to.

Se diz:

prohibited

procure:

mustn’t / not allowed.

Se diz:

optional

procure:

don’t have to.

Se diz:

recommended

procure:

should.

Se diz:

perhaps / possible

procure:

may / might / could.

Se diz:

permitted

procure:

can / may / be allowed to.

A diferença entre:

obligation

advice

possibility

é frequentemente mais importante do que a tradução isolada do verbo.

Prática

1. Complete:

Students ___ show their ID before entering.

  1. must
  2. should to
  3. may to
  4. must to

2. Complete:

I ___ work tomorrow because my office is open.

  1. have to
  2. has to
  3. must to
  4. having to

3. Complete:

She ___ wear a uniform at work.

  1. have to
  2. has to
  3. has
  4. musts

4. Complete:

You ___ smoke here. It’s prohibited.

  1. don’t have to
  2. mustn’t
  3. should
  4. may

5. Complete:

You ___ bring a laptop. The school provides computers.

  1. mustn’t
  2. don’t have to
  3. must
  4. should to

6. Complete:

You’re tired. You ___ rest.

  1. should
  2. must to
  3. may to
  4. should to

7. Complete:

You ___ share your password with other people.

  1. shouldn’t
  2. should
  3. may to
  4. can to

8. Complete:

It ___ rain later.

  1. may
  2. may to
  3. should to
  4. musts

9. Complete:

I ___ stay home tonight, but I’m not sure.

  1. might
  2. must
  3. have to definitely
  4. should to

10. Complete:

We ___ go by train instead.

  1. could
  2. could to
  3. could went
  4. can to

11. Escolha a frase correta:

  1. You must to leave.
  2. You must leave.
  3. You must leaves.
  4. You must leaving.

12. Escolha:

  1. She can speaks English.
  2. She can speak English.
  3. She cans speak English.
  4. She can to speak English.

13. Escolha:

You don’t have to pay.

Significa:

  1. Payment is prohibited.
  2. Payment is not necessary.
  3. Payment is compulsory.
  4. You should pay twice.

14. Escolha:

You mustn’t enter.

Significa:

  1. You don’t need to enter.
  2. You aren’t allowed to enter.
  3. You should enter.
  4. You may enter.

15. Escolha:

You should arrive early.

Significa:

  1. Arriving early is recommended.
  2. Arriving early is prohibited.
  3. Arriving early is impossible.
  4. You arrived early yesterday.

16. Escolha:

She might come later.

Significa:

  1. She will definitely come.
  2. Perhaps she will come.
  3. She must come.
  4. She came yesterday.

17. Complete a pergunta:

___ I have to bring my passport?

  1. Do
  2. Must to
  3. Have
  4. Am

18. Complete:

___ she have to work tomorrow?

  1. Does
  2. Do
  3. Has
  4. Is

19. Complete:

___ I use your phone?

  1. Can
  2. Can to
  3. Do can
  4. Am can

20. Complete:

What ___ I do?

  1. should
  2. should to
  3. do should
  4. am should

21. Corrija:

You should to read the instructions.

22. Corrija:

She musts wear a uniform.

23. Corrija:

He don’t have to work tomorrow.

24. Corrija:

Did you had to pay?

25. Complete com mustn’t ou don’t have to:

  1. You ______ use your phone during the exam. It is prohibited.

  2. You ______ print the assignment. Online submission is accepted.

  3. Visitors ______ enter this area without permission.

  4. We ______ bring food because lunch is included.

26. Complete com should, could, may ou might:

  1. You ______ ask the teacher for help. It would be a good idea.

  2. We ______ go by train if you want another option.

  3. It ______ rain later; the forecast is uncertain.

  4. I ______ stay home tonight, but I haven’t decided.

27. Leia:

All visitors must show identification. Large bags mustn’t be taken inside, but visitors can leave them in lockers. Students don’t have to pay on Fridays.

Responda:

  1. What is required?

  2. What is prohibited?

  3. What is permitted?

  4. What is not necessary for students on Fridays?

28. Leia:

You should arrive at least fifteen minutes before the interview. You don’t have to wear formal clothes, but you must bring a copy of your identification. The interview may last about thirty minutes.

Classifique:

  1. arriving early → obligation, advice ou possibility?

  2. formal clothes → required ou optional?

  3. identification → required ou optional?

  4. interview duration → certainty ou possibility?

29. Complete o diálogo:

A: I have an important test tomorrow. What ___ I do tonight?
B: You ___ review the main topics, but you ___ stay up all night.
A: Do I ___ bring my laptop tomorrow?
B: No, you ___ because the school has computers. But you ___ bring your student ID. It’s required.

30. Produção

Escreva um texto de 100 a 120 palavras com o título:

Advice and rules for a new student

Inclua:

  • duas frases com must/have to;
  • uma com mustn’t;
  • uma com don’t have to;
  • duas com should/shouldn’t;
  • uma com can;
  • uma com could;
  • uma com may/might.

Gabarito comentado

1. A — must

must + base verb.

2. A — have to

Com:

I

use:

have to.

3. B — has to

Com:

she

use:

has to.

4. B — mustn’t

A frase informa:

prohibited.

Logo:

mustn’t.

5. B — don’t have to

Os computadores já são fornecidos.

Portanto:

não é necessário trazer laptop.

6. A — should

É um conselho.

7. A — shouldn’t

Compartilhar senha não é recomendado.

8. A — may

Expressa possibilidade.

9. A — might

I’m not sure

indica possibilidade, não obrigação.

10. A — could

É uma possibilidade/sugestão.

11. B

Depois de:

must

use verbo base.

12. B

Depois de:

can

use:

speak.

13. B

don’t have to

significa:

not necessary.

14. B

mustn’t

significa:

prohibited/not allowed.

15. A

should

é recomendação.

16. B

might

indica possibilidade.

17. A — Do

Do I have to…?

18. A — Does

Does she have to…?

Depois de:

does

use:

have

e não:

has.

19. A — Can

Can I use your phone?

20. A — should

What should I do?

21.

You should read the instructions.

22.

She must wear a uniform.

Modais não recebem:

-s.

23.

He doesn’t have to work tomorrow.

24.

Did you have to pay?

Depois de:

did

use:

have.

25.

mustn’t

Uso do telefone é proibido.

don’t have to

Imprimir não é necessário.

mustn’t

Entrada sem permissão é proibida.

don’t have to

Não é necessário levar comida.

26.

should

É um conselho.

could

Apresenta uma opção.

may / might

Ambas podem indicar possibilidade.

may / might

A decisão ainda não foi tomada.

27.

Visitors must show identification.

Obrigação.

Taking large bags inside.

Proibição.

Leaving large bags in lockers.

Permissão.

Paying.

Estudantes não precisam pagar nas sextas-feiras.

28.

advice

O texto usa:

should.

optional

don’t have to wear formal clothes.

required

must bring identification.

possibility

may last.

29.

A: I have an important test tomorrow. What should I do tonight?
B: You should review the main topics, but you shouldn’t stay up all night.
A: Do I have to bring my laptop tomorrow?
B: No, you don’t have to because the school has computers. But you must bring your student ID. It’s required.

30.

Modelo:

Advice and rules for a new student

New students must bring identification on the first day, and they have to complete the registration form before classes begin. Students mustn’t use their phones during tests. However, they don’t have to bring a laptop because the school provides computers. You should arrive a few minutes early, and you shouldn’t wait until the last day to complete assignments. You can use the library during opening hours. If you have difficulty with a subject, you could ask the teacher for extra help. Some classes may finish earlier on Fridays, and the schedule might change during special events, so students should check their messages regularly.

Tarefa de consolidação

Crie quatro grupos.

Obrigação

Escreva cinco frases com:

must

have to.

Exemplos:

Students must show ID.

I have to submit the report today.

Proibição e ausência de necessidade

Crie cinco pares:

You mustn’t use your phone during the exam.

You don’t have to bring a calculator.

Explique por que os significados são diferentes.

Conselho

Escreva dez situações e responda com:

should

shouldn’t

could.

Exemplo:

I can’t understand this chapter.

You should read it again, and you could ask the teacher for help.

Possibilidade

Crie dez previsões usando:

may

might

could.

Exemplos:

It may rain tonight.

The meeting might finish early.

Depois monte uma tabela:

Meaning Main forms
obligation must / have to
prohibition mustn’t
no necessity don’t have to
advice should / shouldn’t
option/suggestion could
possibility may / might / could
permission can / may

Finalize memorizando os contrastes essenciais:

must = obrigação

mustn’t = proibição

have to = obrigação/necessidade

don’t have to = não é necessário

should = conselho

could = possibilidade ou sugestão

may/might = possibilidade

can = permissão, capacidade ou possibilidade prática

E, antes de escolher um modal em uma questão, pergunte:

A frase está dizendo que algo é obrigatório, proibido, recomendado, permitido ou apenas possível?

Identificar essa função é o passo mais importante para escolher o modal correto.

Aula 77 — Passive Voice: introdução

Objetivos

Ao final desta aula, você deverá ser capaz de:

  • compreender o que é Passive Voice;
  • diferenciar Active Voice e Passive Voice;
  • reconhecer quando o foco está na ação, no resultado ou no objeto;
  • formar corretamente estruturas passivas com be + past participle;
  • transformar frases simples da voz ativa para a passiva;
  • usar a Passive Voice principalmente no Simple Present e no Simple Past;
  • reconhecer passivas com modal verbs;
  • compreender quando o agente pode ser omitido;
  • utilizar corretamente by para indicar quem realizou uma ação;
  • reconhecer a Passive Voice em avisos, notícias, textos acadêmicos e instruções;
  • evitar erros comuns com particípios irregulares;
  • aplicar a estrutura em Reading, Listening, Writing e Speaking.

Desenvolvimento

Em inglês, uma ação pode ser apresentada de diferentes maneiras.

Compare:

The company produces smartphones.

Essa frase está na:

Active Voice

Agora:

Smartphones are produced by the company.

Essa frase está na:

Passive Voice

As duas frases descrevem praticamente a mesma situação.

A diferença principal está no:

foco.

Active Voice

Na voz ativa, normalmente temos:

subject + verb + object.

Exemplo:

The company produces smartphones.

Temos:

subject → the company

verb → produces

object → smartphones.

O foco está em:

quem realiza a ação.

Passive Voice

Na voz passiva, o objeto da frase ativa passa a ocupar a posição de sujeito.

Smartphones are produced by the company.

Agora:

smartphones

é o elemento principal da frase.

O foco está:

no que recebe a ação.

Estrutura geral

A Passive Voice é formada por:

be + past participle

Exemplos:

is produced

are made

was built

were invented

can be used.

O verbo:

be

muda de acordo com o tempo verbal.

O verbo principal fica no:

past participle.

Exemplo básico

Active:

People speak English in many countries.

Passive:

English is spoken in many countries.

Observe:

speak → spoken

e:

is

porque:

English

é singular.

Por que usar Passive Voice?

Use a voz passiva quando:

  • quem fez a ação não é importante;
  • quem fez a ação é desconhecido;
  • o resultado é mais importante;
  • queremos enfatizar o objeto ou processo;
  • o estilo do texto pede maior impessoalidade.

Agente desconhecido

My phone was stolen.

Não sabemos necessariamente:

who stole it.

Não precisamos dizer:

by someone.

Agente irrelevante

English is spoken in many countries.

É desnecessário dizer:

by people.

Isso já é óbvio.

Resultado mais importante

The bridge was built in 2010.

O foco está:

na ponte e em sua construção.

Não necessariamente:

em quem construiu.

Textos científicos e acadêmicos

A voz passiva aparece frequentemente em linguagem formal.

Exemplo:

The samples are analyzed in the laboratory.

O foco está:

no procedimento.

Instruções e processos

The file is uploaded to the system.

The information is stored automatically.

The form is checked before submission.

Simple Present Passive

Estrutura:

am / is / are + past participle.

Exemplos:

Coffee is grown in many countries.

These products are sold online.

English is taught at the school.

The rooms are cleaned every day.

Singular

is + past participle.

Exemplos:

The door is locked every night.

The report is checked before publication.

Plural

are + past participle.

Exemplos:

The documents are stored online.

The computers are used by students.

Am

Também é possível:

I am invited to many meetings.

Embora menos frequente em exemplos básicos, a estrutura existe.

Active → Passive no Simple Present

Active:

The company sells computers.

Passos:

computers → novo sujeito

Simple Present → is/are + participle

sell → sold.

Resultado:

Computers are sold by the company.

Outro exemplo

Active:

Teachers use this platform.

Passive:

This platform is used by teachers.

Simple Past Passive

Estrutura:

was / were + past participle.

Exemplos:

The bridge was built in 1998.

The documents were sent yesterday.

The school was opened in 2015.

The computers were repaired last week.

Singular no passado

was + past participle.

The email was sent yesterday.

The building was designed by a famous architect.

Plural no passado

were + past participle.

The tickets were sold online.

The students were invited to the event.

Active → Passive no Simple Past

Active:

Alexander Graham Bell invented the telephone.

Passive:

The telephone was invented by Alexander Graham Bell.

Estrutura:

was + invented.

Outro exemplo

Active:

The police closed the road.

Passive:

The road was closed by the police.

Past participle

A Passive Voice exige atenção ao:

past participle.

Verbos regulares:

clean → cleaned

open → opened

produce → produced

organize → organized.

Verbos irregulares:

Base form Simple Past Past Participle
write wrote written
make made made
build built built
speak spoke spoken
take took taken
give gave given
see saw seen
buy bought bought
sell sold sold
send sent sent
find found found
steal stole stolen
know knew known
choose chose chosen
break broke broken

Exemplos:

The book was written in 1990.

English is spoken here.

The photos were taken yesterday.

The phone was stolen.

By + agent

Quando queremos informar quem realizou a ação, podemos usar:

by + agent.

Exemplo:

The book was written by George Orwell.

The building was designed by a local architect.

The song was performed by the students.

Quando omitir by

Muitas frases passivas não precisam de agente.

My car was stolen.

Não precisamos dizer:

by someone.

Outro:

The streets are cleaned every morning.

Não é importante informar:

by the cleaning staff.

Quando by é importante

Se a identidade do agente é relevante:

The painting was created by Picasso.

The theory was developed by a group of scientists.

Aqui, o agente acrescenta informação importante.

Passiva negativa

Simple Present:

is not / are not + past participle.

Exemplos:

The building is not used at night.

These products aren’t sold here.

Simple Past:

was not / were not + past participle.

Exemplos:

The meeting wasn’t canceled.

The documents weren’t sent yesterday.

Perguntas no Simple Present Passive

Estrutura:

Is/Are + subject + past participle?

Exemplos:

Is English spoken here?

Are these products made locally?

Is the room cleaned every day?

Perguntas no Simple Past Passive

Was/Were + subject + past participle?

Exemplos:

Was the building constructed in 2010?

Were the emails sent yesterday?

Was the problem solved?

Respostas curtas

Is this product made in Brazil?

Yes, it is.

No, it isn’t.

Outro:

Were the documents sent?

Yes, they were.

No, they weren’t.

Passiva com modal verbs

Uma estrutura muito importante:

modal + be + past participle

Exemplos:

can be used

must be completed

should be checked

may be changed.

Can be

This software can be used on different computers.

Tickets can be bought online.

Must be

The form must be completed before Friday.

Identification must be shown at the entrance.

Should be

The document should be checked before submission.

Passwords should be changed regularly.

May be

The schedule may be changed.

The meeting may be canceled.

Modal + be, não modal + is

Errado:

The form must is completed.

Correto:

The form must be completed.

Active x Passive com modal

Active:

Students must complete the form.

Passive:

The form must be completed by students.

Outro:

You can buy tickets online.

Passive:

Tickets can be bought online.

Present Perfect Passive — reconhecimento

Você pode começar a encontrar:

has/have been + past participle.

Exemplos:

The report has been completed.

The tickets have been sold.

Essa estrutura combina:

Present Perfect

com:

Passive Voice.

O foco desta aula, porém, continua sendo:

Simple Present

Simple Past

modal passive.

Compare

Active:

Someone has stolen my bike.

Passive:

My bike has been stolen.

Mesmo sem aprofundar essa estrutura agora, você deve começar a reconhecê-la.

Passive Voice em notícias

Exemplo:

A new hospital was opened yesterday.

O foco é:

hospital.

Não necessariamente:

quem abriu.

Outro:

Three people were rescued after the accident.

O foco está nas pessoas resgatadas.

Passive Voice em textos históricos

The city was founded in 1616.

The building was constructed in the nineteenth century.

The first computer was developed many years ago.

Passive Voice em tecnologia

Data is stored on the server.

Files are uploaded automatically.

The password is encrypted.

The system was updated yesterday.

Educação

Exams are corrected by teachers.

Assignments are submitted online.

Students are evaluated throughout the course.

The test was administered on Monday.

Viagens

Tickets are sold online.

Passports are checked before boarding.

The flight was canceled because of bad weather.

Luggage is inspected at the airport.

Serviços

Payments are accepted by card.

The room is cleaned every morning.

Breakfast is served from 7 to 10.

The package was delivered yesterday.

Produto e fabricação

This phone is made in Korea.

Coffee is produced in several countries.

Cars are manufactured in large factories.

Processos

A passiva é muito usada para descrever etapas.

Exemplo:

First, the documents are checked. Then they are scanned. Finally, they are stored in the system.

O foco está:

no processo.

Não:

em quem executa cada etapa.

Active Voice x Passive Voice

Compare:

The receptionist checks the documents.

Active.

Foco:

receptionist.

The documents are checked at reception.

Passive.

Foco:

documents/process.

Nem toda frase ativa pode virar passiva facilmente

Para formar uma passiva típica, o verbo precisa normalmente ter:

object.

Exemplo:

Maria opened the door.

Tem objeto:

the door.

Passiva:

The door was opened by Maria.

Agora:

Maria slept.

Não existe objeto.

Não formamos normalmente:

was slept by Maria.

Verbos transitivos

Verbos que recebem objeto podem frequentemente formar passiva:

write a book

open a door

build a house

send an email

repair a computer.

Verbos sem objeto

Exemplos:

sleep

arrive

go

come

não formam passivas comuns da mesma maneira.

Como transformar Active em Passive

Use quatro passos.

Passo 1 — identifique o objeto

The company produces laptops.

Objeto:

laptops.

Passo 2 — transforme o objeto em sujeito

Laptops…

Passo 3 — escolha a forma correta de be

A frase está no Simple Present e:

laptops

é plural.

Então:

are.

Passo 4 — use o past participle

produce → produced.

Resultado:

Laptops are produced by the company.

Exemplo no passado

Active:

The school organized the event.

Objeto:

event.

Tempo:

Simple Past.

Singular:

was.

Participio:

organized.

Passive:

The event was organized by the school.

Manter o tempo verbal

A Passive Voice não muda automaticamente o tempo.

Active:

They clean the room every day.

Simple Present.

Passive:

The room is cleaned every day.

Continua:

Simple Present.

Active:

They cleaned the room yesterday.

Simple Past.

Passive:

The room was cleaned yesterday.

Continua:

Simple Past.

Time expressions permanecem

The email was sent yesterday.

The documents are checked every morning.

The road was closed last night.

Erro frequente 1 — esquecer be

Errado:

English spoken in many countries.

Correto:

English is spoken in many countries.

Erro frequente 2 — usar Simple Past em vez de particípio

Errado:

The book was wrote in 1990.

Correto:

The book was written in 1990.

Erro frequente 3 — concordância

Errado:

The documents is checked.

Correto:

The documents are checked.

Erro frequente 4 — passado plural

Errado:

The emails was sent.

Correto:

The emails were sent.

Erro frequente 5 — modal sem be

Errado:

The form must completed.

Correto:

The form must be completed.

Erro frequente 6 — be + verbo base

Errado:

The report is write every week.

Correto:

The report is written every week.

Erro frequente 7 — usar by sem necessidade

Natural:

The hospital was built in 2010.

Menos natural se o agente não importa:

The hospital was built by people in 2010.

Não inclua:

by someone / by people

quando isso não acrescentar informação.

Erro frequente 8 — confundir adjective e passive

Compare:

The door is closed.

Pode significar:

estado — a porta está fechada.

Ou, em contexto:

passiva — a porta é fechada.

O contexto determina a interpretação.

Interested, bored e excited

Palavras como:

interested

bored

excited

podem funcionar como adjetivos.

I’m interested in science.

Isso não precisa ser analisado como uma passiva comum.

Be born

Uma expressão importante:

be born.

Exemplo:

I was born in 2001.

She was born in London.

Não dizemos:

I born.

A estrutura fixa usa:

was/were born.

Made of / made from

The table is made of wood.

O material ainda é reconhecível.

Paper is made from wood.

O material original foi transformado.

Esse contraste pode aparecer em Reading.

Known for

The city is known for its historic buildings.

Significa:

a cidade é conhecida por…

Outra:

Brazil is known for its cultural diversity.

Used for

This tool is used for cutting paper.

Estrutura:

be used for + -ing/noun.

Outro:

Computers are used for many different tasks.

Used to x be used for

Não confunda:

be used for

com:

used to.

This machine is used for cutting metal.

Finalidade.

I used to live there.

Hábito passado.

São estruturas diferentes.

Passive Voice em Reading

Texto:

The museum was opened in 1985. It is visited by thousands of people every year. Tickets are sold online and at the entrance.

Perguntas:

When was the museum opened?

How are tickets sold?

A Passive Voice é comum em textos informativos.

Scanning com Passive Voice

Pergunta:

When was the building constructed?

Texto:

The building was completed in 1925.

Reconheça a paráfrase:

constructed

e:

completed

podem apontar para informação relacionada dependendo da pergunta e contexto.

Listening

Áudio:

The 8:30 train has been canceled. Passengers are asked to use the 9:00 service instead.

Mesmo antes de dominar o Present Perfect Passive, você pode reconhecer:

canceled

e:

are asked.

Avisos

Passengers are requested to remain seated.

Mobile phones must be switched off.

Tickets must be shown before boarding.

A passiva aparece muito em linguagem institucional.

Writing

Em uma descrição de processo:

First, the information is collected. Then it is checked and organized. Finally, the report is produced.

Essa estrutura torna o texto mais impessoal.

Speaking

Embora a voz ativa seja muito comum na fala, a passiva também pode ser útil.

Pergunta:

Where is coffee produced?

Resposta:

Coffee is produced in many countries.

Pergunta:

When was this building constructed?

Resposta:

It was constructed in the twentieth century.

Perguntas típicas

Where is it made?

When was it built?

How is it produced?

Who was it written by?

What is it used for?

Who was it written by?

Exemplo:

Who was Harry Potter written by?

Resposta:

It was written by J. K. Rowling.

Em registros mais formais, estruturas diferentes podem aparecer, mas essa forma é muito comum na comunicação cotidiana.

Present Passive x Past Passive

Compare:

The room is cleaned every day.

Rotina atual.

The room was cleaned yesterday.

Evento passado.

Active ou Passive?

Pergunte:

O importante é quem faz?

Use frequentemente:

Active.

Exemplo:

The teacher explained the lesson.

Pergunte:

O importante é o que aconteceu com algo?

Use frequentemente:

Passive.

Exemplo:

The lesson was explained clearly.

Quadro geral

Tempo/forma Estrutura Exemplo
Simple Present Passive am/is/are + participle The room is cleaned.
Simple Past Passive was/were + participle The room was cleaned.
Modal Passive modal + be + participle The room must be cleaned.
Present Perfect Passive have/has been + participle The room has been cleaned.

Vocabulário-chave

active voice — voz ativa

passive voice — voz passiva

subject — sujeito

object — objeto

agent — agente

past participle — particípio passado

by — por/pelo/pela

produce — produzir

manufacture — fabricar

build — construir

construct — construir

write — escrever

publish — publicar

deliver — entregar

cancel — cancelar

repair — reparar

store — armazenar

use — usar

design — projetar

invent — inventar

Estratégia de prova

Para reconhecer uma Passive Voice, procure:

uma forma do verbo be

seguida por:

past participle.

Exemplos:

is produced

are sold

was built

were sent

must be completed.

Depois pergunte:

Quem ou o quê recebe a ação?

Isso ajuda a diferenciar passiva de ativa.

Em questões de transformação:

  1. encontre o objeto da ativa;
  2. coloque-o no início;
  3. mantenha o tempo verbal;
  4. escolha a forma correta de be;
  5. use o particípio;
  6. acrescente by + agent apenas se necessário.

Prática

1. Identifique a Passive Voice:

  1. They produce cars in this factory.
  2. Cars are produced in this factory.
  3. They are producing cars.
  4. They produced cars.

2. Complete:

English ___ spoken in many countries.

  1. is
  2. does
  3. has
  4. speaking

3. Complete:

These computers ___ used by students.

  1. is
  2. are
  3. was
  4. has

4. Complete:

The bridge ___ built in 2010.

  1. is
  2. was
  3. were
  4. did

5. Complete:

The emails ___ sent yesterday.

  1. was
  2. were
  3. are yesterday
  4. did

6. Complete:

The book was ___ in 1995.

  1. write
  2. wrote
  3. written
  4. writing

7. Complete:

The photos were ___ during the trip.

  1. took
  2. take
  3. taken
  4. taking

8. Complete:

This product is ___ in several countries.

  1. sell
  2. sold
  3. selling
  4. sells

9. Complete:

The form must ___ completed today.

  1. be
  2. is
  3. being
  4. been to

10. Complete:

Tickets can ___ bought online.

  1. be
  2. are
  3. being
  4. been

11. Transforme para Passive Voice:

The company produces laptops.

12. Transforme:

Teachers use this platform.

13. Transforme:

The school organized the event.

14. Transforme:

Someone stole my phone.

Não inclua um agente desnecessário.

15. Transforme:

The students completed the project.

16. Transforme com modal passive:

Students must submit the form before Friday.

17. Transforme:

People can buy tickets online.

18. Transforme:

You should check the document.

19. Escolha a frase correta:

  1. The book was wrote by Orwell.
  2. The book was written by Orwell.
  3. The book written by Orwell.
  4. The book did written by Orwell.

20. Escolha:

  1. The documents is checked every day.
  2. The documents are checked every day.
  3. The documents are check every day.
  4. The documents checked every day.

21. Corrija:

The phone was stole yesterday.

22. Corrija:

These products is sold online.

23. Corrija:

The form must completed before Friday.

24. Corrija:

The emails was sent this morning.

25. Identifique se é Active ou Passive:

  1. The teacher corrected the exams.

  2. The exams were corrected yesterday.

  3. The company sells software.

  4. The software is sold internationally.

  5. The road was closed.

26. Complete o texto:

Coffee ___ (grow) in many countries. After the beans are collected, they ___ (transport) to factories. There, they ___ (process) and ___ (prepare) for sale.

Use Simple Present Passive.

27. Complete:

The museum ___ (open) in 1990. It ___ (design) by a local architect. Today, it ___ (visit) by thousands of people every year.

Use a combinação adequada de Simple Past Passive e Simple Present Passive.

28. Leia:

The new library was opened last year. It is used by students and local residents. Computers can be used free of charge, but food must not be taken into the study area.

Responda:

  1. When was the library opened?

  2. Who uses it?

  3. Can visitors use the computers?

  4. What must not be taken into the study area?

29. Explique a diferença de foco:

  1. A technician repaired the computer.

  2. The computer was repaired by a technician.

30. Produção

Escreva um texto de 100 a 120 palavras descrevendo um processo, serviço ou instituição.

Use:

  • pelo menos três frases no Simple Present Passive;
  • duas no Simple Past Passive;
  • uma com can be;
  • uma com must be;
  • uma com by + agent;
  • pelo menos um verbo irregular no particípio.

Gabarito comentado

1. B

Cars are produced in this factory.

Temos:

are + produced.

Isso forma Simple Present Passive.

2. A — is

English

é singular.

English is spoken…

3. B — are

computers

é plural.

4. B — was

bridge

é singular e a construção ocorreu no passado.

5. B — were

emails

é plural e:

yesterday

indica passado.

6. C — written

write → wrote → written.

7. C — taken

take → took → taken.

8. B — sold

sell → sold → sold.

9. A — be

Modal Passive:

must + be + past participle.

10. A — be

can be bought.

11.

Laptops are produced by the company.

O objeto plural:

laptops

torna-se sujeito.

12.

This platform is used by teachers.

13.

The event was organized by the school.

Simple Past:

organized → was organized.

14.

My phone was stolen.

Não é necessário acrescentar:

by someone.

15.

The project was completed by the students.

16.

The form must be submitted before Friday.

17.

Tickets can be bought online.

18.

The document should be checked.

19. B

write → wrote → written.

20. B

documents → are.

E:

checked

é o particípio.

21.

The phone was stolen yesterday.

steal → stole → stolen.

22.

These products are sold online.

23.

The form must be completed before Friday.

24.

The emails were sent this morning.

25.

  1. Active

teacher realiza a ação.

  1. Passive

exams recebem a ação.

  1. Active

company realiza a ação.

  1. Passive

software recebe a ação.

  1. Passive

road recebe a ação de fechar.

26.

Coffee is grown in many countries. After the beans are collected, they are transported to factories. There, they are processed and are prepared for sale.

Todas as frases descrevem um processo geral.

Por isso:

Simple Present Passive.

27.

The museum was opened in 1990. It was designed by a local architect. Today, it is visited by thousands of people every year.

1990 → Simple Past Passive.

today/every year → Simple Present Passive.

28.

It was opened last year.

Students and local residents.

Yes. The computers can be used free of charge.

Food.

29.

A technician repaired the computer.

O foco principal está no:

technician.

The computer was repaired by a technician.

O foco principal está no:

computer

e no fato de ele ter sido reparado.

O evento é praticamente o mesmo, mas a perspectiva muda.

30.

Modelo:

The community library is located near the city center. It is used by students and local residents every day. Books are organized by subject, and computers can be used free of charge. Visitors must be registered before books can be borrowed. The building was constructed about twenty years ago and was renovated by the city government five years later. Several new study rooms were added during the renovation. Today, identification must be shown when a new library card is requested. Food is not allowed in the reading rooms, but drinks can be taken into a small café area. The library is visited by hundreds of people every week.

Tarefa de consolidação

Crie uma tabela com três colunas:

Active Passive Tense
They clean the room. The room is cleaned. Simple Present
They cleaned the room. The room was cleaned. Simple Past
Students must complete the form. The form must be completed. Modal

Adicione pelo menos 20 pares.

Depois faça uma lista de 30 particípios, especialmente irregulares:

write → written

speak → spoken

take → taken

give → given

steal → stolen

build → built

make → made

send → sent

buy → bought

choose → chosen.

Em seguida, transforme dez frases ativas em passivas.

Depois produza cinco frases em cada grupo:

Simple Present Passive

The documents are checked every day.

Simple Past Passive

The documents were checked yesterday.

Modal Passive

The documents must be checked.

Por fim, revise:

Active Voice → foco em quem faz a ação.

Passive Voice → foco em quem ou no que recebe a ação.

E memorize as estruturas:

am/is/are + past participle

was/were + past participle

modal + be + past participle

Use a pergunta:

O importante aqui é quem fez a ação ou o que aconteceu com o objeto?

Se o agente for desconhecido, irrelevante ou menos importante que o resultado, a Passive Voice frequentemente será a escolha mais natural.

Aula 78 — Reported Speech: introdução

Objetivos

Ao final desta aula, você deverá ser capaz de:

  • compreender o que é Reported Speech;
  • diferenciar Direct Speech e Reported Speech;
  • reconhecer verbos introdutórios como say e tell;
  • transformar afirmações simples do discurso direto para o indireto;
  • compreender mudanças básicas de tempo verbal;
  • reconhecer alterações em pronomes, possessivos e referências de tempo;
  • usar estruturas como said that e told + object + that;
  • relatar perguntas simples com asked;
  • reconhecer mudanças em perguntas de yes/no e wh-questions;
  • compreender ordens e pedidos simples com told/asked + object + to-infinitive;
  • identificar situações em que a mudança de tempo verbal pode não ser necessária;
  • aplicar Reported Speech em Reading, Listening, Writing e Speaking;
  • evitar erros frequentes de estrutura.

Desenvolvimento

O Reported Speech é usado quando contamos o que outra pessoa disse.

Compare:

Maria said, “I am tired.”

Isso é:

Direct Speech

Agora:

Maria said that she was tired.

Isso é:

Reported Speech

A ideia principal permanece, mas a forma muda.

Direct Speech

No discurso direto, repetimos as palavras da pessoa.

Exemplo:

Daniel said, “I need help.”

As palavras:

I need help

são apresentadas diretamente.

Em textos escritos, normalmente aparecem entre:

quotation marks.

Reported Speech

No discurso indireto, relatamos a mensagem.

Daniel said that he needed help.

Não precisamos repetir exatamente as palavras originais.

O importante é transmitir:

o conteúdo.

Verbos introdutórios

Os dois verbos básicos são:

say

e:

tell.

No passado:

said

told.

Say

Estrutura frequente:

say + something.

said + that-clause.

Exemplo:

Laura said that she was busy.

Não precisamos indicar diretamente para quem ela falou.

Tell

Estrutura:

tell + person + something.

Exemplo:

Laura told me that she was busy.

Depois de:

told

normalmente precisamos indicar:

quem recebeu a informação.

Say x tell

Compare:

She said that she was tired.

Correto.

She told me that she was tired.

Correto.

Mas:

She told that she was tired.

Incorreto no padrão básico.

Falta:

objeto.

Outro erro:

She said me that she was tired.

Incorreto.

Use:

She told me…

ou:

She said to me…

Mas para este nível, prefira:

told me.

That

Em Reported Speech, podemos usar:

that.

Exemplo:

He said that he was tired.

Na fala e em textos informais, that frequentemente pode ser omitido:

He said he was tired.

As duas formas são corretas.

Mudança de tempo verbal

Quando o verbo introdutório está no passado:

said

told

é comum ocorrer uma mudança do tempo verbal para um tempo mais passado.

Isso é frequentemente chamado de:

backshift.

Present Simple → Past Simple

Direct:

Anna said, “I work at home.”

Reported:

Anna said that she worked at home.

Mudança:

work → worked.

Present Continuous → Past Continuous

Direct:

Tom said, “I am studying.”

Reported:

Tom said that he was studying.

Mudança:

am studying → was studying.

Present Perfect → Past Perfect

Direct:

Emma said, “I have finished.”

Reported:

Emma said that she had finished.

Mudança:

have finished → had finished.

Simple Past → Past Perfect

Direct:

Daniel said, “I went to the museum.”

Reported:

Daniel said that he had gone to the museum.

Mudança:

went → had gone.

No inglês real, especialmente na fala, o Simple Past pode às vezes permanecer quando a sequência temporal já está clara.

Mas, para introdução ao Reported Speech e para exercícios de prova, aprenda primeiro o padrão:

Simple Past → Past Perfect.

Will → would

Direct:

Maria said, “I will call you.”

Reported:

Maria said that she would call me.

Mudança:

will → would.

Can → could

Direct:

He said, “I can swim.”

Reported:

He said that he could swim.

May → might

Direct:

She said, “I may travel.”

Reported:

She said that she might travel.

Must

Must pode mudar dependendo do sentido.

Em obrigação, frequentemente:

must → had to.

Direct:

He said, “I must leave.”

Reported:

He said that he had to leave.

Mas must pode permanecer em alguns contextos, especialmente em regras que ainda valem.

Para este nível, reconheça principalmente:

must → had to

quando relatamos uma necessidade passada.

Quadro básico de mudanças

Direct Speech Reported Speech
Present Simple Past Simple
Present Continuous Past Continuous
Present Perfect Past Perfect
Simple Past Past Perfect
will would
can could
may might
must had to, em muitos contextos

Exemplo completo

Direct:

Julia said, “I am working on a new project.”

Reported:

Julia said that she was working on a new project.

Mudanças:

I → she

am working → was working.

Pronomes também mudam

Direct:

Peter said, “I like my job.”

Reported:

Peter said that he liked his job.

Mudanças:

I → he

my → his.

Outro exemplo

Direct:

Anna told me, “I will help you.”

Reported:

Anna told me that she would help me.

Mudanças:

I → she

you → me

will → would.

Mudança depende de quem fala

Não existe uma transformação mecânica de:

I → he

sempre.

Depende da pessoa original.

Exemplo:

Maria said, “I am tired.”

Maria said that she was tired.

Mas:

Daniel said, “I am tired.”

Daniel said that he was tired.

You

You também depende do contexto.

Direct:

The teacher told me, “You are late.”

Reported:

The teacher told me that I was late.

Mas:

The teacher told the students, “You are late.”

Reported:

The teacher told the students that they were late.

Possessivos

Direct:

Laura said, “My laptop is broken.”

Reported:

Laura said that her laptop was broken.

Direct:

Daniel said, “Our class starts at six.”

Reported:

Daniel said that their class started at six.

Dependendo de quem:

our

representa.

Referências de tempo

Quando mudamos a perspectiva temporal, algumas expressões também podem mudar.

Exemplos frequentes:

now → then

today → that day

tonight → that night

yesterday → the day before

tomorrow → the next day / the following day

last week → the week before

next week → the following week

ago → before.

Today

Direct:

She said, “I am busy today.”

Reported:

She said that she was busy that day.

Tomorrow

Direct:

He said, “I will call tomorrow.”

Reported:

He said that he would call the next day.

Yesterday

Direct:

Emma said, “I saw him yesterday.”

Reported:

Emma said that she had seen him the day before.

Here → there

Também pode haver mudança de lugar.

here → there.

Direct:

She said, “I like it here.”

Reported:

She said that she liked it there.

Isso depende da mudança real de perspectiva.

This e these

Podem mudar para:

this → that

these → those.

Direct:

He said, “This book is interesting.”

Reported:

He said that that book was interesting.

Na prática, muitas vezes reformulamos para evitar repetição pouco natural:

He said that the book was interesting.

Backshift não é sempre obrigatório

Se a informação continua verdadeira, o tempo pode permanecer em alguns contextos.

Exemplo:

Direct:

The teacher said, “Water boils at 100°C.”

Reported:

The teacher said that water boils at 100°C.

Não precisamos mudar para:

boiled

porque a informação continua sendo um fato geral.

Outro exemplo

Direct:

She said, “I live in London.”

Se ela ainda mora lá, alguém pode dizer:

She said that she lives in London.

Mas em exercícios tradicionais de transformação, frequentemente aparece:

She said that she lived in London.

Os dois podem existir dependendo do contexto.

Para provas, observe a convenção exigida pelo exercício.

Se o reporting verb está no presente

Se usamos:

says

tells

não há necessidade normal de backshift.

Direct:

Maria says, “I am tired.”

Reported:

Maria says that she is tired.

Outro:

He tells me, “I work at home.”

Reported:

He tells me that he works at home.

Reported statements

A forma mais simples é:

said/told + statement.

Exemplo:

“I am hungry.”

She said that she was hungry.

“We are leaving.”

They said that they were leaving.

Negativas

Direct:

He said, “I don’t like coffee.”

Reported:

He said that he didn’t like coffee.

Outro:

She said, “I haven’t finished.”

Reported:

She said that she hadn’t finished.

Reported questions — introdução

Também podemos relatar perguntas.

Direct:

She asked, “Are you tired?”

Reported:

She asked if I was tired.

Ou:

She asked whether I was tired.

Yes/No Questions

Para perguntas cuja resposta é:

yes/no

usamos:

asked + if/whether + subject + verb.

Exemplo:

“Do you like English?”

She asked if I liked English.

Sem ordem de pergunta

Atenção:

No Reported Speech, usamos ordem de afirmação.

Direct:

“Are you tired?”

Reported:

She asked if I was tired.

Não:

She asked if was I tired.

Do/does/did desaparecem

Direct:

“Do you work here?”

Reported:

He asked if I worked there.

Não:

He asked if I did work there

como transformação básica.

Pergunta no passado

Direct:

“Did you see Anna?”

Reported:

She asked if I had seen Anna.

Whether

whether

pode substituir:

if

em muitas yes/no questions.

Exemplo:

He asked whether I needed help.

Neste nível, if é normalmente mais simples.

Wh-questions

Quando a pergunta começa com:

what

where

when

why

who

how

mantemos a question word.

Direct:

“Where do you live?”

Reported:

She asked where I lived.

Outro exemplo

Direct:

“Why are you late?”

Reported:

The teacher asked why I was late.

Outro

Direct:

“When will you arrive?”

Reported:

She asked when I would arrive.

Não use if com wh-question

Errado:

She asked if where I lived.

Correto:

She asked where I lived.
