Ordem de declaração

Direct:

Where are you going?

Reported:

She asked where I was going.

Não:

She asked where was I going.

Reported commands

Podemos relatar ordens e instruções.

Estrutura:

told + object + to + base verb.

Direct:

The teacher said, “Open your books.”

Reported:

The teacher told the students to open their books.

Pedido

Estrutura comum:

asked + object + to + base verb.

Direct:

“Please help me.”

Reported:

She asked me to help her.

Ordem negativa

told + object + not to + verb.

Direct:

“Don’t use your phone.”

Reported:

The teacher told us not to use our phones.

Pedido negativo

“Please don’t leave.”

Reported:

She asked me not to leave.

Say não é usado da mesma forma

Errado:

The teacher said us to open the books.

Correto:

The teacher told us to open the books.

Asked x told

asked

para:

  • perguntas;
  • pedidos.

told

para:

  • informações com objeto;
  • ordens/instruções.

Comparação

Direct:

“Are you ready?”

Reported:

She asked if I was ready.

Direct:

“Please sit down.”

Reported:

She asked me to sit down.

Direct:

“Sit down.”

Reported:

She told me to sit down.

Reported Speech em conversas

Direct:

A: “I’m tired.”
B: “I’ll make some coffee.”

Depois:

Anna said that she was tired, and Ben said that he would make some coffee.

Em Reading

Texto:

Sarah said that she had already finished her assignment and that she would submit it later that day.

Você precisa reconhecer:

finished before the reporting point

e:

future from a past perspective.

Em Listening

Você pode ouvir:

Tom said he couldn’t come because he had to work.

Informações:

couldn’t come

had to work.

Uma questão pode perguntar:

Why couldn’t Tom come?

Resposta:

Because he had to work.

Em notícias

Reported Speech aparece muito em:

news

interviews

reports.

Exemplo:

The company said that the new product would be available in June.

Em textos acadêmicos

The researcher explained that the results were preliminary.

Aqui o autor não cita diretamente, mas relata a informação.

Em Writing

Você pode usar para contar uma conversa.

Exemplo:

I spoke to the receptionist yesterday. She told me that the room was available and said that I could check in after 2 p.m.

Em Speaking

Pergunta:

What did your teacher say?

Resposta:

She said that the test would be on Friday.

Pergunta:

What did he ask you?

Resposta:

He asked me if I needed help.

Said x told — revisão prática

He said that…

He told me that…

Nunca:

He told that…

em uso padrão.

Nunca:

He said me…

no padrão básico.

Reported Speech com would

Direct:

“I will help you.”

Reported:

He said that he would help me.

Aqui:

would

não é necessariamente Second Conditional.

É:

future in the past.

Could também pode ter diferentes origens

Direct:

“I can help.”

Reported:

She said that she could help.

Aqui:

could

é resultado do backshift de can.

Não necessariamente habilidade passada original.

Had to

Direct:

“I must leave now.”

Reported:

He said that he had to leave then.

Changes table

Direct Reported
am/is was
are were
work worked
am working was working
have finished had finished
went had gone
will would
can could
may might
must had to
today that day
tomorrow the next day
yesterday the day before
now then
here there

Nem toda mudança deve ser automática

Contexto importa.

Imagine:

Monday: “The meeting is on Friday.”

No mesmo dia, você relata:

She said that the meeting is on Friday.

Isso pode ser natural porque:

Friday ainda está no futuro e a informação continua atual.

Por isso, Reported Speech real é mais flexível que tabelas escolares.

Ainda assim, tabelas de backshift são essenciais para aprender o sistema.

Erro frequente 1 — said me

Errado:

She said me that she was tired.

Correto:

She told me that she was tired.

Ou:

She said that she was tired.

Erro frequente 2 — told sem objeto

Errado:

She told that she was tired.

Correto:

She told me that she was tired.

Erro frequente 3 — não mudar pronome

Direct:

Maria said, “I am tired.”

Errado:

Maria said that I was tired.

Correto:

Maria said that she was tired.

Erro frequente 4 — reported question com ordem interrogativa

Errado:

She asked where did I live.

Correto:

She asked where I lived.

Erro frequente 5 — do/does em reported question

Errado:

He asked if did I like coffee.

Correto:

He asked if I liked coffee.

Erro frequente 6 — tell + infinitive sem objeto

Errado:

The teacher told to study.

Correto:

The teacher told us to study.

Erro frequente 7 — ordem negativa

Errado:

She told me to not go.

Embora essa ordem possa aparecer em alguns contextos reais, a forma mais padrão ensinada é:

She told me not to go.

Erro frequente 8 — will permanece sem motivo

Direct:

He said, “I will call.”

Padrão tradicional:

He said that he would call.

Erro frequente 9 — confundindo asked e told

Pergunta:

“Where do you live?”

Use:

asked.

Não:

told.

Reported Speech e Past Perfect

O Past Perfect aparece bastante porque:

Simple Past → Past Perfect

e:

Present Perfect → Past Perfect.

Compare:

Direct:

“I finished the report.”

Reported:

She said that she had finished the report.

Direct:

“I have finished the report.”

Reported:

She said that she had finished the report.

Duas formas diretas diferentes podem resultar na mesma estrutura relatada.

O contexto pode ser necessário para reconstruir a fala original.

Paráfrases

Direct:

“I can’t come.”

Reported:

He said that he couldn’t come.

Paráfrase:

He said he was unable to come.

Outro:

She told me to wait.

Paráfrase:

She said that I should wait.

Não são estruturalmente idênticas, mas podem transmitir mensagem semelhante dependendo do contexto.

Vocabulário-chave

direct speech — discurso direto

reported speech — discurso indireto

reporting verb — verbo de relato

say — dizer

tell — contar/dizer a alguém

ask — perguntar/pedir

statement — afirmação

question — pergunta

command — ordem

request — pedido

backshift — recuo/mudança para um tempo verbal anterior

pronoun — pronome

quotation marks — aspas

whether — se

the day before — no dia anterior

the next day — no dia seguinte

then — então/naquele momento

Estratégia de prova

Ao transformar Direct Speech em Reported Speech, use esta sequência:

1. Identifique quem falou.

2. Escolha said, told ou asked.

3. Ajuste os pronomes.

4. Verifique se é necessário fazer backshift.

5. Ajuste referências de tempo e lugar.

6. Se for pergunta, remova a ordem interrogativa.

7. Se for ordem/pedido, use to + verb.

Para afirmações:

said that…

told + person + that…

Para yes/no questions:

asked if/whether…

Para wh-questions:

asked + wh-word…

Para ordens:

told + person + to…

Para pedidos:

asked + person + to…

Prática

1. Transforme:

Maria said, “I am tired.”

2. Transforme:

Daniel said, “I work at home.”

3. Transforme:

Anna said, “I am studying.”

4. Transforme:

Peter said, “I have finished the report.”

5. Transforme:

Laura said, “I went to the museum.”

6. Transforme:

Mark said, “I will call you.”

Considere que ele falou com você.

7. Transforme:

Sarah said, “I can help.”

8. Transforme:

Tom said, “I may be late.”

9. Transforme:

Emma said, “I must leave now.”

10. Escolha a frase correta:

  1. She said me that she was tired.
  2. She told me that she was tired.
  3. She told that she was tired.
  4. She said me she tired.

11. Escolha:

  1. He said that he would call.
  2. He said that he will called.
  3. He told that he would call.
  4. He said me that he would call.

12. Complete:

Laura told ___ that she was busy.

  1. me
  2. that only
  3. said
  4. to me that without object

13. Transforme:

She said, “I am busy today.”

Use uma referência temporal alterada.

14. Transforme:

He said, “I will travel tomorrow.”

15. Transforme:

Anna said, “I saw Peter yesterday.”

16. Transforme a pergunta:

She asked, “Are you tired?”

17. Transforme:

He asked, “Do you like coffee?”

18. Transforme:

The teacher asked, “Where do you live?”

19. Transforme:

Maria asked, “Why are you late?”

20. Transforme:

Daniel asked, “When will you arrive?”

21. Transforme a ordem:

The teacher said, “Open your books.”

Considere que falou aos alunos.

22. Transforme:

My mother said, “Don’t forget your keys.”

Considere que falou com você.

23. Transforme o pedido:

Anna said, “Please help me.”

24. Transforme:

The doctor said, “Please sit down.”

Use:

asked.

25. Corrija:

She asked where did I live.

26. Corrija:

He asked if was I ready.

27. Corrija:

The teacher told to us study.

28. Complete o texto:

Direct speech:

Tom said, “I am working on a new project. I started it last week, and I will finish it next month.”

Transforme o trecho inteiro para Reported Speech.

29. Complete:

Direct speech:

Emma asked, “Do you need help?”
I said, “Yes. I can’t open this file.”

Transforme para Reported Speech.

30. Produção

Crie um diálogo de 6 a 8 falas entre duas pessoas. Depois reescreva o conteúdo como um pequeno parágrafo em Reported Speech.

O diálogo deve conter:

  • duas afirmações;
  • uma yes/no question;
  • uma wh-question;
  • um pedido;
  • uma ordem ou instrução;
  • uma frase com will;
  • uma frase com can.

Gabarito comentado

1.

Maria said that she was tired.

Mudanças:

I → she

am → was.

2.

Daniel said that he worked at home.

work → worked.

3.

Anna said that she was studying.

am studying → was studying.

4.

Peter said that he had finished the report.

Present Perfect → Past Perfect.

5.

Laura said that she had gone to the museum.

No padrão tradicional:

Simple Past → Past Perfect.

go → went → gone.

6.

Mark said that he would call me.

Mudanças:

I → he

will → would

you → me.

7.

Sarah said that she could help.

can → could.

8.

Tom said that he might be late.

may → might.

9.

Emma said that she had to leave then.

must → had to

now → then.

10. B

told

precisa do objeto:

me.

11. A

said that…

e:

will → would.

12. A — me

told + person + that…

13.

She said that she was busy that day.

today → that day.

14.

He said that he would travel the next day.

will → would

tomorrow → the next day.

15.

Anna said that she had seen Peter the day before.

saw → had seen

yesterday → the day before.

16.

She asked if I was tired.

Ou:

She asked whether I was tired.

Observe:

subject + verb

e não ordem interrogativa.

17.

He asked if I liked coffee.

do

desaparece.

like → liked.

18.

The teacher asked where I lived.

Não:

where did I live.

19.

Maria asked why I was late.

20.

Daniel asked when I would arrive.

will → would.

21.

The teacher told the students to open their books.

Estrutura:

told + object + to + verb.

22.

My mother told me not to forget my keys.

Ordem negativa:

not to + verb.

23.

Anna asked me to help her.

asked + person + to-infinitive.

24.

The doctor asked me to sit down.

25.

Errado:

She asked where did I live.

Correto:

She asked where I lived.

Reported questions usam ordem de afirmação.

26.

He asked if I was ready.

27.

The teacher told us to study.

Estrutura correta:

told + object + to + verb.

28.

Tom said that he was working on a new project. He said that he had started it the week before and that he would finish it the following month.

Mudanças:

am working → was working

started → had started

last week → the week before

will → would

next month → the following month.

29.

Emma asked if I needed help. I said that I did and explained that I couldn’t open the file.

Uma transformação mais literal também seria:

Emma asked if I needed help. I said that I did because I couldn’t open the file.

A estrutura:

can’t → couldn’t.

30.

Modelo de diálogo:

Anna: “I’m preparing a presentation.”
Ben: “I can help you.”
Anna: “Will you check my slides?”
Ben: “Yes. Where is the file?”
Anna: “Please open the folder on my laptop.”
Ben: “Send me the final version tonight.”
Anna: “I will.”

Reported Speech:

Anna said that she was preparing a presentation. Ben said that he could help her. Anna asked if he would check her slides, and Ben asked where the file was. Anna asked him to open the folder on her laptop. Ben told her to send him the final version that night. Anna said that she would.

Tarefa de consolidação

Crie uma tabela com três colunas:

Direct Speech Reported Speech Change
“I am tired.” She said that she was tired. am → was
“I will call.” He said that he would call. will → would
“I can help.” She said that she could help. can → could

Adicione pelo menos 20 exemplos.

Depois crie cinco grupos.

Statements

Transforme dez afirmações usando:

said that

e:

told me that.

Yes/No Questions

Transforme cinco perguntas usando:

asked if

ou:

asked whether.

Wh-Questions

Transforme cinco perguntas com:

where

when

why

what

how.

Commands

Transforme cinco ordens usando:

told + object + to-infinitive.

Requests

Transforme cinco pedidos usando:

asked + object + to-infinitive.

Depois revise as principais mudanças:

Present Simple → Past Simple

Present Continuous → Past Continuous

Present Perfect → Past Perfect

Simple Past → Past Perfect

will → would

can → could

may → might

must → had to, em muitos contextos

today → that day

tomorrow → the next day

yesterday → the day before

now → then

Finalize memorizando quatro estruturas:

She said that…

She told me that…

She asked if/where…

She told/asked me to…

E use a pergunta central:

Estou repetindo exatamente as palavras da pessoa ou estou relatando o conteúdo do que ela disse?

Quando o foco é relatar a mensagem a partir de outra perspectiva, o Reported Speech é a estrutura adequada.

Aula 79 — Relative clauses: ampliação

Objetivos

Ao final desta aula, você deverá ser capaz de:

  • revisar o conceito de relative clauses;
  • diferenciar defining e non-defining relative clauses em nível introdutório;
  • usar corretamente who, which, that, whose e where;
  • compreender o uso de when em orações relativas;
  • reconhecer quando o pronome relativo funciona como sujeito ou objeto;
  • omitir o pronome relativo quando isso for possível;
  • evitar repetição desnecessária de pronomes;
  • usar relative clauses para unir ideias e produzir textos mais naturais;
  • reconhecer relative clauses em Reading;
  • empregar essas estruturas em Writing e Speaking;
  • usar relative clauses como estratégia de comunicação quando não souber uma palavra;
  • evitar erros frequentes de concordância, pontuação e escolha do pronome relativo.

Desenvolvimento

As relative clauses são orações usadas para acrescentar informações sobre:

a person

a thing

a place

a time

possession.

Exemplo:

The woman who works here is very helpful.

A oração:

who works here

dá mais informação sobre:

the woman.

Outro:

This is the book that I bought yesterday.

A oração:

that I bought yesterday

explica qual livro estamos mencionando.

Estrutura básica

Normalmente temos:

noun + relative pronoun + relative clause.

Exemplo:

The student who answered the question got an extra point.

Temos:

noun → the student

relative pronoun → who

relative clause → answered the question.

Who

Usamos who principalmente para:

people.

Exemplos:

The teacher who helped me was very patient.

I know a student who speaks three languages.

The woman who called you is my manager.

Which

Usamos which para:

things

e frequentemente:

animals.

Exemplos:

The computer which is on the desk is mine.

I bought a book which explains the topic clearly.

The dog which lives next door is very friendly.

That

That pode substituir who ou which em muitas defining relative clauses.

Exemplos:

The man that works here is my uncle.

The book that I bought was expensive.

Portanto:

who → people

which → things

that → people or things

em muitos contextos definidores.

Where

Usamos where para:

places.

Exemplo:

This is the school where I studied.

Outro:

I know a café where we can work quietly.

Outro:

The city where she lives is very large.

Whose

Whose indica:

possession.

Exemplo:

I know a student whose brother is a doctor.

Aqui:

whose brother

significa:

the student’s brother.

Outro:

The woman whose car was stolen called the police.

When

When pode ser usado com palavras relacionadas a tempo.

Exemplos:

I remember the day when we first met.

That was the year when I started university.

Summer is the season when many people travel.

Em muitos casos:

when

pode ser omitido ou substituído por outras estruturas.

Mas, neste nível, concentre-se em reconhecer:

time noun + when.

Defining Relative Clauses

Uma defining relative clause identifica exatamente a pessoa ou coisa de que estamos falando.

Exemplo:

The student who sits near the door is absent today.

Sem:

who sits near the door

não sabemos qual estudante.

Portanto, essa informação é:

essential.

Outro exemplo

The laptop that I bought last year is already broken.

A relative clause:

that I bought last year

identifica qual laptop.

Sem vírgulas

Defining relative clauses normalmente não usam vírgulas.

Correto:

The book that I borrowed is excellent.

Não:

The book, that I borrowed, is excellent.

Non-defining Relative Clauses

Uma non-defining relative clause acrescenta informação extra.

Exemplo:

My brother, who lives in São Paulo, is visiting us.

Já sabemos quem é:

my brother.

A informação:

who lives in São Paulo

é adicional.

Uso de vírgulas

Non-defining relative clauses ficam entre vírgulas.

Maria, who works at the university, is traveling this week.

Se retirarmos:

who works at the university

a frase principal continua identificando Maria claramente.

Defining x Non-defining

Compare:

The students who studied passed the exam.

Significa:

os estudantes que estudaram passaram.

Isso pode sugerir que:

nem todos estudaram.

Agora:

The students, who studied for several weeks, passed the exam.

A oração entre vírgulas apenas acrescenta informação sobre um grupo já identificado.

That em non-defining clauses

Em geral, não usamos that em non-defining relative clauses.

Correto:

My laptop, which I bought last year, is still working well.

Evite:

My laptop, that I bought last year, is still working well.

Who em defining e non-defining

Defining:

The man who called me was polite.

Non-defining:

Daniel, who called me yesterday, was very polite.

Which em defining e non-defining

Defining:

The phone which is on the table is mine.

Non-defining:

My phone, which I bought last year, is already slow.

Subject relative pronoun

O pronome relativo pode ser o sujeito da oração.

Exemplo:

The woman who works here is my aunt.

Na relative clause:

who works here

who realiza a ação:

works.

Por isso, não podemos omitir who.

Não:

The woman works here is my aunt.

Object relative pronoun

O pronome relativo também pode funcionar como objeto.

Exemplo:

The book that I bought was expensive.

Na relative clause:

I bought that.

O sujeito é:

O objeto é:

that/the book.

Nesse caso, em defining clauses, podemos frequentemente omitir o pronome relativo.

The book I bought was expensive.

Outro exemplo

The film which we watched was excellent.

Também:

The film we watched was excellent.

Subject x object

Compare:

The man who called me is my teacher.

Who é sujeito de:

called.

Não pode ser omitido.

Agora:

The man who I called is my teacher.

Who é objeto de:

called.

Pode ser omitido em uma defining clause:

The man I called is my teacher.

Teste prático

Depois do pronome relativo, veja o que aparece.

who works…

Não há outro sujeito.

Então:

who

é sujeito.

Agora:

who I met…

Temos:

I

como sujeito.

Então:

who

é objeto.

That como objeto

The book that I read was useful.

Pode virar:

The book I read was useful.

Which como objeto

The program which we installed is free.

Pode virar:

The program we installed is free.

Omissão não ocorre normalmente quando o relativo é sujeito

Correto:

The student who answered was correct.

Não:

The student answered was correct.

Who x whom

Você pode encontrar:

whom

principalmente em registros formais quando a pessoa é objeto.

Exemplo:

The person whom I contacted replied quickly.

Em inglês cotidiano:

The person who I contacted…

ou:

The person I contacted…

são muito comuns.

Para B1, é suficiente reconhecer whom sem precisar priorizá-lo na produção.

Preposições

Compare:

The person who I spoke to was helpful.

Essa forma é muito natural.

Mais formal:

The person to whom I spoke was helpful.

No nível atual, priorize:

relative pronoun + clause + preposition.

Exemplo:

The company that I work for is expanding.

The person I talked to was helpful.

Where x which + preposition

Compare:

This is the hotel where we stayed.

Também:

This is the hotel which we stayed at.

Ou:

This is the hotel that we stayed at.

Ou, omitindo o objeto:

This is the hotel we stayed at.

Whose para pessoas

I met a woman whose daughter studies medicine.

Não:

whose her daughter.

Whose já indica posse.

Whose para coisas

Também pode ser usado com coisas, especialmente em registros mais formais.

A company whose products are sold worldwide…

Aqui:

whose products

significa:

the company’s products.

Erro de repetição

Errado:

The man who he works here is my uncle.

Correto:

The man who works here is my uncle.

Who já funciona como sujeito.

Outro erro:

The book that I bought it was expensive.

Correto:

The book that I bought was expensive.

That já representa o objeto.

Relative clauses para combinar frases

Temos:

I know a woman. She works at the hospital.

Podemos unir:

I know a woman who works at the hospital.

Outro:

I bought a laptop. It was very expensive.

I bought a laptop which was very expensive.

Com objeto

I bought a book. You recommended the book.

I bought the book that you recommended.

Ou:

I bought the book you recommended.

Com lugar

This is the café. We met there.

This is the café where we met.

Com posse

I know a student. His father is a teacher.

I know a student whose father is a teacher.

Com tempo

I remember the day. We first met on that day.

I remember the day when we first met.

Relative clauses em descrições de pessoas

A good teacher is someone who explains ideas clearly.

A reliable friend is someone who helps you when you have problems.

Definições

Essa estrutura é muito útil em provas orais.

Exemplo:

A pharmacist is a person who works with medicines.

A library is a place where people can borrow books.

A charger is a device that provides power to a battery.

Estratégia de circumlocution

Se você esquecer uma palavra durante o Speaking, use relative clauses.

Imagine que você esqueceu:

dentist.

Pode dizer:

It’s a person who takes care of your teeth.

Esqueceu:

refrigerator.

It’s a machine that keeps food cold.

Esqueceu:

library.

It’s a place where you can borrow books.

Isso permite continuar falando.

Objetos

It’s something that you use to open a door.

Resposta:

a key.

Outro:

It’s a device that you use to take photos.

Resposta possível:

a camera.

Lugares

It’s a place where you can buy medicine.

pharmacy.

It’s a place where planes arrive and leave.

airport.

Pessoas

It’s someone who teaches students.

teacher.

Defining clauses em Reading

Texto:

Students who want to participate in the course must register online.

Isso não significa:

todos os estudantes.

Significa:

apenas os estudantes que querem participar.

Essa restrição é importante.

Outro exemplo

Employees who work at night receive an additional payment.

A oração identifica:

which employees.

Non-defining clauses em Reading

The city museum, which was opened in 1985, receives thousands of visitors.

A informação principal:

the museum receives thousands of visitors.

A informação adicional:

opened in 1985.

Pontuação pode mudar o significado

Compare:

My brothers who live in Rio are coming.

Pode sugerir:

tenho vários irmãos, mas apenas os que moram no Rio vêm.

Agora:

My brothers, who live in Rio, are coming.

Sugere:

meus irmãos moram no Rio e estão vindo.

As vírgulas influenciam a interpretação.

Who ou that?

Defining:

The woman who works here…

The woman that works here…

As duas são possíveis em muitos contextos.

Em pessoas, who costuma ser uma escolha muito natural.

Which ou that?

Defining:

The laptop which I bought…

The laptop that I bought…

Ambas possíveis.

Na fala cotidiana, that é muito frequente.

That não substitui where diretamente em toda frase

This is the place where I work.

Também:

This is the place that I work at.

Mas não:

This is the place that I work

se a construção exigir a preposição:

work at a place.

Where com lugar

The office where I work…

Não precisa de:

at.

Evite:

the office where I work at.

Use uma das duas:

the office where I work

ou:

the office that I work at.

When com tempo

the year when I graduated.

Também:

the year I graduated.

Em defining clauses, when pode frequentemente ser omitido.

Whose x who’s

Não confunda:

whose

com:

who’s.

Whose:

posse.

The woman whose phone rang…

Who’s:

who is

ou:

who has.

Who’s calling?

Relative clause + verb agreement

O verbo concorda com o substantivo representado pelo pronome relativo.

The student who works here…

Singular:

works.

The students who work here…

Plural:

work.

One of the students who…

Estruturas de concordância mais complexas podem aparecer em níveis mais altos.

Neste nível, concentre-se em identificar claramente:

singular noun → singular verb

plural noun → plural verb.

Relative clauses com superlativos

Exemplo:

It’s the best book that I’ve read this year.

Outro:

This is the most interesting place that we’ve visited.

That é muito comum nessas estruturas.

Relative clauses com something, anything, everything

Exemplos:

I need something that works offline.

Is there anything that I can do?

Everything that we need is here.

Someone / anyone

I need someone who can help me.

Is there anyone who speaks English?

All

That’s all that I know.

Relative clauses com Present Perfect

This is the best film that I’ve seen this year.

She is someone who has helped me a lot.

Com Passive Voice

This is a product that is made locally.

The building, which was constructed in 1920, is now a museum.

Assim, relative clauses podem combinar conteúdos anteriores.

Com modais

I need a computer that can run this program.

We need someone who can speak Spanish.

This is a place where you can study quietly.

Com conditionals

I need a hotel that will be affordable if we stay for a week.

Ou, mais naturalmente:

I need a hotel that is affordable and has free Wi-Fi.

Relative clauses em anúncios

We are looking for candidates who have experience in customer service.

The course is designed for students who want to improve their English.

Em notícias

The company, which was founded in 2010, has opened a new office.

Em turismo

We visited a village that is famous for its traditional architecture.

The hotel where we stayed was very quiet.

Em tecnologia

I use an app that helps me organize my tasks.

The laptop which I bought last year still works well.

Em educação

Students who complete all activities receive a certificate.

The library, which is open until 9 p.m., has several study rooms.

Em trabalho

Employees who work remotely use an online platform.

The manager, who joined the company last year, introduced the new system.

Non-defining clauses e informações próprias

Nomes próprios frequentemente aparecem com non-defining clauses:

London, which is the capital of the UK, attracts millions of tourists.

A identidade de:

London

já está clara.

Informação única

The Sun, which is a star, provides energy to Earth.

Não usamos a relative clause para identificar qual Sol.

Ela apenas adiciona informação.

Sem that em non-defining clauses

Correto:

My teacher, who is from Canada, speaks French.

Não:

My teacher, that is from Canada, speaks French.

Não omita pronome em non-defining clause

Correto:

My laptop, which I bought last year, is slow.

Não:

My laptop, I bought last year, is slow.

A omissão do pronome relativo é uma característica principalmente de defining relative clauses quando ele funciona como objeto.

Defining object omission

The book that I bought…

The book which I bought…

The book I bought…

As três podem ser corretas.

Non-defining object

This book, which I bought yesterday, is excellent.

Não omita:

which.

Uso formal de preposição + which

The system in which the data is stored…

Mais cotidiano:

The system that the data is stored in…

Ou:

The system the data is stored in…

Para B1, concentre-se no padrão cotidiano, mas reconheça formas formais em Reading.

Relative adverb where

Forma cotidiana:

the city where I was born.

Forma mais formal:

the city in which I was born.

Relative adverb when

the day when we met.

Mais formal:

the day on which we met.

Relative clauses e clareza

Compare:

I spoke to a teacher. The teacher teaches English.

Repetitivo.

Melhor:

I spoke to a teacher who teaches English.

Relative clauses ajudam a reduzir repetição.

Produção escrita

Texto básico:

I visited a museum. The museum was in the city center. It had an exhibition. The exhibition was about technology.

Mais natural:

I visited a museum that was in the city center and had an exhibition about technology.

Ou:

I visited a museum in the city center which had an exhibition about technology.

Cuidado com frases muito longas

Relative clauses melhoram o texto, mas não coloque informações demais em uma única frase.

Difícil:

I visited a museum that was built in 1920 that has many rooms that contain objects that were found…

Melhor:

I visited a museum that was built in 1920. It has several rooms containing historical objects.

Use relative clauses para clareza, não apenas para aumentar complexidade.

Erro frequente 1 — repetir o sujeito

Errado:

The man who he called me is my teacher.

Correto:

The man who called me is my teacher.

Erro frequente 2 — repetir o objeto

Errado:

The book that I bought it is interesting.

Correto:

The book that I bought is interesting.

Erro frequente 3 — who para coisa

Evite:

The computer who is broken…

Use:

The computer which is broken…

ou:

The computer that is broken…

Erro frequente 4 — which para pessoa

Evite:

The woman which works here…

Use:

who

ou, em defining clauses:

that.

Erro frequente 5 — where + preposição repetida

Errado:

This is the city where I live in.

Correto:

This is the city where I live.

Ou:

This is the city that I live in.

Erro frequente 6 — whose + possessive

Errado:

The student whose his laptop broke…

Correto:

The student whose laptop broke…

Erro frequente 7 — that em non-defining clause

Evite:

My brother, that lives abroad, is visiting.

Use:

My brother, who lives abroad, is visiting.

Erro frequente 8 — omissão de sujeito relativo

Errado:

The student sits there is my friend.

Correto:

The student who sits there is my friend.

Erro frequente 9 — concordância

Errado:

The students who studies here…

Correto:

The students who study here…

Quadro geral

Referência Pronome/advérbio Exemplo
pessoa who The woman who works here…
pessoa/coisa em defining clause that The book that I bought…
coisa which The laptop which is on the desk…
posse whose The student whose phone rang…
lugar where The school where I studied…
tempo when The year when I graduated…

Defining x Non-defining

Característica Defining Non-defining
informação necessária sim não
vírgulas não sim
that possível normalmente não
omitir objeto relativo possível não
função identificar adicionar informação

Subject x Object

Tipo Exemplo Pode omitir?
sujeito The man who called me… não
objeto The man who I called… sim, em defining
sujeito The book that explains this… não
objeto The book that I bought… sim

Vocabulário-chave

relative clause — oração relativa

relative pronoun — pronome relativo

defining — restritiva/definidora

non-defining — explicativa/não definidora

essential information — informação essencial

extra information — informação adicional

who — que/quem, para pessoas

which — que/o qual, para coisas

that — que, em defining clauses

whose — cujo/cuja/de quem

where — onde

when — quando

subject — sujeito

object — objeto

possession — posse

omit — omitir

comma — vírgula

Estratégia de prova

Primeiro identifique:

A relative clause descreve pessoa, coisa, lugar, tempo ou posse?

Pessoa:

who.

Coisa:

which.

Pessoa ou coisa em defining clause:

that.

Lugar:

where.

Posse:

whose.

Tempo:

when.

Depois pergunte:

A informação é necessária para identificar o substantivo?

Se sim:

defining → sem vírgulas.

Se for apenas informação extra:

non-defining → com vírgulas.

Por fim, verifique:

o pronome relativo é sujeito ou objeto?

Se for objeto em uma defining clause:

pode ser omitido.

Prática

1. Complete:

The woman ___ works here is my aunt.

  1. who
  2. where
  3. whose
  4. when

2. Complete:

The laptop ___ I bought is already broken.

  1. where
  2. that
  3. whose
  4. who

3. Complete:

This is the café ___ we met.

  1. who
  2. which person
  3. where
  4. whose

4. Complete:

I know a student ___ mother is a doctor.

  1. who
  2. whose
  3. which
  4. where

5. Complete:

I remember the day ___ we first met.

  1. when
  2. who
  3. whose
  4. which person

6. Escolha:

The man ___ called me was very polite.

  1. who
  2. where
  3. whose
  4. when

7. Escolha:

The man ___ I called didn’t answer.

  1. who
  2. where
  3. when
  4. whose house only

8. Qual pronome pode ser omitido?

  1. The woman who works here…
  2. The book that I bought…
  3. The student who studies every day…
  4. The dog which lives next door…

9. Complete:

The computer ___ is on the desk is mine.

  1. which
  2. who
  3. whose
  4. where

10. Complete:

The city ___ she lives is very large.

  1. who
  2. where
  3. whose
  4. when

11. Escolha a frase correta:

  1. The man who he works here is my uncle.
  2. The man who works here is my uncle.
  3. The man which works here is my uncle.
  4. The man where works here is my uncle.

12. Escolha:

  1. The book that I bought it was expensive.
  2. The book that I bought was expensive.
  3. The book who I bought was expensive.
  4. The book where I bought was expensive.

13. Complete:

This is the student ___ laptop was stolen.

  1. who
  2. whose
  3. which
  4. where

14. Complete:

The hotel ___ we stayed was comfortable.

  1. where
  2. who
  3. whose person
  4. when

15. Escolha a defining relative clause:

  1. My brother, who lives abroad, is visiting.
  2. The students who completed the course received certificates.
  3. London, which is a large city, attracts tourists.
  4. Maria, who is my friend, called me.

16. Escolha a non-defining relative clause:

  1. The student who arrived late apologized.
  2. The laptop that I bought is expensive.
  3. My laptop, which I bought last year, is slow.
  4. The person I called didn’t answer.

17. Una:

I know a woman. She works at the hospital.

Use:

who.

18. Una:

I bought a book. You recommended it.

Use:

that.

19. Una:

This is the school. I studied there.

Use:

where.

20. Una:

I know a student. His father teaches English.

Use:

whose.

21. Una:

I remember the year. I started university that year.

Use:

when.

22. Omita o relative pronoun se possível:

The film that we watched was excellent.

23. O relative pronoun pode ser omitido? Explique:

The student who answered the question got the highest score.

24. Corrija:

The woman which works at reception is helpful.

25. Corrija:

This is the café where we met at.

26. Corrija:

I know a man whose his daughter studies medicine.

27. Corrija a pontuação e o pronome:

My teacher that comes from Canada speaks French.

Considere que:

my teacher

já identifica uma pessoa específica e a origem canadense é informação adicional.

28. Complete o texto:

I recently started a course ___ focuses on digital skills. The teacher, ___ has worked in technology for many years, explains the topics clearly. We use a platform ___ we can access exercises and videos. I also met a student ___ brother works as a programmer.

29. Leia:

The students who submitted the assignment before Friday received feedback on Monday. The course coordinator, who joined the university last year, reviewed the final reports.

Responda:

  1. Did all students necessarily receive feedback?

  2. Is “who joined the university last year” essential to identify the course coordinator?

  3. Which relative clause is defining?

  4. Which is non-defining?

30. Produção

Escreva um texto de 100 a 120 palavras descrevendo:

uma pessoa, um lugar, um curso, uma tecnologia ou uma instituição fictícia.

Use:

  • duas relative clauses com who;
  • duas com which/that;
  • uma com where;
  • uma com whose;
  • uma non-defining relative clause;
  • uma defining relative clause com pronome relativo omitido.

Gabarito comentado

1. A — who

woman

é pessoa.

2. B — that

laptop

é coisa e:

that I bought

é uma defining relative clause.

Também seria possível:

which I bought.

3. C — where

café

é lugar.

4. B — whose

Indica posse:

the student’s mother.

5. A — when

day

é referência temporal.

6. A — who

who

é sujeito de:

called.

7. A — who

who

é objeto de:

I called.

Também poderíamos omitir:

The man I called…

8. B

The book that I bought…

Aqui:

I

já é o sujeito da relative clause.

Logo:

that

funciona como objeto e pode ser omitido:

The book I bought…

9. A — which

computer

é coisa.

Também poderia ser:

that.

10. B — where

the city where she lives.

11. B

Não repetimos:

who + he.

12. B

Não repetimos o objeto com:

it.

13. B — whose

whose laptop

indica posse.

14. A — where

The hotel where we stayed…

15. B

The students who completed the course…

A clause identifica exatamente quais estudantes receberam certificados.

16. C

My laptop, which I bought last year, is slow.

A informação entre vírgulas é adicional.

17.

I know a woman who works at the hospital.

18.

I bought the book that you recommended.

Também:

I bought the book you recommended.

Como that é objeto, pode ser omitido.

19.

This is the school where I studied.

20.

I know a student whose father teaches English.

21.

I remember the year when I started university.

Também seria possível:

I remember the year I started university.

22.

The film we watched was excellent.

A omissão é possível porque:

we

é o sujeito

e:

that

é objeto.

23.

Não.

who

é o sujeito de:

answered.

Sem ele:

The student answered the question got the highest score.

A estrutura ficaria incorreta.

24.

The woman who works at reception is helpful.

Em uma defining clause com pessoa:

who

é a escolha mais natural.

25.

This is the café where we met.

Ou:

This is the café that we met at.

Não use:

where … at

ao mesmo tempo.

26.

I know a man whose daughter studies medicine.

Whose já expressa posse.

27.

My teacher, who comes from Canada, speaks French.

A relative clause é:

non-defining.

Por isso:

  • usamos vírgulas;
  • preferimos who;
  • não usamos that.

28.

I recently started a course that/which focuses on digital skills. The teacher, who has worked in technology for many years, explains the topics clearly. We use a platform where we can access exercises and videos. I also met a student whose brother works as a programmer.

29.

  1. Não necessariamente.

A frase diz:

The students who submitted the assignment before Friday…

Portanto, o grupo está restrito aos estudantes que entregaram antes de sexta-feira.

  1. Não.

the course coordinator

já identifica a pessoa no contexto.

who submitted the assignment before Friday.

É defining.

who joined the university last year.

É non-defining.

30.

Modelo:

I attend a fictional language center that offers courses for students who want to prepare for international exams. The teacher who teaches my class has worked abroad for several years. She uses an online platform which contains exercises, videos and practice tests. The platform we use in class can also be accessed from home. The school, which was opened five years ago, has several quiet study rooms. There is also a library where students can borrow books and use computers. I often study with a classmate whose sister is also learning English. It is a place that combines technology and traditional teaching methods, which makes the course varied and practical.

Tarefa de consolidação

Monte uma tabela:

Referência Relative word Exemplo
people who The person who called…
things which/that The book that I bought…
places where The school where I studied…
possession whose The student whose laptop…
time when The day when we met…

Depois produza dez pares distinguindo:

subject relative

e:

object relative.

Exemplo:

The man who called me…

The man who I called…

Marque em quais frases o pronome pode ser omitido.

Depois crie cinco pares de:

defining

e:

non-defining.

Exemplo:

The students who studied passed.

The students, who had studied for several weeks, passed.

Em seguida, pratique circumlocution com dez palavras.

Defina sem dizer a palavra.

Exemplo:

It’s a person who teaches students.

teacher.

It’s a place where you can borrow books.

library.

It’s something that you use to open a door.

key.

Finalize revisando:

who → people

which → things

that → people/things em defining clauses

whose → possession

where → places

when → time

Defining → sem vírgulas, informação necessária

Non-defining → com vírgulas, informação extra

Object relative em defining clause → pode ser omitido

Subject relative → não pode ser omitido

Use três perguntas antes de completar uma relative clause:

Estou falando de pessoa, coisa, lugar, tempo ou posse?

A informação é essencial ou adicional?

O pronome relativo funciona como sujeito ou objeto?

Essas três decisões resolvem grande parte das questões de relative clauses no nível B1.

Aula 80 — Gerunds e infinitives: padrões frequentes

Objetivos

Ao final desta aula, você deverá ser capaz de:

  • revisar o uso de gerunds e infinitives;
  • reconhecer verbos seguidos normalmente por verb-ing;
  • reconhecer verbos seguidos normalmente por to + base verb;
  • identificar verbos que aceitam as duas estruturas;
  • compreender casos em que gerund e infinitive mudam o significado;
  • usar gerunds após preposições;
  • usar infinitives para expressar finalidade;
  • reconhecer estruturas com object + infinitive;
  • usar corretamente padrões frequentes em Reading, Writing, Listening e Speaking;
  • evitar erros comuns como enjoy to study ou want studying.

Desenvolvimento

Em inglês, alguns verbos podem ser seguidos por outro verbo.

Quando isso acontece, o segundo verbo pode aparecer principalmente de duas formas:

verb-ing

ou:

to + base verb.

Compare:

I enjoy reading.

e:

I want to read.

As duas frases possuem dois verbos, mas o padrão é diferente.

Não podemos simplesmente escolher entre:

reading

e:

to read

livremente.

Muitas vezes, o primeiro verbo determina a estrutura.

Gerund

Chamamos de gerund a forma:

verb + -ing

quando ela funciona de maneira semelhante a um substantivo ou aparece em determinados padrões verbais.

Exemplos:

reading

studying

traveling

working.

Frase:

Reading is important.

Aqui:

reading

é o sujeito da frase.

Outro:

I enjoy reading.

Aqui, aparece depois de:

enjoy.

Infinitive

Nesta aula, o foco principal será o:

to-infinitive.

Estrutura:

to + base verb.

Exemplos:

to study

to travel

to work

to learn.

Frase:

I want to study.

Outro:

She decided to leave.

Verbos seguidos por gerund

Alguns verbos frequentemente exigem:

verb-ing.

Entre os mais importantes:

enjoy

avoid

finish

keep

mind

suggest

consider

practice

miss

imagine.

Enjoy + -ing

I enjoy reading.

She enjoys traveling.

We enjoy studying together.

Não:

I enjoy to read.

No padrão básico, use:

enjoy + gerund.

Avoid + -ing

Try to avoid making the same mistake.

He avoids driving at night.

We should avoid wasting time.

Finish + -ing

I finished writing the report.

She finished studying at midnight.

Não:

finished to write

no significado de concluir uma atividade.

Keep + -ing

Keep practicing.

She kept asking questions.

They kept working despite the problem.

Indica:

continuar fazendo algo.

Mind + -ing

Muito comum em perguntas:

Do you mind opening the window?

Would you mind waiting a minute?

A ideia é:

você se importaria de…?

Suggest + -ing

She suggested taking the train.

I suggest studying this chapter again.

Não:

She suggested to take the train.

No padrão básico, use:

suggest + -ing.

Consider + -ing

I’m considering changing jobs.

We considered staying at another hotel.

Practice + -ing

You should practice speaking English.

She practices writing every day.

Miss + -ing

I miss living near the beach.

He misses working with his old team.

Imagine + -ing

Imagine living in another country.

Can you imagine working there?

Verbos seguidos por infinitive

Outros verbos normalmente são seguidos por:

to + base verb.

Entre os mais importantes:

want

need

decide

plan

hope

expect

promise

agree

refuse

learn

manage

offer

choose

would like.

Want + infinitive

I want to learn English.

She wants to travel.

They want to leave early.

Não:

I want learning English.

Need + infinitive

I need to study.

We need to leave now.

She needs to buy a new charger.

Decide + infinitive

I decided to stay home.

They decided to take the train.

Plan + infinitive

We’re planning to travel next month.

She plans to apply for the course.

Atenção:

plan

pode aparecer no Continuous:

I’m planning to travel.

Mas o segundo verbo continua:

to travel.

Hope + infinitive

I hope to see you soon.

She hopes to study abroad.

Expect + infinitive

We expect to arrive at six.

They expect to finish tomorrow.

Promise + infinitive

I promise to call you.

She promised to help.

Agree + infinitive

They agreed to meet at eight.

I agreed to help with the project.

Refuse + infinitive

He refused to answer.

She refused to sign the document.

Learn + infinitive

She learned to drive at eighteen.

I’m learning to use the new software.

Manage + infinitive

We managed to finish on time.

Essa estrutura significa:

conseguimos completar algo, apesar da dificuldade.

Offer + infinitive

She offered to help.

He offered to carry my bag.

Choose + infinitive

I chose to stay.

They chose to travel by train.

Would like + infinitive

I’d like to order some coffee.

We’d like to visit the museum.

Não:

I’d like visiting the museum

se a intenção é expressar desejo específico.

Verb + gerund ou infinitive

Alguns verbos podem aceitar as duas estruturas.

Exemplos importantes:

like

love

hate

prefer

start

begin

continue.

Like

I like reading.

I like to read before bed.

As duas formas podem ser corretas.

Frequentemente:

like + -ing

fala de gosto geral pela atividade.

like + infinitive

pode enfatizar hábito, escolha ou algo considerado adequado.

Mas essa distinção não é absoluta.

Love

She loves traveling.

She loves to travel.

Ambas são possíveis.

Hate

I hate waiting.

I hate to wait.

Ambas podem ocorrer, embora:

hate + -ing

seja muito comum para aversão a uma atividade.

Prefer

I prefer walking to driving.

Outra estrutura:

I prefer to walk.

Também:

I’d prefer to stay home tonight.

Start

It started raining.

It started to rain.

As duas formas são possíveis.

Begin

She began studying.

She began to study.

Continue

He continued working.

He continued to work.

Gerund depois de preposição

Uma regra muito importante:

depois de preposição, normalmente usamos verb-ing.

Exemplos:

I’m interested in learning English.

She’s good at solving problems.

Thank you for helping me.

He left without saying goodbye.

Preposições frequentes

in

at

for

about

of

without

before

after.

Exemplos:

Before leaving, check the door.

After finishing the test, review your answers.

She is worried about missing the train.

About + -ing

We talked about moving to another city.

I’m thinking about taking a course.

Without + -ing

He left without paying.

She answered without thinking.

Before/after + -ing

Before going to bed, I check my alarm.

After completing the form, click “Submit”.

Adjective + preposition + gerund

Exemplos:

interested in learning

good at writing

tired of waiting

worried about arriving late.

Be used to + gerund

Uma estrutura importante:

be used to + noun/gerund.

Significa:

estar acostumado a.

Exemplo:

I’m used to waking up early.

She’s used to working at night.

Aqui:

to

é preposição.

Por isso:

waking

working.

Used to + base verb

Não confunda com:

used to + base verb.

Exemplo:

I used to wake up early.

Significa:

eu costumava acordar cedo.

Compare:

I used to work at night.

Hábito passado.

I’m used to working at night.

Estou acostumado a trabalhar à noite.

Look forward to + gerund

Outro caso importante:

look forward to + verb-ing.

Exemplo:

I look forward to meeting you.

We’re looking forward to traveling next month.

Não:

look forward to meet.

Mais uma vez:

to

é preposição nessa expressão.

Infinitive para finalidade

Usamos:

to + base verb

para explicar:

purpose.

Exemplo:

I went to the library to study.

Por quê fui à biblioteca?

to study.

Outro:

She called me to ask a question.

I use this app to organize my tasks.

For x to para finalidade

Compare:

I use this app to study.

Ação/finalidade.

This app is for studying.

Aqui:

for + gerund.

As duas podem expressar finalidade com estruturas diferentes.

Verbo + objeto + infinitive

Alguns verbos aparecem em estruturas como:

verb + person/object + to-infinitive.

Exemplos:

want someone to…

ask someone to…

tell someone to…

advise someone to…

encourage someone to…

invite someone to…

Want + object + infinitive

I want you to help me.

She wants him to call.

Observe:

want + person + to + verb.

Ask + object + infinitive

She asked me to wait.

The teacher asked us to finish the exercise.

Essa estrutura já apareceu em Reported Speech.

Tell + object + infinitive

He told me to sit down.

The teacher told the students to study.

Negativa:

He told me not to leave.

Advise + object + infinitive

The teacher advised us to practice more.

She advised me to arrive early.

Encourage + object + infinitive

The course encourages students to speak English.

Invite + object + infinitive

They invited us to attend the event.

Make e let — sem to

Alguns verbos são diferentes.

Depois de:

make

e:

let

usamos normalmente:

object + base verb

sem to.

Make

The teacher made us rewrite the exercise.

Não:

made us to rewrite.

Let

My parents let me travel alone.

Não:

let me to travel.

Help

Help pode ocorrer com ou sem to.

She helped me carry the boxes.

She helped me to carry the boxes.

As duas formas são possíveis.

Stop + gerund

stop + -ing

significa:

parar uma atividade.

Exemplo:

He stopped smoking.

Significa:

ele deixou de fumar.

Outro:

Stop talking!

Stop + infinitive

stop + to-infinitive

significa:

parar outra atividade para fazer algo.

Exemplo:

We stopped to eat.

Significa:

interrompemos nossa atividade para comer.

Compare

She stopped talking.

Ela parou de falar.

She stopped to talk to me.

Ela parou o que estava fazendo para conversar comigo.

O significado muda.

Remember + infinitive

remember to do

significa:

lembrar de fazer algo.

Exemplo:

Remember to send the email.

A ação ainda precisa ser feita.

Remember + gerund

remember doing

significa:

lembrar de ter feito algo.

Exemplo:

I remember sending the email.

Tenho memória de ter enviado.

Compare

Remember to lock the door.

Não esqueça de trancar.

I remember locking the door.

Lembro que tranquei.

Forget + infinitive

forget to do

significa:

esquecer de realizar algo.

Exemplo:

I forgot to call Anna.

A ligação não aconteceu.

Forget + gerund

forget doing

refere-se à memória de uma experiência anterior e é menos frequente em contextos básicos.

Exemplo:

I’ll never forget visiting that city.

Aqui:

não esquecerei a experiência.

Try + infinitive

try to do

significa:

tentar realizar algo, fazer esforço.

Exemplo:

I tried to open the door, but it was locked.

Try + gerund

try doing

pode significar:

experimentar uma solução para ver se funciona.

Exemplo:

If the computer is slow, try restarting it.

Aqui:

restart

é uma estratégia a experimentar.

Compare

Try to restart the computer.

Faça esforço para reiniciá-lo.

Try restarting the computer.

Experimente reiniciar para ver se resolve.

Regret — reconhecimento

Você pode encontrar:

regret doing

para arrependimento de algo feito.

Exemplo:

I regret saying that.

Também existe:

regret to inform…

em linguagem formal, com significado diferente.

Esse padrão será mais importante em níveis superiores.

Mean — reconhecimento

mean to do

pode significar:

ter intenção.

I meant to call you.

Já:

mean doing

pode indicar:

implicar.

This job means working on weekends.

Por enquanto, concentre-se em reconhecer a diferença.

Gerund como sujeito

Reading improves vocabulary.

Traveling can be expensive.

Learning a language takes time.

Aqui o gerund funciona como:

subject.

Infinitive como sujeito

Também é possível:

To learn a language takes time.

Mas em inglês cotidiano, muitas vezes a forma com gerund é mais natural:

Learning a language takes time.

It + infinitive

Uma construção muito comum:

It is + adjective + to-infinitive.

Exemplos:

It’s important to study regularly.

It’s difficult to understand this text.

It’s useful to take notes.

Adjective + infinitive

happy to help

ready to leave

difficult to understand

easy to use

important to remember.

Exemplos:

I’m happy to help.

This program is easy to use.

It’s important to arrive early.

Too + adjective + infinitive

Conteúdo já estudado:

It’s too expensive to buy.

I’m too tired to study.

Adjective + enough + infinitive

The room is big enough to hold fifty people.

She’s old enough to drive.

Gerund em proibições e avisos

Você pode encontrar:

No smoking.

No parking.

No swimming.

Essas formas são comuns em placas.

Reading

Texto:

Students interested in joining the course should complete the online form. The program aims to help participants improve their speaking skills. Students are encouraged to practice using English outside class and to avoid translating every sentence.

Padrões:

interested in joining

help participants improve

encouraged to practice

avoid translating.

Listening

Áudio:

I’ve decided to take an evening course because I enjoy learning languages, but I need to improve my speaking.

Identifique:

decided to take

enjoy learning

need to improve.

Writing

Evitar repetir estruturas simples melhora o texto.

Básico:

I study English. I want better English. I practice every day.

Mais natural:

I want to improve my English, so I try to practice every day. I enjoy reading short texts and listening to podcasts.

Speaking

Pergunta:

What do you enjoy doing in your free time?

Resposta:

I enjoy reading and watching films.

Pergunta:

What do you plan to do next year?

Resposta:

I plan to continue studying English and to start another course.

Pergunta com prefer

Do you prefer studying alone or studying with other people?

Resposta:

I prefer studying alone because I can concentrate better.

Padrões não devem ser traduzidos palavra por palavra

Em português:

“Eu gosto de estudar.”

Isso não significa que sempre exista uma estrutura única equivalente.

Em inglês:

I like studying.

ou:

I like to study.

Mas:

“Eu evito estudar tarde.”

é:

I avoid studying late.

Não:

I avoid to study late.

Por isso, memorize:

verb + pattern

e não apenas:

tradução do verbo.

Crie unidades lexicais

Em vez de memorizar:

avoid = evitar

memorize:

avoid doing something.

Em vez de:

decide = decidir

memorize:

decide to do something.

Em vez de:

suggest = sugerir

memorize:

suggest doing something.

Isso reduz erros.

Verb patterns com partículas

Também memorize estruturas inteiras:

interested in doing

good at doing

look forward to doing

decide to do

want someone to do

tell someone to do.

Erro frequente 1 — enjoy + infinitive

Errado:

I enjoy to read.

Correto:

I enjoy reading.

Erro frequente 2 — want + gerund

Errado:

I want traveling.

Correto:

I want to travel.

Erro frequente 3 — suggest + infinitive

Errado:

She suggested to go by train.

Correto:

She suggested going by train.

Erro frequente 4 — decide + gerund

Errado:

We decided staying home.

Correto:

We decided to stay home.

Erro frequente 5 — preposição + infinitive

Errado:

I’m interested in to learn English.

Correto:

I’m interested in learning English.

Erro frequente 6 — look forward to + infinitive

Errado:

I look forward to meet you.

Correto:

I look forward to meeting you.

Erro frequente 7 — tell sem objeto

Errado:

The teacher told to study.

Correto:

The teacher told us to study.

Erro frequente 8 — make + to

Errado:

She made me to wait.

Correto:

She made me wait.

Erro frequente 9 — stop

He stopped smoking.

não é igual a:

He stopped to smoke.

A primeira:

deixou de fumar.

A segunda:

parou outra atividade para fumar.

Erro frequente 10 — forget/remember

I remembered to send the email.

Significa:

não esqueci de enviar.

I remembered sending the email.

Significa:

tenho a lembrança de ter enviado.

Quadro de padrões frequentes

Palavra/estrutura Padrão Exemplo
enjoy -ing I enjoy reading.
avoid -ing Avoid making mistakes.
finish -ing I finished writing.
suggest -ing She suggested going.
consider -ing I’m considering moving.
practice -ing Practice speaking.
want to-infinitive I want to leave.
decide to-infinitive We decided to stay.
plan to-infinitive I plan to travel.
hope to-infinitive I hope to see you.
need to-infinitive I need to study.
promise to-infinitive I promise to call.
ask + object to-infinitive She asked me to wait.
tell + object to-infinitive He told me to leave.
preposition -ing I’m interested in learning.
make + object base verb She made me wait.
let + object base verb They let me enter.

Mudança de significado

Estrutura Significado
stop doing parar a atividade
stop to do parar outra atividade para fazer algo
remember to do lembrar de fazer
remember doing lembrar de ter feito
forget to do esquecer de fazer
try to do tentar, fazer esforço
try doing experimentar como solução

Vocabulário-chave

gerund — gerúndio/forma verbal em -ing com função nominal ou em padrões específicos

infinitive — infinitivo

to-infinitive — to + verbo base

base verb — verbo em sua forma básica

verb pattern — padrão verbal

avoid — evitar

consider — considerar

suggest — sugerir

manage — conseguir realizar

refuse — recusar-se

promise — prometer

offer — oferecer-se

mind — importar-se

recommendation — recomendação

purpose — finalidade

preposition — preposição

remember — lembrar

forget — esquecer

try — tentar/experimentar

Estratégia de prova

Quando uma questão apresenta dois verbos juntos, não tente decidir apenas pela tradução.

Observe o primeiro verbo.

Pergunte:

Este verbo exige -ing ou to-infinitive?

Memorize grupos.

Gerund

enjoy

avoid

finish

suggest

consider

practice.

Infinitive

want

need

decide

plan

hope

promise.

Depois verifique se existe:

uma preposição.

Se houver:

normalmente use -ing.

Exemplo:

interested in ___

Resposta:

learning.

Outra pista:

finalidade.

Se a ideia for:

“para fazer algo”,

use frequentemente:

to + verb.

I went there to study.

Em verbos como:

stop

remember

try

não escolha apenas pela forma: analise o significado.

Prática

1. Complete:

I enjoy ___ English.

  1. study
  2. studying
  3. to studying
  4. studied

2. Complete:

She decided ___ early.

  1. leaving
  2. to leave
  3. leave to
  4. left

3. Complete:

We should avoid ___ late.

  1. arriving
  2. to arrive
  3. arrive to
  4. arrived

4. Complete:

I want ___ another language.

  1. learning
  2. to learn
  3. learn to
  4. learned

5. Complete:

She suggested ___ by train.

  1. traveling
  2. to travel
  3. travel to
  4. traveled

6. Complete:

They plan ___ next month.

  1. traveling
  2. to travel
  3. travel to
  4. traveled

7. Complete:

He finished ___ the report.

  1. write
  2. writing
  3. to write
  4. wrote

8. Complete:

I hope ___ you soon.

  1. seeing
  2. to see
  3. saw
  4. see to

9. Complete:

She is interested in ___ French.

  1. learning
  2. to learn
  3. learn
  4. learned

10. Complete:

Thank you for ___ me.

  1. help
  2. helping
  3. to help
  4. helped

11. Complete:

I’m looking forward to ___ you.

  1. meet
  2. meeting
  3. to meet
  4. met

12. Complete:

I went to the library ___.

  1. studying
  2. to study
  3. study to
  4. studied

13. Complete:

The teacher asked us ___ the exercise.

  1. finish
  2. to finish
  3. finishing only
  4. finished

14. Complete:

She made me ___ for an hour.

  1. to wait
  2. waiting
  3. wait
  4. waited

15. Complete:

My parents let me ___ alone.

  1. travel
  2. to travel
  3. traveling
  4. traveled to

16. Escolha a frase correta:

  1. I enjoy to read.
  2. I enjoy reading.
  3. I enjoy read.
  4. I enjoying to read.

17. Escolha:

  1. She wants studying abroad.
  2. She wants to study abroad.
  3. She wants study to abroad.
  4. She want to studying abroad.

18. Escolha:

  1. He suggested taking a taxi.
  2. He suggested to take a taxi.
  3. He suggested take a taxi.
  4. He suggested us to taking a taxi.

19. Escolha:

He stopped smoking.

Significa:

  1. Ele parou outra atividade para fumar.
  2. Ele deixou de fumar.
  3. Ele começou a fumar.
  4. Ele esqueceu de fumar.

20. Escolha:

He stopped to smoke.

Significa:

  1. Ele deixou de fumar permanentemente.
  2. Ele parou o que estava fazendo para fumar.
  3. Ele esqueceu de fumar.
  4. Ele evitou fumar.

21. Escolha:

Remember to lock the door.

Significa:

  1. Lembre-se de que você trancou a porta.
  2. Não esqueça de trancar a porta.
  3. Pare de trancar a porta.
  4. Tente trancar a porta como experimento.

22. Escolha:

I remember locking the door.

Significa:

  1. Tenho a lembrança de ter trancado a porta.
  2. Preciso me lembrar de trancar no futuro.
  3. Nunca tranquei a porta.
  4. Pretendo trancar a porta.

23. Complete:

If the program doesn’t work, try ___ it.

  1. restart
  2. restarting
  3. to restarting
  4. restarted

Considere que reiniciar é uma solução a experimentar.

24. Complete:

I tried ___ the door, but it was too heavy.

  1. opening
  2. to open
  3. opened
  4. open to

Considere que o foco é o esforço para abrir.

25. Corrija:

I avoid to study late at night.

26. Corrija:

She decided going home.

27. Corrija:

I’m good at to solve problems.

28. Complete o texto:

Laura enjoys ___ (learn) languages and hopes ___ (study) abroad next year. She has decided ___ (apply) for a course in Canada. Before ___ (send) her application, she plans ___ (ask) her teacher to check it.

29. Complete:

Daniel wants ___ (improve) his English. His teacher suggested ___ (practice) every day and advised him ___ (listen) to English podcasts. Daniel is also interested in ___ (join) a conversation group.

30. Produção

Escreva um texto de 100 a 120 palavras sobre seus planos e hábitos de estudo de um personagem fictício.

Inclua:

  • dois verbos seguidos por gerund;
  • três verbos seguidos por to-infinitive;
  • uma estrutura com preposição + gerund;
  • uma estrutura de finalidade com infinitive;
  • uma estrutura com object + infinitive;
  • uma frase com stop, remember ou try em que a escolha entre gerund e infinitive altere o significado.

Gabarito comentado

1. B — studying

enjoy + -ing.

2. B — to leave

decide + to-infinitive.

3. A — arriving

avoid + -ing.

4. B — to learn

want + to-infinitive.

5. A — traveling

suggest + -ing.

6. B — to travel

plan + to-infinitive.

7. B — writing

finish + -ing.

8. B — to see

hope + to-infinitive.

9. A — learning

Depois da preposição:

in

use:

verb-ing.

10. B — helping

for + gerund.

11. B — meeting

A expressão é:

look forward to + -ing.

Aqui:

to

é preposição.

12. B — to study

O infinitive expressa finalidade:

fui à biblioteca para estudar.

13. B — to finish

ask + object + to-infinitive.

14. C — wait

make + object + base verb.

Não usamos:

to.

15. A — travel

let + object + base verb.

16. B

enjoy reading.

17. B

want to study.

18. A

suggest taking.

19. B

stop doing

significa:

deixar de realizar a atividade.

20. B

stop to do

significa:

interromper outra ação para realizar aquela atividade.

21. B

remember to do

refere-se a uma ação que ainda precisa ser lembrada.

22. A

remember doing

refere-se à memória de uma ação já realizada.

23. B — restarting

try doing

significa:

experimentar uma solução.

24. B — to open

try to do

indica esforço/tentativa de realizar a ação.

25.

I avoid studying late at night.

avoid + -ing.

26.

She decided to go home.

decide + infinitive.

27.

I’m good at solving problems.

Depois de:

at

use:

-ing.

28.

Laura enjoys learning languages and hopes to study abroad next year. She has decided to apply for a course in Canada. Before sending her application, she plans to ask her teacher to check it.

Análise:

enjoy + learning.

hope + to study.

decide + to apply.

before + sending.

plan + to ask.

ask + object + to check.

29.

Daniel wants to improve his English. His teacher suggested practicing every day and advised him to listen to English podcasts. Daniel is also interested in joining a conversation group.

want + infinitive.

suggest + gerund.

advise + object + infinitive.

interested in + gerund.

30.

Modelo:

Lucas wants to improve his English because he plans to take an international exam next year. He enjoys reading short articles and practices listening to English every evening. He has also decided to study vocabulary more systematically. His teacher encouraged him to speak more during class and suggested joining an online conversation group. Lucas is interested in learning through podcasts because he can listen while traveling. He sometimes goes to the library to study without distractions. When he finds a difficult exercise, he tries reading the instructions again before asking for help. He also remembers to review new words before going to bed because regular revision helps him remember them.

Tarefa de consolidação

Crie duas listas principais.

Verb + gerund

Inclua:

enjoy

avoid

finish

keep

mind

suggest

consider

practice

miss

imagine.

Produza uma frase para cada um.

Verb + infinitive

Inclua:

want

need

decide

plan

hope

expect

promise

agree

refuse

manage.

Produza uma frase para cada um.

Depois crie um terceiro grupo:

preposition + gerund

Exemplos:

interested in learning

good at writing

worried about arriving late

without saying anything

before leaving

after finishing.

Em seguida, crie pares para os verbos que mudam de significado:

stop doing / stop to do

remember doing / remember to do

try doing / try to do

Explique a diferença em uma frase.

Depois memorize estruturas completas em vez de palavras isoladas:

enjoy doing something

avoid doing something

suggest doing something

want to do something

decide to do something

plan to do something

ask someone to do something

tell someone to do something

make someone do something

be interested in doing something

look forward to doing something

Finalize perguntando:

Qual padrão vem depois desta palavra?

e, nos casos em que as duas formas são possíveis:

A escolha entre -ing e infinitive muda apenas o estilo ou muda o significado?

No nível B1, dominar esses padrões torna a produção muito mais natural, porque a escolha entre gerund e infinitive passa a ser feita pela estrutura lexical e pelo significado, e não apenas por tradução.

Aula 81 — Phrasal verbs essenciais

Objetivos

Ao final desta aula, você deverá ser capaz de:

  • compreender o que são phrasal verbs;
  • reconhecer a estrutura verb + particle;
  • diferenciar phrasal verbs separáveis e inseparáveis;
  • identificar quando um pronome deve aparecer no meio da estrutura;
  • compreender phrasal verbs frequentes em contextos de estudo, trabalho, tecnologia, viagens e vida cotidiana;
  • inferir o significado de phrasal verbs pelo contexto;
  • evitar traduções literais inadequadas;
  • reconhecer phrasal verbs em Reading e Listening;
  • empregar phrasal verbs frequentes em Writing e Speaking;
  • distinguir significados diferentes de um mesmo verbo-base;
  • utilizar estratégias para aprender phrasal verbs por contexto e não apenas por listas isoladas.

Desenvolvimento

Um phrasal verb é uma combinação formada normalmente por:

verb + particle.

A partícula pode ser:

preposition

ou:

adverb.

Exemplos:

wake up

turn on

look for

give up

find out.

Muitas vezes, o significado final não pode ser deduzido apenas pelo significado individual das palavras.

Compare:

look

significa:

olhar.

Mas:

look for

significa:

procurar.

E:

look after

significa:

cuidar de.

Por isso, é importante aprender o phrasal verb como uma unidade.

Verb + particle

Exemplo:

turn on.

turn → virar.

on → ligado/sobre.

Mas:

turn on the computer

significa:

ligar o computador.

Outro:

give up.

Não significa literalmente:

dar para cima.

Significa:

desistir.

Phrasal verbs podem ter significado literal

Alguns são relativamente fáceis de interpretar.

Exemplo:

sit down.

sentar-se.

stand up.

levantar-se.

Mas outros são mais idiomáticos.

find out.

Significa:

descobrir.

give up.

Significa:

desistir.

Separáveis e inseparáveis

Uma distinção importante é saber se o objeto pode aparecer:

entre o verbo e a partícula

ou apenas:

depois de toda a expressão.

Separable phrasal verbs

Exemplo:

turn on.

Podemos dizer:

Turn on the computer.

Ou:

Turn the computer on.

As duas formas são possíveis.

Outro exemplo

pick up.

I picked up the phone.

I picked the phone up.

Pronome em phrasal verb separável

Quando usamos um pronome, ele normalmente precisa ficar no meio.

Correto:

Turn it on.

Não:

Turn on it.

Correto:

Pick it up.

Não:

Pick up it.

Essa regra é muito importante.

Inseparable phrasal verbs

Exemplo:

look for.

Correto:

I’m looking for my keys.

Não:

I’m looking my keys for.

Com pronome:

I’m looking for them.

Não:

I’m looking them for.

Outro inseparável

look after.

She looks after her younger brother.

She looks after him.

Não:

She looks him after.

Phrasal verbs sem objeto

Alguns não precisam de objeto.

Exemplo:

wake up.

I wake up at seven.

Outro:

grow up.

She grew up in a small town.

Turn on

Significa:

ligar.

Usado com:

lights

computers

devices

machines.

Exemplos:

Turn on the light.

Turn the computer on.

Turn it on.

Turn off

Significa:

desligar.

Exemplos:

Please turn off your phone.

Turn the TV off.

Turn it off.

Turn up

Pode significar:

aumentar o volume/intensidade.

Exemplo:

Turn up the volume.

Também pode significar:

aparecer/chegar inesperadamente.

Exemplo:

He turned up late.

Neste nível, aprenda primeiro o contexto.

Turn down

Pode significar:

diminuir volume/intensidade.

Turn down the music.

Também pode significar:

recusar.

She turned down the job offer.

Observe como o mesmo phrasal verb pode ter mais de um significado.

Pick up

Pode significar:

pegar algo.

Pick up your bag.

Também:

buscar alguém.

I’ll pick you up at eight.

Também:

atender telefone.

He picked up the phone.

Put down

Significa frequentemente:

colocar algo em uma superfície.

Put the book down.

Também pode significar:

escrever/anotar

em certos contextos.

Put your name down on the list.

Put on

Pode significar:

vestir.

Put on your jacket.

Também:

ligar/colocar para tocar.

Put on some music.

Take off

Pode significar:

tirar roupa/acessório.

Take off your shoes.

Também:

decolar.

The plane took off at 9 a.m.

A estrutura precisa ser interpretada pelo contexto.

Get up

Significa:

levantar-se da cama ou de uma posição.

I get up at six every day.

Não confunda com:

wake up.

Wake up x get up

I wake up at six.

Significa:

deixo de dormir.

I get up at six fifteen.

Significa:

saio da cama.

É possível:

wake up → remain in bed → get up later.

Go out

Pode significar:

sair.

We went out for dinner.

Também pode ser usado para luz/fogo:

The lights went out.

The fire went out.

Come back

Significa:

voltar.

What time did you come back?

Go back

Também:

voltar.

Mas a escolha depende da perspectiva.

I’ll go back to the office tomorrow.

Come back here!

Get back

Também pode significar:

voltar/retornar.

I got back home at eleven.

Pode ainda significar:

receber algo de volta.

I got my money back.

Look for

Significa:

procurar.

I’m looking for my wallet.

Find

Não confunda:

look for

com:

find.

look for → procurar.

find → encontrar.

Exemplo:

I looked for my keys for twenty minutes and finally found them.

Find out

Significa:

descobrir uma informação.

I found out that the meeting was canceled.

Outro:

We need to find out what happened.

Look at

Significa:

olhar para.

Look at this photo.

Look after

Significa:

cuidar de.

She looks after her grandmother.

Look up

Pode significar:

procurar informação em uma fonte.

Look up the word in a dictionary.

É separável:

Look the word up.

Com pronome:

Look it up.

Look forward to

Significa:

esperar algo com entusiasmo.

Estrutura:

look forward to + noun/gerund.

Exemplo:

I’m looking forward to the holidays.

I’m looking forward to seeing you.

Não:

looking forward to see you.

Aqui:

to

é preposição.

Give up

Significa:

desistir

ou:

abandonar um hábito.

Don’t give up.

He gave up smoking.

Carry on

Significa:

continuar.

Carry on working.

She carried on talking.

Keep on

Também pode significar:

continuar fazendo algo.

He kept on asking questions.

Go on

Pode significar:

continuar.

Please go on.

Também:

acontecer.

What’s going on?

A expressão:

What’s going on?

significa:

O que está acontecendo?

Set up

Pode significar:

configurar

instalar

organizar

criar.

Tecnologia:

I need to set up my new computer.

Organização:

They set up a new company.

Log in

Significa:

entrar em um sistema.

Log in with your username and password.

Também:

log into.

Log into your account.

Log out

Significa:

sair da conta/sistema.

Don’t forget to log out.

Sign up

Significa:

inscrever-se.

I signed up for an online course.

Sign in

Pode significar:

entrar em uma conta

ou:

registrar presença.

Please sign in at reception.

Sign out

Pode significar:

registrar saída

ou:

sair de um sistema.

Shut down

Significa:

desligar completamente.

Tecnologia:

Shut down the computer before leaving.

Também pode ser usado para:

fechar operações.

The factory was shut down.

Start up

Pode significar:

iniciar uma máquina/sistema.

The computer takes a long time to start up.

Back up

Em tecnologia:

fazer backup.

Back up your files regularly.

Como substantivo:

backup.

Exemplo:

I have a backup of the document.

Plug in

Significa:

conectar à tomada ou a uma porta.

Plug in the charger.

É separável:

Plug the charger in.

Com pronome:

Plug it in.

Unplug

Não é exatamente phrasal verb, mas é importante no mesmo campo lexical:

Unplug the device.

Fill in

Pode significar:

preencher espaços de um formulário.

Fill in your name and address.

Em alguns contextos:

fill out a form

é muito frequente, especialmente no inglês americano.

Fill out

Fill out this form.

Significa:

preencher um formulário.

Write down

Significa:

anotar.

Write down the address.

Write it down.

Não:

Write down it.

Hand in

Muito importante em educação.

Significa:

entregar um trabalho/documento.

You must hand in the assignment by Friday.

É separável:

Hand the assignment in.

Com pronome:

Hand it in.

Give back

Significa:

devolver.

Give the book back to me.

Give it back.

Take back

Pode significar:

devolver algo para uma loja.

I took the jacket back because it was too small.

Também:

retirar algo que disse.

I take that back.

Bring back

Significa:

trazer de volta.

Please bring the book back tomorrow.

Send back

Significa:

enviar/devolver.

I sent the product back because it was damaged.

Call back

Significa:

ligar novamente.

I’ll call you back later.

Com pronome:

I’ll call her back.

Hang up

Significa:

desligar uma chamada.

Don’t hang up.

She hung up before I could answer.

Hold on

Em telefonemas:

espere.

Hold on a moment, please.

Também significa literalmente:

segurar-se

dependendo do contexto.

Speak up

Significa:

falar mais alto.

Could you speak up, please?

Slow down

Significa:

reduzir velocidade.

Slow down!

Também pode ser metafórico:

You need to slow down and rest.

Hurry up

Significa:

apressar-se.

Hurry up! The bus is coming.

Calm down

Significa:

acalmar-se.

Try to calm down.

Work out

Possui vários significados.

Pode significar:

exercitar-se.

I work out three times a week.

Também:

resolver/descobrir uma solução.

We need to work out the answer.

Também:

dar certo.

Everything worked out well.

O contexto é essencial.

Figure out

Significa:

compreender

descobrir

resolver.

I can’t figure out how this program works.

Muito comum em inglês cotidiano.

Sort out

Pode significar:

resolver/organizar um problema.

We need to sort out this problem.

Outro:

I’ll sort out the documents later.

Deal with

Significa:

lidar com.

How do you deal with stress?

The support team deals with technical problems.

É inseparável:

deal with the problem.

Não:

deal the problem with.

Run out of

Significa:

ficar sem algo.

We’ve run out of coffee.

My phone ran out of battery.

Estrutura:

run out of + noun.

Run out

Sem objeto:

Time is running out.

Significa:

o tempo está acabando.

Use up

Significa:

usar tudo de algo.

We used up all the paper.

Throw away

Significa:

jogar fora.

Don’t throw away that document.

Don’t throw it away.

Clean up

Significa:

limpar/organizar.

We need to clean up the room.

Tidy up

Significa:

arrumar.

Please tidy up your desk.

Put away

Significa:

guardar.

Put your books away.

Put them away.

Take out

Pode significar:

retirar.

Take the books out of the bag.

Também:

levar alguém para sair.

He took her out for dinner.

Check in

Usado em:

hotels

airports.

We checked in at the hotel at 3 p.m.

You should check in online before the flight.

Check out

Hotel:

We checked out at eleven.

Também pode significar:

olhar/verificar algo.

Informal:

Check out this website.

Get on

Transportes:

get on a bus/train/plane.

We got on the bus.

Também pode significar:

ter uma boa relação.

I get on well with my colleagues.

Get off

get off a bus/train/plane.

We got off the train at the next station.

Get in

Muito usado para:

car/taxi.

Get in the car.

Get out of

Get out of the car.

Get into

Também:

entrar em veículo pequeno ou espaço.

She got into the taxi.

Pode ter significados mais abstratos em outros contextos.

Transport: on x in

Normalmente:

get on/off → bus, train, plane.

get in/out of → car, taxi.

Take over

Pode significar:

assumir controle/responsabilidade.

Maria will take over the project next month.

Take on

Pode significar:

assumir uma tarefa ou responsabilidade.

I can’t take on any more work.

Put off

Significa:

adiar.

We had to put off the meeting.

Com pronome:

We put it off.

Call off

Significa:

cancelar.

They called off the event because of the weather.

They called it off.

Bring forward

Pode significar:

antecipar uma data ou horário.

The meeting was brought forward to Monday.

Essa expressão pode aparecer em contextos profissionais mais formais.

Find out x figure out

Compare:

I found out that the exam is on Friday.

Descobri uma informação.

I figured out how to solve the problem.

Consegui compreender/resolver.

Look for x look up

I’m looking for my dictionary.

Procurando o objeto físico.
