7. Verifique se alguma alternativa transforma associação em causalidade ou possibilidade em certeza.

Antes de marcar uma resposta, pergunte:

O estudo realmente demonstrou isso ou apenas encontrou evidências que sugerem essa possibilidade?

Essa pergunta evita um dos erros mais frequentes em questões de Reading B1 sobre divulgação científica.

Aula 87 — Identificação de ideia principal e detalhes

Objetivos

Ao final desta aula, você deverá ser capaz de:

  • identificar a ideia principal de um texto;
  • distinguir ideia principal de informações secundárias;
  • localizar detalhes específicos;
  • reconhecer exemplos, explicações e evidências que sustentam a ideia principal;
  • diferenciar tema, tópico e ideia principal;
  • identificar a função de cada parágrafo;
  • usar skimming para compreensão global;
  • usar scanning para localizar detalhes;
  • reconhecer paráfrases entre texto e questão;
  • interpretar títulos e primeiras frases como pistas;
  • identificar informações explícitas e implícitas;
  • evitar alternativas que usam detalhes verdadeiros como se fossem a ideia central;
  • aplicar essas estratégias em textos jornalísticos, científicos, acadêmicos e cotidianos.

Desenvolvimento

Uma das habilidades mais importantes em Reading é saber responder a duas perguntas diferentes:

What is this text mainly about?

e:

What specific information does the text give?

A primeira pergunta busca:

main idea.

A segunda busca:

details.

Confundir essas duas categorias é uma das causas mais comuns de erro em provas de leitura.

Topic

O topic é o assunto geral.

Exemplo:

renewable energy.

Isso é apenas:

o tema.

Ainda não sabemos:

o que o texto diz sobre renewable energy.

Main idea

A main idea é a mensagem principal que o texto apresenta sobre o tópico.

Exemplo:

Tema:

renewable energy.

Ideia principal:

Renewable energy is becoming more important because it can reduce dependence on fossil fuels.

Agora temos:

topic + central message.

Detail

Um detalhe desenvolve, explica ou comprova a ideia principal.

Exemplos:

Solar energy is becoming cheaper.

Many countries are building wind farms.

Renewable sources produced 30% of the country’s electricity last year.

Essas informações ajudam a sustentar a ideia central.

Topic x main idea x detail

Considere:

Many cities are investing in public transport to reduce traffic and pollution. New bus routes have been introduced, train networks are being expanded, and some cities are creating more bicycle lanes.

Temos:

Topic → urban transport.

Main idea → cities are investing in different forms of public transport and mobility to reduce traffic and pollution.

Details → new bus routes, expanded train networks, bicycle lanes.

Tema não é suficiente

Se a pergunta é:

What is the main idea?

Resposta fraca:

Public transport.

Isso é apenas:

topic.

Resposta melhor:

Cities are improving public transport to reduce traffic and pollution.

Generalização correta

A main idea é normalmente:

ampla o suficiente para representar o texto inteiro

mas:

específica o suficiente para dizer algo sobre o tópico.

Muito ampla:

This text is about cities.

Muito específica:

One city added twelve buses.

Adequada:

Cities are improving transport systems to address traffic problems.

Main idea explícita

Às vezes, a ideia principal aparece claramente em uma frase.

Exemplo:

Regular physical activity has several benefits for physical and mental health.

Depois o texto explica:

  • improves cardiovascular health;
  • helps control weight;
  • may reduce stress;
  • may improve sleep.

A primeira frase funciona como:

topic sentence.

Topic sentence

A topic sentence é a frase que apresenta a ideia central de um parágrafo.

Ela aparece frequentemente:

no início do parágrafo.

Mas pode aparecer:

  • no meio;
  • no final;
  • de forma implícita.

Topic sentence no início

Online learning offers students greater flexibility. Learners can access lessons from different locations, organize study around work schedules and review recorded material when necessary.

Main idea:

Online learning offers flexibility.

Os demais elementos:

details/examples.

Topic sentence no final

Many workers no longer commute every day. Meetings can be held online, employees may live farther from the office, and companies can reduce the amount of office space they use. For these reasons, remote work has changed how many organizations operate.

Aqui a principal conclusão aparece:

no final.

Main idea implícita

Nem todo texto diz:

“The main idea is…”

Exemplo:

The library stays open until midnight during exam periods. Extra study rooms become available, additional computers are installed, and staff provide longer support hours.

Podemos inferir:

The library provides additional services during exam periods.

Essa ideia não aparece exatamente em uma única frase, mas resume os detalhes.

Supporting details

Detalhes de apoio podem ter várias funções.

Podem:

  • dar exemplos;
  • fornecer números;
  • apresentar causas;
  • mostrar consequências;
  • explicar processos;
  • apresentar evidências;
  • comparar situações;
  • dar definições.

Example detail

Many devices can help people reduce energy use. For example, smart thermostats can automatically adjust room temperature.

Ideia principal:

devices can reduce energy use.

Detalhe:

smart thermostats.

Numerical detail

The program was successful. More than 80% of participants completed the course.

O número:

sustenta a avaliação de sucesso.

Cause detail

The flight was delayed because of heavy rain.

Detalhe:

heavy rain

explica:

why the flight was delayed.

Consequence detail

Temperatures increased significantly. As a result, electricity use rose because more people used air conditioning.

Detalhe:

higher electricity use

é uma consequência.

Evidence

Textos acadêmicos e científicos frequentemente apresentam:

claim + evidence.

Exemplo:

Short breaks may improve concentration. In one study, students who took a five-minute break performed 8% better on a concentration task.

Claim:

short breaks may improve concentration.

Evidence:

8% better performance.

Perguntas de ideia principal

Formulações frequentes:

What is the main idea of the text?

What is the article mainly about?

What is the main point?

Which sentence best summarizes the passage?

What is the writer mainly discussing?

What is the purpose of the paragraph?

Perguntas de detalhes

Formulações:

According to the text…

How many…?

When…?

Where…?

Why…?

Which of the following…?

What happened after…?

What does the author say about…?

Identificação rápida

Se a questão usa:

mainly

main idea

overall

best summary

pense em:

visão global.

Se usa:

according to the text

how many

when

why

pense em:

informação específica.

Skimming para ideia principal

Use skimming.

Leia rapidamente:

  1. título;
  2. primeira frase;
  3. primeira e última frases de cada parágrafo;
  4. palavras repetidas;
  5. conclusão.

Objetivo:

entender a estrutura geral.

Não pare em cada palavra desconhecida.

Scanning para detalhes

Use scanning quando sabe o que procura.

Pergunta:

How many people participated?

Procure:

numbers

participants

study

sample.

Pergunta:

Why was the project delayed?

Procure:

delayed

because

due to

reason.

Title como pista

Título:

Why More Cities Are Planting Trees

Provável tema:

urban tree planting.

Provável ideia:

cities are planting trees because of environmental or social benefits.

Mas:

confirme no texto.

Não responda apenas pelo título.

Primeiro parágrafo

Em muitos textos jornalísticos:

main information appears early.

Em textos acadêmicos e argumentativos, o primeiro parágrafo pode apresentar:

problema

tese

contexto.

Último parágrafo

Pode apresentar:

conclusion

recommendation

future implications.

Por isso, para perguntas globais:

início + final

são muito importantes.

Palavras repetidas

Se o texto repete:

sleep

concentration

students

study

é provável que o tópico esteja relacionado a:

sleep and student concentration.

Mas precisamos saber:

qual relação o texto estabelece.

Semantic field

Palavras diferentes podem pertencer ao mesmo campo.

Exemplo:

buses

trains

commuting

traffic

passengers.

Todas apontam para:

transport.

Não procure apenas repetições exatas.

Main idea como paráfrase

Texto:

More people are using bicycles to travel to work, and cities are responding by building safer cycle lanes.

Questão:

What is the passage mainly about?

Resposta correta pode ser:

The growth of cycling is influencing urban transport planning.

Essa frase não aparece literalmente.

É uma:

paraphrase.

Detalhes também podem ser parafraseados

Texto:

The course is free of charge.

Questão:

How much does the course cost?

Resposta:

Nothing.

Você precisa reconhecer:

free of charge = no cost.

Palavra-chave não basta

Erro:

Pergunta:

Why did Sarah move?

Texto:

Sarah moved to Manchester last year. She had recently accepted a new job there.

O aluno encontra:

moved

e escolhe algo relacionado à cidade.

Mas a resposta para:

why

é:

because she had accepted a new job.

Sempre leia:

a relação entre as informações.

Who/what/why/how

As perguntas mudam o tipo de detalhe procurado.

Who? → pessoa/grupo.

What? → ação/coisa/evento.

When? → tempo.

Where? → lugar.

Why? → razão.

How? → método/maneira.

Distinguindo main idea de exemplo

Texto:

Many forms of exercise can improve cardiovascular health. Walking, swimming and cycling are common examples.

Pergunta:

Main idea?

Não:

walking.

Não:

swimming.

Resposta:

Different forms of exercise can improve cardiovascular health.

Distinguindo ideia central de estatística

Texto:

Digital payments are becoming more common. In one survey, 72% of young adults said they preferred paying by phone or card rather than cash.

Ideia:

digital payments are increasingly common.

Detalhe:

72%.

Alternativa verdadeira, mas incorreta

Esse é um tipo frequente de armadilha.

Texto inteiro:

trata dos benefícios e desafios do trabalho remoto.

Alternativa:

Many employees save commuting time.

Isso pode ser verdade segundo o texto.

Mas se a pergunta é:

What is the main idea?

é específica demais.

Too narrow

Uma resposta:

cobre apenas um detalhe.

Too broad

Uma resposta:

é tão geral que não representa a mensagem específica.

Exemplo:

Texto sobre:

how smartphones affect sleep.

Resposta ampla demais:

Technology affects people’s lives.

Pode ser verdadeira, mas:

não resume o foco específico.

Unsupported

Outra alternativa pode simplesmente:

não ser sustentada.

Texto:

Some employees prefer remote work.

Alternativa:

All employees want to work remotely.

Não sustentada.

Contradiction

Texto:

The number decreased.

Alternativa:

The number increased.

Contradição direta.

Partially true

Texto:

The program offers English, mathematics and computing.

Alternativa:

The program teaches English.

É verdadeira.

Mas se a pergunta pede:

full description

ela pode ser incompleta.

Main idea de parágrafo x texto inteiro

Uma prova pode perguntar:

What is the main idea of paragraph 3?

Não responda com:

main idea of the entire article.

Leia apenas:

função daquele parágrafo.

Funções de parágrafo

Um parágrafo pode:

introduce the topic

describe a problem

explain a cause

present evidence

give an example

compare alternatives

discuss limitations

present a conclusion.

Exemplo de estrutura

Parágrafo 1:

apresenta crescimento do ensino online.

Parágrafo 2:

explica benefícios.

Parágrafo 3:

apresenta desafios.

Parágrafo 4:

conclui que modelo híbrido pode combinar vantagens.

Ideia global:

Online education has benefits and challenges, and hybrid models may provide a useful balance.

Pronouns e detalhes

Detalhes podem depender de referente.

The researchers introduced a new device. It was tested in three hospitals.

Pergunta:

What was tested?

Resposta:

the new device.

Você precisa identificar:

it.

This

The city reduced ticket prices. This increased passenger numbers.

This

refere-se:

à redução do preço.

Detalhe:

consequence.

Former/latter

Texto:

The study compared walking and cycling. The latter produced slightly better results.

latter → cycling.

Esse tipo de referência pode determinar a resposta.

Informação explícita

Texto:

The course begins on May 6.

Pergunta:

When does it begin?

Resposta explícita:

May 6.

Inferência simples

Texto:

The course begins at 6 p.m. and is designed for people who work during the day.

Podemos inferir:

evening scheduling makes it easier for daytime workers to attend.

O texto não diz exatamente isso, mas:

é logicamente sustentado.

Inferência não é invenção

Texto:

Maria took an umbrella because dark clouds were approaching.

Inferência:

She expected rain.

Razoável.

Inferência:

She hates sunny weather.

Não há suporte.

Detail questions com NOT

Muito cuidado:

Which of the following is NOT mentioned?

Agora você deve encontrar:

três informações presentes

e:

uma ausente.

Leia:

NOT

com atenção.

EXCEPT

Também:

All of the following are mentioned EXCEPT…

Mesmo princípio.

Negative questions

Marque visualmente:

NOT

EXCEPT

FALSE

para evitar responder ao oposto.

Sequência cronológica

Textos narrativos podem exigir ordem.

Exemplo:

First, researchers collected samples. They then analyzed them in the laboratory. Finally, they published the results.

Pergunta:

What happened before the samples were analyzed?

Resposta:

They were collected.

Cause x sequence

Não confunda:

happened before

com:

caused.

Uma coisa ocorrer antes não significa:

causou a outra.

Comparações

Texto:

Group A scored higher than Group B, but lower than Group C.

Detalhes:

C > A > B.

Uma questão pode reformular essa relação.

Quantifiers

Preste atenção:

some

many

most

all

few.

Texto:

Most participants completed the course.

Não significa:

all participants.

Approximation

around 200

approximately 200

about 200.

Não significa:

exactly 200.

At least

pelo menos.

At least 500 people attended.

Então:

500 ou mais.

Fewer than

menos de.

Fewer than 100 people completed the survey.

Então:

não pode ser 100 ou mais.

More than

mais de.

Main idea em textos argumentativos

Texto:

Some people believe cities should invest more in roads. However, expanding public transport may be a more sustainable solution because it can reduce congestion and pollution.

Main idea:

Public transport may be a more sustainable solution to urban transport problems than expanding roads.

However como pista

Palavras de contraste podem mostrar:

onde está o verdadeiro argumento do autor.

Exemplo:

Many people think X. However, recent evidence suggests Y.

Frequentemente o autor quer destacar:

Although

Although online learning offers flexibility, some students find it difficult to remain motivated.

O texto apresenta:

benefício + limitação.

A ideia principal pode incluir:

ambos.

Main idea equilibrada

Se o texto discute vantagens e desvantagens, não escolha uma alternativa que menciona:

apenas vantagens

ou:

apenas desvantagens.

Purpose x main idea

Não são exatamente iguais.

Main idea

o que o texto diz.

Purpose

por que o autor escreveu.

Exemplo:

Main idea:

A new recycling program reduced waste during its first year.

Purpose:

to inform readers about the results of the program.

Inform x persuade

Notícia:

normalmente informa.

Campanha:

pode persuadir.

Manual:

instrui.

Anúncio:

promove/informa.

Identificando purpose por verbos

Alternativas podem usar:

inform

explain

compare

describe

persuade

warn

recommend.

Summary

Uma boa síntese inclui:

main idea

e:

principais pontos de apoio.

Não inclui:

todos os detalhes.

Exemplo

Texto:

A study of 500 students found that those who used a study schedule completed more assignments on time. Researchers say planning may help students manage their workload, although the study did not determine whether scheduling directly caused better performance.

Resumo adequado:

A study found an association between using study schedules and completing assignments on time, though it did not establish causation.

Resumo inadequado

The study included 500 students.

É só um detalhe.

Outro inadequado:

Planning definitely makes every student perform better.

Exagera.

Main idea e palavras abstratas

Às vezes, a resposta correta é mais abstrata que o texto.

Texto fala sobre:

  • longer library hours;
  • more computers;
  • extra study rooms.

Resposta:

The university is expanding academic support during exams.

Essa frase agrupa os detalhes em:

conceito mais amplo.

Categorization

Essa habilidade exige perceber que:

buses + trains + cycle lanes

podem ser resumidos como:

transport infrastructure.

doctors + clinics + vaccination

podem ser:

healthcare services.

Reading com vocabulário desconhecido

Não deixe uma palavra bloquear a ideia global.

Texto:

The city installed permeable pavements in several streets to reduce flooding.

Mesmo sem conhecer:

permeable

podemos perceber:

city + streets + reduce flooding.

Ideia principal provavelmente envolve:

uma medida urbana contra enchentes.

Pistas de contexto

Use:

examples

definitions

contrast

cause/effect

word formation

surrounding sentences.

Primeiro e último parágrafo

Para textos maiores:

leia primeiro e último parágrafo

para obter:

overview.

Depois volte para:

detalhes.

Técnica de uma frase

Após ler um parágrafo, tente dizer:

This paragraph is mainly about…

em uma frase curta.

Isso ajuda a construir:

mapa do texto.

Marginal notes

Mentalmente ou no rascunho:

P1 — problem

P2 — causes

P3 — solution

P4 — results.

Depois:

main idea = relationship among these sections.

Reading passage 1

Libraries Adapt to Changing Study Habits

University libraries are changing the services they offer as students increasingly use digital materials. Although printed books remain important, many students now access articles, textbooks and reference materials online.

In response, several universities have increased the number of computers, charging points and group-study spaces available in their libraries. Some have also extended opening hours during examination periods.

However, university staff say physical libraries remain important. Students continue to use them as quiet places to study, work with classmates and receive support from librarians.

Rather than disappearing, libraries appear to be changing their role by combining traditional resources with digital services and flexible study spaces.

Leitura do texto 1

Topic:

university libraries.

Não basta.

Main idea:

University libraries are adapting to digital study habits while continuing to provide important physical study spaces and traditional services.

Detalhes:

more computers

charging points

group-study spaces

longer opening hours

students still use physical libraries.

Reading passage 2

Small Changes Reduce Office Energy Use

A six-month project involving four office buildings tested whether simple changes could reduce electricity use. Employees received weekly information about energy consumption and were encouraged to switch off lights and computers when they were not needed.

By the end of the project, electricity use had fallen by an average of 12%. The largest reductions occurred in departments where employees regularly received feedback about their energy use.

Project organizers said the results showed that small behavioral changes could contribute to lower energy consumption. However, they noted that the project did not examine whether the improvements would continue over several years.

Leitura do texto 2

Main idea:

Simple behavior changes combined with regular feedback were associated with reduced office electricity use during a six-month project.

Detalhes:

four offices

weekly information

lights/computers switched off

12% decrease

long-term effects unknown.

Reading passage 3

Why Some Adults Return to Education

Adults return to formal education for many reasons. Some want to gain qualifications that will help them change careers, while others need additional training for their current jobs.

Personal interests can also be important. Some adult learners enroll in courses because they want to study a subject they did not have the opportunity to explore when they were younger.

Returning to education can be challenging because adult students often have work and family responsibilities. For this reason, evening, weekend and online courses have become important options for many learners.

Flexible learning opportunities can therefore make education more accessible to adults with different professional and personal commitments.

Leitura do texto 3

Main idea:

Adults return to education for professional and personal reasons, and flexible course options can help them overcome practical barriers.

Vocabulário-chave

main idea — ideia principal

topic — tópico/assunto

detail — detalhe

supporting detail — detalhe de apoio

topic sentence — frase principal do parágrafo

evidence — evidência

example — exemplo

cause — causa

effect — efeito

purpose — propósito

summary — resumo

paragraph — parágrafo

explicit — explícito

implicit — implícito

inference — inferência

overall — geral/no conjunto

mainly — principalmente

according to — de acordo com

support — sustentar/apoiar

mention — mencionar

Estratégia de prova

Para questões de ideia principal:

1. Leia o título.

2. Leia o primeiro e o último parágrafo.

3. Identifique palavras e conceitos repetidos.

4. Pergunte: qual frase cobre a maior parte do texto?

5. Elimine respostas muito amplas.

6. Elimine respostas muito específicas.

7. Elimine afirmações não sustentadas ou exageradas.

Para questões de detalhes:

1. Leia a pergunta antes de voltar ao texto.

2. Identifique palavras-chave.

3. Procure sinônimos e paráfrases, não apenas palavras iguais.

4. Leia uma ou duas frases ao redor da informação.

5. Confira quantificadores, negativos, datas e números.

Uma regra essencial:

Main idea requires synthesis. Detail questions require localization.

Prática

Com base no Texto 1:

1. What is the main idea of the text?

  1. Printed books are no longer used by university students.
  2. University libraries are adapting their services while remaining important physical study spaces.
  3. Students only use libraries during exams.
  4. Universities should remove all printed books.

2. Which is a supporting detail?

  1. Libraries are adapting to changing study habits.
  2. Some universities have added more charging points.
  3. Libraries combine traditional and digital services.
  4. Physical libraries continue to have a role.

3. Why have some libraries increased the number of computers and charging points?

  1. Students increasingly use digital materials.
  2. Printed books are illegal.
  3. Librarians no longer work there.
  4. Students stopped using technology.

4. According to the text, why do students still use physical libraries?

  1. Only to borrow printed novels.
  2. To study, work with classmates and receive support.
  3. Because digital materials are unavailable.
  4. Only because classes are held there.

5. Which statement is NOT supported?

  1. Printed books are still important.
  2. Digital materials are increasingly used.
  3. Physical libraries have become completely unnecessary.
  4. Libraries are changing the services they offer.

6. What does the final paragraph mainly do?

  1. Gives a specific statistic.
  2. Summarizes how the role of libraries is changing.
  3. Describes one student’s routine.
  4. Explains how books are printed.

Com base no Texto 2:

7. What is the main idea?

  1. Office buildings should stop using computers.
  2. Simple behavioral changes and feedback helped reduce electricity use during the project.
  3. Electricity became more expensive during six months.
  4. Four offices closed permanently.

8. How long did the project last?

  1. Four months.
  2. Six months.
  3. Twelve months.
  4. Several years.

9. What were employees encouraged to do?

  1. Buy new computers.
  2. Switch off unnecessary lights and computers.
  3. Work only at night.
  4. Use more electricity.

10. By how much did electricity use fall on average?

  1. 4%
  2. 6%
  3. 12%
  4. 20%

11. Where were the largest reductions observed?

  1. Departments receiving regular feedback.
  2. Buildings without employees.
  3. Departments that used more lighting.
  4. Offices outside the project.

12. What limitation is mentioned?

  1. No electricity data were collected.
  2. The project did not examine whether improvements would continue for years.
  3. Employees did not receive information.
  4. The project had no measurable result.

13. Which option is true but too specific to be the main idea?

  1. Electricity use fell by an average of 12%.
  2. Feedback and behavioral changes can contribute to lower energy use.
  3. The project investigated ways to reduce office electricity use.
  4. Small changes may help reduce energy consumption.

Com base no Texto 3:

14. What is the text mainly about?

  1. Only the financial cost of adult education.
  2. Reasons adults return to education and the importance of flexible learning options.
  3. Why young students prefer online courses.
  4. Why all adults should change careers.

15. Which professional reason is mentioned?

  1. Adults want to avoid qualifications.
  2. Some want qualifications to change careers.
  3. All adults are unemployed.
  4. Most adults want to become teachers.

16. Which personal reason is mentioned?

  1. Studying a subject they previously had no opportunity to explore.
  2. Receiving a salary from the university.
  3. Avoiding all family responsibilities.
  4. Moving to another country.

17. What challenge do adult learners often face?

  1. Lack of any subject to study.
  2. Work and family responsibilities.
  3. Too much free time.
  4. Universities prohibit adult students.

18. Which options help address this challenge?

  1. Evening, weekend and online courses.
  2. Only morning courses.
  3. Fewer educational opportunities.
  4. Shorter careers.

19. What is the function of the last paragraph?

  1. It gives a new unrelated example.
  2. It presents the general conclusion of the text.
  3. It contradicts all previous paragraphs.
  4. It gives a date.

20. Which sentence best summarizes the passage?

  1. All adults return to education because they dislike their jobs.
  2. Adults may study for different reasons, and flexible learning can help them combine education with other responsibilities.
  3. Adult education is only useful for career change.
  4. Online courses are the only form of adult education.

21. Identifique TOPIC, MAIN IDEA ou DETAIL:

  1. “Public transport.”

  2. “Cities are investing in public transport to reduce congestion and pollution.”

  3. “The city added 30 electric buses last year.”

22. Identifique a melhor main idea:

Texto:

Many employees value flexible working arrangements. Working from home can reduce commuting time, while flexible hours can make it easier to manage family responsibilities. However, some employees still prefer working in an office because they find collaboration easier.

  1. Employees have families.
  2. Working from home reduces commuting.
  3. Flexible work has advantages, although some employees prefer office-based work.
  4. Offices have employees.

23. Qual alternativa é ampla demais para o texto anterior?

  1. Work has changed throughout human history.
  2. Flexible work has advantages and limitations.
  3. Some workers value flexibility.
  4. Office work may make collaboration easier for some people.

24. Qual alternativa é específica demais para representar a main idea?

  1. Flexible work can affect employees in different ways.
  2. Some employees save commuting time by working from home.
  3. Flexible arrangements have both benefits and limitations.
  4. Different workers may prefer different arrangements.

25. Leia:

A new cycling route opened in the city center in June. During its first month, around 12,000 journeys were recorded. City officials say the route is part of a broader plan to encourage active transport.

Qual é o detalhe numérico?

26. Qual é a ideia principal do trecho anterior?

27. Leia:

Researchers interviewed 600 teenagers about their use of social media. Most participants said they used at least one social platform every day, but only 35% said they regularly posted public content.

A afirmação:

Most teenagers regularly posted public content.

é verdadeira ou falsa segundo o texto? Explique.

28. Leia:

The town’s population increased from 40,000 to 46,000 over five years, mainly because more people moved into the area for work.

Responda:

  1. What happened to the population?

  2. By how many people did it increase?

  3. What main reason is given?

29. Resuma em uma frase:

The university has extended library opening hours, created additional study spaces and installed more computers during the examination period. Students can also access online support from librarians until midnight.

30. Produção

Leia o texto:

A local school introduced a breakfast program after teachers noticed that some students were arriving without eating in the morning. During the first three months, around 120 students regularly used the service. Teachers reported that many participating students appeared more attentive during early lessons. However, the school has not conducted a formal study to determine whether the breakfast program directly caused the change in attention. The program will continue for the rest of the academic year.

Produza:

  • o topic;
  • a main idea em uma frase;
  • quatro supporting details;
  • uma informação que não pode ser concluída a partir do texto;
  • um resumo de 60 a 80 palavras.

Gabarito comentado

1. B

A alternativa cobre:

digital adaptation

e:

continued importance of physical libraries.

As demais são muito específicas ou contradizem o texto.

2. B

more charging points

é um exemplo concreto de mudança nos serviços.

Portanto:

supporting detail.

3. A

O primeiro parágrafo explica que:

students increasingly use digital materials.

O segundo apresenta as mudanças:

in response.

Essa expressão indica relação entre as ideias.

4. B

O texto menciona:

quiet study

group work

librarian support.

5. C

O texto afirma o contrário:

physical libraries remain important.

6. B

O parágrafo final sintetiza:

libraries are not disappearing; their role is changing.

Essa é função típica de:

conclusion/summary.

7. B

É a alternativa que representa o projeto inteiro:

behavior + feedback + reduced energy use.

8. B — Six months

Detalhe explícito.

9. B

Os trabalhadores foram incentivados a:

switch off lights and computers when unnecessary.

10. C — 12%

Questão numérica direta.

11. A

largest reductions

ocorreram onde havia:

regular feedback.

12. B

O texto limita as conclusões ao período estudado.

Não sabemos:

se o efeito continuaria por anos.

13. A

A redução de:

12%

é verdadeira, mas é apenas:

um detalhe específico.

Não representa sozinha a ideia global.

14. B

A resposta inclui os dois grandes eixos:

reasons for returning

e:

flexible learning.

15. B

O texto menciona:

qualifications that will help them change careers.

16. A

Alguns adultos querem estudar:

subjects they could not explore when younger.

17. B

work and family responsibilities.

18. A

O texto oferece:

evening

weekend

online

como alternativas.

19. B

O último parágrafo generaliza a relação:

flexibility → greater accessibility.

20. B

É a única opção que resume:

diferentes motivações

e:

necessidade de flexibilidade.

21.

  1. TOPIC

Public transport

é apenas o assunto.

  1. MAIN IDEA

Apresenta:

assunto + mensagem central.

  1. DETAIL

30 electric buses

é informação específica.

22. C

O texto apresenta:

benefits of flexibility

mas também:

preference for office work among some workers.

A alternativa C representa ambos.

23. A

Work has changed throughout human history.

É ampla demais.

O texto é especificamente sobre:

flexible working arrangements.

24. B

commuting time

é apenas um dos benefícios apresentados.

Logo, é específica demais para resumir o texto inteiro.

25.

Around 12,000 journeys were recorded during the first month.

Esse é o detalhe numérico.

26.

Modelo:

The city has opened a new cycling route as part of a broader effort to encourage active transport.

27.

Falsa.

O texto afirma:

most participants used social media every day

mas apenas:

35%

publicavam conteúdo público regularmente.

A alternativa troca:

daily use

por:

regular public posting.

28.

It increased.

By 6,000 people.

Cálculo:

46,000 − 40,000 = 6,000.

More people moved into the area for work.

29.

Modelo:

The university has expanded library and online study support during the examination period.

Esse resumo reúne:

longer hours

more study spaces

more computers

online librarian support

em uma ideia mais geral.

30.

Topic

A school breakfast program.

Main idea

A local school introduced a breakfast program for students who were arriving without eating, and teachers observed possible improvements in attention, although no causal relationship has been formally established.

Supporting details

  1. The program was introduced after teachers noticed that some students arrived without breakfast.

  2. Around 120 students regularly used the service during the first three months.

  3. Teachers reported that many participating students appeared more attentive in early lessons.

  4. The program will continue for the rest of the academic year.

Informação que não pode ser concluída

The breakfast program definitely caused the improvement in attention.

O próprio texto afirma:

no formal study has established causation.

Resumo

A local school introduced a breakfast program after teachers noticed that some students were arriving without eating. Around 120 students regularly used the service during its first three months. Teachers observed that many participants appeared more attentive during early lessons, although no formal study has shown that breakfast directly caused this change. The program is expected to continue throughout the rest of the academic year.

Tarefa de consolidação

Para dez textos curtos, preencha:

Topic

Main idea

Detail 1

Detail 2

Detail 3

Author’s purpose

One possible inference

One conclusion that would be unsupported

Depois pratique transformar detalhes em uma generalização.

Exemplo:

more computers

longer opening hours

online support

additional study rooms

Generalização:

The university expanded student support services.

Faça o processo inverso também.

Main idea:

Cities are encouraging sustainable transport.

Crie detalhes possíveis:

new cycle lanes

more buses

lower public transport fares

pedestrian areas.

Depois treine os três principais tipos de resposta errada:

Too broad — ampla demais.

Too narrow — específica demais.

Unsupported — não sustentada.

Para cada texto, crie uma alternativa de cada tipo e uma correta.

Pratique ainda as palavras das perguntas:

mainly

main idea

best summary

according to

why

how many

NOT

EXCEPT

mentioned

implied

inferred.

Finalize memorizando:

Topic = sobre o que o texto fala.

Main idea = o que o texto diz principalmente sobre esse assunto.

Supporting details = informações que explicam, exemplificam ou sustentam essa ideia.

Antes de marcar uma resposta de ideia principal, pergunte:

Essa alternativa representa o texto inteiro ou apenas uma frase dele?

Antes de responder a uma questão de detalhe, pergunte:

Qual informação específica a pergunta está pedindo e onde ela provavelmente aparece?

Dominar essa distinção permite ler de forma seletiva: você deixa de tratar todas as frases como igualmente importantes e passa a enxergar a hierarquia das informações no texto.

Aula 88 — Referência pronominal e coesão

Objetivos

Ao final desta aula, você deverá ser capaz de:

  • compreender o que é referência pronominal;
  • identificar a que palavra ou ideia um pronome se refere;
  • reconhecer relações de coesão entre frases e parágrafos;
  • interpretar corretamente it, they, this, that, these, those e outros elementos referenciais;
  • compreender o uso de who, which, that e whose como elementos coesivos;
  • identificar referentes de pronomes pessoais e possessivos;
  • reconhecer referências a ideias inteiras, e não apenas a substantivos;
  • compreender o papel de conectores na coesão textual;
  • distinguir referência anafórica e referência catafórica em nível introdutório;
  • evitar ambiguidades na leitura;
  • usar contexto, número e significado para identificar referentes;
  • aplicar essas estratégias em Reading B1.

Desenvolvimento

Quando lemos um texto, muitas palavras não podem ser compreendidas isoladamente.

Considere:

Sarah bought a new laptop. She needed it for university.

Temos:

She → Sarah

it → a new laptop.

Os pronomes evitam repetição.

Sem eles:

Sarah bought a new laptop. Sarah needed the new laptop for university.

A frase fica:

repetitiva.

A coesão ajuda o texto a funcionar como:

uma sequência conectada de ideias.

Cohesion

Cohesion significa:

coesão.

Refere-se às relações linguísticas que conectam partes do texto.

Essas conexões podem ser feitas por:

  • pronomes;
  • palavras repetidas;
  • sinônimos;
  • substituições;
  • conectores;
  • relative pronouns;
  • expressões como this problem, these results, such changes.

Reference

Reference é o mecanismo pelo qual uma palavra aponta para:

outra palavra

ou:

uma ideia.

Exemplo:

The company launched a new app. It became popular quickly.

It

refere-se a:

the new app.

Antecedent

O elemento ao qual o pronome se refere é chamado de:

antecedent.

Exemplo:

The students finished the project. They submitted it on Friday.

Antecedentes:

they → the students

it → the project.

Referência anafórica

Quando uma palavra aponta para algo já mencionado anteriormente, temos:

anaphoric reference.

Exemplo:

Maria called the university. She wanted more information.

She

aponta para algo anterior:

Maria.

Esse é o padrão mais comum em Reading.

Referência catafórica

Às vezes, o pronome aparece primeiro e a informação vem depois.

Exemplo:

When he entered the room, Daniel looked nervous.

he

é explicado depois por:

Daniel.

Isso é chamado:

cataphoric reference.

No nível B1, basta reconhecer que nem sempre o referente aparece antes.

Subject pronouns

Principais:

I

you

he

she

it

we

they.

Em textos, os mais importantes para referência são:

he

she

it

they.

He

Normalmente aponta para:

homem/menino previamente mencionado.

David works at the hospital. He is a nurse.

She

Laura studies biology. She wants to become a researcher.

It

It pode ser mais complexo.

Pode apontar para:

  • coisa;
  • animal;
  • situação;
  • evento;
  • ideia anterior.

Exemplo simples:

I bought a book. It was expensive.

it → book.

It para situação

The road was closed for six hours. It caused major delays.

Nesse caso:

it

pode referir-se ao fato de:

the road being closed

dependendo do contexto.

Mas frequentemente uma frase mais natural seria:

This caused major delays.

They

Pode apontar para:

plural noun.

Exemplo:

The researchers interviewed 200 students. They answered questions about sleep.

Quem respondeu?

the students.

Mas cuidado.

Texto:

The researchers interviewed 200 students. They later published the results.

Agora:

they

provavelmente refere-se a:

the researchers.

A gramática sozinha nem sempre resolve.

Precisamos usar:

meaning.

Number agreement

Número ajuda.

The student lost her notebook. She looked for it.

she → singular person.

it → singular object.

The students lost their notebooks. They looked for them.

they → plural people.

them → plural objects.

Object pronouns

Principais:

me

you

him

her

it

us

them.

Exemplo:

I spoke to Daniel. I asked him about the course.

him → Daniel.

Outro:

The books were on the desk. I moved them.

them → books.

Possessive adjectives

my

your

his

her

its

our

their.

Exemplo:

Emma submitted her assignment.

her → Emma.

Their

The students completed their projects.

their → students.

Its

The company changed its policy.

its → company.

Não confunda:

its

com:

it’s.

Its:

possessive.

It’s:

it is

ou:

it has.

Possessive pronouns

mine

yours

his

hers

ours

theirs.

Exemplo:

My laptop is old, but hers is new.

hers → her laptop.

Demonstratives

this

that

these

those.

Podem apontar para:

objetos

ou:

ideias.

This + noun

Pollution has increased rapidly. This problem affects several neighborhoods.

this problem

retoma:

pollution increasing rapidly.

These + noun

The city introduced new bus routes and reduced ticket prices. These changes increased passenger numbers.

these changes

retoma:

new routes + reduced prices.

That

Pode apontar para:

algo anterior

ou comparar elementos.

Exemplo:

The population of City A is larger than that of City B.

that

substitui:

the population.

Those

The salaries of experienced workers are higher than those of new employees.

those

substitui:

the salaries.

This como referência a frase inteira

Exemplo:

The university extended library opening hours until midnight. This helped students study after evening classes.

This

não representa apenas:

library.

Representa:

the decision to extend opening hours.

Isso é extremamente importante em Reading.

These findings

Muito comum em divulgação científica.

Participants who exercised regularly reported better sleep. These findings suggest that physical activity may be associated with sleep quality.

These findings

refere-se:

aos resultados apresentados anteriormente.

This result

Group A scored 10% higher than Group B. This result surprised the researchers.

this result → Group A scoring 10% higher.

This change

Bus fares were reduced by 20%. This change increased passenger numbers.

This suggests that

Estrutura comum:

This suggests that…

O:

this

normalmente resume:

evidence immediately before it.

Such

Such também pode criar coesão.

The city experienced several days of extreme heat. Such conditions can be dangerous for older adults.

such conditions

significa:

conditions like those just mentioned.

Such a change

Working hours were reduced significantly. Such a change can affect productivity.

One / ones

Podem substituir substantivos.

I need a new laptop because my old one is slow.

one → laptop.

Plural:

These shoes are more comfortable than the old ones.

ones → shoes.

Do so

Em textos mais formais, pode substituir uma ação.

Participants were asked to complete the form, but only 80% did so.

did so → completed the form.

So como substituição de ideia

“Will prices increase?”
“Experts believe so.”

so → that prices will increase.

Not

Também:

“Will the meeting be canceled?”
“Probably not.”

not → the meeting will probably not be canceled.

Relative pronouns e coesão

Relative clauses conectam informações.

The researcher who led the study works at Central University.

who → researcher.

Which

The device, which costs less than $50, was tested in three schools.

which → device.

That

The book that I borrowed was useful.

that → book.

Whose

The student whose project won the prize…

whose → student

e indica:

possession.

Where

The town where the study was conducted…

where → town.

When

The year when the program started…

when → year.

Pronome relativo e antecedente

Para identificar o referente:

  1. procure o substantivo imediatamente anterior;
  2. verifique se o significado faz sentido;
  3. confira singular/plural;
  4. leia a oração inteira.

Which referindo-se a uma oração inteira

Observe:

The train was delayed for three hours, which caused many passengers to miss their connections.

Aqui:

which

não se refere apenas:

train.

Refere-se ao fato:

de o trem ter atrasado três horas.

Isso é comum em textos B1/B2.

Outro exemplo

The company reduced prices, which increased sales.

which → the fact that the company reduced prices.

Reference chain

Um texto pode criar uma cadeia:

A research team developed a new sensor. The device was tested in three cities. It produced accurate results in most conditions. These findings encouraged the researchers to continue the project.

Temos:

a new sensor

→ the device

→ it.

Depois:

accurate results

→ these findings.

Essas cadeias ajudam a manter:

continuidade temática.

Lexical cohesion

Coesão não depende apenas de pronomes.

Também pode ocorrer por palavras semanticamente relacionadas.

Exemplo:

A new hospital opened last month. The medical center has 200 beds.

hospital

e:

medical center

podem apontar para:

a mesma instituição.

Repetition

The project began in January. The project will continue until June.

Repetição também cria coesão, embora escritores frequentemente usem outras formas para evitar excesso.

Synonymy

The company launched a new device. The product will be sold internationally.

device → product.

General word

A new train service started yesterday. The system connects five towns.

system

é uma forma mais geral de retomar:

train service.

Superordinate terms

Exemplo:

Buses, trains and bicycles are becoming more common. These forms of transport can reduce car use.

forms of transport

resume:

buses, trains and bicycles.

Cohesion x coherence

Não são exatamente iguais.

Cohesion:

conexões linguísticas visíveis.

Coherence:

lógica geral e sentido do texto.

Um texto pode ter muitos conectores, mas ainda ser:

incoerente

se as ideias não fizerem sentido juntas.

Connectors

Elementos de coesão importantes:

however

therefore

moreover

in addition

for example

as a result

because

although

while

first

then

finally.

Addition

also

in addition

moreover

furthermore.

Exemplo:

The course is free. In addition, students receive all materials.

Contrast

but

however

although

while

whereas.

Exemplo:

The program was expensive. However, it produced positive results.

Cause

because

because of

due to.

Result

so

therefore

consequently

as a result.

Example

for example

for instance

such as.

Sequence

first

next

then

finally.

Reference and connectors together

The city reduced bus fares. As a result, more people started using public transport. This increase was particularly strong during weekends.

As a result → conecta causa e consequência.

This increase → retoma aumento no número de passageiros.

Identificação de referente em prova

Pergunta típica:

What does “it” in line 8 refer to?

Não responda:

pela palavra mais próxima automaticamente.

Use um procedimento.

Método 1 — procure candidatos

Exemplo:

The company tested a new battery in an electric vehicle. It lasted 20% longer than the previous model.

Candidatos:

company

battery

vehicle.

Qual pode:

last 20% longer?

Provavelmente:

battery.

Método 2 — concordância

They

precisa normalmente de referente plural.

it

normalmente singular.

these

plural.

this

singular ou ideia inteira.

Método 3 — semântica

The researchers interviewed the patients after they left the hospital.

Quem:

left the hospital?

Provavelmente:

patients.

Não:

researchers

dependendo do contexto.

Ambiguidade real

Algumas frases podem ser ambíguas.

Maria spoke to Ana after she finished work.

Quem terminou o trabalho?

Pode ser:

Maria

ou:

Ana.

Sem contexto adicional, não podemos determinar.

Em provas bem elaboradas, haverá normalmente:

pistas suficientes.

Não invente certeza

Se a frase é genuinamente ambígua:

reconheça a ambiguidade.

It impessoal

Nem todo it possui antecedente.

Exemplo:

It is raining.

O:

it

não aponta para um substantivo anterior.

Outro:

It is important to study regularly.

Esse it é:

dummy/impersonal it.

Não procure antecedente.

Weather it

It is cold today.

It was raining.

Sem antecedente lexical.

Time

It is five o’clock.

Distance

It is ten kilometers from here to the airport.

Anticipatory it

It is difficult to understand this text.

O it funciona estruturalmente, enquanto a ideia real é:

to understand this text.

There como estrutura existencial

Também não confunda:

There are three problems.

Aqui:

there

não significa necessariamente:

naquele lugar.

É uma estrutura:

existential there.

They genérico

Em alguns contextos:

they say…

pode significar:

people say

sem um referente específico.

Exemplo:

They say the weather will improve.

Mas em textos de prova, veja se existe um grupo específico mencionado anteriormente.

You genérico

You need water to survive.

You pode significar:

people in general.

Não necessariamente:

o leitor individualmente.

We inclusivo

We all need access to clean water.

Pode incluir:

writer + readers + people generally.

This/that e distância discursiva

De modo simplificado:

this/these

frequentemente mantêm a ideia mais próxima do foco atual.

that/those

podem marcar maior distância ou comparação.

Mas essa distinção é flexível em textos reais.

Former e latter

Considere:

The study compared online and face-to-face learning. The former offered more flexibility, while the latter produced more classroom interaction.

former → online learning.

latter → face-to-face learning.

The first / the second

Outra forma:

Two methods were tested. The first was faster, but the second was more accurate.

Respectively

Anna and David scored 80 and 90 points, respectively.

Significa:

Anna → 80

David → 90.

Essa palavra ajuda a estabelecer referência entre listas.

Reference by repetition of noun

Às vezes o texto repete parte do substantivo:

A new recycling program started in April. The program has already collected 50 tons of material.

Isso reduz ambiguidade.

Nominalization e coesão

Textos mais formais podem transformar ações em substantivos.

The city decided to expand the service. This decision was welcomed by residents.

decided → decision.

A palavra:

decision

retoma:

a ação descrita anteriormente.

Outros exemplos

Prices increased rapidly. This increase affected consumers.

The company expanded. The expansion created new jobs.

Researchers discovered a problem. The discovery led to further studies.

Esse processo é muito frequente em textos acadêmicos.

Word families ajudam

improve → improvement

decide → decision

expand → expansion

reduce → reduction

discover → discovery

develop → development.

Reconhecer a família ajuda a seguir a referência.

Synonyms e reference

Children

pode ser retomado por:

young people

students

dependendo do contexto.

Mas verifique se os grupos realmente são equivalentes.

Não assuma automaticamente que:

students = all young people.

Texto 1

Remote Work and Office Space

Many companies expanded remote work during the last few years. This change allowed employees to work from home more frequently and reduced the number of people using offices every day.

As a result, some organizations began reconsidering the amount of office space they needed. Several companies moved to smaller buildings, while others redesigned their existing offices to include more shared work areas.

These strategies can reduce costs, but they may also create challenges. Employees sometimes report difficulty finding quiet spaces when many colleagues come to the office on the same day.

For this reason, some companies now use booking systems that allow workers to reserve desks or meeting rooms before arriving.

Cadeias no texto 1

expanded remote work → this change.

smaller buildings/redesigned offices → these strategies.

difficulty finding spaces → this reason.

A compreensão depende de identificar:

qual ideia está sendo retomada.

Texto 2

A New Water-Monitoring Project

Researchers installed sensors in five rivers to measure water temperature and pollution levels. The devices send information to a central computer every hour.

This allows researchers to identify sudden changes more quickly. When unusual measurements are detected, they can investigate the affected area and collect additional samples.

The project began in March and will continue for two years. Its main goal is to provide local authorities with more detailed information about river conditions.

Scientists say the system could eventually be expanded to other regions.

Cadeias no texto 2

sensors → the devices.

sending information → this.

researchers → they.

project → its.

system → conjunto de sensores/monitoramento.

Texto 3

Community Gardens

A city has created ten community gardens on unused public land. Local residents can grow vegetables and herbs in them, and schools are also using some of the spaces for environmental education.

The gardens have become popular, particularly in neighborhoods where many people live in apartments without private outdoor areas. This has encouraged the city to consider creating additional sites next year.

Supporters say the project provides several benefits. It gives residents access to fresh food, creates opportunities for social interaction and makes use of land that was previously empty.

Cadeias no texto 3

gardens → them.

gardens becoming popular → this.

community gardens initiative → the project.

the project → it.

Vocabulário-chave

reference — referência

pronoun — pronome

antecedent — antecedente

cohesion — coesão

coherence — coerência

referent — referente

anaphoric reference — referência ao que apareceu antes

cataphoric reference — referência ao que aparece depois

demonstrative — demonstrativo

substitution — substituição

repetition — repetição

synonym — sinônimo

connector — conector

linking word — palavra de ligação

this change — essa mudança

these results — esses resultados

such conditions — tais condições

former — primeiro de dois elementos

latter — segundo de dois elementos

Estratégia de prova

Quando uma questão perguntar:

What does “it/they/this/these/which” refer to?

Use quatro passos.

1. Olhe para trás no texto

Procure:

possíveis antecedentes.

2. Verifique número e tipo

it → normalmente singular.

they/them → plural.

this → singular ou ideia.

these → plural.

who → pessoa.

which → coisa ou ideia anterior.

3. Teste o significado

Substitua mentalmente o pronome pelo candidato.

Exemplo:

The sensor was tested for six months. It produced accurate results.

Teste:

The sensor produced accurate results.

Faz sentido.

4. Observe se o pronome resume uma frase inteira

Exemplo:

Ticket prices were reduced. This increased demand.

this

não é:

ticket prices.

É:

the reduction in ticket prices.

Essa distinção resolve muitas questões B1.

Prática

Com base no Texto 1:

1. What does “This change” refer to?

  1. Employees moving to another country.
  2. The expansion of remote work.
  3. The construction of new offices.
  4. The reduction of salaries.

2. In “the amount of office space they needed”, what does “they” refer to?

  1. offices
  2. employees
  3. organizations/companies
  4. buildings

3. What does “These strategies” refer to?

  1. Moving to smaller buildings and redesigning offices.
  2. Working more hours.
  3. Increasing salaries.
  4. Building private homes.

4. In “but they may also create challenges”, what does “they” refer to?

  1. employees
  2. strategies
  3. offices only
  4. costs

5. What does “For this reason” refer to?

  1. The cost of remote work.
  2. Difficulties finding suitable office spaces when many employees attend.
  3. The popularity of home offices.
  4. The construction of large offices.

Com base no Texto 2:

6. What does “The devices” refer to?

  1. rivers
  2. sensors
  3. computers
  4. samples

7. What does “This” refer to in “This allows researchers…”?

  1. Rivers becoming polluted.
  2. The devices sending information every hour.
  3. Researchers collecting samples.
  4. The project lasting two years.

8. In “they can investigate”, what does “they” refer to?

  1. measurements
  2. researchers
  3. rivers
  4. computers

9. What does “Its” refer to in “Its main goal”?

  1. March
  2. the central computer
  3. the project
  4. local authorities

10. What does “the system” most likely refer to?

  1. The water-monitoring arrangement using sensors and data.
  2. One river only.
  3. The local government.
  4. March.

Com base no Texto 3:

11. What does “them” refer to?

Local residents can grow vegetables and herbs in them.

  1. vegetables
  2. schools
  3. community gardens
  4. apartments

12. What does “some of the spaces” refer to?

  1. some of the gardens
  2. some schools
  3. private apartments
  4. vegetables

13. What does “This” refer to?

This has encouraged the city to consider creating additional sites.

  1. Apartments having private gardens.
  2. The gardens becoming popular.
  3. Schools closing.
  4. Land becoming expensive.

14. What does “the project” refer to?

  1. The apartment construction project.
  2. The community garden initiative.
  3. A school exam.
  4. A private farming company.

15. What does “It” refer to?

It gives residents access to fresh food.

  1. fresh food
  2. the project
  3. social interaction
  4. the city government only

16. Identifique o referente:

Sarah bought a new tablet because her old one was broken.

one → ______

17. Identifique:

The researchers published two reports. The first focused on health, while the second examined education.

the second → ______

18. Identifique:

Air pollution increased during the winter. This led to more respiratory complaints.

This → ______

19. Identifique:

The city opened three new clinics. These facilities provide basic healthcare.

These facilities → ______

20. Identifique:

The course includes reading and listening activities. The former is assessed with two texts, while the latter uses short recordings.

former → ______

latter → ______

21. Escolha o referente correto:

The teacher spoke to the students after they completed the test.

O referente mais provável de:

they

é:

  1. teacher
  2. students
  3. test
  4. impossible to infer in any context

22. Leia:

The company introduced flexible working hours. This decision was popular with employees.

Qual relação coesiva existe entre:

introduced flexible working hours

e:

this decision?

  1. Contradição.
  2. Nominalização/referência à ação anterior.
  3. Comparação numérica.
  4. Não existe relação.

23. Leia:

The population increased by 8%. This growth was mainly caused by migration.

O que:

this growth

retoma?

24. Leia:

The device was cheap and easy to use, which made it attractive to small schools.

O que which retoma mais provavelmente?

  1. only the device
  2. the fact that the device was cheap and easy to use
  3. small schools
  4. use only

25. Leia:

The university extended library hours and created more study spaces. These changes were introduced during the exam period.

Liste os dois elementos retomados por:

these changes.

26. Classifique como referência ou conector:

  1. however

  2. it

  3. therefore

  4. these findings

  5. although

  6. they

27. Corrija a ambiguidade:

Laura spoke to Emma after she finished the presentation.

Reescreva de duas formas:

  1. deixando claro que Laura terminou a apresentação;

  2. deixando claro que Emma terminou a apresentação.

28. Complete com um elemento coesivo adequado:

The university reduced course fees. ______ made the program more accessible to low-income students.

  1. This
  2. They
  3. Those person
  4. Them

29. Complete o texto:

Researchers developed a new educational app. ______ was tested by 300 students for three months. The participants completed weekly activities, and ______ results were recorded automatically. At the end of the study, most students reported that the app was easy to use. ______ finding encouraged the research team to conduct a larger study.

Preencha com:

it / their / this

nas posições adequadas.

30. Produção

Escreva um texto de 130 a 160 palavras sobre um projeto fictício de uma escola, universidade, empresa ou comunidade.

Use intencionalmente:

  • it com antecedente claro;
  • they com antecedente plural;
  • this change;
  • these results;
  • its;
  • one/ones;
  • uma relative clause com which ou who;
  • um conector de contraste;
  • um conector de consequência.

Depois, abaixo do texto, indique o referente de cada elemento pronominal utilizado.

Gabarito comentado

1. B

This change

retoma:

companies expanded remote work.

A mudança foi:

maior uso de trabalho remoto.

2. C

Quem reconsiderou o espaço necessário?

some organizations.

Logo:

they → organizations/companies.

3. A

As estratégias mencionadas imediatamente antes são:

moving to smaller buildings

e:

redesigning existing offices.

4. B

they

retoma:

these strategies.

Teste:

These strategies may also create challenges.

Faz sentido.

5. B

A razão imediatamente anterior é:

employees sometimes have difficulty finding quiet spaces when many colleagues are present.

Por isso:

companies use booking systems.

6. B — sensors

Primeiro:

Researchers installed sensors.

Depois:

The devices…

É substituição lexical:

sensors → devices.

7. B

This

resume a ação anterior:

the devices send information every hour.

Essa transmissão frequente:

allows researchers to detect sudden changes.

8. B

Quem pode:

investigate

e:

collect samples?

researchers.

9. C — the project

The project began in March…

Its main goal…

10. A

the system

refere-se ao sistema de monitoramento descrito no texto:

sensores + envio de dados + análise.

11. C

them → community gardens.

12. A

spaces

retoma:

gardens.

As escolas usam:

some of the gardens.

13. B

A frase anterior diz que:

the gardens have become popular.

Essa popularidade:

encouraged the city to consider expansion.

14. B

the project

é a iniciativa dos:

community gardens.

15. B

It gives residents…

It → the project.

16.

tablet.

Mais precisamente:

her old tablet.

17.

the second report.

18.

the increase in air pollution during winter.

Não apenas:

air pollution.

O demonstrativo resume:

a situação/evento anterior.

19.

the three new clinics.

Aqui temos coesão lexical:

clinics → facilities.

20.

former → reading activities.

latter → listening activities.

21. B

O significado mais natural é:

students completed the test.

O plural:

they

também corresponde:

students.

22. B

A ação:

introduced flexible working hours

é retomada como substantivo:

this decision.

Isso é um mecanismo importante de coesão.

23.

the 8% increase in population.

increase → growth

é uma relação lexical dentro da mesma família de significado.

24. B

O which retoma a proposição:

the device was cheap and easy to use.

Essa combinação de características:

made it attractive.

25.

extending library opening hours

e:

creating more study spaces.

These changes resume:

duas ações anteriores.

26.

  1. connector

however → contraste.

  1. reference

it → pronome.

  1. connector

therefore → consequência.

  1. reference

these findings → retoma resultados anteriores.

  1. connector

although → contraste/concessão.

  1. reference

they → pronome.

27.

  1. Laura terminou:

After Laura finished the presentation, she spoke to Emma.

Ou:

Laura spoke to Emma after Laura had finished the presentation.

  1. Emma terminou:

Laura spoke to Emma after Emma finished the presentation.

Repetir o nome pode ser preferível quando o pronome criaria ambiguidade.

28. A — This

This

retoma:

the university reduced course fees.

A redução tornou:

the program more accessible.

29.

Researchers developed a new educational app. It was tested by 300 students for three months. The participants completed weekly activities, and their results were recorded automatically. At the end of the study, most students reported that the app was easy to use. This finding encouraged the research team to conduct a larger study.

it → app.

their → participants/students.

this → finding that most students considered the app easy to use.

30.

Modelo:

A community center introduced a free evening course for adults who wanted to improve their digital skills. It initially offered twenty places, but demand was much higher than expected. The organizers therefore created two additional groups, and they also extended the course from six to eight weeks. This change allowed more time for practical activities. The program has its own computer room, although some machines are older than the newer ones used in other courses. At the end of the first term, participants completed a short assessment. These results showed that most learners had improved their basic computer skills. The course, which was originally planned as a temporary project, will therefore continue next year. However, its organizers still need additional funding to expand it further.

Referentes:

It → the free evening course.

they → the organizers.

This change → extending the course from six to eight weeks.

its → the program/course.

ones → machines/computers.

These results → results of the assessment.

which → the course.

segundo its → the course/project organizers’ program.

Tarefa de consolidação

Pegue dez textos curtos e sublinhe:

todos os pronomes;

demonstrativos;

possessivos;

relative pronouns;

expressões como this change, these findings, such problems.

Para cada item, escreva:

referential expression → antecedent

Exemplo:

it → the sensor

they → the researchers

this result → the 12% reduction

these findings → the results of the study.

Depois crie cinco cadeias coesivas.

Exemplo:

a new application
→ the app
→ it
→ the software
→ this tool.

Faça o mesmo com:

a research project

a hospital

a public transport program

a group of students

a scientific study.

Em seguida, pratique referências a ideias inteiras.

Exemplo:

The university reduced fees.

Crie:

This made the course more accessible.

This decision increased enrollment.

The change was welcomed by students.

Depois revise nominalizações importantes:

decide → decision

increase → increase/growth

reduce → reduction

improve → improvement

expand → expansion

discover → discovery

develop → development.

Observe como uma ação pode ser retomada como:

substantivo

na frase seguinte.

Finalize memorizando o procedimento:

1. Localize o pronome ou expressão referencial.

2. Procure candidatos próximos.

3. Verifique singular/plural e pessoa/coisa.

4. Teste o significado.

5. Pergunte se a referência é a uma palavra específica ou a uma ideia inteira.

Em Reading B1, não basta entender cada frase separadamente. A compreensão do texto depende de acompanhar quem, o quê e qual ideia continua sendo retomada ao longo dos parágrafos. É justamente essa rede de referências que produz a coesão textual.

Aula 89 — Conectores e relações lógico-semânticas

Objetivos

Ao final desta aula, você deverá ser capaz de:

  • compreender o papel dos connectors na organização de textos;
  • identificar relações de adição, contraste, causa, consequência, exemplificação, sequência, condição, concessão e conclusão;
  • reconhecer conectores frequentes em Reading B1;
  • distinguir conectores com significados próximos, como because, because of, although, however, therefore e despite;
  • compreender como a pontuação muda de acordo com o conector;
  • identificar a relação lógica entre duas ideias mesmo quando o conector não está explícito;
  • usar conectores para prever o desenvolvimento do texto;
  • reconhecer paráfrases entre conectores;
  • diferenciar causa de consequência;
  • usar conectores corretamente em Writing e Speaking;
  • evitar erros estruturais frequentes;
  • melhorar a interpretação de textos jornalísticos, científicos e acadêmicos.

Desenvolvimento

Os connectors, também chamados de:

linking words

linking expressions

discourse markers

são palavras ou expressões que mostram:

como uma ideia se relaciona com outra.

Considere:

It was raining. We stayed home.

As duas frases estão relacionadas, mas a relação não está explicitamente marcada.

Podemos escrever:

We stayed home because it was raining.

Agora fica claro:

chuva → causa

ficar em casa → consequência.

Relações lógico-semânticas

Em Reading, uma das habilidades mais importantes é identificar relações como:

addition

contrast

cause

effect/result

example

sequence

condition

concession

purpose

conclusion.

Mesmo quando você não entende todas as palavras, reconhecer o conector pode indicar:

o papel da próxima informação.

Addition

Conectores de adição introduzem:

informação adicional.

Principais:

and

also

in addition

moreover

furthermore

as well as

besides.

And

O conector mais básico:

The course includes Reading and Writing.

Também conecta orações:

The library was renovated, and new computers were installed.

Also

The course teaches grammar. It also includes pronunciation practice.

Posição frequente:

subject + also + main verb.

Exemplo:

Students also receive online materials.

Com o verbo be:

The course is also available online.

In addition

The program is free. In addition, students receive all materials.

Normalmente acrescenta:

outro ponto relevante.

Moreover

Mais formal:

The new system is cheaper. Moreover, it is easier to use.

Furthermore

Também mais formal:

The study had a large sample. Furthermore, participants came from several regions.

As well as

The course develops speaking skills as well as reading skills.

Pode ser entendido como:

além de.

Besides

Besides reducing costs, the system saves time.

Dependendo do contexto:

além de.

Adição em Reading

Texto:

The new library offers longer opening hours. In addition, students can access digital materials from home.

A segunda frase:

adiciona outro benefício.

Se a questão perguntar a função de:

in addition

resposta:

addition.

Contrast

Conectores de contraste mostram:

diferença

oposição

informação inesperada.

Principais:

but

however

although

though

even though

while

whereas

on the other hand

in contrast.

But

The course is expensive, but it is very popular.

Temos:

negative point → expensive

contrasting point → popular.

However

The course is expensive. However, it is very popular.

However conecta ideias, mas funciona de maneira diferente de:

but.

Normalmente aparece:

depois de ponto

ou:

depois de ponto e vírgula.

Exemplo:

The results were positive. However, further research is needed.

Erro comum com however

Evite:

The results were positive, however further research is needed.

Em escrita formal, prefira:

The results were positive. However, further research is needed.

Ou:

The results were positive; however, further research is needed.

Although

Although the course is expensive, it is very popular.

Estrutura:

although + clause.

Outro:

The course is very popular although it is expensive.

Though

Muito semelhante a:

although.

Though the test was difficult, most students passed.

Em contextos mais informais, though também pode aparecer no final:

It was difficult, though.

Even though

Marca contraste/concessão mais forte:

Even though it was raining heavily, the event continued.

Although x but

Evite usar os dois na mesma estrutura básica.

Errado:

Although the course is expensive, but it is popular.

Correto:

Although the course is expensive, it is popular.

Ou:

The course is expensive, but it is popular.

While

Pode mostrar contraste:

While some students prefer online classes, others prefer face-to-face lessons.

Mas também pode significar:

enquanto

no sentido temporal.

I listened to music while I studied.

O contexto determina a relação.

Whereas

Online courses offer flexibility, whereas classroom courses provide more direct interaction.

É muito útil em:

comparisons.

On the other hand

Working from home saves commuting time. On the other hand, some employees miss face-to-face interaction.

Apresenta:

outro lado da questão.

In contrast

City A reduced car use. In contrast, City B experienced an increase.

Cause

Conectores causais explicam:

why something happened.

Principais:

because

because of

since

as

due to.

Because

Estrutura:

because + clause.

Exemplo:

The flight was canceled because the weather was bad.

Depois de:

because

temos:

subject + verb.

Because of

Estrutura:

because of + noun/noun phrase.

The flight was canceled because of bad weather.

Não:

because of the weather was bad.

Compare

We stayed home because it was raining.

We stayed home because of the rain.

Since

Pode indicar causa:

Since the weather was bad, the event was canceled.

Mas também pode ter sentido temporal:

since 2020.

Por isso:

observe o contexto.

As

Também pode expressar causa:

As the roads were flooded, buses were delayed.

Mas as possui outros usos.

No B1, reconheça principalmente:

causa

quando conecta duas orações dessa forma.

Due to

The flight was delayed due to fog.

Estrutura comum:

due to + noun phrase.

Exemplo:

The event was canceled due to heavy rain.

Cause verbs

A relação causal também pode aparecer sem conector tradicional.

Exemplos:

Pollution causes health problems.

Heavy rain led to flooding.

The error resulted in delays.

Lead to

lead to + noun.

Lack of sleep can lead to concentration problems.

Result in

result in + result.

The power failure resulted in major delays.

Consequence / Result

Conectores de consequência mostram:

what happened because of something else.

Principais:

so

therefore

consequently

as a result

thus.

So

It was raining, so we stayed home.

Muito comum na fala e em textos menos formais.

Therefore

Mais formal:

The road was flooded. Therefore, the bus service was suspended.

Consequently

The company lost several customers. Consequently, sales fell.

As a result

Temperatures increased significantly. As a result, energy use rose.

Muito frequente em textos acadêmicos e jornalísticos.

Thus

Mais formal:

The sample was too small. Thus, the results cannot be generalized.

No B1, é importante principalmente:

reconhecer.

Cause x result

Compare:

The road was closed because of flooding.

Flooding:

cause.

Road closure:

result.

Agora:

There was flooding, so the road was closed.

A mesma relação é apresentada a partir da consequência.

Because x therefore

The event was canceled because the weather was bad.

The weather was bad. Therefore, the event was canceled.

A relação é a mesma, mas:

direção da construção muda.

Purpose

Conectores de finalidade explicam:

why someone does something

no sentido de objetivo.

Principais:

to

in order to

so that.

To + infinitive

I went to the library to study.

Finalidade:

study.

In order to

Mais explícito/formal:

The city added more buses in order to reduce traffic.

So that

The university extended opening hours so that students could study later.

Estrutura:

so that + subject + verb.

Purpose x cause

Compare:

I went home because I was tired.

Causa.

I went home to rest.

Finalidade.

Example

Conectores de exemplificação introduzem:

exemplos.

Principais:

for example

for instance

such as

including.

For example

Many activities improve cardiovascular health. For example, walking can be beneficial.

For instance

Muito semelhante:

Some digital tools can improve learning. For instance, online quizzes provide immediate feedback.

Such as

Renewable energy sources, such as solar and wind power, are becoming more common.

Depois de:

such as

aparecem exemplos.

Including

The course covers several skills, including Reading and Writing.

Example x definition

Se o texto diz:

such as…

não significa que a lista seja necessariamente:

completa.

Exemplo:

languages such as English and Spanish

não significa:

only English and Spanish.

Sequence

Conectores de sequência organizam:

ordem de eventos

ou:

etapas de processo.

Principais:

first

first of all

then

next

after that

afterwards

finally

eventually

meanwhile.

First

First, complete the form.

Then

Then, upload the document.

Next

Next, click “Submit”.

After that

After that, wait for confirmation.

Finally

Finally, check your email.

Eventually

After several attempts, the researchers eventually found a solution.

Significa:

finalmente, depois de algum tempo.

Não:

ocasionalmente.

Meanwhile

The firefighters entered the building. Meanwhile, police closed the road.

Duas ações ocorrem:

aproximadamente ao mesmo tempo.

Before / after

Before submitting the form, check your information.

After finishing the exam, review your answers.

Também mostram:

relação temporal.

Condition

Conectores condicionais mostram que:

uma situação depende de outra.

Principais:

if

unless

as long as

provided that.

If

If it rains, the event will be canceled.

Unless

Unless you register, you cannot attend.

Equivale aproximadamente a:

If you don’t register…

As long as

You can use the room as long as you follow the rules.

Significa:

contanto que.

Provided that

Mais formal:

You can join the course provided that you meet the requirements.

Concession

Concessão é uma relação em que uma informação:

poderia levar a determinada expectativa

mas:

o resultado é diferente.

Principais:

although

even though

despite

in spite of.

Although

Although the test was difficult, most students passed.

Expectativa possível:

difficult test → fewer students pass.

Resultado:

most passed.

Despite

Estrutura:

despite + noun / gerund.

Despite the rain, the event continued.

Despite feeling tired, she continued working.

Não:

despite it was raining.

In spite of

Mesmo padrão:

In spite of the rain, the event continued.

Despite the fact that

Se queremos uma oração:

Despite the fact that it was raining, the event continued.

Mas para B1, é mais simples dominar:

although + clause

despite + noun.

Although x despite

Compare:

Although it was raining, we went out.

Despite the rain, we went out.

Concession x simple contrast

Contraste:

John likes tea, but Maria likes coffee.

Concessão:

Although John was tired, he continued working.

Na concessão, existe:

uma expectativa contrariada.

Comparison

Conectores úteis:

similarly

likewise

in the same way

compared with

than.

Similarly

Solar power is becoming cheaper. Similarly, wind energy costs have fallen.

Compared with

Compared with last year, sales increased.

Than

The new system is faster than the old one.

Clarification / Reformulation

Textos podem explicar uma ideia novamente.

Principais:

in other words

that is

in other words

meaning that.

In other words

The service is compulsory. In other words, all students must attend.

That is

The project will run for one semester, that is, approximately six months.

Meaning that

The application deadline has passed, meaning that new applications are no longer accepted.

Conclusion

Conectores de conclusão:

in conclusion

overall

in summary

to sum up

therefore, dependendo do contexto.

Overall

Overall, the results were positive.

Significa:

considerando o conjunto.

In conclusion

In conclusion, the program appears to have achieved its main goals.

Muito comum em:

essays

reports.

In summary

In summary, regular exercise has several health benefits.

Generalization

in general

generally

overall.

Exemplo:

In general, participants were satisfied with the course.

Exception

Conectores/expressões:

except

except for

apart from.

Except for

All classes are free except for the advanced course.

Apart from

Pode significar:

exceto por

ou:

além de

dependendo do contexto.

Exemplo:

Apart from one minor problem, the project was successful.

Conectores e pontuação

A estrutura é importante.

Coordinating conjunctions

Como:

and

but

so.

Podem conectar orações:

The study was small, but the results were interesting.

Subordinating conjunctions

Como:

because

although

if

while.

Introduzem uma oração subordinada.

Because the study was small, researchers were cautious.
