28.

The new bus system has several advantages. For example, buses arrive more frequently than before. In addition, ticket prices have been reduced. However, some passengers still complain about overcrowding during peak hours. The city plans to add more buses to reduce this problem.

Relações:

for example → exemplo.

in addition → adição.

however → contraste.

to → finalidade.

29.

Contrast/concession between the positive result and a limitation.

O estudo encontrou resultado positivo, mas:

sample size was limited.

Result/consequence.

Por causa da limitação:

researchers recommended a larger study.

Only 60 participants were included.

Researchers recommended a larger study before strong conclusions were drawn.

30.

Modelo:

Online education offers several advantages for students. It can provide greater flexibility because learners do not always need to travel to a school or university. In addition, recorded classes can sometimes be reviewed more than once. For example, students who work during the day may study in the evening. However, online learning also has challenges. Some learners find it difficult to stay motivated, although they have access to many digital resources. Technical problems may also interrupt classes. As a result, students need reliable internet access and basic digital skills. If teachers provide clear instructions and regular feedback, online courses can become more effective. Interaction is also important because students may feel isolated when they study entirely alone. In conclusion, online education can be useful and flexible, but its success depends on appropriate technology, organization and support.

Tarefa de consolidação

Crie uma tabela com os principais grupos:

Relação Conectores
addition and, also, in addition, moreover
contrast but, however, whereas
concession although, even though, despite
cause because, because of, due to
result so, therefore, as a result
example for example, for instance, such as
purpose to, in order to, so that
condition if, unless, as long as
sequence first, then, next, finally
conclusion overall, in conclusion, in summary

Depois produza cinco pares para cada contraste estrutural:

because + clause

because of + noun

Exemplo:

We stayed home because it was raining.

We stayed home because of the rain.

Faça o mesmo com:

although + clause

despite + noun/gerund

Exemplo:

Although she was tired, she continued.

Despite being tired, she continued.

Depois construa dez cadeias de:

cause → result

Exemplo:

Heavy rain caused flooding. As a result, several roads were closed.

Em seguida, crie cinco textos curtos com:

uma ideia;

um contraste;

uma causa;

uma consequência;

um exemplo.

Marque cada conector e indique sua função.

Treine também as paráfrases:

because of = due to

however = nevertheless, em muitos contextos

therefore = as a result

for example = for instance

in addition = moreover/furthermore

despite = in spite of

Por fim, aplique este procedimento ao Reading:

1. Identifique o conector.

2. Classifique a relação lógico-semântica.

3. Leia a ideia anterior.

4. Preveja que tipo de informação deve vir depois.

5. Verifique se a interpretação realmente corresponde ao texto.

Antes de responder, pergunte:

A segunda ideia acrescenta, contrasta, explica, exemplifica ou resulta da primeira?

Quando essa relação é identificada corretamente, o texto deixa de parecer apenas uma sequência de frases e passa a ser entendido como uma estrutura lógica de informações conectadas.

Aula 90 — Inferência contextual

Objetivos

Ao final desta aula, você deverá ser capaz de:

  • compreender o que é inferência contextual;
  • distinguir informação explícita de informação inferida;
  • usar pistas do contexto para descobrir significados aproximados;
  • inferir o sentido de palavras desconhecidas sem depender imediatamente de dicionário;
  • identificar pistas de definição, exemplo, contraste, causa, consequência e reformulação;
  • usar prefixos, sufixos e famílias de palavras como apoio à inferência;
  • compreender o papel de conectores na construção de significado;
  • inferir relações entre personagens, eventos e ideias;
  • distinguir inferência legítima de suposição sem apoio textual;
  • reconhecer quando uma conclusão é forte demais para o texto;
  • usar conhecimento de mundo sem substituir as evidências do texto;
  • aplicar estratégias de inferência em textos jornalísticos, científicos e cotidianos;
  • responder questões típicas de Reading B1 que usam implied, suggests, can be inferred e expressões semelhantes.

Desenvolvimento

Em Reading, nem todas as respostas aparecem escritas exatamente da mesma forma que a pergunta.

Às vezes, o texto apresenta:

clues

e o leitor precisa:

combine them.

Esse processo é chamado de:

inference.

Em português:

inferência.

O que é inferência?

Inferir significa chegar a uma conclusão com base em:

informações disponíveis

mesmo quando essa conclusão não foi escrita diretamente.

Exemplo:

Julia put on a coat, took an umbrella and left the house.

O texto não diz:

The weather was cold and rainy.

Mas podemos inferir:

Julia expected cold or rainy weather.

Temos pistas:

coat

umbrella.

Explicit information

Informação explícita aparece diretamente.

The train leaves at 8:30.

Pergunta:

What time does the train leave?

Resposta:

8:30.

Não há inferência.

Implicit information

Informação implícita precisa ser deduzida.

Daniel arrived at the station at 8:35 and saw the train moving away.

Podemos inferir:

Daniel missed the train.

O texto não diz literalmente:

He missed it.

Mas as informações tornam essa conclusão razoável.

Inferência não é adivinhação

Uma inferência precisa ser:

supported by the text.

Não é:

inventar qualquer possibilidade.

Exemplo:

Daniel arrived at 8:35 and the train had already left.

Podemos inferir:

he did not catch that train.

Não podemos inferir:

Daniel was traveling to London.

O texto não fornece essa informação.

Text evidence

Sempre pergunte:

What evidence supports this conclusion?

Se você não consegue apontar uma pista:

provavelmente está supondo demais.

Informação explícita x inferência x suposição

Texto:

Maria arrived at the office carrying a wet umbrella.

Explícito:

Maria had a wet umbrella.

Inferência razoável:

It was probably raining recently.

Suposição sem apoio:

Maria dislikes rain.

Palavras típicas nas questões

Questões de inferência podem usar:

What can be inferred from the text?

What does the text suggest?

What is implied?

We can understand that…

Which statement is most likely true?

What can we conclude?

Why probably…?

Quando encontrar essas formulações:

não procure apenas uma frase idêntica à resposta.

Procure:

pistas combinadas.

Inferir significado de palavras

Um dos usos mais importantes da inferência é descobrir:

vocabulary in context.

Texto:

The path was slippery after the heavy rain, so walkers had to move slowly.

Talvez você não conheça:

slippery.

Mas temos:

heavy rain

walkers moved slowly.

Podemos inferir:

slippery = difficult to walk on safely because the surface is wet/smooth.

Não precisamos de tradução perfeita

Em uma prova, muitas vezes basta saber:

positive or negative?

person, object or action?

approximate meaning?

Por exemplo:

The room was crowded, so we had difficulty finding a seat.

Mesmo sem conhecer:

crowded

podemos inferir:

there were many people.

Isso já pode ser suficiente.

Context clues

As principais pistas contextuais incluem:

definition

explanation

example

synonym

contrast

cause and effect

word formation

general context.

Definition clue

O próprio texto explica a palavra.

A nocturnal animal is an animal that is active mainly at night.

Mesmo sem conhecer:

nocturnal

a definição aparece depois:

active mainly at night.

Apposition

Outra forma:

Photosynthesis, the process by which plants use light to produce energy, is essential for plant life.

A expressão entre vírgulas explica:

photosynthesis.

Parentheses

The device uses sensors (small instruments that detect changes in the environment).

Os parênteses dão:

definição.

Meaning that

The road is inaccessible, meaning that vehicles cannot reach the area.

inaccessible

pode ser inferido por:

vehicles cannot reach.

In other words

The material is biodegradable. In other words, it can break down naturally over time.

A segunda frase:

reformula a primeira.

That is

The program is compulsory, that is, all students must participate.

compulsory = required.

Example clue

Texto:

Many mammals, such as dogs, cats and whales, care for their young.

Mesmo sem conhecer:

mammals

os exemplos ajudam a compreender:

um grupo de animais incluindo dogs, cats and whales.

Such as

É uma forte pista de:

examples.

For example

Some renewable energy sources are widely available. For example, solar energy can be produced in many regions.

O exemplo ajuda a entender:

renewable energy source.

Including

Several symptoms, including fever, coughing and tiredness, were reported.

Esses exemplos ajudam a compreender:

symptoms.

Synonym clue

O texto pode fornecer uma palavra de significado parecido.

The new device is portable, or easy to carry from one place to another.

portable

é explicado por:

easy to carry.

Reformulação por segunda frase

The population remained stable. In other words, it did not increase or decrease significantly.

stable

≈:

not changing much.

Contrast clue

Palavras como:

but

however

although

unlike

whereas

podem indicar que o significado é oposto ao de outra informação.

Exemplo:

Unlike his outgoing sister, Daniel is quite reserved.

Se conhecemos:

outgoing

e vemos:

unlike

podemos inferir:

reserved

está relacionado a:

quieter / less socially open.

Outro exemplo

The first task was simple, but the second was extremely complex.

Se não conhecemos:

complex

o contraste com:

simple

é uma pista forte.

Antonyms no contexto

The hotel was not luxurious; it was quite basic.

basic

é contrastado com:

luxurious.

Cause-and-effect clue

Exemplo:

The roads were icy, so drivers reduced their speed.

Mesmo sem conhecer:

icy

podemos inferir:

road conditions were potentially dangerous/slippery because of ice.

Outro exemplo

The medicine caused drowsiness, so patients were advised not to drive.

Podemos inferir:

drowsiness

envolve:

sleepiness.

Porque:

people should not drive.

Result clue

The room was poorly ventilated, and as a result it became extremely hot.

poorly ventilated

deve envolver:

insufficient movement of fresh air.

General context

Às vezes nenhuma frase define diretamente a palavra.

É preciso usar:

the whole passage.

Exemplo:

The hikers had already walked for eight hours. Their water bottles were empty, and the nearest village was still several kilometers away. They were exhausted.

Mesmo sem conhecer:

exhausted

o contexto sugere:

extremely tired.

Word formation

Conteúdo da Aula 82 também ajuda na inferência.

Exemplo:

reusable.

Podemos analisar:

re- + use + -able.

re- = again.

-able = can be.

Logo:

reusable = can be used again.

Prefixos negativos

unhappy

impossible

illegal

irregular

unclear.

Mesmo sem conhecer a palavra completa, o prefixo pode indicar:

negation/opposite.

Mis-

misunderstood

misinformed

misspelled.

Pista:

incorrectly.

Re-

rebuild

rewrite

reconsider.

Pista:

again.

-less

harmless

useless

homeless.

Pista geral:

without.

-ful

helpful

useful

careful.

Pista:

having/providing a quality.

-er / -or

Frequentemente pessoa:

researcher

teacher

director.

-tion / -ment / -ness

Frequentemente:

nouns.

Mesmo sem conhecer o significado, você pode inferir:

classe gramatical.

Classe gramatical como pista

Texto:

The new system improved efficiency.

Mesmo sem conhecer:

efficiency

vemos:

improved + noun.

A palavra representa provavelmente:

uma qualidade ou resultado.

Determiners

an unexpected ______

deve normalmente ser:

noun.

very ______

frequentemente:

adjective/adverb

dependendo da posição.

Sentence structure

Exemplo:

The scientist carefully examined the unusual sample.

Mesmo sem conhecer:

examined

sabemos que:

scientist = subject

sample = object.

Então:

examined

é uma ação realizada sobre a amostra.

Coesão como pista

Texto:

The city introduced a new recycling program. This initiative began in March.

Mesmo se:

initiative

for desconhecida, sabemos que retoma:

recycling program.

Logo, significa algo próximo de:

program/project/action.

Pronoun reference

The company developed a new device. It can detect changes in temperature.

Para entender:

it

precisamos conectar ao:

device.

Inferência depende de coesão.

Connectors como pista

The system was inexpensive. However, it was unreliable.

however

indica contraste.

Se:

inexpensive

é vantagem,

unreliable

provavelmente é:

desvantagem.

Addition

The device is small. In addition, it is lightweight.

lightweight

provavelmente apresenta:

outra característica positiva.

Result

The software was difficult to use. Therefore, many employees required additional training.

Podemos inferir:

usability problem caused need for training.

Although

Although the treatment was effective, it caused several side effects.

Temos:

positivo x negativo.

Inferindo emoções

Texto:

When Ana saw her exam result, she smiled, called her parents immediately and told them she had passed.

Podemos inferir:

she was happy/pleased.

Não precisamos que o texto diga:

Ana was happy.

Cuidado com emoções excessivamente específicas

Podemos inferir:

positive emotion.

Mas talvez não:

she was the happiest she had ever been.

Isso seria exagero.

Inferindo relações

Texto:

Thomas called Rachel “Mom” and asked if he could borrow the car.

Podemos inferir:

Rachel is probably Thomas’s mother.

A palavra:

Mom

é forte evidência.

Inferindo localização

Passengers were asked to fasten their seat belts before takeoff.

Podemos inferir:

they were on an aircraft.

Pistas:

passengers

seat belts

takeoff.

Inferindo profissão

Emma examined the patient, asked about his symptoms and prescribed medication.

Podemos inferir:

Emma is likely a doctor/healthcare professional authorized to prescribe medication.

Inferindo tempo

The streets were dark, and most shops had already closed for the day.

Podemos inferir:

it was probably evening/night.

Não necessariamente:

exactly 10 p.m.

Inferindo causa

Jack arrived late. His bus had broken down on the way to work.

Podemos inferir:

bus problem caused or contributed to lateness.

Inferindo consequência

The company lost its largest customer and reduced production the following month.

Podemos inferir:

losing the customer may have contributed to reduced production

se o contexto apresenta essa ligação.

Mas cuidado:

sequência temporal não prova causalidade automaticamente.

Causality caution

Texto:

People who exercise more reported lower stress.

Podemos inferir:

an association was found.

Não:

exercise definitely caused lower stress.

Essa distinção já apareceu na divulgação científica.

Inferência e modais

Texto:

The project may create new jobs.

Inferência correta:

job creation is possible.

Incorreta:

new jobs will definitely be created.

Likely

The storm is likely to reach the coast.

Inferência:

reaching the coast is considered probable.

Não:

guaranteed.

Apparently

Apparently, the system failed because of a software problem.

Marca:

informação não apresentada como certeza absoluta.

Seems / appears

The treatment appears to be effective.

Inferência:

early evidence is positive.

Não:

effectiveness has been conclusively proved.

Quantifiers

Inferência precisa respeitar:

some

many

most

all.

Texto:

Most students passed.

Podemos inferir:

more than half passed.

Não:

everyone passed.

Few

Few residents supported the proposal.

Podemos inferir:

support was limited.

Almost all

Almost all participants completed the task.

Não:

all participants.

Approximately

approximately 500.

Não:

exactly 500.

Inferência numérica

Texto:

The number rose from 200 to 300.

Podemos inferir:

increase = 100.

Também:

50% increase.

Porque:

100 / 200 = 0.5.

Comparative inference

City A has 50,000 residents. City B has twice as many.

Podemos inferir:

City B ≈ 100,000.

Before/after

The meeting began after Maria arrived.

Podemos inferir:

Maria arrived before the meeting began.

Unless

You cannot enter unless you have a ticket.

Podemos inferir:

a ticket is required for entry.

Even though

Even though she was tired, she continued studying.

Podemos inferir:

tiredness did not stop her.

Despite

Despite the rain, attendance was high.

Podemos inferir:

rain might normally be expected to reduce attendance, but it did not do so substantially.

Reading between the lines

Expressão comum:

read between the lines.

Significa:

understand information not directly stated.

Mas isso não significa:

invent hidden meanings.

A inferência deve continuar:

text-based.

Background knowledge

Conhecimento de mundo pode ajudar.

Texto:

The temperature fell below zero, and drivers were warned about ice.

Sabemos que:

below zero temperatures can produce icy conditions.

Mas o texto ainda fornece pistas suficientes.

Perigo do excesso de conhecimento externo

Se o texto diz:

The animal was found in Australia.

Não conclua automaticamente:

it was a kangaroo.

Mesmo que cangurus sejam associados à Austrália.

Regra

Use conhecimento externo para:

interpret clues.

Não para:

replace missing evidence.

Inferência lexical em etapas

Ao encontrar palavra desconhecida:

1. Ignore por alguns segundos.

Leia a frase toda.

2. Identifique a classe gramatical.

Noun?

Verb?

Adjective?

Adverb?

3. Procure conectores.

Contraste?

Causa?

Exemplo?

4. Observe prefixos e sufixos.

5. Leia a frase anterior e seguinte.

6. Substitua por uma palavra genérica.

Exemplo:

positive thing

negative condition

action

person.

7. Veja se isso é suficiente para responder.

Muitas vezes:

não é necessário conhecer tradução exata.

Substituição aproximada

Texto:

The organization provides grants to students who cannot afford university fees.

Se não conhece:

grants

pode pensar:

some kind of financial support.

Isso provavelmente basta.

Afford

Pelo contexto:

cannot afford university fees

podemos inferir:

cannot pay/have enough money for.

Contexto maior

The medicine is inexpensive and widely available, making it an affordable option for many patients.

Se não conhece:

affordable

temos:

inexpensive

como pista.

Logo:

not too expensive / financially accessible.

Definição indireta

The material is transparent, allowing light to pass through it.

Podemos inferir:

transparent = allows light to pass through.

Example + category

Several amphibians, including frogs and salamanders, are sensitive to environmental changes.

Mesmo sem conhecer:

amphibians

sabemos que:

frogs and salamanders

são exemplos dessa categoria.

Contrast + antonym

Unlike permanent structures, temporary buildings can be removed easily.

temporary

é contrastado com:

permanent.

Cause + unknown noun

Heavy traffic caused congestion throughout the city center, and journeys took twice as long.

Podemos inferir:

congestion

envolve:

traffic becoming slow/crowded.

Inferência de intenção

Texto:

The company lowered prices just before the holiday season.

Podemos talvez inferir:

it wanted to attract more buyers.

Mas a força dessa inferência depende do restante do texto.

Se nada menciona objetivo:

trate como possibilidade, não fato.

Purpose language

in order to

to

so that

fornece intenção explicitamente.

The company reduced prices to attract more customers.

Aqui não precisamos inferir:

finalidade está explícita.

Tone inference

Também podemos inferir:

attitude/tone.

Texto:

Unfortunately, the project failed to meet any of its main targets.

Palavra:

unfortunately

indica tom:

negative/disappointed.

Cautiously positive

The early findings are encouraging, although more research is needed.

Tom:

cautiously optimistic.

Pistas:

encouraging

although more research is needed.

Critical

Critics argue that the plan is too expensive and provides few benefits.

A crítica é atribuída a:

critics.

Não necessariamente:

ao autor.

Speaker attitude em diálogos

“Another two-hour delay? That’s just great.”

Dependendo de contexto e tom, pode ser:

sarcasm.

No Reading B1 escrito, ironia pode aparecer, mas normalmente as pistas serão claras.

Inferência em anúncios

Applicants should be available to work evenings and weekends.

Podemos inferir:

the job may require work outside normal daytime hours.

Course advertisement

No previous experience is required.

Inferência:

beginners may apply.

Hotel notice

Guests are asked to leave rooms by 11 a.m.

Inferência:

check-out is by 11 a.m.

Scientific inference

Texto:

The study included only 40 participants from one university.

Podemos inferir:

generalization may be limited.

Se o texto discute limitações, essa inferência é ainda mais forte.

News inference

The road remained closed at 8 p.m., and officials said repairs would continue overnight.

Podemos inferir:

the road was unlikely to reopen immediately.

Não necessariamente:

it remained closed for several days.

Multiple clues

As melhores inferências frequentemente combinam várias pistas.

Texto:

Leo checked the departure board repeatedly, looked at his watch and walked quickly toward platform 6.

Inferência:

he was probably worried about catching a train.

Pistas:

departure board

watch

platform.

Uma pista isolada pode não bastar

Leo looked at his watch.

Isso sozinho não prova:

he was late.

Pode haver várias razões.

Degree of confidence

Você pode pensar em:

certain from text

strongly supported

possible

unsupported.

Em provas, escolha:

strongly supported.

Inferência forte

Texto:

The shop closes at 6. Anna arrived at 6:30 and found the doors locked.

Inferência:

she arrived after the shop had closed.

Muito forte.

Inferência fraca

Anna was angry because the shop was closed.

Não sabemos se:

angry.

Negação e inferência

Texto:

The program is not available to students under 18.

Inferência:

students under 18 cannot participate.

Double negatives

It is not uncommon.

Significa aproximadamente:

it is relatively common.

Atenção a:

not + negative adjective.

Hardly

Hardly any students failed.

Significa:

very few failed.

Não:

many failed.

Rarely

The system rarely fails.

Inferência:

it usually works.

Only

Only registered users can access the file.

Inferência:

non-registered users cannot access it.

Until

The library is open until 10 p.m.

Inferência:

it closes at around 10 p.m., assuming ordinary interpretation.

No longer

The service is no longer free.

Inferência:

it used to be free.

Essa é uma inferência linguística muito importante.

Still

She still works at the hospital.

Implica:

she worked there before and continues now.

Already

The train has already left.

Implica:

departure occurred earlier than the relevant moment, sometimes earlier than expected.

Yet

The results haven’t been published yet.

Implica:

publication is expected or possible later.

Again

The prices increased again.

Implica:

they had increased before.

Continue

The company continued reducing costs.

Implica:

cost reduction had already begun earlier.

Stop

He stopped working at the hospital.

Implica:

he worked there before.

Start/begin

She started studying medicine.

Implica:

previously she was not studying medicine.

Return

The researchers returned to the site.

Implica:

they had been there before.

Inferências gramaticais

Present Perfect:

I’ve lived here for five years.

Inferência:

I still live here

em leitura normal.

Simple Past:

I lived there for five years.

Inferência normal:

I don’t live there now.

Used to

She used to work here.

Implica:

she no longer works here.

Still x anymore

He doesn’t work here anymore.

Implica:

he worked here before.

Second Conditional

If I had more time, I would exercise every day.

Frequentemente implica:

I don’t have enough time now.

Comparative

This version is cheaper than the old one.

Implica:

old version costs more.

Superlative

It was the most difficult task.

Implica:

other tasks were less difficult.

Too

The box is too heavy to carry.

Implica:

it cannot reasonably be carried under the stated circumstances.

Enough

She is experienced enough to lead the project.

Implica:

her experience meets the required level.

Inferência a partir de connectors

Although the price increased, demand remained high.

Podemos inferir:

a price increase might normally be expected to reduce demand, but it did not.

Because

The event was canceled because of the storm.

Inferência:

without that storm, cancellation might not have occurred — embora isso nem sempre possa ser afirmado com certeza absoluta.

Therefore

The evidence was limited. Therefore, researchers avoided strong conclusions.

Inferência:

limited evidence was the reason for caution.

Texto 1

Late-Night Study Spaces

During examination periods, Westbridge University keeps part of its main library open until 2 a.m. The service was introduced after students reported difficulty finding quiet places to study late in the evening.

Students must show a university identification card to enter after 10 p.m. Food is allowed only in one designated area, and security staff remain in the building throughout the night.

Last semester, the late-night section was used by more than 1,500 students. Because demand was higher than expected, the university is considering opening another study area during the next examination period.

Inferências possíveis — texto 1

Podemos inferir:

the service is intended to meet demand for late study spaces.

people without university ID cannot normally enter after 10 p.m.

the service was popular enough for expansion to be considered.

Não podemos inferir:

every student prefers studying at night.

Texto 2

Urban Trees and Summer Temperatures

Researchers measured temperatures on streets with different levels of tree cover during a particularly hot summer. Streets with more trees were, on average, cooler during the afternoon than streets with little or no tree cover.

The researchers say shade from trees probably explains part of the difference. However, they note that other factors, such as building height and street width, may also influence local temperatures.

The study therefore does not prove that planting trees alone will solve urban heat problems, but the findings support including vegetation in broader city-planning strategies.

Inferências possíveis — texto 2

Podemos inferir:

trees may contribute to cooler streets.

researchers do not consider tree planting a complete solution by itself.

multiple factors affect urban temperature.

Não:

trees are the only cause of cooler temperatures.

Texto 3

A Different Kind of Job Interview

When Sara arrived for the interview, she expected to sit in an office and answer questions about her previous jobs. Instead, she and five other candidates were asked to work together on a short problem-solving activity.

The interviewers watched how the candidates communicated, shared ideas and responded when the group disagreed. Sara later said that the experience had surprised her, but she understood why the company had used the activity.

The job description had emphasized teamwork and communication skills.

Inferências possíveis — texto 3

Podemos inferir:

the company wanted to observe teamwork in practice.

the group activity was related to skills required for the job.

Sara had expected a more traditional interview.

Não:

Sara definitely got the job.

Vocabulário-chave

inference — inferência

infer — inferir

imply — implicar/sugerir indiretamente

explicit — explícito

implicit — implícito

context clue — pista contextual

evidence — evidência

assumption — suposição

definition — definição

example — exemplo

contrast — contraste

cause — causa

consequence — consequência

suggest — sugerir/indicar

likely — provável

unlikely — improvável

apparently — aparentemente

approximately — aproximadamente

support — sustentar

conclude — concluir

Estratégia de prova

Ao responder uma questão de inferência, use:

TEXT + LOGIC, not imagination.

Procedimento:

1. Localize a parte relevante do texto.

2. Sublinhe as pistas.

3. Formule uma conclusão mínima.

Evite adicionar detalhes desnecessários.

4. Confira a força da alternativa.

Se o texto diz:

may

e a resposta diz:

definitely

desconfie.

5. Elimine alternativas que dependem de informação externa.

6. Pergunte: consigo provar essa resposta usando o texto?

Para vocabulário desconhecido:

part of speech → nearby clues → connector → word formation → approximate meaning.

Não tente traduzir imediatamente.

Prática

Com base no Texto 1:

1. Why was the late-night library service introduced?

  1. Students wanted more food options.
  2. Students had difficulty finding quiet places to study late.
  3. The university wanted to close during the day.
  4. Security staff requested it.

2. What can be inferred about entry after 10 p.m.?

  1. Anyone can enter.
  2. University identification is required.
  3. Food is required.
  4. Students must pay.

3. What does the use of more than 1,500 students suggest?

  1. The service had significant demand.
  2. Nobody used the service.
  3. Students disliked the library.
  4. The university will certainly close it.

4. Why is the university considering another study area?

  1. Existing demand was higher than expected.
  2. The first area was never used.
  3. The building has no security staff.
  4. Students requested fewer spaces.

5. Which statement cannot be inferred?

  1. Some students need late-night study space.
  2. The service may be expanded.
  3. Every university student studies after midnight.
  4. Access is controlled at night.

Com base no Texto 2:

6. What can be inferred about streets with more trees?

  1. They were generally cooler in the study.
  2. They were always exactly ten degrees cooler.
  3. Trees completely eliminated summer heat.
  4. Buildings had no effect on temperature.

7. Why do researchers mention building height and street width?

  1. To show that other factors may affect temperature.
  2. To prove trees have no effect.
  3. To explain why no measurements were taken.
  4. To describe tree species.

8. Which conclusion is best supported?

  1. Planting trees alone will solve urban heat.
  2. Trees may be one useful part of broader heat-reduction strategies.
  3. Tree cover has no relationship with temperature.
  4. All cities must use identical planning strategies.

9. The word “broader” most likely means:

  1. involving a wider range of measures
  2. physically shorter
  3. less important
  4. temporary

10. The phrase “does not prove” signals:

  1. a limitation in the conclusion
  2. complete certainty
  3. a definition
  4. a sequence marker

Com base no Texto 3:

11. What kind of interview had Sara expected?

  1. A group sports activity.
  2. A traditional question-and-answer interview.
  3. An online examination.
  4. No interview.

12. Why did the company probably use the group activity?

  1. To evaluate teamwork and communication.
  2. To teach candidates mathematics.
  3. To reduce the number of interviewers.
  4. To provide entertainment.

13. What evidence supports this inference?

  1. The interviewers observed communication and the job required teamwork.
  2. Sara arrived early.
  3. There were six candidates.
  4. The interview took place in an office.

14. Can we infer that Sara was hired?

  1. Yes, definitely.
  2. No, the text does not provide that information.
  3. Yes, because she understood the activity.
  4. Yes, because she attended the interview.

15. What does “Instead” signal?

  1. The actual interview was different from Sara’s expectation.
  2. A cause.
  3. A scientific definition.
  4. A future prediction.

16. Infer the meaning of the underlined concept:

The path was slippery, so we walked slowly and carefully after the rain.

  1. very wide
  2. difficult to walk on safely
  3. completely dry
  4. brightly colored

17. Infer:

The room was crowded, and we could hardly find a place to sit.

  1. empty
  2. full of people
  3. cold
  4. expensive

18. Infer:

The medicine caused drowsiness, so patients were told not to drive.

  1. hunger
  2. sleepiness
  3. excitement
  4. increased strength

19. Infer:

The material is transparent, allowing light to pass through it.

  1. light can pass through it
  2. it is extremely heavy
  3. it cannot be seen
  4. it produces electricity

20. Infer:

The organization provides grants to students who cannot afford university fees.

  1. financial support
  2. examinations
  3. punishments
  4. classrooms

21. Identifique a inferência:

The service is no longer free.

  1. It was free before.
  2. It has never been free.
  3. It will always be free.
  4. No information about price is available.

22. Identifique:

She still works at the hospital.

  1. She has just started.
  2. She worked there before and continues now.
  3. She never worked there.
  4. She plans to leave immediately.

23. Identifique:

The results haven’t been published yet.

  1. They were published yesterday.
  2. Publication may happen later.
  3. They will never be published.
  4. There are no results.

24. Identifique:

He used to live in London.

  1. He definitely lives there now.
  2. He lived there in the past, but normally not now.
  3. He has never lived there.
  4. He visits every day.

25. Leia:

Most participants preferred the new system.

Qual conclusão é incorreta?

  1. More than half probably preferred it.
  2. Some participants may not have preferred it.
  3. Every participant preferred it.
  4. The new system had majority preference.

26. Leia:

The device costs half as much as the previous model.

Se o modelo antigo custa $200, quanto custa aproximadamente o novo?

27. Leia:

The number of users rose from 400 to 600.

  1. By how many users did it increase?

  2. What was the percentage increase?

28. Leia:

Although the restaurant was almost full, we found a table immediately.

Qual expectativa foi contrariada?

29. Leia:

The course requires no previous programming experience.

O que podemos inferir sobre iniciantes?

30. Produção

Leia o texto:

Liam arrived at the office fifteen minutes before an important meeting. He turned on his laptop, but the screen remained black. After trying two different chargers, he borrowed a colleague’s computer and quickly copied his presentation from an online storage service. When the manager entered the room, Liam was already connecting the borrowed computer to the projector.

Produza:

  • quatro informações explícitas;
  • quatro inferências razoáveis;
  • duas conclusões que não podem ser feitas;
  • o significado contextual provável de borrowed;
  • uma explicação das pistas usadas em cada inferência.

Gabarito comentado

1. B

A causa está explícita:

students reported difficulty finding quiet places to study late.

2. B

O texto diz:

Students must show a university identification card to enter after 10 p.m.

Logo:

controlled entry requiring university ID.

3. A

Mais de:

1,500 students

usaram o espaço.

Isso apoia:

substantial demand.

Não podemos concluir:

todos os estudantes usaram.

4. A

O texto conecta diretamente:

demand was higher than expected

com:

considering another area.

5. C

Nada sustenta:

every student studies after midnight.

Isso é uma generalização excessiva.

6. A

O texto diz:

streets with more trees were, on average, cooler.

Observe:

on average.

Não:

always.

7. A

Eles mostram que:

temperature has multiple possible influences.

Isso limita uma conclusão causal simplista.

8. B

É a conclusão mais compatível com:

broader city-planning strategies.

9. A

No contexto:

broader strategies

significa estratégias que incluem:

more than one type of action.

10. A

does not prove

estabelece:

limite da evidência.

11. B

Ela esperava:

sit in an office and answer questions about previous jobs.

Isso descreve:

traditional question-and-answer interview.

12. A

As pistas são:

group problem-solving

interviewers watched communication and idea sharing

job description emphasized teamwork and communication.

13. A

Essa opção combina:

observação direta

e:

requisito da vaga.

É a evidência mais forte.

14. B

Nada informa:

resultado da seleção.

Participar e compreender o processo:

não significa ser contratada.

15. A

Instead

marca contraste entre:

expectation

e:

what actually happened.

16. B

Pistas:

after rain

walked slowly and carefully.

Logo:

slippery

significa algo como:

escorregadio / difícil de caminhar com segurança.

17. B

Pista:

could hardly find a place to sit.

Logo:

many people were present.

18. B

Se pacientes não devem dirigir:

drowsiness

provavelmente envolve:

sleepiness/reduced alertness.

19. A

A definição está explícita:

allowing light to pass through it.

20. A

Pista:

students who cannot afford fees.

Logo, grants são:

financial support/funding.

21. A

no longer

implica:

era verdade antes, mas não é mais.

Logo:

the service was free before.

22. B

still

marca:

continuação de uma situação anterior.

23. B

not … yet

normalmente implica:

algo ainda não ocorreu, mas pode/espera-se que ocorra depois.

24. B

used to

descreve:

estado/hábito passado que normalmente não continua.

25. C

most

não significa:

all.

Portanto, não podemos afirmar:

every participant.

26.

$100.

Se o novo custa:

half as much

e o anterior custa:

$200,

então:

200 ÷ 2 = 100.

27.

200 users.

Cálculo:

600 − 400 = 200.

50%.

Cálculo:

200 / 400 × 100 = 50%.

28.

A expectativa provável era:

se o restaurante estava quase cheio, poderia ser difícil encontrar mesa imediatamente.

Mas:

they found one immediately.

É uma relação de concessão.

29.

Podemos inferir:

beginners can probably enroll/apply.

A frase:

no previous programming experience required

remove experiência anterior como requisito.

30.

Informações explícitas

  1. Liam arrived fifteen minutes before the meeting.

  2. His laptop screen remained black.

  3. He tried two different chargers.

  4. He borrowed a colleague’s computer.

Outras possíveis:

he copied his presentation from online storage.

he connected the borrowed computer to the projector.

Inferências razoáveis

  1. Liam’s laptop was not working properly.

Pistas:

screen remained black

tried two chargers

needed another computer.

  1. He probably needed the laptop for the meeting.

Pistas:

important meeting

presentation

connecting computer to projector.

  1. His presentation had been stored online before the technical problem occurred.

Pista:

he copied it from an online storage service.

  1. Liam found a solution before the meeting started.

Pistas:

borrowed another computer

copied the presentation

was connecting it when the manager entered.

Conclusões que não podem ser feitas

Liam’s own laptop was permanently broken.

O problema pode ter sido temporário.

The meeting was successful.

O texto termina antes de informar o resultado da reunião.

Borrowed

No contexto:

used temporarily something belonging to a colleague, with the expectation of returning it.

Em português:

emprestado / pegou emprestado.

Tarefa de consolidação

Pegue dez textos curtos e divida as informações em três colunas:

Explicit Reasonable inference Unsupported assumption
The door was locked. The person could not enter normally. The owner was angry.

Depois escolha vinte palavras desconhecidas em textos B1 e aplique:

1. Classe gramatical

2. Frase inteira

3. Frase anterior/posterior

4. Conectores

5. Definições ou exemplos

6. Prefixos/sufixos

7. Significado aproximado

Não use dicionário até terminar essa primeira tentativa.

Em seguida, pratique inferências geradas por palavras específicas:

still → situation continues

no longer → situation ended

already → happened before the reference point

yet → not happened so far, possibly later

again → happened before

used to → past state/habit normally no longer true

continue → action/state existed before

return → person/object was there before

only → exclusion of other possibilities

most → majority, not all

approximately → not exact

Crie também pares entre conclusão legítima e exagero:

Text: The results suggest that X may help.

Legitimate inference: X might be useful.

Exaggeration: X definitely works for everyone.

Repita com:

associated with / caused

some / all

most / every

likely / certain

may / will

preliminary / definitive.

Finalize aplicando a regra central:

Infer only what the evidence allows.

Antes de marcar uma alternativa, pergunte:

Quais palavras ou fatos do texto sustentam exatamente esta conclusão?

Se não houver evidência suficiente, a alternativa pode até parecer plausível, mas não é uma inferência textual válida.

Aula 91 — Listening B1: entrevistas e notícias

Objetivos

Ao final desta aula, você deverá ser capaz de:

  • compreender entrevistas e notícias curtas em inglês no nível B1;
  • identificar tema, ideia principal e propósito de um áudio;
  • reconhecer quem está falando e qual é a função de cada participante;
  • distinguir perguntas, respostas, comentários e informações atribuídas;
  • identificar detalhes específicos, como nomes, datas, locais, números e razões;
  • compreender Reported Speech e Passive Voice em notícias faladas;
  • reconhecer opinião, fato, previsão e possibilidade;
  • interpretar mudanças de assunto e conectores no discurso oral;
  • identificar paráfrases entre o áudio e as alternativas da prova;
  • compreender redução, ligação e pronúncia natural de palavras frequentes;
  • usar contexto para inferir palavras não compreendidas;
  • distinguir informação essencial de detalhes secundários;
  • aplicar estratégias de primeira e segunda escuta;
  • evitar depender da compreensão de 100% das palavras.

Desenvolvimento

No nível B1, atividades de Listening geralmente apresentam fala relativamente natural, mas ainda organizada e contextualizada.

Dois gêneros muito frequentes são:

interviews

e:

news reports.

Eles exigem estratégias diferentes.

Em uma entrevista, normalmente precisamos acompanhar:

perguntas

respostas

opiniões

experiências

explicações.

Em uma notícia, precisamos localizar:

o que aconteceu

onde

quando

quem esteve envolvido

causas

consequências

declarações.

Listening não é tradução simultânea

Um erro comum é tentar:

ouvir → traduzir cada palavra → compreender.

Esse processo é lento demais.

Uma estratégia mais eficiente:

ouvir → reconhecer unidades de sentido → construir a mensagem.

Considere:

The city council has announced a new public transport program starting next month.

Você não precisa traduzir mentalmente cada palavra.

Pode captar blocos:

city council

announced

new transport program

next month.

Isso já fornece a informação principal.

Listening for gist

Gist significa:

ideia geral.

Perguntas típicas:

What are the speakers mainly discussing?

What is the interview about?

What is the main topic of the news report?

Why is the speaker talking?

Na primeira escuta, procure:

topic

situation

speakers

main message.

Listening for detail

Depois da compreensão geral, procure:

  • numbers;
  • names;
  • dates;
  • times;
  • reasons;
  • places;
  • opinions;
  • changes;
  • problems;
  • solutions.

Estratégia de duas escutas

Em provas com duas reproduções, não tente resolver tudo na primeira.

Primeira escuta

Objetivo:

gist.

Pergunte:

Who?

Where?

Topic?

General situation?

Segunda escuta

Objetivo:

details.

Procure:

specific answers.

Antes do áudio

Use alguns segundos para:

  • ler as perguntas;
  • identificar palavras-chave;
  • prever o vocabulário;
  • descobrir que tipo de informação será necessário.

Pergunta:

Why did the speaker change jobs?

Antes de ouvir, você já sabe procurar:

reason.

Palavras possíveis:

because

wanted

needed

decided

opportunity

salary

career.

Prediction

Se o título diz:

Interview with a Wildlife Photographer

Você pode prever:

animals

travel

cameras

nature

work

experiences.

Isso reduz a carga cognitiva.

Não procure necessariamente a mesma palavra

Questão:

Why did Emma leave her previous job?

Áudio:

I wanted to try something different and have more flexible working hours.

A alternativa pode dizer:

She wanted a change and greater flexibility.

É:

paraphrase.

Entrevistas

Uma entrevista geralmente possui:

interviewer

e:

interviewee.

Interviewer

entrevistador.

Normalmente:

  • faz perguntas;
  • introduz temas;
  • pede esclarecimentos;
  • muda de assunto.

Interviewee

entrevistado.

Normalmente:

  • relata experiências;
  • explica decisões;
  • apresenta opiniões;
  • descreve trabalho ou projetos.

Sinais de pergunta

Frases frequentes:

Can you tell us about…?

Why did you decide to…?

How did you become interested in…?

What was the biggest challenge?

What are you working on now?

What are your plans for the future?

Reconhecer esses padrões permite prever:

o tipo de resposta.

Why did you…?

Espere:

reason.

How did you…?

Espere:

process / method.

When did you…?

Espere:

time.

What do you think about…?

Espere:

opinion.

What are you planning to…?

Espere:

future plan.

Mudança de assunto

Entrevistadores usam expressões como:

Now, let’s talk about…

Moving on to…

What about…?

I’d also like to ask…

Finally…

Essas expressões ajudam a dividir:

o áudio em partes.

Signposting

Chamamos essas pistas de:

signposting language.

Elas mostram a organização do discurso.

Exemplos:

first of all

actually

however

so

anyway

finally

as I mentioned earlier.

Actually

Muito comum na fala.

Significa:

na verdade.

Exemplo:

I thought the job would be difficult, but actually it was easier than I expected.

Não:

atualmente.

Well

Em entrevistas:

Well, I started working there in 2022.

Well pode funcionar apenas como:

marcador discursivo.

Não precisa ser traduzido literalmente.

You know

you know

pode ser marcador de fala.

Nem sempre adiciona informação relevante.

I mean

I mean…

pode introduzir:

correção

esclarecimento

reformulação.

Hesitation

Na fala natural:

um

uh

well

you know

sort of

podem aparecer.

Não se preocupe em interpretar cada marcador.

Concentre-se:

nas palavras informativas.

Correção durante a fala

Exemplo:

The event starts on Thursday — sorry, I mean Friday.

Resposta correta:

Friday.

Em Listening, a informação final pode corrigir:

algo dito antes.

Números corrigidos

There were about 60 people — actually, closer to 70.

Resposta:

approximately 70.

Não marque automaticamente:

Opinion markers

Em entrevistas:

I think…

I believe…

In my opinion…

For me…

I would say…

indicam:

opinião.

Experience

I’ve worked…

I started…

I used to…

When I was…

indicam:

experiência passada.

Preferences

I prefer…

I’d rather…

I really enjoy…

I don’t mind…

Strong x weak opinion

I definitely think…

forte.

I suppose…

mais cauteloso.

I guess…

opinião/tentativa menos firme.

Agreement

I agree.

Exactly.

That’s right.

Absolutely.

Partial agreement

I agree to some extent.

That’s true, but…

I see your point, however…

Disagreement

I don’t really agree.

I’m not sure about that.

I see it differently.

Em provas, desacordo nem sempre aparece com:

I disagree.

Pode ser indireto.

Exemplo de desacordo indireto

A:

Working from home is always better.

B:

It can be useful, but I still prefer working in an office.

B:

não concorda completamente.

Notícias

Uma notícia curta frequentemente começa com:

main event.

Exemplo:

A new health center has opened in the north of the city, providing services to more than 20,000 residents.

Primeira frase:

main information.

Depois vêm:

  • details;
  • quotations;
  • causes;
  • context;
  • consequences.

Who, What, Where, When, Why, How

Ao ouvir uma notícia, procure:

Who?

What happened?

Where?

When?

Why?

How?

News introduction

Você pode ouvir:

In today’s news…

Our next story…

Turning to…

In local news…

Essas expressões:

introduzem notícias ou mudam de assunto.

Breaking news

breaking news

refere-se:

informação recente e em desenvolvimento.

No B1, normalmente você precisa reconhecer:

mudança de assunto ou urgência.

News verbs

Palavras frequentes:

announce

report

confirm

warn

say

state

explain

claim

expect.

Announce

divulgar oficialmente.

The university has announced a new scholarship program.

Confirm

confirmar.

Police confirmed that the road had reopened.

Warn

alertar.

Officials warned residents to avoid the area.

Claim

alegar/afirmar.

The company claims that the product is safe.

Não significa necessariamente:

o jornalista confirma isso.

According to

According to local officials…

Identifica:

source.

Reported Speech em Listening

Você pode ouvir:

The mayor said the project would create new jobs.

Pergunta:

What did the mayor say?

Resposta:

The project would create new jobs.

Passive Voice em notícias

Muito comum:

The road was closed.

Three people were taken to hospital.

A new school will be built.

Concentre-se em:

what happened.

Quem fez a ação pode não aparecer

The event was canceled.

Não sabemos necessariamente:

quem cancelou.

Não invente o agente.

Headlines faladas e resumos

Antes da notícia completa, um apresentador pode dizer:

A new study suggests that regular walking may improve sleep quality.

Depois:

detalhes.

Esse resumo inicial pode ajudar muito.

Linguagem de possibilidade

Notícias e entrevistas usam:

may

might

could

probably

likely

possibly.

Exemplo

The new system could reduce waiting times.

Não significa:

it will definitely reduce them.

Expected to

The event is expected to attract thousands of visitors.

Isso é:

expectation/prediction.

Reportedly

The company is reportedly planning to open a new office.

Indica:

informação relatada, não necessariamente oficialmente confirmada.

Notícias com números

Números são difíceis porque passam rapidamente.

Treine:

13 / 30

14 / 40

15 / 50

16 / 60

17 / 70

18 / 80

19 / 90.

Teen x ty

Compare:

thirteen

thirty.

fourteen

forty.

fifteen

fifty.

sixteen

sixty.

O padrão de tonicidade costuma ajudar.

Em termos gerais:

thirTEEN

versus:

THIRty.

Datas

Você pode ouvir:

May the fifteenth.

the fifteenth of May.

Ambos:

May 15.

Anos

1998

normalmente:

nineteen ninety-eight.

2026

pode ser:

twenty twenty-six

ou:

two thousand and twenty-six.

Porcentagens

twenty-five percent.

Decimais

3.5

three point five.

Dinheiro

$15.50

pode ser:

fifteen dollars fifty

ou:

fifteen dollars and fifty cents.

Horários

quarter past seven → 7:15.

half past eight → 8:30.

quarter to nine → 8:45.

Approximation

about 500

around 500

roughly 500

não significa:

exatamente 500.

Over

over 2,000.

Significa:

more than 2,000.

Nearly

nearly 80%.

Significa:

almost 80%.

At least

at least 100.

Significa:

100 or more.

Listening e connected speech

Na fala natural, palavras se conectam.

Exemplo escrito:

What are you doing?

Pode soar aproximadamente como uma sequência contínua, não como quatro palavras perfeitamente separadas.

O importante é reconhecer:

chunks.

Chunks

Aprenda expressões completas:

I’d like to…

going to…

have to…

used to…

a lot of…

kind of…

as a result…

Isso é mais eficiente do que tentar ouvir:

palavra por palavra.

Weak forms

Palavras gramaticais podem ser pronunciadas de forma reduzida.

Exemplo:

to

em:

I want to go.

pode soar bem mais fraco que:

want

ou:

go.

O mesmo ocorre com:

a

the

of

can

em diversos contextos.

Content words

Palavras mais importantes costumam receber maior destaque:

nouns

main verbs

adjectives

numbers.

Exemplo:

The TRAIN leaves at SEVEN THIRTY.

Mesmo que você não capte cada palavra:

train

7:30

podem ser suficientes.

Can x can’t

Pode ser difícil.

Observe:

contexto

e:

pronúncia.

Exemplo:

You can park here.

versus:

You can’t park here.

Em algumas variedades, a diferença acústica pode estar na vogal, na consoante final e na tonicidade.

Não dependa apenas de:

ouvir o “t”.

Use contexto.

Positive x negative

Palavras de negação podem ser curtas:

not

n’t

never

no longer

hardly.

Elas podem inverter:

toda a resposta.

Hardly

I hardly ever drive.

Significa:

almost never.

Não:

frequentemente.

Used to

I used to work nights.

Significa:

past habit, normally no longer true.

Se a pergunta for:

Does the speaker still work nights?

Resposta provável:

no.

Still

I still work there.

Significa:

continues.

Anymore

I don’t work there anymore.

Significa:

stopped.

Yet

We haven’t decided yet.

Significa:

no decision so far.

Already

We’ve already finished.

Significa:

finished before now/reference time.

Entonação

Entonação pode dar pistas sobre:

  • question;
  • surprise;
  • uncertainty;
  • enthusiasm.

Mas em nível B1:

não dependa apenas da entonação.

Combine com:

palavras e contexto.

Stress contrast

I said TUESDAY, not Thursday.

A palavra enfatizada indica:

correção.

Correction markers

actually

sorry

I mean

rather

podem introduzir:

informação corrigida.

Paraphrase traps

Áudio:

The hotel is within walking distance of the station.

Alternativa:

The station is close enough to reach on foot.

Mesma ideia.

Outra

Áudio:

The course is free of charge.

Alternativa:

Students don’t have to pay.

Outra

Áudio:

He turned down the offer.

Alternativa:

He refused the offer.

Outra

Áudio:

The event has been put off.

Alternativa:

The event has been postponed.

Distractors

Questões de Listening frequentemente incluem:

informações mencionadas, mas não corretas para a pergunta.

Exemplo:

A:

Did you travel on Monday?

B:

I planned to, but the flight was full, so I went on Tuesday.

Alternativas:

  1. Monday
  2. Tuesday
  3. Wednesday

O áudio menciona:

Monday

mas resposta:

Tuesday.

Intention x reality

Palavras importantes:

planned to

wanted to

was going to

não significam necessariamente:

did.

Exemplo:

I was going to take the train, but I drove instead.

O transporte usado:

car.

Previous plan x final action

I thought about studying medicine, but eventually I chose biology.

Resposta para:

What did the speaker study?

Biology.

Não:

Medicine.

Problem x solution

Entrevistas frequentemente apresentam:

problem → response.

Exemplo:

The original venue was too small, so we moved the event to a larger hall.

Pergunta:

Why was the venue changed?

Resposta:

The original one was too small.

Reason x result

Áudio:

Because ticket sales were low, the concert was canceled.

Cause:

low ticket sales.

Result:

cancellation.

Fact x opinion

The course lasts twelve weeks.

Fato.

I think twelve weeks is too short.

Opinião.

News source x reporter opinion

Residents say the new road is too noisy.

Isso é:

residents’ opinion.

Não necessariamente:

reporter’s opinion.

Interviewer question may contain information

A:

You worked in Japan for three years. What did you learn there?

Informação explícita:

worked in Japan for three years.

Mesmo que entrevistado não repita.

Speaker attitude

Pergunta típica:

How does the speaker feel about…?

Procure:

  • evaluative adjectives;
  • intonation;
  • phrases like I was delighted / disappointed / worried.

Positive attitude

It was a fantastic experience.

I really enjoyed it.

Negative

I was disappointed.

It was frustrating.

Mixed

It was difficult, but I learned a lot.

Resposta correta pode ser:

challenging but valuable.

Interview practice 1

Considere a transcrição de um áudio fictício:

Interviewer: Today we’re talking to Maya Lewis, who recently changed careers from banking to environmental education. Maya, why did you decide to make such a big change?

Maya: I’d worked in banking for nearly eight years. The salary was good, but I wanted a job where I could spend more time working on environmental projects. I started volunteering at a community garden on weekends, and eventually I realized that was the kind of work I wanted to do full-time.

Interviewer: Was it difficult to change careers?

Maya: At first, yes. I had experience managing projects, but I didn’t have a formal qualification in environmental education. So I took an evening course while I was still working at the bank. Six months later, I applied for my current job.

Interviewer: And what do you enjoy most now?

Maya: Probably working with schools. We run workshops for children about food, recycling and biodiversity. No two days are exactly the same.

Informações principais

previous career → banking.

duration → nearly eight years.

motivation → wanted environmental work.

first step → volunteering.

qualification gap → no formal qualification.

solution → evening course.

current favorite → working with schools.

News practice 1

Presenter: A new community health center has opened in Westbrook, providing basic medical services to around 15,000 residents. The center was officially opened on Monday and includes consultation rooms, a small pharmacy and a vaccination area.

According to local health officials, the project was developed because residents previously had to travel more than 20 kilometers for some basic services. The center will initially open from Monday to Saturday, but officials say Sunday opening may be introduced next year if demand is high enough.

More than 300 people visited the center during its first two days.

Informações principais

what → new health center opened.

where → Westbrook.

population → around 15,000 residents.

why → long travel for basic services.

current schedule → Monday–Saturday.

Sunday → possible next year, conditional.

early use → 300+ visitors in first two days.

Entrevista prática 2

Interviewer: Daniel, your company introduced a four-day working week last year. How has it gone?

Daniel: Better than we expected, actually. Employees work slightly longer hours from Monday to Thursday, but they have Friday off. At first, some managers were worried that productivity would fall.

Interviewer: Did it?

Daniel: Not overall. In fact, our internal reports show that productivity has remained approximately the same, while staff absence has fallen slightly.

Interviewer: So will the company keep the system?

Daniel: We’re still reviewing the data, but it’s likely. Most employees want it to continue.

Pontos:

initial concern → lower productivity.

actual result → productivity roughly stable.

absence → slightly lower.

future → likely continuation, not confirmed.

News practice 2

Presenter: Heavy rain has caused travel problems across the northern region this morning. Several roads have been closed because of flooding, and train services between Greenford and Lake City are experiencing delays of up to forty minutes.

Transport officials are asking people to avoid unnecessary journeys until conditions improve. No major injuries have been reported, although emergency teams were called to several flooded homes overnight.

Weather forecasters say the rain is expected to continue until early this evening.

Pontos:

cause → heavy rain.

roads → closed.

trains → delays up to 40 minutes.

advice → avoid unnecessary journeys.

injuries → no major injuries reported.

forecast → rain until early evening.

Vocabulário-chave

interview — entrevista

interviewer — entrevistador

interviewee — entrevistado

news report — notícia/reportagem

presenter — apresentador

reporter — repórter

headline — manchete

source — fonte

statement — declaração

gist — ideia geral

detail — detalhe

signposting — sinalização discursiva

according to — de acordo com

announce — anunciar

confirm — confirmar

warn — alertar

claim — alegar

delay — atraso/atrasar

approximately — aproximadamente

eventually — finalmente/depois de algum tempo

currently — atualmente

Estratégia de prova

Antes do áudio:

leia as perguntas.

Marque palavras como:

why

when

how many

what changed

opinion

future plan.

Na primeira escuta:

identifique situação e assunto.

Na segunda:

busque detalhes.

Durante a escuta:

não pare mentalmente por causa de uma palavra desconhecida.

Se perder uma parte:

retorne imediatamente ao fluxo.

Evite o erro:

“não entendi esta palavra, então perdi todo o resto”.

Outra regra:

a última informação pode corrigir uma anterior.

Se ouvir:

I planned to go on Monday, but I went on Tuesday.

Resposta:

Tuesday.

Finalmente:

preste atenção aos modais.

may/could → possibility

will → stronger future statement

likely → probable

might → uncertain possibility

Prática

Com base na Entrevista prática 1:

1. What was Maya’s previous job area?

  1. Education
  2. Banking
  3. Healthcare
  4. Journalism

2. How long had she worked in that area?

  1. Nearly eight years
  2. Six months
  3. Two years
  4. Twenty years

3. Why did she want to change careers?

  1. Her salary was too low.
  2. She wanted to work more with environmental projects.
  3. Her company closed.
  4. She wanted to move abroad.

4. What helped her discover the kind of work she wanted?

  1. A television program.
  2. Volunteering at a community garden.
  3. A university exam.
  4. A job interview.

5. What qualification problem did she have?

  1. She had no project-management experience.
  2. She lacked a formal qualification in environmental education.
  3. She could not speak English.
  4. She had no work experience.

6. What did she do about this?

  1. Took an evening course.
  2. Returned to banking permanently.
  3. Stopped working.
  4. Moved to another country.

7. What does she enjoy most now?

  1. Working with schools.
  2. Working in banks.
  3. Writing financial reports.
  4. Traveling abroad.

Com base na News practice 1:

8. What has opened?

  1. A school.
  2. A community health center.
  3. A supermarket.
  4. A railway station.

9. Approximately how many residents may benefit?

  1. 1,500
  2. 15,000
  3. 50,000
  4. 150,000

10. Why was the center developed?

  1. Residents had to travel long distances for some services.
  2. The town had too many hospitals.
  3. The pharmacy was too large.
  4. Schools requested it.

11. When will it initially open?

  1. Monday to Friday only.
  2. Monday to Saturday.
  3. Every Sunday only.
  4. Weekends only.

12. Is Sunday opening confirmed for next year?

  1. Yes, definitely.
  2. No; it may happen if demand is high.
  3. It has already started.
  4. Sunday opening was canceled permanently.

13. How many people visited during the first two days?

  1. Fewer than 30.
  2. Exactly 150.
  3. More than 300.
  4. More than 3,000.

Com base na Entrevista prática 2:

14. What change did the company introduce?

  1. Remote work every day.
  2. A four-day working week.
  3. A six-hour workday.
  4. Weekend work.

15. What were some managers initially worried about?

  1. Salaries would increase.
  2. Productivity would fall.
  3. Employees would work Fridays.
  4. The office would close.

16. What happened to productivity?

  1. It collapsed.
  2. It increased by 50%.
  3. It remained approximately the same.
  4. It was not measured.

17. What happened to staff absence?

  1. It increased significantly.
  2. It fell slightly.
  3. It remained exactly the same.
  4. It disappeared completely.

18. Will the company definitely keep the system?

  1. Yes.
  2. No.
  3. It is likely, but still under review.
  4. The company has already ended it.

Com base na News practice 2:

19. What caused the travel problems?

  1. Snow.
  2. Heavy rain.
  3. Road construction.
  4. A strike.

20. What has happened to several roads?

  1. They were widened.
  2. They were closed.
  3. They were made free.
  4. They were reopened immediately.

21. How long are some train delays?

  1. Up to 14 minutes.
  2. Up to 40 minutes.
  3. Exactly 4 hours.
  4. More than 8 hours.

22. What are officials advising people to do?

  1. Travel more.
  2. Avoid unnecessary journeys.
  3. Use flooded roads.
  4. Visit the region.

23. Have major injuries been reported?

  1. Yes, many.
  2. No major injuries have been reported.
  3. Exactly three.
  4. The report says everyone was injured.

24. How long is the rain expected to continue?

  1. Until early evening.
  2. For one week.
  3. Until tomorrow afternoon.
  4. It has already stopped.

25. Identifique o detalhe correto:

Áudio fictício:

I originally planned to study chemistry, but after my first semester I changed to biology.

What did the speaker finally study?

  1. Chemistry
  2. Biology
  3. Physics
  4. Both necessarily

26. Identifique:

The train was supposed to leave at 6:15, but there’s been a delay of twenty minutes.

What is the new expected departure time?

27. Interprete:

The course costs £80, although students under 18 pay only £50.

How much does a 17-year-old pay?

28. Parafraseie:

Áudio:

The conference has been put off until June.

Complete:

The conference has been ______ until June.

29. Analise:

Officials say the new service could reduce waiting times.

Qual alternativa é adequada?

  1. Waiting times will definitely disappear.
  2. Officials believe a reduction is possible.
  3. The service has already eliminated delays.
  4. Officials confirmed exact future results.

30. Produção de escuta simulada

Leia apenas uma vez cada transcrição abaixo, sem voltar ao início, e responda mentalmente às perguntas.

Trecho A

I started learning Spanish because my company opened an office in Madrid. At first, I only wanted enough Spanish for short business trips, but I enjoyed the course so much that I continued studying after the trips became less frequent. I’ve now been studying for almost three years.

Responda:

  • Why did the speaker begin learning Spanish?
  • Did the original reason remain the only reason?
  • How long has the speaker been studying?

Trecho B

A local museum will remain closed until Friday following a problem with its electrical system. The museum was originally expected to reopen on Wednesday, but repairs have taken longer than planned. Visitors who bought tickets online can use them on any date during the next three months.

Responda:

  • Why is the museum closed?
  • When was it originally expected to reopen?
  • When will it now reopen?
  • What can ticket holders do?

Trecho A

Why?

Because the speaker’s company opened an office in Madrid.

Did the original reason remain the only reason?

No.

A pessoa começou por trabalho, mas:

enjoyed the course

e continuou mesmo quando as viagens diminuíram.

How long?

Almost three years.

Because of a problem with its electrical system.

Original reopening?

Wednesday.

New reopening?

Friday.
