Se o autor diz:

may

não escreva:

certainly.

Se diz:

argues

não apresente necessariamente como:

proven fact.

Article says x author argues

reports/describes

para informações.

argues/claims

para posições.

Claim

Cuidado:

claim

pode sugerir que uma afirmação:

está sendo apresentada por alguém, não confirmada independentemente.

Steps for summary writing

Use cinco etapas.

1. READ

Compreenda o texto inteiro.

2. IDENTIFY

Localize as ideias essenciais.

3. REMOVE

Elimine exemplos, repetições e detalhes secundários.

4. PARAPHRASE

Reescreva com estrutura própria.

5. CHECK

Compare resumo com a fonte.

Checklist de fidelidade

Pergunte:

Did I change any fact?

Did I add any information?

Did I exaggerate?

Did I remove an important limitation?

Did I preserve numbers when they mattered?

Did I preserve the author’s level of certainty?

Método 5W1H para notícias

Para notícias:

Who?

What?

Where?

When?

Why?

How?

Nem todas precisam entrar.

Selecione:

as essenciais.

Exemplo jornalístico

Original:

A city council launched a six-month free bus program on Sundays. The initiative aims to reduce traffic in the city center. Around 35,000 passengers used the service on its first Sunday, 20% more than usual. Officials say more data are needed before deciding whether the service will become permanent.

Resumo:

A city has introduced a six-month free Sunday bus program to reduce traffic. Initial passenger numbers were higher than usual, but officials will collect more data before deciding whether to make the service permanent.

Método científico

Procure:

research question

sample/method

main result

limitation/conclusion.

Exemplo científico

Original:

Researchers studied 180 university students to examine whether short walking breaks affected concentration. Students who took a walking break scored 8% higher on average than those who studied continuously. However, the sample included only young adults.

Resumo:

A study of university students found that short walking breaks were associated with better concentration scores, although the findings were limited to a young adult sample.

Não precisa conservar todo número

O:

180

e:

8%

podem ser importantes ou não dependendo do limite.

Versão mais curta:

A study found that short walking breaks may support concentration in university students, although the sample was limited to young adults.

Summary sentence

Treinar resumo em:

uma frase

é excelente exercício.

Texto:

The university extended library hours, installed more computers and created additional study areas during examinations.

Resumo:

The university expanded study support during the exam period.

Abstraction

Esse processo exige transformar:

several details

em:

broader category.

computers + study spaces + opening hours

→

study support.

Não generalize demais

Original:

Three schools introduced recycling programs.

Ruim:

Schools everywhere are becoming environmentally sustainable.

Muito amplo.

Summary length reduction

Uma técnica:

Original idea

100%.

First reduction

50%.

Final summary

25–35%.

Não é uma regra matemática fixa, mas ajuda a pensar em:

compression.

Texto integrado 1

Why Some Companies Are Redesigning Offices

Remote and hybrid work have changed how many companies use office buildings. Because fewer employees are present every day, some organizations no longer need the same number of individual desks.

As a result, companies are creating more shared workspaces, meeting areas and rooms for collaborative activities. Some have also reduced the total amount of office space they rent.

However, these changes can create problems when many employees choose to visit the office on the same day. For this reason, some businesses have introduced desk-booking systems.

Overall, offices are becoming more flexible as companies adapt their physical spaces to new working patterns.

Main points — texto 1

hybrid/remote work changed office needs.

companies use more shared/flexible spaces.

reduced space can create capacity problems.

booking systems are one response.

Possible summary

Remote and hybrid work are changing office design because companies need fewer permanent desks. Many organizations are introducing shared spaces or renting smaller offices, although busy days can create capacity problems. Some companies therefore use booking systems to manage office space more efficiently.

Texto integrado 2

A Study of Urban Noise

Researchers measured noise levels in eight city neighborhoods over a period of four months. They found that areas near major roads were generally noisier than residential streets farther from heavy traffic.

Participants living in the noisiest areas also reported more difficulty sleeping. However, the study did not establish that traffic noise directly caused the sleep problems because other factors were not fully controlled.

The researchers recommend further studies involving larger populations and longer observation periods.

Possible summary

A four-month study found higher noise levels near major roads and more reported sleep difficulties among residents of noisier areas. However, the research did not establish a direct causal relationship, and the researchers recommend larger, longer studies.

Texto integrado 3

Adult Learning Program Expands

A community education program for adults will add new evening and weekend classes after more than 600 people enrolled during its first year. The program currently offers digital skills, English and basic mathematics.

Organizers say many participants work during the day, making flexible schedules particularly important. New courses will include workplace communication and introductory programming.

Most classes will remain free, although two advanced courses will require a small fee.

Possible summary

A successful adult education program is expanding its evening and weekend classes after strong first-year enrollment. The program focuses on flexible learning for working adults and will add communication and programming courses, while most classes will remain free.

Vocabulário-chave

summary — resumo

summarize — resumir

main idea — ideia principal

key point — ponto essencial

supporting detail — detalhe de apoio

paraphrase — paráfrase

source — fonte

concise — conciso

accurate — preciso/fiel

relevant — relevante

irrelevant — irrelevante

omit — omitir

include — incluir

reduce — reduzir

combine — combinar

rephrase — reformular

word limit — limite de palavras

neutral — neutro

faithful — fiel

Estratégia de prova

Em uma tarefa de resumo, use a sequência:

MAIN IDEA → KEY POINTS → PARAPHRASE → CHECK

Primeiro, escreva em rascunho:

Main idea:

Point 1:

Point 2:

Point 3:

Depois pergunte:

Which details can I remove?

Então produza o resumo sem olhar frase por frase para o original.

Isso reduz:

cópia involuntária.

Ao terminar, compare.

Procure quatro erros:

Addition — acrescentei algo que não estava lá?

Distortion — alterei o sentido?

Omission — removi algo essencial?

Overstatement — tornei a conclusão forte demais?

Prática

Leia:

The town opened a new public library in March. The building includes study rooms, computers and a children’s area. More than 8,000 people visited during the first month. The council says the library was built to improve access to educational and digital resources.

1. Qual é a ideia principal?

  1. Children like libraries.
  2. A new public library has opened to improve access to resources.
  3. The town has 8,000 residents.
  4. Computers are expensive.

2. Qual detalhe pode ser removido em um resumo muito curto?

  1. A library opened.
  2. Its purpose is to improve access.
  3. It has a children’s area.
  4. It is a public library.

3. Escolha o melhor resumo:

  1. The town is wonderful because it has a library.
  2. A town opened a public library to improve access to educational and digital resources, attracting thousands of visitors in its first month.
  3. The library has computers, and I think that is useful.
  4. In March, there were study rooms and children and computers and 8,000 people.

Leia:

A study followed 250 office workers for six months. Participants who took short walking breaks during the day reported slightly lower stress levels. However, the researchers said the study did not prove that walking directly caused the difference.

4. Qual informação é essencial?

  1. The study involved office workers.
  2. Walking definitely eliminates stress.
  3. Researchers proved causation.
  4. The study lasted exactly six years.

5. Qual resumo é inadequado por exagero?

  1. A study found lower reported stress among workers who took walking breaks, but it did not establish causation.
  2. Researchers proved that walking breaks prevent stress.
  3. Walking breaks were associated with slightly lower reported stress.
  4. The study found a relationship but not direct causation.

6. O que deve ser preservado?

  1. The limitation about causation.
  2. Only the number 250.
  3. Every small procedural detail.
  4. Nothing from the final sentence.

7. Parafraseie:

The company reduced its office space because more employees were working remotely.

8. Parafraseie:

The number of passengers increased significantly.

Use:

increase

como substantivo.

9. Reduza:

The course is completely free for all students, and students do not have to pay any money to participate in it.

10. Reduza:

One of the main reasons why many adults choose evening courses is because they work during the daytime.

11. Combine:

The program is online. It lasts twelve weeks. It is free.

12. Combine mantendo contraste:

The device is cheap. It is not very accurate.

13. Remova informação secundária:

The study was conducted by Dr. Sarah Thompson, who has worked at the university for 17 years. It found that students who reviewed vocabulary regularly remembered more words.

Escreva uma versão resumida.

14. Identifique o problema:

Fonte:

Some participants reported better sleep.

Resumo:

All participants slept better.

  1. accurate paraphrase
  2. overgeneralization
  3. good compression
  4. correct inference

15. Identifique:

Fonte:

The treatment may reduce symptoms.

Resumo:

The treatment cures the condition.

Qual é o problema?

16. Identifique:

Fonte:

The city introduced a pilot program lasting six months.

Resumo:

The city permanently introduced the program.

Qual é o problema?

17. Escolha o melhor resumo:

Fonte:

Online learning provides flexibility because students can study from different locations. However, some learners find it harder to remain motivated without regular classroom interaction.

  1. Online learning is perfect for all students.
  2. Online learning offers flexibility but can create motivation challenges for some learners.
  3. Students study in different places.
  4. Classroom learning is always better.

18. Resuma em uma frase:

The university extended library opening hours, added more computers and created new quiet study spaces during the examination period.

19. Resuma:

Bus fares were reduced by 20%. Passenger numbers then rose by 15%.

Use uma relação de causa ou sequência sem afirmar certeza causal maior do que os dados permitem.

20. Resuma:

Researchers interviewed 400 adults about sleep. Most people who reported exercising regularly also reported better sleep, although the study did not establish that exercise caused the difference.

21. Leia:

A community center introduced free weekend classes in English, mathematics and digital skills. The courses were designed for adults who could not attend weekday classes because of work. More than 500 people registered in the first three months.

Produza um resumo de:

25–35 palavras.

22. Leia:

A city planted 5,000 trees in neighborhoods with little green space. Officials say the project aims to provide shade, improve local air quality and create more attractive public spaces. The trees will be monitored for three years.

Produza:

uma frase de resumo.

23. Leia:

A company tested a four-day working week for six months. Productivity remained approximately stable, while employee absence fell slightly. Most workers said they preferred the new schedule. The company has not yet decided whether the change will become permanent.

Qual informação não pode ser omitida em um resumo equilibrado?

  1. The change is not yet permanent.
  2. Six months necessarily.
  3. Every worker’s name.
  4. The office address.

24. Escreva um resumo de 35–50 palavras para o texto da questão 23.

25. Reescreva de modo neutro:

Fortunately, the brilliant new transport system has finally solved the terrible traffic problem.

Preserve apenas uma afirmação que possa funcionar em um resumo factual, sem linguagem avaliativa não necessária.

26. Compare:

Fonte:

Officials expect the new center to serve approximately 20,000 residents.

Resumo A:

The center will definitely serve exactly 20,000 residents.

Resumo B:

Officials expect the center to serve about 20,000 residents.

Qual preserva melhor o sentido e por quê?

27. Resuma sem copiar literalmente:

Many students prefer online courses because they can organize their study around work and family responsibilities.

28. Resuma os pontos:

Problem: heavy traffic
Measure: new bus routes
Result: passenger numbers increased
Future: city may expand the program

Produza duas frases.

29. Leia:

Scientists tested a low-cost water sensor in several rural communities. The device produced results similar to laboratory equipment in most conditions, but its accuracy fell during periods of very high humidity. Researchers say more testing is needed.

Escreva um resumo de 40–55 palavras.

30. Produção

Leia o texto:

A university introduced a free online study-support program for first-year students after surveys showed that many new students had difficulty organizing their study time. The program includes weekly planning activities, short videos about study strategies and online meetings with tutors. During its first semester, approximately 700 students used at least one part of the service. Students who completed most of the activities reported feeling more confident about managing their workload. However, the university has not yet established whether the program directly improved academic grades. Organizers plan to continue the service next year and collect more detailed data.

Produza:

  • a main idea;
  • quatro key points;
  • três detalhes que podem ser omitidos em um resumo curto;
  • um resumo de 70–90 palavras;
  • uma frase explicando por que seria incorreto escrever:
    > “The program improved students’ grades.”

Gabarito comentado

1. B

O foco é:

new public library

improved access to resources.

2. C

children’s area

é um detalhe possível de remover em:

summary muito curto.

3. B

A alternativa preserva:

evento

propósito

interesse inicial.

Não adiciona opinião pessoal.

4. A

A população estudada é:

office workers.

É uma informação relevante.

5. B

O texto não prova:

causation.

Além disso:

prevent stress

é mais forte que:

slightly lower reported stress.

6. A

A limitação é essencial porque impede uma conclusão exagerada.

7.

Modelo:

The company used less office space as remote work became more common.

Ou:

Increased remote work allowed the company to reduce its office space.

8.

There was a significant increase in passenger numbers.

9.

The course is free for all students.

A segunda parte apenas repete:

free.

10.

Many adults choose evening courses because they work during the day.

11.

The program is a free twelve-week online course.

12.

The device is cheap but not very accurate.

13.

A university study found that students who reviewed vocabulary regularly remembered more words.

O nome da pesquisadora e seus:

17 years at university

não são necessários para a ideia principal.

14. B — overgeneralization

some

foi transformado em:

all.

Isso altera o sentido.

15.

O resumo:

transforma possibilidade de redução de sintomas

em:

cura.

Isso é:

overstatement/distortion.

16.

pilot

e:

six months

indicam caráter experimental/temporário.

permanently introduced

altera o sentido.

17. B

Preserva:

advantage

e:

limitation.

18.

Modelo:

The university expanded study facilities and library access during the examination period.

19.

Modelo:

After bus fares were reduced by 20%, passenger numbers rose by 15%.

A palavra:

after

preserva a sequência sem afirmar necessariamente que:

price reduction was the only cause.

20.

A survey of adults found an association between regular exercise and better reported sleep, but it did not establish that exercise caused the difference.

21.

Modelo, 30 palavras:

A community center introduced free weekend English, mathematics and digital-skills classes for working adults unable to attend weekdays, attracting more than 500 registrations within three months.

22.

Modelo:

A city planted 5,000 trees in areas with limited green space to improve shade, air quality and public spaces, with monitoring planned for three years.

23. A

Se omitirmos:

not yet permanent

podemos fazer parecer que:

a política já foi adotada definitivamente.

Isso altera o status do projeto.

24.

Modelo:

A six-month trial of a four-day working week found stable productivity, slightly lower staff absence and strong employee support. However, the company is still reviewing the results and has not decided whether to make the schedule permanent.

25.

Uma versão neutra:

The new transport system has reduced traffic problems.

Se a fonte original apenas usa linguagem avaliativa e não fornece evidência para:

solved,

não deveríamos manter:

completely solved

como fato.

26.

Resumo B.

about

preserva:

approximately.

expect

preserva:

expectativa.

Resumo A transforma:

approximate expectation

em:

exact certainty.

27.

Modelo:

Online courses are popular with students who need flexibility to combine study with work and family responsibilities.

28.

Modelo:

The city introduced new bus routes to address heavy traffic, after which passenger numbers increased. Officials are now considering expanding the program.

29.

Modelo:

Researchers tested a low-cost water sensor in rural communities and found that it produced results similar to laboratory equipment in most conditions. However, accuracy decreased in very high humidity, so the team says further testing is required before wider use.

30.

Main idea

The university created an online support program to help first-year students manage their studies, with promising self-reported results but no confirmed effect on grades.

Four key points

  1. The program was created because new students reported difficulty organizing study time.

  2. It provides planning activities, study-strategy videos and tutor meetings.

  3. Around 700 students used at least part of the program.

  4. Students completing most activities reported greater confidence, but academic improvement has not been established.

Three details that could be omitted in a short summary

Depending on the word limit:

the exact figure of approximately 700 students;

the fact that the program ran during its first semester;

the exact list of every component of the service.

These can be compressed into:

online study-support activities.

Summary

A university introduced a free online support program to help first-year students manage their study time. The service provides planning activities, study-strategy resources and access to tutors. Around 700 students used it during the first semester, and regular participants reported greater confidence in managing their workload. However, the university has not established whether the program improves academic grades. The service will continue next year while organizers collect more detailed data.

Why the statement is incorrect

“The program improved students’ grades.”

Isso não é sustentado porque o texto afirma explicitamente que:

the university has not yet established whether the program directly improved academic grades.

O resultado relatado foi:

greater confidence in workload management,

não:

confirmed grade improvement.

Tarefa de consolidação

Pratique o processo de compressão com cinco textos de aproximadamente 150–250 palavras.

Para cada texto:

1. Escreva a main idea em uma frase.

2. Selecione três a cinco key points.

3. Risque exemplos e repetições.

4. Produza um resumo com cerca de metade do tamanho.

5. Reduza novamente para aproximadamente um terço.

Depois compare as versões e verifique:

o que pôde ser removido

sem:

perder o sentido central.

Crie também uma tabela:

Source Summary
because the weather was bad because of bad weather
prices increased rapidly there was a rapid increase in prices
started a new program launched a new program
approximately 500 about 500
was associated with was linked to
further studies are needed more research is needed

Pratique ainda os principais erros:

Adding information

Changing the meaning

Turning possibility into certainty

Turning some into all

Removing an important contrast

Copying entire sentences

Including personal opinion

Keeping too many examples

Writing almost the same length as the source

Antes de entregar um resumo, faça cinco perguntas:

Is it shorter?

Is it accurate?

Does it contain the main idea?

Did I use my own wording where possible?

Did I avoid adding my own opinion?

Finalize com a regra central:

A good summary is not the shortest possible text. It is the shortest text that still preserves the essential meaning of the source.

No nível B1, resumir bem significa saber decidir:

what must stay

e:

what can safely disappear.

Aula 96 — Speaking B1: opinião, justificativa e comparação

Objetivos

Ao final desta aula, você deverá ser capaz de:

  • expressar opiniões de forma clara em Speaking B1;
  • justificar uma opinião com razões simples e relevantes;
  • desenvolver respostas além de “yes/no”;
  • comparar duas opções, situações ou ideias;
  • apresentar semelhanças e diferenças oralmente;
  • usar estruturas como I think, in my opinion, because, however, whereas e both;
  • explicar preferências;
  • usar comparativos e superlativos com segurança;
  • concordar e discordar de maneira apropriada;
  • apresentar vantagens e desvantagens;
  • ganhar tempo de forma natural enquanto organiza a resposta;
  • corrigir-se durante a fala sem interromper completamente a comunicação;
  • manter uma resposta organizada por aproximadamente 30–90 segundos;
  • lidar com perguntas de acompanhamento;
  • usar exemplos para sustentar ideias;
  • evitar respostas excessivamente curtas;
  • controlar a força das afirmações com may, might, can e usually;
  • aplicar estratégias de fluência adequadas a exames de proficiência B1.

Desenvolvimento

No nível B1, Speaking não exige:

perfect English.

O objetivo principal é conseguir:

communicate clearly

develop ideas

explain reasons

compare options

respond appropriately.

Uma resposta simples, clara e bem desenvolvida costuma ser mais eficaz do que tentar produzir:

complicated grammar

com muitos erros.

Resposta curta x resposta desenvolvida

Pergunta:

Do you prefer studying alone or with other people?

Resposta curta:

Alone.

A informação está correta, mas demonstra muito pouco.

Resposta melhor:

I prefer studying alone because I can organize my time more easily and concentrate better. However, studying with other people can be useful when I need to discuss a difficult topic.

Agora temos:

opinion

reason

additional explanation

contrast.

Estrutura básica para opinião

Uma técnica útil:

Opinion → Reason → Example

Exemplo:

I think public transport is important because it allows many people to travel without using private cars. For example, frequent bus services can reduce the number of cars entering city centers.

Estrutura ampliada

Para respostas mais longas:

Opinion

Reason 1

Example

Reason 2

Contrast or limitation

Conclusion

Exemplo

Pergunta:

Do you think online learning is useful?

Resposta:

Yes, I think online learning can be very useful, especially for people who need flexible schedules. One reason is that students can study from different locations and often choose when to complete activities. For example, someone who works during the day may study in the evening. Another advantage is that online platforms can provide access to a large number of resources. However, some students may find it difficult to stay motivated without regular face-to-face contact. Overall, I think online learning is useful when students receive enough support.

Expressando opinião

Formas básicas:

I think…

I believe…

In my opinion,…

In my view,…

I think

I think cities should invest more in public transport.

I believe

I believe students benefit from regular reading practice.

In my opinion

In my opinion, working from home can be convenient for many employees.

In my view

In my view, technology should support teachers rather than replace them.

Não repetir a mesma expressão

Evite:

I think… I think… I think…

Você pode começar com:

I think…

e depois desenvolver diretamente.

Exemplo:

I think public libraries are still very important. They provide free access to information and give people quiet places to study.

Justificativa

A opinião precisa de:

reasons.

Expressões úteis:

because…

one reason is that…

another reason is that…

mainly because…

this is because…

Because

I prefer studying in the morning because I can concentrate better.

One reason is that

One reason is that public transport can be cheaper than driving.

Another reason

Another reason is that it may reduce traffic congestion.

Giving examples

Exemplos tornam a resposta mais concreta.

For example,…

For instance,…

Such as…

Exemplo

Technology can support language learning. For example, students can use pronunciation tools to practice outside the classroom.

Personal example

Quando apropriado:

For example, when I study vocabulary, I remember words more easily if I use them in sentences.

Em Speaking:

personal examples

podem ajudar bastante porque são fáceis de desenvolver.

Hypothetical example

Você não precisa contar uma experiência real.

For example, a student who works full-time may prefer an online course because it offers more flexibility.

Expressando preferência

I prefer X to Y.

I would prefer…

I’d rather…

For me, X is more suitable.

Prefer

I prefer studying at home to studying in a café.

Não:

prefer X than Y.

Would prefer

I would prefer to live in a smaller city because it is usually quieter.

Would rather

I’d rather travel by train because I find it more comfortable.

Estrutura:

would rather + base verb.

Comparação

Em provas B1, você pode receber:

  • duas fotografias;
  • duas situações;
  • duas opções;
  • duas formas de fazer algo.

Pode ser solicitado:

compare them

say which you prefer

explain why.

Similarity

Expressões:

Both…

They both…

In both situations…

Similarly…

Both

Both pictures show people studying.

They both

They both seem to be working in groups.

In both situations

In both situations, people are using technology.

Difference

Use:

but

however

while

whereas

unlike.

While

In the first picture, the students are working indoors, while the people in the second picture are outside.

Whereas

The first situation seems formal, whereas the second seems more relaxed.

Unlike

Unlike the first picture, the second one shows a large group.

Comparatives

Muito úteis no Speaking.

bigger than

smaller than

quieter than

cheaper than

easier than

more convenient than

more flexible than

less stressful than.

Exemplo

Traveling by train is usually more comfortable than traveling by bus.

Softening

Evite tornar comparação absoluta se você não tem certeza.

Em vez de:

Cities are better than small towns.

Prefira:

Cities may be more convenient for people who need access to many services.

It seems

Ao descrever imagens:

It seems…

They seem to be…

It looks like…

Essas formas são úteis porque você:

não conhece necessariamente o contexto real da imagem.

Exemplo

It looks like they are waiting for a train.

They seem to be discussing a project.

In the foreground / background

Em descrição de imagem:

in the foreground

in the background

on the left

on the right

in the middle.

Mas não fique apenas descrevendo

Se a tarefa diz:

compare the pictures

não basta listar objetos.

Fraco:

In picture one there are three people. There is a table. In picture two there are two people. There is a computer.

Melhor:

Both pictures show people studying, but the environments are different. The first group appears to be studying together in a classroom, whereas the second person seems to be studying alone at home.

Compare + speculate

Depois:

The group might be working on a shared project, while the person at home may be preparing independently for an exam.

Agora temos:

descrição + comparação + inferência.

Compare + preference

Personally, I would prefer the second situation because I find it easier to concentrate when I study alone.

Estrutura para comparação de imagens

Uma resposta simples:

General similarity

Difference 1

Difference 2

Possible interpretation

Preference

Modelo

Both pictures show people doing physical activity. In the first picture, several people are exercising together in a gym, whereas the second picture shows one person running outdoors. The gym activity seems more social and structured, while running outside may provide more freedom. Personally, I would prefer exercising outdoors because I enjoy being in open spaces, although group exercise can be motivating.

Comparing options

Pergunta:

Which is better for a holiday: a city or the countryside?

Resposta:

Both can be good choices, but they offer different experiences. A city usually has more restaurants, museums and entertainment, whereas the countryside is often quieter and less crowded. I would probably choose the countryside because I prefer relaxing places, although I might choose a city for a shorter trip.

Advantages and disadvantages

Estruturas:

One advantage is…

Another advantage is…

One disadvantage is…

The main drawback is…

Exemplo

One advantage of working from home is that employees can save commuting time. Another benefit is greater flexibility. However, one disadvantage is that some people may feel isolated.

Balance

No B1, mostrar:

both sides

pode melhorar muito a resposta.

Pergunta:

Is social media useful?

Resposta fraca:

Yes, it’s good.

Melhor:

I think social media can be useful because it helps people communicate and find information quickly. However, it can also become distracting, so I think it is important to use it in moderation.

Agreeing

I agree.

I completely agree.

That’s true.

Exactly.

I think so too.

Agreeing with reason

Melhor:

I agree because reliable public transport can reduce dependence on cars.

Partial agreement

I agree to some extent.

That’s true, but…

I see your point, but…

I partly agree.

Exemplo

I see your point, but I think online courses can be difficult for students who need more direct support.

Disagreement

Use formas educadas:

I don’t completely agree.

I’m not sure I agree.

I see it differently.

I understand your point, but…

Evite

You’re wrong.

em tarefas colaborativas, a menos que o contexto justifique uma linguagem muito direta.

Interaction

Em alguns exames, Speaking é feito com:

another candidate.

Você também precisa:

react.

Inviting opinion

What do you think?

Do you agree?

How about you?

What about this option?

Suggesting

We could…

Maybe we should…

How about…?

Why don’t we…?

Exemplo

We could choose the train because it is faster.

Responding

That’s a good idea.

That might work.

I’m not sure about that because…

I think the other option might be better.

Reaching agreement

So, shall we choose…?

I think we agree that…

Then maybe the best option is…

Justifying choice

Não diga apenas:

Let’s choose the library.

Acrescente:

because it is quiet and everyone can use the study materials there.

Fluency

Fluência não significa:

speaking very fast.

Significa conseguir:

keep speaking without excessive breakdowns.

Falar um pouco mais devagar e claramente é:

melhor

do que falar rápido e se perder.

Gaining time

Expressões naturais:

Let me think…

That’s an interesting question.

I’d say…

Well,…

I haven’t thought about that before, but…

Exemplo

That’s an interesting question. I’d say public transport is more important in large cities because…

Essas expressões fornecem:

alguns segundos para organizar a resposta.

Não abusar

Não responda:

Well… um… let me think… you know… well…

e nunca chegue ao ponto.

Use:

one short filler

e continue.

Reformulation

Se não souber uma palavra:

explique de outra forma.

Isso é extremamente importante no B1.

Exemplo

Você esqueceu:

helmet.

Pode dizer:

the thing you wear on your head when you ride a bicycle.

Isso demonstra:

communicative ability.

Circumlocution

Estruturas úteis:

It’s a thing that…

It’s a place where…

It’s a person who…

It’s something you use to…

Exemplo

A pharmacist is a person who prepares or provides medicines.

Self-correction

Você pode corrigir-se.

I started the course last year — sorry, two years ago.

Isso é normal.

Useful correction phrases

Sorry, I mean…

Let me correct that…

What I meant was…

Exemplo

There were fifteen people — sorry, fifty people.

Não começar tudo novamente

Se errar uma palavra:

corrija

e:

continue.

If you do not understand the examiner

Você pode pedir repetição.

Could you repeat the question, please?

Sorry, could you say that again?

Could you explain what you mean by…?

Isso é melhor que:

responder a uma pergunta que você não compreendeu.

Verificar palavra

Do you mean…?

Expandindo respostas

Pergunta:

Do you like reading?

Estratégia:

Answer + Why + Example.

Yes, I do. I especially like reading non-fiction because I enjoy learning about science and technology. For example, I often read short articles when I want to understand a new topic.

Outra

Do you exercise regularly?

Yes, usually a few times a week. I think exercise is important because it helps me relax and maintain a routine. I usually prefer walking because it doesn’t require special equipment.

Past experiences

Pergunta:

Tell me about a course you enjoyed.

Estrutura:

what

when

why

result.

I took a short programming course last year. I enjoyed it because the lessons included practical activities rather than only theory. For example, we built a small project at the end. I think that practical approach helped me remember the content better.

Future plans

Pergunta:

What would you like to learn in the future?

I’d like to improve my English speaking skills because I want to communicate more confidently. I also hope to practice listening with more natural speech. If possible, I’d like to take a course that includes regular conversation practice.

Opinion question

Should university education be free?

Uma resposta B1 pode:

acknowledge complexity.

I think public access to university education should be as affordable as possible because cost can prevent some people from studying. However, universities also need resources to provide good teaching and facilities. So I think governments should provide strong financial support, especially for students who cannot afford the costs.

Do not memorize fixed essays

Memorizar respostas completas pode causar problemas:

answer doesn’t fit question

unnatural delivery

difficulty adapting.

Melhor memorizar:

flexible structures.

Building blocks

Memorize:

In my opinion…

One reason is…

For example…

However…

On the other hand…

Overall…

Esses blocos podem ser adaptados a:

many topics.

Pronunciation and intelligibility

No B1, objetivo:

be understandable.

Não precisa:

imitate a native accent.

Priorize:

  • final consonants;
  • word stress;
  • clear vowels;
  • important grammatical distinctions.

Third-person -s

works

studies

lives.

Não precisa exagerar, mas:

tente produzir claramente.

Past endings

worked

played

wanted.

Numbers

Fale com cuidado:

thirteen / thirty

fourteen / forty

fifteen / fifty.

Word stress

Exemplos:

imPORtant

eduCAtion

techNOLogy

comPARison.

Pronúncia inadequada pode:

dificultar compreensão

mesmo quando vocabulário está correto.

Sentence stress

Destaque palavras importantes:

I prefer ONLINE COURSES because they’re more FLEXIBLE.

Palavras gramaticais podem ser:

menos fortes.

Intonation

Em opiniões:

natural rise/fall.

Evite:

falar toda a resposta com mesma entonação.

Speaking and grammar

Não tente demonstrar toda a gramática aprendida em uma resposta.

Use estruturas que:

você controla.

Useful B1 grammar

Present Simple

Simple Past

Present Perfect

comparatives

modal verbs

First Conditional

Second Conditional básico

relative clauses

gerunds/infinitives.

Present Perfect

I’ve studied English for several years.

Comparison

Online learning is more flexible than classroom learning.

First Conditional

If public transport improves, more people may use it.

Second Conditional

If I had the choice, I’d study in a quieter place.

Relative clause

A library is a place where students can work without many distractions.

Modals

Schools should provide…

Technology can help…

This may be useful…

Accuracy x fluency

Não pare a cada frase pensando:

Is every verb perfect?

Se você percebe erro pequeno:

continue.

Corrija apenas quando:

o erro altera significativamente o sentido

ou:

a correção é rápida.

Exemplos de tarefa B1

Question

Do you think people should exercise every day?

Resposta:

I think regular exercise is important, although I don’t think everyone needs to do intense exercise every day. Activities such as walking or cycling can help people stay active and may also reduce stress. For example, someone who works at a desk all day might benefit from taking a walk in the evening. Overall, I think being active regularly is more important than doing very difficult exercise every day.

Comparison task

Compare studying at home and studying in a library.

Resposta:

Both places can be good for studying, but they offer different advantages. Studying at home is usually more convenient because you don’t need to travel, and you have access to your own things. A library, however, may be quieter and more structured. It also provides books and other resources. Personally, I prefer studying in a library when I need to concentrate, whereas I prefer home for shorter and more relaxed study sessions.

Decision task

Your class can visit a museum, a science center or a park. Discuss the options and choose one.

Resposta possível:

I think all three options could be interesting. A museum would be useful for learning about history, while a park would be better for outdoor activities. However, I think the science center might be the best choice because it combines learning with interactive activities. Students could probably participate in experiments and demonstrations, which may be more engaging than simply looking at exhibits. What do you think?

Responding to partner

I agree. The science center sounds more interactive. Also, if the weather is bad, an indoor activity would be more practical.

Agora há:

interaction

agreement

additional reason.

Vocabulário-chave

opinion — opinião

reason — razão

justification — justificativa

comparison — comparação

similarity — semelhança

difference — diferença

preference — preferência

advantage — vantagem

disadvantage — desvantagem

benefit — benefício

drawback — desvantagem

agree — concordar

disagree — discordar

partly agree — concordar parcialmente

compare — comparar

whereas — enquanto/ao passo que

however — no entanto

both — ambos

more suitable — mais adequado

in my opinion — na minha opinião

overall — no geral

Estratégia de prova

Para perguntas de opinião, use:

O-R-E

Opinion

Reason

Example.

Se precisar falar mais:

O-R-E-C

Opinion

Reason

Example

Contrast/Conclusion.

Para comparação:

S-D-D-P

Similarity

Difference

Difference

Preference.

Exemplo mental:

Both = study

difference = place

difference = interaction

preference = library.

Isso evita:

ficar sem direção durante a resposta.

Se travar:

não fique em silêncio tentando encontrar a palavra perfeita.

Use:

simpler vocabulary

ou:

circumlocution.

Prática

1. Expanda a resposta:

Do you prefer reading printed books or e-books?

Resposta inicial:

Printed books.

Transforme em:

opinion + reason + example.

2. Expanda:

Is public transport important?

Use:

opinion + two reasons.

3. Expanda:

Do you like studying alone?

Inclua:

one advantage + one limitation.

4. Complete oralmente:

In my opinion, schools should ______ because ______.

5. Complete:

I prefer ______ to ______ because ______.

6. Complete com contraste:

Online courses are flexible, whereas ______.

7. Complete com both:

Both ______ and ______ can ______.

8. Complete:

One advantage of working from home is ______. However, ______.

9. Torne a frase menos absoluta:

Social media is bad for everyone.

10. Torne menos absoluta:

Classroom learning is always better than online learning.

11. Compare:

bicycle × car

Use:

cheaper than

however.

12. Compare:

city × countryside

Use:

whereas.

13. Compare:

studying alone × studying in groups

Inclua:

both

while.

14. Dê opinião:

Should students have homework every day?

Fale por aproximadamente:

40–60 seconds.

15. Dê opinião:

Is technology making people’s lives better?

Inclua:

advantage

disadvantage

conclusion.

16. Responda:

What is more important when choosing a job: salary or job satisfaction?

Compare os dois fatores.

17. Responda:

Would you rather work from home or in an office?

Use:

would rather

because

however.

18. Responda:

Which is better for learning a language: reading or speaking?

Evite escolher imediatamente sem:

comparar ambos.

19. Concorde parcialmente:

“Online courses are better than classroom courses.”

Use:

I agree to some extent…

20. Discorde educadamente:

“People don’t need libraries anymore because everything is online.”

Use:

I don’t completely agree…

21. Convide opinião:

Você disse:

I think the museum is the best option because it is educational and inexpensive.

Adicione:

uma pergunta ao parceiro.

22. Reaja:

Partner:

I think the park is better because it’s free.

Responda concordando e acrescentando:

one additional reason.

23. Reaja discordando:

Partner:

We should choose the most expensive option because it must be the best.

Responda de forma educada.

24. Circumlocution

Você esqueceu a palavra:

umbrella.

Explique em inglês sem usar:

umbrella.

25. Circumlocution

Você esqueceu:

librarian.

Explique.

26. Self-correction

Corrija naturalmente:

I moved here in 2023 — no, 2022.

Use:

sorry, I mean…

27. Estruture uma comparação de imagens fictícias:

Picture A:

three students working around a table.

Picture B:

one student working on a laptop at home.

Fale incluindo:

similarity

two differences

speculation

preference.

28. Resposta longa

Pergunta:

What are the advantages and disadvantages of living in a large city?

Fale usando:

advantage 1

advantage 2

disadvantage

personal conclusion.

29. Decision task

Você e outro candidato precisam escolher a melhor atividade para uma turma:

outdoor sports

museum visit

film session

science workshop.

Prepare:

  • one advantage of each;
  • your preferred option;
  • one question to partner;
  • one phrase for agreeing;
  • one phrase for disagreeing.

30. Speaking task

Fale por 60–90 segundos:

Some people prefer studying online, while others prefer traditional classrooms. Compare the two and say which one you think is more suitable for adult learners.

Inclua:

  • both;
  • whereas;
  • um comparative;
  • uma vantagem de cada;
  • uma limitação;
  • uma preferência;
  • uma justificativa;
  • um exemplo;
  • conclusão.

Gabarito comentado

1.

Modelo:

I prefer printed books because I find them easier to read for long periods. I also like making notes directly on the page. For example, when I study, I can underline important information without using another device.

Estrutura:

preference + reason + example.

2.

Modelo:

Yes, I think public transport is very important. One reason is that it allows people who do not own cars to travel to work or school. It can also reduce the number of private vehicles on the road, which may help reduce traffic.

3.

Modelo:

Yes, I usually prefer studying alone because I can work at my own pace and concentrate on the topics I find difficult. However, studying alone can be less useful when I need to discuss ideas or get another person’s opinion.

4.

Resposta possível:

In my opinion, schools should provide more practical activities because students need opportunities to apply what they learn.

Várias respostas são possíveis se:

opinião + razão

estiverem claras.

5.

I prefer studying in a library to studying in a café because libraries are usually quieter.

Observe:

prefer X to Y.

6.

Online courses are flexible, whereas classroom courses provide more direct face-to-face interaction.

7.

Both printed books and e-books can be useful for studying.

8.

One advantage of working from home is that employees can save commuting time. However, some people may miss direct interaction with colleagues.

9.

Modelo:

Social media can have negative effects for some users, especially when it is used excessively.

Muito melhor que:

bad for everyone.

10.

Classroom learning may be more suitable for students who need regular face-to-face support, but online learning can work well for more independent learners.

11.

Modelo:

A bicycle is usually cheaper than a car and does not require fuel. However, a car is more practical for long journeys or when carrying several passengers.

12.

Cities usually provide easier access to services, whereas the countryside is often quieter and less crowded.

13.

Both studying alone and studying in groups can be useful. Studying alone allows you to work at your own pace, while group study gives you more opportunities to discuss ideas with other people.

14.

Modelo:

I don’t think students necessarily need homework every day. Homework can be useful because it gives learners an opportunity to review what they studied in class. However, too much homework may create stress and leave little time for other activities. I think the amount should depend on the subject and the students’ needs rather than being given every day automatically.

15.

Modelo:

I think technology has improved many parts of people’s lives because communication and access to information are much faster. For example, people can study, work and communicate from different locations. However, technology can also be distracting, and some people spend too much time online. Overall, I think technology is beneficial when it is used responsibly.

16.

Modelo:

Both salary and job satisfaction are important. A good salary provides financial security, whereas job satisfaction can affect motivation and well-being. Personally, I think job satisfaction is slightly more important if the salary is enough to meet a person’s needs, because spending many years in a job you dislike can be very stressful.

17.

I’d rather work from home because I would save commuting time and have more flexibility. However, I think going to an office sometimes is useful for meeting colleagues and discussing projects face to face.

18.

Modelo:

Both reading and speaking are important for learning a language. Reading helps learners develop vocabulary and understand sentence structures, while speaking develops the ability to communicate quickly. If I had to choose one, I would probably choose speaking because my main goal would be communication. However, I would still use reading to support vocabulary development.

19.

I agree to some extent because online courses are more flexible. However, classroom courses may be better for students who need direct interaction and regular support.

20.

I don’t completely agree. A lot of information is available online, but libraries still provide study spaces, computers and support from staff. They can also be important for people who do not have reliable internet access at home.

21.

What do you think?

Ou:

Do you agree?

Ou:

Would you choose the museum too?

22.

Modelo:

I agree. The park is free, and it would also give students an opportunity to spend time outdoors.

23.

Modelo:

I’m not sure I agree. A higher price doesn’t necessarily mean the activity is better. I think we should consider what students would learn and whether everyone could participate.

Isso demonstra:

polite disagreement + justification.

24.

It’s something you carry when it’s raining. You hold it above your head to keep yourself dry.

Isso é:

effective circumlocution.

25.

It’s a person who works in a library and helps people find books or information.

26.

I moved here in 2023 — sorry, I mean 2022.

Correção:

curta e natural.

27.

Modelo:

Both pictures show students studying. In the first picture, three students are working together around a table, whereas the second picture shows one person studying alone at home. The first situation looks more social and may involve a group project. The second seems quieter and more independent. I think the student at home may find it easier to concentrate, although the group can exchange ideas. Personally, I would prefer studying alone when I need to focus.

28.

Modelo:

Living in a large city has several advantages. First, people usually have easier access to jobs, universities, hospitals and entertainment. Public transport may also be more available. However, large cities can be expensive, crowded and noisy, and commuting may take a long time. Personally, I think city life is useful for people who value opportunities and services, but I would prefer a quieter area if the essential services were still accessible.

29.

Possível planejamento:

Outdoor sports
+ exercise/social
- weather dependent

Museum
+ educational
- may be less interactive

Film
+ relaxing/easy organization
- limited participation

Science workshop
+ educational + interactive
- possibly higher cost

Preference:
science workshop.

Question:
What do you think about the science workshop?

Agree:
That’s a good point.

Disagree:
I see your point, but I think…

O objetivo é preparar:

language for interaction,

não escrever uma redação antes de falar.

30.

Modelo:

Both online learning and traditional classroom learning can be useful for adult students, but they offer different advantages. Online courses are usually more flexible because learners can study from different locations and often organize classes around work or family responsibilities. Traditional classrooms, whereas, provide more direct interaction with teachers and classmates. A better formulation is: Traditional classrooms, on the other hand, provide more direct interaction with teachers and classmates.

For example, an adult who works full-time may find it much easier to attend an online course in the evening. However, online learning requires good organization, and some students may find it harder to stay motivated. Classroom courses can provide more structure and immediate support.

In my opinion, online learning is more suitable for many adult learners because flexibility is especially important when people have work and family commitments. However, the best choice depends on the learner’s needs and study habits.

Observe a correção:

whereas precisa conectar diretamente duas estruturas contrastantes.

Forma correta:

Online courses are usually more flexible, whereas traditional classrooms provide more direct interaction.

Tarefa de consolidação

Pratique diariamente cinco respostas de aproximadamente:

45–60 seconds.

Use temas como:

technology

education

health

transport

work

environment

travel

social media

reading

exercise.

Para cada pergunta, use:

Opinion

Reason

Example

Contrast

Conclusion.

Depois pratique comparações usando:

Both…

The first…, while the second…

X is more… than Y

However…

Personally, I would prefer…

Grave respostas e verifique:

□ Did I answer the question directly?

□ Did I give at least one reason?

□ Did I provide an example?

□ Did I compare both options?

□ Did I use connectors naturally?

□ Did I speak in complete ideas?

□ Did I avoid excessive pauses?

□ Did I correct myself naturally when necessary?

□ Was my pronunciation understandable?

□ Did I finish with a clear point?

Treine também circumlocution. Escolha objetos e profissões e explique-os sem dizer o nome:

a pharmacy

a mechanic

a passport

a printer

a laboratory

a receptionist

a suitcase

a thermometer

a scholarship

a deadline.

Pratique interação com estas expressões:

What do you think?

Do you agree?

That’s a good point.

I agree to some extent.

I see your point, but…

I’m not completely sure about that.

Maybe we could…

Why don’t we…?

So, shall we choose…?

Por fim, pratique esta estrutura mental antes de começar qualquer resposta:

ANSWER → WHY → EXAMPLE → OTHER SIDE → FINAL POINT

Não procure construir a frase perfeita antes de começar. Em Speaking B1, é mais importante demonstrar que você consegue manter a comunicação, justificar suas ideias e organizar a fala de maneira compreensível do que produzir uma resposta linguisticamente sofisticada, mas hesitante e difícil de sustentar.

Aula 97 — Reconhecimento de sinônimos e paráfrases

Objetivos

Ao final desta aula, você deverá ser capaz de:

  • reconhecer sinônimos frequentes em textos de nível B1;
  • identificar paráfrases entre texto e questão;
  • compreender que palavras diferentes podem expressar ideias semelhantes;
  • distinguir sinônimo exato de aproximação contextual;
  • reconhecer reformulações gramaticais sem alteração significativa de sentido;
  • identificar mudanças entre voz ativa e passiva;
  • reconhecer equivalência entre verbos, substantivos e adjetivos da mesma família;
  • perceber quando uma expressão é mais forte ou mais fraca que outra;
  • evitar alternativas incorretas que parecem sinônimas, mas alteram o sentido;
  • identificar equivalências entre phrasal verbs e verbos simples;
  • reconhecer paráfrases de causa, consequência, contraste e finalidade;
  • usar sinônimos e paráfrases em Reading, Listening, Writing e Speaking;
  • desenvolver estratégias para provas em que a resposta correta raramente repete exatamente as palavras do texto.

Desenvolvimento

Em exames de proficiência, uma habilidade central é reconhecer que:

the question may not use the same words as the text.

O texto pode dizer:

The course is free.

A questão pode dizer:

Students do not have to pay.

As palavras são diferentes, mas:

the meaning is equivalent.

Isso é:

paraphrase.

Synonym

Synonym significa:

sinônimo.

Duas palavras são sinônimas quando possuem:

meaning that is the same or very similar.

Exemplos:

begin = start

large = big

purchase = buy

difficult = hard

approximately = about.

Mas atenção:

sinônimos raramente são completamente intercambiáveis em todos os contextos.

Context matters

Compare:

a big mistake

é natural.

a large mistake

é possível em alguns contextos, mas menos comum.

Então:

similar meaning does not always mean identical usage.

Paraphrase

Uma paraphrase reformula uma ideia usando:

different words

ou:

different grammatical structure.

Exemplo:

The city reduced bus fares.

Paráfrase:

Bus tickets became cheaper.

Não temos sinônimos palavra por palavra.

Temos:

equivalent overall meaning.

Por que isso é importante em provas?

Se a questão repetisse o texto exatamente:

seria muito fácil localizar a resposta.

Por isso, provas usam:

synonyms

rewording

grammatical transformation

generalization

specific-to-general shifts.

Exemplo típico

Texto:

The company postponed the meeting until Friday.

Pergunta:

When was the meeting put off until?

Você precisa reconhecer:

postpone = put off.

Outra

Texto:

More than 500 people attended the event.

Pergunta:

Over how many people were present?

more than = over

attended = were present at.

Sinônimos frequentes — verbos

begin = start

end = finish

buy = purchase

help = assist/support

need = require

choose = select

improve = get better

decrease = reduce/fall

increase = rise/grow

continue = carry on

discover = find out

postpone = put off

cancel = call off

return = come back

investigate = examine

show = demonstrate/indicate, dependendo do contexto.

Begin / start

The course begins in June.

The course starts in June.

Equivalentes.

End / finish

The meeting ended at five.

The meeting finished at five.

Muito próximos.

Need / require

The job requires experience.

You need experience for the job.

Mesma ideia geral.

Help / assist

Staff can help visitors.

Staff can assist visitors.

Assist é:

mais formal.

Choose / select

Students can choose three subjects.

Students can select three subjects.

Muito próximos.

Increase / rise / grow

Prices increased.

Prices rose.

Equivalência forte.

Mas:

grow

é mais natural em certos contextos:

population grew.

Decrease / fall / drop / reduce

Compare:

Prices fell.

Prices decreased.

Mas:

The company reduced prices.

Aqui:

reduce

é transitivo:

someone reduced something.

Já:

prices fell

é intransitivo.

Reformulação gramatical

The company reduced prices.

Paráfrase:

Prices fell because of the company’s decision.

A estrutura muda:

active → intransitive description.

Phrasal verbs e equivalentes

Muito frequentes:

put off = postpone

call off = cancel

find out = discover/learn

carry on = continue

give up = stop trying

look for = search for

pick up = collect, dependendo do contexto

set up = establish/create

turn down = refuse/reject

look after = take care of

run out of = have no more of.

Exemplo

The event was called off.

=>

The event was canceled.

Outro

She turned down the job offer.

=>

She refused the job offer.

Cuidado com múltiplos sentidos

pick up

pode significar:

  • collect someone;
  • lift something;
  • learn informally;
  • improve.

Então:

context determines the equivalent.

Sinônimos frequentes — substantivos

job = position, em alguns contextos

problem = issue

result = finding/outcome

chance = opportunity

help = support/assistance

goal = aim/objective

choice = option

cost = expense

benefit = advantage

drawback = disadvantage

change = modification/shift, dependendo do contexto.

Result x finding

Em ciência:

findings

frequentemente:

research results.

Aim / goal / objective

The aim of the program is to reduce waste.

The goal of the program is to reduce waste.

Muito semelhantes.

Opportunity

The course gives students an opportunity to practice.

=>

The course gives students a chance to practice.

Sinônimos frequentes — adjetivos

difficult = hard

easy = simple, em alguns contextos

important = significant

cheap = inexpensive

expensive = costly

quick = fast

safe = secure, dependendo do contexto

common = widespread/frequent, conforme contexto

useful = helpful

possible = potential, em algumas estruturas

accurate = precise/correct, conforme contexto.

Cheap x inexpensive

The device is inexpensive.

=>

The device is cheap.

Mas:

cheap

às vezes pode sugerir:

low quality

em certos contextos.

inexpensive

é mais neutro.

Important x significant

significant

pode significar:

important

ou, em estatística:

statistically significant.

Contexto importa.

Common x frequent

common problem

frequent problem

podem ser próximos.

Mas:

frequent

enfatiza:

happening often.

common

pode enfatizar:

widespread/not unusual.

Sinônimos frequentes — advérbios e quantificadores

approximately = about = around = roughly

almost = nearly

mainly = primarily

usually = generally

often = frequently

immediately = straight away / at once

currently = at present / now

eventually = finally, after some time.

Approximately

approximately 200 people.

=>

about 200 people.

Nearly

Nearly half the participants…

=>

Almost half…

Mainly

The course is mainly designed for adults.

=>

The course is primarily intended for adults.

Free

Paráfrase:

free of charge

costs nothing

no payment is required.

Expensive

Paráfrases:

costs a lot

high-cost

not cheap.

Mas:

not cheap

pode ser menos forte que:

expensive.

Required

required

=>

necessary

compulsory, dependendo do contexto

must.

Exemplo:

Attendance is compulsory.

=>

Students must attend.

Optional

optional

=>

not compulsory

not required

students can choose whether to do it.

Allowed

allowed

=>

permitted

can.

Prohibited

prohibited

=>

not allowed

must not.

Modal paraphrases

must = have to, em muitos contextos

should = it is advisable to

may/might = it is possible that

can = be able to / be possible, dependendo do uso

mustn’t = not allowed to.

Exemplo

Students must submit the form by Friday.

=>

Students have to submit the form by Friday.

Should

You should arrive early.

=>

It is advisable to arrive early.

May

Prices may increase.

=>

It is possible that prices will increase.

Cuidado com mustn’t

You mustn’t enter.

Não é:

You don’t have to enter.

mustn’t

=>

prohibited.

don’t have to

=>

optional/not necessary.

Active x passive

Texto:

The city opened a new library.

Paráfrase:

A new library was opened by the city.

Mesmo evento.

Active without agent

Researchers developed a new sensor.

=>

A new sensor was developed.

O agente pode ser omitido se:

not essential.

Passive to active

The road was closed because of flooding.

=>

Officials closed the road because of flooding.

Só é equivalente se:

officials

for realmente conhecido ou permitido pelo contexto.

Não invente:

agent.

Noun x verb

Muito usado em paráfrases.

prices increased

=>

there was an increase in prices.

Another

the company expanded

=>

the company’s expansion.

Decide / decision

The city decided to continue the program.

=>

The city made a decision to continue the program.

Improve / improvement

The system improved significantly.

=>

There was a significant improvement in the system.

Reduce / reduction

The program reduced waste.

=>

The program led to a reduction in waste.

Word families

Reconheça:

employ → employment → employee → employer

decide → decision

improve → improvement

develop → development

educate → education → educational

succeed → success → successful

analyze → analysis

conclude → conclusion.

Adjective x noun

The system is efficient.

=>

The system operates efficiently.

Ou:

The system has high efficiency.

A última é mais formal e nem sempre a mais natural.

Cause paraphrases

because

because of

due to

as a result of

podem expressar relações semelhantes com estruturas diferentes.

Because

The match was canceled because it was raining.

Because of

The match was canceled because of the rain.

Due to

The match was canceled due to heavy rain.

Mesma relação:

rain → cancellation.

Result paraphrases

so

therefore

as a result

consequently.

Exemplo:

It was raining, so the match was canceled.

=>

It was raining. Therefore, the match was canceled.

Cause verbs

cause

lead to

result in.

Heavy rain caused flooding.

=>

Heavy rain led to flooding.

Reverse relation

Flooding resulted from heavy rain.

Agora:

result from

introduz:

cause.

Compare:

X results in Y.

=>

X causes Y.

Y results from X.

=>

Y is caused by X.

Contrast paraphrases

but

however

although

despite.

Example

Although the course was expensive, many students enrolled.

=>

The course was expensive. However, many students enrolled.

=>

Despite the high price, many students enrolled.

A estrutura muda, mas:

core contrast remains.

Although x despite

although + clause

despite + noun/gerund.

Exemplo:

Although she was tired, she continued.

=>

Despite being tired, she continued.

Addition

also

in addition

furthermore

moreover.

Exemplo:

The program is free. It also provides materials.

=>

The program is free. In addition, materials are provided.

Purpose

to

in order to

so that.

Exemplo:

The university extended hours to help students study.

=>

The university extended hours in order to help students study.

Ou:

The university extended hours so that students could study later.

Condition

unless

pode ser parafraseado com:

if…not.

You cannot enter unless you have a ticket.

=>

You cannot enter if you do not have a ticket.

Comparative paraphrases

X is cheaper than Y.

=>

Y is more expensive than X.

Another

City A is larger than City B.

=>

City B is smaller than City A.

Equality

X is as expensive as Y.

=>

X and Y cost the same.

Twice

City A has twice as many residents as City B.

=>

City A’s population is double City B’s.

Quantifier paraphrases

more than = over

fewer than = under/less than, dependendo do substantivo e registro

approximately = around/about

the majority = most

a small number = few

half = 50%.

More than

More than 1,000 people attended.

=>

Over 1,000 people attended.

Most

Most participants agreed.

=>

The majority of participants agreed.

Não:

all participants.

Some

some

não é igual a:

most.

Esse é um dos principais distratores.

Few

Few students failed.

=>

Only a small number of students failed.

Hardly any

Hardly any students failed.

=>

Almost no students failed.

Time paraphrases

before

earlier than

prior to, mais formal.

After

later than

following.

Exemplo:

After the meeting…

=>

Following the meeting…

Currently

currently

=>

at present

now.

Previously

previously

=>

before

in the past.

No longer

no longer

=>

not anymore.

The service is no longer free.

=>

The service isn’t free anymore.

Still

still

pode ser parafraseado como:

continues to.

She still works there.

=>

She continues to work there.

Yet

hasn’t happened yet

=>

has not happened so far.

Frequency

rarely

=>

not often.

frequently

=>

often.

occasionally

=>

sometimes.

Synonym traps

Nem toda palavra parecida:

preserves meaning.

Big x important

a big decision

pode significar:

important decision.

Mas:

a big building

não significa:

important building.

Old

Pode significar:

not new

ou:

aged.

Contexto:

an old computer

versus:

an old man.

Issue

Pode significar:

problem

ou:

topic/matter.

environmental issues

pode ser:

environmental problems/topics.

Current

current situation

=>

present situation.

Não confundir com:

corrente elétrica.

Eventually

eventually

=>

finally, after some time.

Não:

possibly

nem:

occasionally.

Actually

actually

=>

in fact.

Não:

currently.

Sensible

sensible

=>

reasonable/practical.

Não:

sensitive.

Comprehensive synonym recognition

O objetivo não é memorizar:

listas infinitas.

É reconhecer:

relations in context.

Exemplo de Reading

Texto:

The new system has reduced waiting times.

Questão:

What has happened since the new system was introduced?

Alternativa correta:

People now spend less time waiting.

Não há:

reduced

nem:

waiting times

da mesma maneira.

Mas a ideia é equivalente.

Outro

Texto:

The course is aimed at people with little previous experience.

Alternativa:

The course is designed mainly for beginners.

Equivalências:

aimed at = designed for

little previous experience = beginners.

Outro

Texto:

Residents expressed concern about the project’s cost.

Alternativa:

Local people were worried about how expensive the project might be.

Equivalências:

residents = local people

expressed concern = were worried

cost = how expensive.

Paráfrase envolvendo inferência limitada

Texto:

The company has not yet decided whether to continue the program.

Alternativa correta:

The program’s future is still uncertain.

Essa não é palavra por palavra.

Mas é:

logical paraphrase.

Exagero disfarçado

Texto:

The program may help reduce traffic.

Alternativa:

The program will solve the traffic problem.

Não é paráfrase.

Mudanças:

may → will

reduce → solve.

A alternativa ficou:

much stronger.

Another trap

Texto:

Some residents opposed the plan.

Alternativa:

Residents opposed the plan.

Essa frase pode sugerir:

grupo geral.

Perde:

some.

All/most/some

Sempre preserve:

quantifier strength.

Paraphrase hierarchy

Você pode encontrar diferentes níveis.

Nível 1 — lexical

begin = start.

Nível 2 — phrase

free of charge = no payment required.

Nível 3 — grammar

Researchers conducted the study.

=>

The study was conducted by researchers.

Nível 4 — conceptual

The hotel is within walking distance.

=>

The hotel is close enough to reach on foot.

Common conceptual paraphrases

available 24 hours a day

=>

open all day and all night.

within walking distance

=>

close enough to walk.

work remotely

=>

work from home/another location.

compulsory

=>

required.

optional

=>

not required.

affordable

=>

not too expensive.

overcrowded

=>

containing too many people.

Definitions as paraphrases

A vegetarian is someone who does not eat meat.

Se a questão diz:

people who avoid meat

pode se referir:

vegetarians.

Reading exam technique

Quando ler uma questão:

não procure imediatamente as mesmas palavras.

Pergunte:

What other ways could this idea be expressed?

Step 1 — identify key meaning

Pergunta:

Why was the meeting put off?

Meaning:

reason + postponed meeting.

Procure:

meeting postponed/delayed

cause/reason.

Step 2 — think of synonyms

put off

→ postpone/delay.

Step 3 — locate equivalent idea

Texto:

The meeting was postponed because several speakers could not attend.

Resposta:

because some speakers were unavailable.

Listening and paraphrases

No Listening, isso é ainda mais importante.

Áudio:

I’m not particularly keen on driving.

Questão:

The speaker does not really enjoy driving.

Paráfrase.

Another

Áudio:

The hotel wasn’t nearly as expensive as I’d expected.

Alternativa:

The speaker found the hotel cheaper than expected.

Negative paraphrases

not very expensive

≈ relatively cheap.

Mas cuidado:

not impossible

não significa:

easy.

Pode apenas significar:

possible.

Double meaning strength

not bad

pode significar:

fairly good

em linguagem coloquial.

Mas depende:

tone/context.

Writing and paraphrase

Em Writing, paráfrase ajuda a evitar:

repetition.

Exemplo:

Primeira frase:

Online learning offers flexibility.

Depois:

This type of education allows students to organize their study around other responsibilities.

Temos:

online learning

=>

this type of education.

Speaking

Se esquecer uma palavra:

paraphrase.

Você não sabe:

crowded.

Pode dizer:

There were too many people in the place.

Isso mantém:

communication.

Circumlocution

a place where…

a person who…

something used for…

something that means…

Essas estruturas são:

practical paraphrasing tools.

Text 1

Community Sports Program

The city has launched a free weekend sports program for teenagers. Activities include football, swimming and athletics, and no previous experience is required. Officials say the project was created to encourage young people to become more physically active.

During the first month, more than 800 teenagers took part. Because demand was higher than expected, additional sessions will be introduced next month.

Possible paraphrases

launched → started

free → no payment required

no previous experience required → beginners can participate

encourage physical activity → help young people become more active

more than 800 → over 800

demand higher than expected → more people wanted to participate than organizers had predicted

additional sessions → more sessions.

Text 2

Workplace Training

Employees at a technology company can now complete professional training online. Previously, workers had to travel to the company’s main office for most courses.

The new system gives staff greater flexibility and reduces travel costs. However, some employees say they still prefer face-to-face training because it provides more opportunities for direct discussion.

Possible paraphrases

complete training online → take courses remotely

previously → in the past

had to → were required to

greater flexibility → more freedom in when/where training is completed

reduces travel costs → makes travel less expensive/reduces money spent on travel

face-to-face → in person

direct discussion → immediate personal interaction.

Text 3

Urban Air Study

Researchers monitored air quality in twelve neighborhoods for six months. They found that pollution levels were generally higher near roads with heavy traffic.

However, the scientists warned that traffic was not the only factor affecting air quality. Weather conditions and nearby industrial activity may also have influenced the results.

Possible paraphrases

monitored → observed/measured over time

generally higher → usually greater

heavy traffic → large amount of traffic

not the only factor → other causes may also be involved

influenced → affected.

Vocabulário-chave

synonym — sinônimo

paraphrase — paráfrase

rephrase — reformular

equivalent — equivalente

similar meaning — significado semelhante

context — contexto

word family — família de palavras

reformulation — reformulação

active voice — voz ativa

passive voice — voz passiva

phrasal verb — verbo frasal

approximate meaning — significado aproximado

overstatement — exagero

understatement — formulação mais fraca

distractor — alternativa distratora

preserve meaning — preservar o sentido

Estratégia de prova

Ao comparar texto e alternativa, verifique quatro elementos:

Meaning

Quantity

Certainty

Time

Exemplo:

Texto:

Some students may need more support.

Alternativa:

All students definitely need more support.

Meaning geral parece próximo, mas:

some → all

may → definitely.

Logo:

não é paráfrase.

Use o teste:

Could I replace one sentence with the other without changing the essential meaning?

Se a resposta for:

yes,

provavelmente existe equivalência.

Se:

certainty, quantity, time or cause

mudarem:

provavelmente é distractor.

Prática

1. Escolha o sinônimo mais próximo:

begin

  1. end
  2. start
  3. stop
  4. remove

2.

approximately

  1. exactly
  2. about
  3. never
  4. only

3.

purchase

  1. sell
  2. buy
  3. borrow
  4. lose

4.

postpone

  1. put off
  2. turn on
  3. give back
  4. find out

5.

cancel

  1. carry on
  2. call off
  3. set up
  4. sign up

6.

continue

  1. give up
  2. turn down
  3. carry on
  4. take off

7.

discover information

  1. find out
  2. put away
  3. take on
  4. turn off

8. Escolha a paráfrase correta:

The course is free of charge.

  1. The course is expensive.
  2. Students do not have to pay.
  3. Students must pay later.
  4. Payment is difficult.

9.

Attendance is compulsory.

  1. Students may attend if they want.
  2. Students must attend.
  3. Students cannot attend.
  4. Attendance is unusual.

10.

Previous experience is not required.

  1. Only experts can participate.
  2. Beginners may participate.
  3. Experience is compulsory.
  4. No one can participate.

11.

The meeting was put off until Friday.

  1. The meeting was canceled permanently.
  2. The meeting was postponed until Friday.
  3. The meeting began on Friday.
  4. The meeting ended early.

12.

More than 2,000 people attended.

  1. Exactly 2,000 attended.
  2. Under 2,000 attended.
  3. Over 2,000 attended.
  4. Almost nobody attended.

13.

The service is no longer free.

  1. The service has never been free.
  2. The service isn’t free anymore.
  3. The service will always be free.
  4. The service is free again.

14.

Most participants agreed.

  1. Every participant agreed.
  2. The majority agreed.
  3. Very few agreed.
  4. Nobody agreed.

15.

The city reduced bus fares.

Qual é a melhor paráfrase?

  1. Bus tickets became cheaper.
  2. Bus tickets became more expensive.
  3. The city stopped buses.
  4. The city increased traffic.

16.

Prices rose rapidly.

Reescreva usando:

increase.

17.

The company expanded internationally.

Reescreva usando:

expansion.

18.

The researchers conducted the study.

Transforme para Passive Voice.

19.

The road was closed because of flooding.

Reescreva usando:

due to.

20.

Although the device was cheap, it was unreliable.

Reescreva usando:

however.

21.

Despite the bad weather, the event continued.

Reescreva usando:

although.

22.

You cannot enter unless you have a ticket.

Reescreva usando:

if.

23.

City A is more expensive than City B.

Reescreva mantendo o sentido e começando por:

City B…

24. Identifique se é TRUE PARAPHRASE ou DISTORTION:

Texto:

The program may reduce traffic.

Alternativa:

The program could help lower traffic levels.

25.

Texto:

The program may reduce traffic.

Alternativa:

The program will eliminate traffic.

26.

Texto:

Some residents opposed the plan.

Alternativa:

A number of residents were against the plan.

27.

Texto:

Some residents opposed the plan.

Alternativa:

All residents rejected the plan.

28. Texto e questão:

Texto:

The course is aimed at adults who have little previous experience with computers.

Questão:

Who is the course mainly designed for?

Qual resposta é melhor?

  1. Advanced computer engineers.
  2. Adult beginners.
  3. Children only.
  4. Professional programmers.

29. Leia:

The hotel is within walking distance of the station and offers rooms at affordable prices.

Qual alternativa parafraseia corretamente?

  1. The hotel is far from the station and expensive.
  2. Guests can walk from the station, and the rooms are reasonably priced.
  3. The hotel provides free train tickets.
  4. The station is inside the hotel.

30. Produção

Parafraseie o texto abaixo em 60–80 palavras sem alterar o sentido:

A city has introduced a six-month pilot program offering free bus travel on Sundays. Officials hope the project will encourage more people to use public transport and reduce traffic in the city center. Passenger numbers were higher than expected during the first month, but the city has not yet decided whether the program will become permanent. More data will be collected before a final decision is made.

Gabarito comentado

1. B — start

begin = start.

2. B — about

approximately = about/around.

3. B — buy

purchase

é uma forma mais formal de:

buy.

4. A — put off

postpone = put off.

5. B — call off

call off = cancel.

6. C — carry on

carry on = continue.

7. A — find out

find out

pode significar:

discover/learn information.

8. B

free of charge

=>

no payment required.

9. B

compulsory

=>

required.

Logo:

students must attend.

10. B

Se:

previous experience is not required,

então:

beginners may participate.

Isso é uma paráfrase conceitual.

11. B

put off = postpone.

12. C

more than = over.

Não:

exactly.

13. B

no longer

=>

not anymore.

14. B

most

=>

the majority.

Não:

all.

15. A

reduced fares

significa:

ticket prices became lower/cheaper.

16.

There was a rapid increase in prices.

Mudança:

verb → noun.

17.

The company underwent international expansion.

Ou, de forma mais natural:

The company’s international expansion increased.

Mas isso altera levemente a informação se não houver contexto.

Melhor:

The company experienced international expansion.

Ainda assim, a forma mais natural continua sendo:

The company expanded internationally.

O exercício mostra que:

nem toda transformação nominal produz uma frase tão natural quanto o original.

18.

The study was conducted by the researchers.

Se o agente não for necessário:

The study was conducted.

19.

The road was closed due to flooding.

20.

The device was cheap. However, it was unreliable.

21.

Although the weather was bad, the event continued.

22.

You cannot enter if you do not have a ticket.

23.

City B is less expensive than City A.

Ou:
