City B is cheaper than City A.

24. TRUE PARAPHRASE

may

e:

could

mantêm possibilidade.

reduce

e:

help lower

são semanticamente próximos no contexto.

25. DISTORTION

Mudanças:

may → will

reduce → eliminate.

A alternativa é muito mais forte.

26. TRUE PARAPHRASE

some residents

=>

a number of residents.

opposed

=>

were against.

27. DISTORTION

some

foi transformado em:

all.

Além disso:

opposed

e:

rejected

podem ser próximos, mas a alteração de quantidade já torna a alternativa incorreta.

28. B — Adult beginners

adults

little previous experience

=>

adult beginners.

29. B

within walking distance

=>

close enough to walk.

affordable

=>

reasonably priced/not too expensive.

30.

Modelo:

A city has started a six-month trial that allows passengers to use buses for free on Sundays. Authorities hope the initiative will increase public transport use and help lower traffic in the city center. More passengers than expected used the service during its first month. However, the project has not been made permanent, and officials will examine additional data before deciding whether it should continue.

Tarefa de consolidação

Crie um caderno de paráfrases dividido em categorias.

Verbos

start = begin

reduce = decrease

rise = increase

postpone = put off

cancel = call off

continue = carry on

refuse = turn down

discover = find out.

Substantivos

aim = goal

result = finding

benefit = advantage

drawback = disadvantage

chance = opportunity.

Adjetivos

inexpensive = cheap

significant = important

difficult = hard

useful = helpful

likely = probable.

Expressões

free of charge = no payment required

within walking distance = close enough to walk

compulsory = required

optional = not required

no longer = not anymore.

Depois pratique transformações:

verb → noun

prices increased → there was an increase in prices

active → passive

researchers collected data → data were collected

because → because of

because it rained → because of the rain

although → despite

although it was difficult → despite the difficulty

unless → if not

unless you register → if you do not register.

Crie ainda vinte pares:

uma paráfrase correta

e:

uma distorção.

Exemplo:

Source: Some people may benefit.

Correct: Certain people could benefit.

Distortion: Everyone will benefit.

Ao revisar, observe principalmente mudanças em:

quantity

some / most / all

certainty

may / will / definitely

time

used to / still / no longer

cause

associated with / caused

degree

reduce / eliminate

frequency

sometimes / often / always.

Finalize com a regra:

Do not match words; match meaning.

Em provas de proficiência, a alternativa correta frequentemente é aquela que expressa a mesma ideia com vocabulário ou estrutura diferentes, enquanto os distratores preservam algumas palavras do texto, mas alteram um detalhe importante do significado.

Aula 98 — Estratégias de prova B1

Objetivos

Ao final desta aula, você deverá ser capaz de:

  • compreender como organizar uma prova de proficiência em nível B1;
  • administrar o tempo entre Reading, Listening, Writing e Speaking;
  • identificar rapidamente o tipo de questão;
  • decidir quando usar skimming, scanning, inferência ou leitura detalhada;
  • reconhecer distratores frequentes;
  • lidar com sinônimos, paráfrases e reformulações;
  • evitar erros causados por palavras absolutas, quantificadores e mudanças de certeza;
  • responder questões de Reading com maior eficiência;
  • desenvolver estratégias específicas para Listening;
  • planejar textos de Writing antes de começar a escrever;
  • revisar respostas escritas de forma sistemática;
  • organizar respostas orais com clareza;
  • lidar com palavras desconhecidas sem interromper a compreensão;
  • decidir quando avançar e quando revisar uma questão;
  • reduzir erros por ansiedade, pressa ou excesso de interpretação;
  • aplicar uma estratégia integrada para uma prova B1 completa.

Desenvolvimento

Uma prova de proficiência não avalia apenas:

how much English you know.

Ela também avalia:

how effectively you use your English under test conditions.

Um candidato pode conhecer bastante inglês e ainda perder pontos porque:

  • administra mal o tempo;
  • lê tudo lentamente;
  • procura correspondência palavra por palavra;
  • ignora instruções;
  • não responde todas as partes de uma tarefa;
  • modifica o sentido de uma informação;
  • fica preso em uma única questão difícil.

Por isso, estratégia de prova é:

part of exam performance.

Primeira regra — leia o comando

Antes de responder qualquer questão, identifique:

What exactly do I have to do?

Palavras importantes:

choose

complete

match

summarize

compare

explain

give your opinion

identify

according to the text

infer

NOT

EXCEPT.

NOT e EXCEPT

Questão:

Which statement is NOT mentioned?

Se você lê rapidamente e ignora:

NOT

pode escolher exatamente o oposto do necessário.

Estratégia:

marque mentalmente ou visualmente palavras negativas.

Também:

FALSE

incorrect

except.

Conheça o formato antes de começar

Se possível, descubra antes da prova:

  • número de seções;
  • número de questões;
  • duração;
  • possibilidade de retornar a questões anteriores;
  • quantidade de reproduções no Listening;
  • limite de palavras do Writing;
  • duração do Speaking;
  • critérios de correção.

A estratégia depende:

do formato real do exame.

Gestão de tempo

Nunca pense apenas:

tenho 90 minutos.

Divida:

section by section.

Exemplo hipotético:

Reading — 35 minutes

Writing — 35 minutes

Review — 10 minutes.

Se a prova integra várias habilidades, ajuste conforme:

pontuação

dificuldade

número de itens.

Time budget

Defina:

maximum time per task.

Se uma questão objetiva está consumindo tempo excessivo:

mark it and move on

quando o formato permitir.

Custo de oportunidade

Cinco minutos em uma única questão podem impedir você de responder:

várias questões mais fáceis.

Portanto:

difficult question ≠ unlimited time.

Three-pass strategy

Uma abordagem possível para questões objetivas:

First pass

responda as fáceis.

Second pass

retorne às moderadas.

Third pass

use remaining time on difficult questions and review.

Isso evita:

começar a prova travado.

Accuracy x speed

Não tente responder:

as fast as possible.

Mas também não tente:

compreender cada frase perfeitamente.

Objetivo:

sufficient understanding for accurate answers.

Reading B1 — visão geral

No Reading, você precisa alternar entre:

skimming

scanning

careful reading

inference.

Usar a mesma velocidade para tudo é:

inefficient.

Skimming

Use para:

main idea

topic

overall structure

purpose.

Leia:

  • title;
  • first sentence;
  • key sentences;
  • beginning/end of paragraphs.

Pergunta típica:

What is the text mainly about?

Não procure:

cada detalhe.

Scanning

Use para:

dates

numbers

names

places

specific details.

Pergunta:

How many participants took part?

Procure:

numbers + participants/study/sample.

Detailed reading

Use quando:

  • duas alternativas parecem possíveis;
  • questão depende de contraste;
  • você precisa interpretar causa;
  • pronome/referrer é importante;
  • inferência exige combinar informações.

Não leia tudo três vezes

Estratégia ruim:

full slow reading → questions → full slow reading again.

Melhor:

preview → questions → targeted rereading.

Leia o título

O título ajuda a prever:

topic

vocabulary

genre.

Exemplo:

Scientists Test Low-Cost Water Sensor

Você pode esperar:

researchers

device

testing

results.

Identifique o gênero

É:

news article?

scientific communication?

email?

notice?

opinion text?

O gênero ajuda a prever:

structure and purpose.

Jornalístico

Procure:

event

source

numbers

consequences.

Divulgação científica

Procure:

research question

method

result

limitation.

Argumentativo

Procure:

position

reasons

examples

conclusion.

Texto informativo

Procure:

definitions

explanations

categories

sequence.

Main idea

Para:

What is the main idea?

Elimine alternativas:

too broad

too narrow

unsupported.

Too broad

Texto:

benefits of urban trees.

Alternativa:

Cities have environmental problems.

Verdade geral, mas:

broad demais.

Too narrow

Texto:

urban trees reduce heat, provide shade and support biodiversity.

Alternativa:

Trees provide shade.

Verdadeira, mas:

detail only.

Detail questions

Leia:

a frase antes

e:

a frase depois

da informação localizada.

Isso evita responder com:

palavra isolada sem contexto.

Reference questions

Pergunta:

What does “this” refer to?

Procedimento:

  1. olhe para trás;
  2. encontre candidatos;
  3. confira singular/plural;
  4. teste o sentido;
  5. verifique se a referência é a uma ideia inteira.

Inference questions

Pergunta:

What can be inferred?

Use:

text + logic.

Não use:

imagination.

Escolha a conclusão:

most strongly supported.

Vocabulary in context

Não traduza a palavra sozinha.

Observe:

  • word class;
  • sentence;
  • previous/next sentence;
  • contrast;
  • examples;
  • prefixes/suffixes.

Exemplo:

The room was crowded, so we could hardly find a seat.

crowded

≈:

full of people.

Unknown words

Pergunte:

Do I actually need this word?

Muitas vezes:

no.

Se a questão não depende dela:

continue.

Synonyms and paraphrases

Questão:

Why was the event postponed?

Texto:

The event was put off because of heavy rain.

Reconheça:

postponed = put off.

Não procure apenas:

postponed

no texto.

Match meaning, not words

Distratores frequentemente repetem:

vocabulary from the text

mas mudam:

meaning.

Example

Texto:

The study may help researchers understand the problem.

Distrator:

Researchers have completely solved the problem.

Algumas palavras relacionadas aparecem, mas:

meaning changed drastically.

Quantity traps

Observe:

some

many

most

all

few

almost all.

Texto:

most students.

Não marque:

all students.

Certainty traps

Observe:

may

might

could

likely

definitely

prove.

Texto:

may improve.

Alternativa:

will definitely improve.

Errada.

Degree traps

Texto:

reduce.

Alternativa:

eliminate.

Errada se o texto não sustenta:

complete removal.

Time traps

Texto:

used to work.

Alternativa:

still works.

Possivelmente errada.

Texto:

plans to open.

Alternativa:

has opened.

Errada.

Association x causation

Texto:

X was associated with Y.

Alternativa:

X caused Y.

Não trate como:

equivalent.

Positive x negative

Não perca:

not

never

rarely

hardly

no longer.

Uma palavra pode inverter:

entire answer.

Connectors

Palavras como:

however

therefore

although

because

in addition

indicam:

logical structure.

After however

Espere:

contrast / limitation.

After therefore

Espere:

result / conclusion.

After for example

Espere:

supporting example.

Prioritize contrast

Em questões difíceis, informações depois de:

however

but

although

podem ser especialmente importantes.

Reading elimination strategy

Se não sabe a resposta imediatamente:

Option A

contradicted?

Elimine.

Option B

unsupported?

Elimine.

Option C

too strong?

Elimine.

Option D

accurately paraphrases?

Possível correta.

Don’t choose because “it sounds right”

Uma resposta pode ser verdadeira no mundo real e:

not supported by the text.

Pergunta de Reading:

answer from the passage.

Listening B1 — visão geral

No Listening, o áudio continua:

mesmo se você ficar pensando.

Por isso:

recovery is essential.

Antes do áudio

Leia as perguntas.

Identifique:

what type of information is required.

Pergunta:

Why did she leave the job?

Procure:

reason.

Pergunta:

How many people attended?

Procure:

number.

Prediction

Título:

Interview with a Chef

Prediga:

food

career

restaurant

training

experiences.

Não significa:

inventar respostas.

Significa preparar:

vocabulary expectations.

First listening

Procure:

gist

speakers

main topic

general situation.

Second listening

Procure:

details

corrections

numbers

reasons

final decisions.

Distractors in Listening

Áudio:

We originally planned to leave on Thursday, but we changed it to Friday.

Questão:

When will they leave?

Resposta:

Friday.

Thursday é:

distractor mentioned in audio.

Plan x reality

Observe:

planned

wanted

hoped

intended

versus:

actually did.

Expected x actual

I expected it to be difficult, but it was quite easy.

Resposta sobre realidade:

easy.

Correction markers

sorry

actually

I mean

rather.

Exemplo:

There were 30 people — sorry, 13.

Resposta:

Numbers

Preste atenção a:

thirteen / thirty

fourteen / forty

fifteen / fifty.

Use:

context + stress.

Note-taking

Anote:

keywords

não:

full sentences.

Exemplo:

bus delay 40m / rain / avoid travel.

If you miss a word

Não faça:

mental rewind.

O áudio não volta.

Faça:

keep listening.

Talvez a informação seja:

repeated or paraphrased.

Negation

Preste atenção:

didn’t

doesn’t

can’t

won’t

hardly

rarely.

Opinion vs fact

Áudio:

I think the new system is easier.

Isso é:

speaker’s opinion.

Não:

objective fact.

Speaker attitude

Procure:

adjectives

emphasis

evaluative language.

I was delighted.

→ positive.

It was frustrating.

→ negative.

News Listening

Use:

Who? What? Where? When? Why? How?

Interview Listening

Use:

question type → expected answer type.

Why? → reason.

What do you think? → opinion.

When? → time.

What happened? → event.

Lecture Listening

Ouça:

signposting.

First…

Moving on…

For example…

However…

To sum up…

Isso transforma o áudio em:

sections.

Writing B1 — visão geral

O maior erro em Writing é começar:

sem planejamento.

Antes:

read prompt carefully.

Identify all task requirements

Prompt:

Compare online and classroom learning and say which you prefer.

Requisitos:

  1. compare;
  2. give preference.

Se fizer só:

comparison,

falta parte.

Planning time

Use alguns minutos para:

generate 2–3 main points.

Exemplo:

Online:

flexibility

less travel.

Classroom:

direct interaction

structure.

Opinion:

online for working adults.

Paragraph structure

Uma estrutura simples:

introduction

body 1

body 2

conclusion.

Para texto menor:

topic sentence

support

example

conclusion.

Writing and relevance

Não escreva tudo que sabe sobre:

topic.

Escreva o que:

answers the prompt.

Example

Prompt:

Advantages of public transport.

Não gaste metade do texto explicando:

history of cars.

Clear sentences

No B1:

clarity > unnecessary complexity.

Frase simples correta:

Public transport can reduce traffic.

Melhor que uma tentativa confusa com:

multiple advanced clauses.

Use controlled connectors

however

because

therefore

in addition

for example

while.

Não coloque:

moreover / furthermore / nevertheless

em todas as frases só para parecer avançado.

Opinion Writing

Estrutura:

position → reason → example → additional reason → conclusion.

Comparison Writing

Estrutura:

similarity → differences → evaluation/preference.

Summary Writing

Lembre:

main idea + key points

sem:

personal opinion.

Word limit

Respeite.

Se houver:

minimum

e:

maximum,

planeje ficar:

safely inside the range.

Writing review

Reserve tempo.

Não termine no último segundo se puder evitar.

First review — content

Did I answer every part?

Is the main idea clear?

Did I include support?

Second review — grammar

Cheque:

verb tense

subject-verb agreement

articles

plural

prepositions.

Third review — form

Cheque:

spelling

punctuation

capitalization.

High-value corrections

Se o tempo é curto, priorize:

errors that affect meaning.

Exemplo:

not

ausente pode alterar:

entire sentence.

Repeated vocabulary

Não entre em pânico.

Repetição moderada é melhor que:

incorrect synonym.

Se souber alternativas:

use them.

Speaking B1 — visão geral

No Speaking, evite respostas:

one word.

Expand with O-R-E

Opinion

Reason

Example.

Pergunta:

Do you like learning online?

Resposta:

Yes, I do. I think online learning is useful because it gives students more flexibility. For example, people who work during the day can study in the evening.

Comparison formula

Both…

while/whereas…

Personally…

Exemplo:

Both options are useful, but they are suitable for different situations. A train is usually faster, whereas a bus may be cheaper. Personally, I’d choose the train for a long journey.

If you need time

Use:

Let me think…

I’d say…

That’s an interesting question.

Depois:

answer.

If you don’t know a word

Use:

circumlocution.

It’s something you use to…

It’s a place where…

It’s a person who…

If you make a mistake

Sorry, I mean…

Corrija e siga.

If you don’t understand

Could you repeat the question, please?

Melhor que:

guessing the task.

Interaction

Em prova com parceiro:

respond to the partner.

Use:

I agree.

That’s a good point.

I see your point, but…

What do you think?

Fluency x perfection

Não interrompa constantemente sua própria fala para:

correct every small mistake.

Priorize:

communication.

Pronunciation

Objetivo:

intelligibility.

Priorize:

  • word stress;
  • important final sounds;
  • clear numbers;
  • negative forms;
  • key content words.

Stress important information

I prefer TRAINS because they’re FASTER.

Exam anxiety and cognitive load

Em uma prova, sua memória de trabalho está ocupada por:

  • idioma;
  • instruções;
  • tempo;
  • respostas;
  • pressão.

Por isso:

simplify decisions.

Use rotinas fixas.

Reading routine

question → locate → read context → answer.

Listening routine

preview → gist → detail → move on.

Writing routine

plan → write → check.

Speaking routine

answer → reason → example.

Quanto mais automatizadas essas rotinas:

menos energia mental será gasta decidindo o que fazer.

Quando uma questão está difícil

Pergunte:

What do I know for sure?

Elimine:

clearly wrong options.

Depois compare:

remaining choices.

Educated guess

Se não houver penalidade por erro:

não deixe questão em branco.

Mas siga:

regras específicas do exame.

Never change answers automatically

Não altere uma resposta apenas porque:

“talvez a primeira esteja errada”.

Mude quando encontrar:

concrete reason or evidence.

First instinct

A primeira impressão:

pode estar correta ou incorreta.

O critério deve ser:

evidence.

Checking

Ao revisar questão objetiva:

compare option with exact text evidence.

Time warnings

Crie checkpoints.

Exemplo:

at 20 min → should be around question X.

Isso ajuda a detectar:

atraso.

Don’t spend review time rewriting everything

Em Writing:

don’t restart a complete text

por causa de:

one imperfect sentence.

Corrija:

locally.

Instructions trump habits

Se um exame pede:

only one answer

não marque:

two.

Se pede:

maximum three words

não responda:

full sentence.

Answer format matters

Uma resposta semanticamente correta pode perder ponto se:

violates format.

Spelling in Listening/Reading answers

Se a prova exige escrever palavras:

spelling may matter.

Ouça e escreva:

names

places

numbers

com cuidado.

Singular/plural

Pergunta:

How many books?

Se resposta é:

3 books,

não escreva:

3 book

se o sistema avalia forma.

Transfer answers carefully

Em prova com folha de respostas:

reserve time.

Erro de alinhamento pode afetar:

many questions.

Check numbering

Especialmente após:

skipping a question.

Reading checklist

Antes de marcar:

□ I understood the question.

□ I found textual evidence.

□ I checked quantifiers.

□ I checked certainty.

□ I checked negative words.

□ I considered paraphrase.

Listening checklist

□ I read the questions first.

□ I listened for the final information.

□ I checked corrections.

□ I distinguished plan from reality.

□ I didn’t stop after missing one word.

Writing checklist

□ Answered every part.

□ Clear paragraph structure.

□ Reasons/examples included.

□ Connectors logical.

□ Tenses consistent.

□ Word limit respected.

□ Final review completed.

Speaking checklist

□ Direct answer.

□ Reason.

□ Example.

□ Comparison if asked.

□ Clear conclusion/preference.

□ Continued speaking after small errors.

Error log

Após simulados, não registre apenas:

score.

Registre:

why did I get it wrong?

Categorias:

paraphrase

grammar

inference

time management

misread question

listening distractor

careless mistake.

Example error log

Q12 — chose “all” although text said “most” → quantifier error.

Q18 — heard Monday and ignored correction to Tuesday → Listening correction distractor.

Writing — forgot second part of prompt → task completion.

Esse tipo de revisão produz:

targeted improvement.

Test simulation

Treine sob:

realistic conditions.

Use:

  • timer;
  • no dictionary when not allowed;
  • continuous Listening;
  • exact word limit;
  • complete Speaking response.

Estudar apenas sem pressão de tempo não treina:

exam execution.

Difficulty order

Em treino, você pode identificar:

personal weak sections.

Na prova, porém:

follow exam rules.

Nem sempre é possível escolher:

section order.

Avoid perfectionism

Uma questão difícil não precisa:

“feel completely solved”

antes de você avançar.

Em teste cronometrado:

sufficient evidence is enough.

Estratégia de prova

Use uma regra geral:

Understand the task before solving the language.

Depois:

Use the minimum amount of processing necessary to answer accurately.

Isso significa:

  • não traduzir tudo;
  • não reler tudo sem motivo;
  • não escrever mais do que a tarefa pede;
  • não falar dez frases quando três boas frases bastam;
  • não ficar preso em uma palavra desconhecida.

Outra regra:

Protect easy points.

Erros simples em:

instructions

numbers

negatives

word limits

answer transfer

podem custar pontos que não dependem de inglês avançado.

Prática

1. Uma questão pergunta:

What is the text mainly about?

Qual estratégia deve ser priorizada?

  1. scanning for one number
  2. skimming for overall meaning
  3. translating every word
  4. searching only the last sentence

2. Uma questão pergunta:

How many people participated?

Priorize:

  1. scanning
  2. writing
  3. pronunciation
  4. comparison

3. Texto:

Most participants preferred the new system.

Qual alternativa é inadequada?

  1. The majority preferred it.
  2. More than half probably preferred it.
  3. Every participant preferred it.
  4. The new system had majority support.

4. Texto:

The treatment may reduce symptoms.

Qual alternativa é equivalente?

  1. It definitely cures the condition.
  2. It might help reduce symptoms.
  3. It always works.
  4. It eliminates all symptoms.

5. Texto:

The meeting was put off.

Qual paráfrase?

  1. canceled forever
  2. postponed
  3. started
  4. shortened

6. Você encontra uma palavra desconhecida que não é necessária para responder à questão. O melhor é:

  1. spend five minutes trying to translate it
  2. stop the test
  3. continue and focus on relevant information
  4. assume the entire text is impossible

7. Listening:

I was going to travel on Monday, but I eventually left on Wednesday.

Quando a pessoa viajou?

  1. Monday
  2. Wednesday
  3. both
  4. impossible to know

8. Listening:

There were fifty people — sorry, fifteen.

Qual número deve ser considerado?

  1. 50
  2. 15
  3. 65
  4. both

9. Listening:

Você perde uma palavra importante. O áudio continua. Melhor reação:

  1. continue listening
  2. stop mentally and reconstruct it for 30 seconds
  3. abandon all remaining questions
  4. choose randomly immediately

10. Writing prompt:

Compare studying at home and in a library and say which you prefer.

Quantas tarefas principais existem?

  1. one: describe home
  2. two: compare + state preference
  3. one: describe library
  4. three: write a scientific report

11. Qual introdução responde melhor ao prompt anterior?

  1. Libraries have books.
  2. Studying at home and in a library can both be effective, but they provide different study environments.
  3. I studied yesterday.
  4. Education has existed for centuries.

12. Em Writing, a frase está correta?

Although the course was difficult, but I completed it.

Se não, corrija.

13. Em Writing, qual é melhor para B1?

  1. Uma frase extremamente complexa com vários erros.
  2. Uma frase clara e correta com vocabulário adequado.

Explique.

14. Speaking:

Pergunta:

Do you prefer buses or cars?

Resposta:

Buses.

Como pode ser melhorada?

15. Speaking:

Você esquece a palavra:

helmet.

O que deve fazer?

  1. stop speaking
  2. explain it using simpler English
  3. change language completely
  4. remain silent

16. Speaking:

Você não entende a pergunta.

Qual resposta é adequada?

  1. Could you repeat the question, please?
  2. I will answer something else.
  3. Never mind.
  4. No English.

17. Classifique o erro:

Texto: Some residents opposed the plan.
Resposta: All residents opposed it.

  1. synonym error
  2. quantifier distortion
  3. correct paraphrase
  4. spelling error

18. Classifique:

Texto: X was associated with Y.
Resposta: X caused Y.

  1. causation distortion
  2. correct summary
  3. pronunciation error
  4. time error

19. Classifique:

Texto: The service used to be free.
Resposta: The service is still free.

  1. time/status distortion
  2. correct paraphrase
  3. spelling problem
  4. comparison

20. Qual alternativa é melhor quando duas respostas parecem possíveis?

  1. choose the one with the most familiar vocabulary
  2. return to the text and look for evidence distinguishing them
  3. always choose the longest
  4. always choose option C

21. Reading

Texto:

The new system reduced waiting times, although some users reported technical problems.

Qual resumo é melhor?

  1. The system completely solved every problem.
  2. The system reduced waiting times but had some technical issues.
  3. The system failed.
  4. Users reported no problems.

22. Listening

Áudio:

The train was due at 8:10, but it’s running twenty minutes late.

Qual horário esperado?

23. Writing

Você tem 30 minutos e precisa escrever 170–200 palavras.

Proponha uma divisão de tempo entre:

  • planning;
  • writing;
  • reviewing.

24. Reading

Pergunta:

Which statement is NOT mentioned?

O que você deve fazer antes de avaliar as opções?

25. Listening

Por que ler as alternativas antes do áudio pode ajudar?

26. Speaking

Construa uma resposta de 40–60 segundos para:

Is it better to study alone or with other people?

Inclua:

  • opinion;
  • reason;
  • advantage of the other side;
  • conclusion.

27. Writing

Crie um mini-outline para:

Do the advantages of working from home outweigh the disadvantages?

Inclua:

  • position;
  • two advantages;
  • one disadvantage;
  • conclusion.

28. Error log

Classifique:

“I chose Tuesday because I heard the word Tuesday, but the speaker later corrected it to Thursday.”

Qual categoria de erro?

29. Simulação de decisão

Você tem quatro minutos restantes e:

  • uma questão difícil em branco;
  • três questões já respondidas que deseja revisar;
  • precisa transferir duas respostas para a folha.

Qual deve ser sua prioridade geral?

30. Plano de prova

Crie um protocolo pessoal B1 com no máximo 12 passos, cobrindo:

  • início da prova;
  • Reading;
  • Listening;
  • Writing;
  • Speaking;
  • revisão final.

Gabarito comentado

1. B — skimming

A pergunta busca:

overall meaning.

Logo:

skimming.

2. A — scanning

Você procura:

specific numerical information.

final action.

correction.

Recuperação rápida é essencial.

pode perder várias informações seguintes.

O comando exige:

e:

Ambas precisam aparecer.

Essa frase:

e:

12.

Incorreta na estrutura básica.

Use:

Although the course was difficult, I completed it.

Ou:

The course was difficult, but I completed it.

13. B

Em B1, uma frase clara e correta demonstra:

effective communication.

Complexidade que compromete:

grammar and meaning

não melhora automaticamente a resposta.

14.

Modelo:

I prefer buses because they are usually cheaper than using a private car, especially in cities. Cars are more flexible, but I think public transport is more practical when services are frequent.

Agora há:

preference

reason

comparison.

15. B

Use circumlocution:

It’s something you wear on your head when you ride a bicycle or motorcycle.

16. A

Pedir repetição é:

normal and communicatively appropriate.

some → all.

18. A — causation distortion

causation.

22.

8:30.

Cálculo:

8:10 + 20 minutes = 8:30.

23.

Uma divisão possível:

Planning: 4–5 minutes

Writing: 20–21 minutes

Review: 4–5 minutes.

Não é uma regra fixa.

O importante é:

reservar tempo real para revisão.

24.

Identificar claramente:

NOT.

Depois procurar quais três alternativas aparecem/são sustentadas e qual:

não é mencionada.

25.

Porque permite prever:

topic

vocabulary

information type

possible distractors.

Isso direciona:

attention.

26.

Modelo:

I usually prefer studying alone because I can work at my own pace and spend more time on difficult topics. I also find it easier to concentrate when the environment is quiet. However, studying with other people can be useful because students can exchange ideas and help each other understand difficult material. Overall, I prefer studying alone for revision, but I think group study is useful for discussions and collaborative tasks.

27.

Mini-outline:

Position: advantages generally outweigh disadvantages for suitable jobs.

Advantage 1: saves commuting time.

Advantage 2: greater flexibility.

Disadvantage: less face-to-face interaction / isolation.

Conclusion: useful when employees have appropriate support and the job allows remote work.

28.

Listening distractor/correction error.

Mais especificamente:

failed to update answer after correction.

Esse tipo deve entrar no:

error log.

29.

Prioridade geral:

first ensure all required answers are transferred correctly;

then attempt the blank question efficiently;

use remaining time to review answers with concrete doubts.

Transferência incorreta pode:

invalidate answers already solved.

A ordem exata depende do formato, mas:

protecting completed answers

é prioridade alta.

30.

Modelo de protocolo:

1. Read all instructions before starting.

2. Note the available time and establish checkpoints.

3. In Reading, identify the question type before searching the text.

4. Use skimming for main ideas and scanning for specific details.

5. Check paraphrases, quantifiers, certainty and negative words before selecting an answer.

6. In Listening, preview questions and predict the type of information required.

7. Listen for gist first and details/corrections second when two listenings are available.

8. If one word is missed, continue listening instead of stopping mentally.

9. In Writing, identify every part of the task and make a short outline before writing.

10. Reserve time to review content, grammar, spelling and word count.

11. In Speaking, use answer → reason → example and keep communicating after small mistakes.

12. Before submitting, check unanswered items, answer transfer and task requirements.

Tarefa de consolidação

Faça um simulado B1 cronometrado e, ao terminar, não analise apenas:

total score.

Crie uma tabela como:

Questão Erro Categoria Causa Estratégia futura
4 wrong paraphrase procurei palavras iguais procurar significado equivalente
11 wrong quantifier ignorei “most” marcar some/most/all
18 wrong Listening aceitei primeira data esperar correções
Writing partial task completion esqueci segunda parte sublinhar comandos

Depois calcule quantos erros foram causados por:

lack of vocabulary

grammar

inference

paraphrase

time management

instructions

careless reading

listening distractors.

Isso ajuda a descobrir se o problema é realmente:

“meu inglês é insuficiente”

ou se parte importante da pontuação está sendo perdida por:

exam technique.

Crie também um conjunto pessoal de alertas:

NOT / EXCEPT

some ≠ all

may ≠ will

associated with ≠ caused

planned ≠ actually did

original time ≠ final time

put off = postpone

however = important contrast

word limit

answer every part of the task.

Antes de cada simulado, leia apenas esses alertas.

Durante Writing, pratique sempre:

PLAN → WRITE → REVIEW

Durante Speaking:

ANSWER → WHY → EXAMPLE → CONTRAST → FINAL POINT

Durante Reading:

QUESTION → LOCATE → CONTEXT → PARAPHRASE → ANSWER

Durante Listening:

PREVIEW → PREDICT → LISTEN → UPDATE → MOVE ON

A estratégia final para uma prova B1 pode ser resumida em uma ideia:

Não tente demonstrar tudo o que sabe. Use o inglês que você sabe da forma mais eficiente possível para resolver exatamente a tarefa apresentada.

Aula 99 — Revisão geral B1

Objetivos

Ao final desta aula, você deverá ser capaz de:

  • revisar os principais conteúdos gramaticais do nível B1;
  • consolidar diferenças entre tempos verbais frequentes;
  • revisar conditionals, modal verbs, Passive Voice e Reported Speech;
  • reconhecer padrões de gerund e infinitive;
  • revisar relative clauses e phrasal verbs frequentes;
  • consolidar vocabulário de educação, trabalho, ciência, saúde e sociedade;
  • revisar estratégias de Reading B1;
  • identificar ideia principal, detalhes, inferências e referências pronominais;
  • reconhecer sinônimos, paráfrases e relações lógico-semânticas;
  • revisar estratégias para Listening em entrevistas, notícias e palestras;
  • consolidar técnicas de Writing para parágrafos, opinião, comparação e resumo;
  • revisar estratégias de Speaking para opinião, justificativa e comparação;
  • identificar erros frequentes de nível B1;
  • integrar gramática, vocabulário e habilidades em tarefas semelhantes às de exames de proficiência.

Desenvolvimento

O nível B1 representa uma transição importante.

No A1 e A2, grande parte do esforço está em:

construir frases corretas

compreender informações diretas

lidar com situações cotidianas.

No B1, passa a ser necessário também:

connect ideas

explain reasons

compare alternatives

infer meaning

summarize information

understand paraphrases

express opinions with support.

Portanto, a revisão B1 não deve ser apenas:

grammar review.

Ela precisa integrar:

Grammar + Vocabulary + Reading + Listening + Writing + Speaking.

Present Perfect

Estrutura:

have/has + past participle.

Exemplo:

I have visited London twice.

Usos principais:

  • experiências;
  • passado com resultado presente;
  • situações que começaram no passado e continuam.

Experience

Have you ever worked abroad?

I’ve never visited Canada.

Não há:

specific finished past time.

Current result

I’ve lost my keys.

Resultado presente:

I don’t have them now.

For e since

I’ve lived here for five years.

I’ve lived here since 2021.

for

duration.

since

starting point.

Present Perfect x Simple Past

Compare:

I’ve visited London twice.

Experiência até agora.

I visited London in 2024.

Evento em:

finished specific past time.

Marcadores de Simple Past

yesterday

last week

two years ago

in 2023.

Marcadores frequentes de Present Perfect

ever

never

already

yet

just

so far

recently

for

since.

Been x gone

Maria has gone to the bank.

Ela:

está lá ou a caminho.

Maria has been to the bank.

Ela:

foi e voltou.

Present Perfect Continuous

Estrutura:

have/has been + verb-ing.

Exemplo:

I’ve been studying for three hours.

Foco:

duration/activity.

Compare:

I’ve written five pages.

Revisão integrada — Texto 1

Flexible Working Program

A technology company introduced a six-month flexible working program last year. Employees were allowed to choose whether they worked from home or from the office on three days each week.

According to the company’s internal report, staff absence fell slightly during the trial, while overall productivity remained approximately the same. Most employees said they wanted the system to continue.

However, some managers reported communication problems when team members worked on different schedules. As a result, the company introduced regular online meetings and asked teams to choose at least one day each week when everyone would be in the office.

The trial has now ended, but the company has not yet decided whether the system will become permanent.

Revisão integrada — Texto 2

Short Walks and Concentration

Researchers at a university studied whether short walking breaks were associated with concentration during long study periods. A total of 220 students participated.

One group studied continuously for 90 minutes, while another group took a ten-minute walking break halfway through the session. Both groups then completed the same concentration task.

Students who took the walking break performed slightly better on average. However, the researchers warned that the study was relatively small and involved only university students.

The findings suggest that short breaks may support concentration, but further research is needed before stronger conclusions can be made.

Revisão integrada — Listening transcript

Presenter: Today we’re talking to Mark Evans, who recently completed a professional training course in digital marketing.

Interviewer: Mark, why did you choose the course?

Mark: I originally wanted to take a face-to-face course, but the classes were only available during working hours. So I chose the online version instead. It was actually more flexible than I expected.

Interviewer: Was there anything you found difficult?

Mark: At first, yes. I found it hard to organize my time because there wasn’t a fixed daily schedule. After the first month, though, I started planning specific study periods each week, and that helped a lot.

Interviewer: Would you take another online course?

Mark: Probably, yes. I still prefer face-to-face discussion, but the flexibility was extremely useful.

Estratégia de prova

Na revisão final B1, não tente memorizar:

hundreds of isolated rules.

Organize o conhecimento em contrastes.

Present Perfect x Simple Past

experience/current relevance x finished past.

Present Perfect Simple x Continuous

result x duration/activity.

Zero x First x Second Conditional

general truth x realistic future x hypothetical situation.

Mustn’t x don’t have to

prohibition x no necessity.

Because x because of

clause x noun phrase.

Although x despite

clause x noun/gerund.

Association x causation

relationship x direct cause.

Some x all

limited quantity x totality.

May x will

possibility x stronger future statement.

Reading x Listening strategy

locate evidence x keep up with moving audio.

Antes de responder, faça uma pergunta simples:

What exactly does the language allow me to conclude?

Essa pergunta reduz muitos erros B1.

Prática

Com base no Texto 1:

1. How long did the flexible working trial last?

  1. Three days
  2. Six months
  3. One year
  4. Permanently

2. What were employees allowed to do?

  1. Stop working three days a week.
  2. Choose home or office work on three days each week.
  3. Work only from home.
  4. Choose their salary.

3. What happened to productivity?

  1. It fell dramatically.
  2. It doubled.
  3. It remained approximately the same.
  4. It was not measured.

4. What did most employees want?

  1. The system to continue.
  2. The company to close.
  3. More working hours.
  4. No online meetings.

5. What problem did some managers report?

  1. Higher salaries.
  2. Communication difficulties.
  3. Lack of computers.
  4. Excessive office space.

6. What was one response to the problem?

  1. Canceling flexible work immediately.
  2. Regular online meetings.
  3. Removing managers.
  4. Reducing salaries.

7. Is the flexible system permanent now?

  1. Yes.
  2. No decision has been made yet.
  3. It was rejected permanently.
  4. It is compulsory worldwide.

Com base no Texto 2:

8. What was the study examining?

  1. Whether walking breaks were associated with concentration.
  2. Whether students could run faster.
  3. Whether walking caused perfect grades.
  4. Whether universities should close.

9. How many students participated?

  1. 90
  2. 110
  3. 220
  4. 440

10. What did the second group do?

  1. Slept for 90 minutes.
  2. Took a ten-minute walking break.
  3. Completed no concentration task.
  4. Walked for the entire session.

11. What was the main result?

  1. The walking group performed slightly better on average.
  2. All students achieved perfect results.
  3. Walking had no relationship with performance.
  4. The continuous-study group scored twice as high.

12. What limitation was mentioned?

  1. No students participated.
  2. The study was relatively small and included only university students.
  3. No concentration task was used.
  4. The study lasted several years.

13. Which statement is supported?

  1. Walking definitely improves everyone’s concentration.
  2. Short walking breaks may support concentration.
  3. Walking eliminates concentration problems.
  4. The study proves causation for all age groups.

  4. People use bicycles.

52. Inferência:

A six-month program reduced energy use by 10%, but researchers do not know whether the reduction will continue in the long term.

  3. Energy use did not change.
  4. Researchers ended all energy use.

A city introduced free Sunday bus travel as a six-month trial. Passenger numbers increased during the first two months, and local businesses reported more visitors to the city center. However, the program is expensive, and officials have not yet decided whether it will continue after the trial.

Tarefa de consolidação

Construa uma revisão final em seis blocos.

Bloco 1 — Grammar

Revise e produza dois exemplos de cada:

Present Perfect

Present Perfect Continuous

Past Perfect

will

going to

Zero Conditional

First Conditional

Second Conditional

modal verbs

Passive Voice

Reported Speech

relative clauses

gerunds

infinitives.

Bloco 2 — Vocabulary

Crie mapas lexicais para:

education

work

science

health

society.

Inclua:

nouns

verbs

adjectives

collocations

word families.

Bloco 3 — Reading

Faça textos curtos e responda:

main idea

supporting details

pronoun reference

connector function

inference

vocabulary in context

paraphrase.

Bloco 4 — Listening

Para cada áudio, identifique:

gist

numbers

reasons

correction

final decision

speaker opinion.

Bloco 5 — Writing

Produza:

one paragraph

one opinion text

one comparison

one summary.

Revise:

task completion

coherence

cohesion

grammar

word count.

Bloco 6 — Speaking

Treine respostas usando:

Answer → Reason → Example → Contrast → Final Point

e comparações usando:

Both → Difference → Difference → Preference

Por fim, crie um error log B1.

Divida os erros em:

grammar

vocabulary

paraphrase

inference

listening distractor

writing organization

speaking fluency

careless mistake.

Para cada erro, registre:

What did I answer?

What was correct?

Why did I make the mistake?

What rule or strategy prevents it?

Finalize revisando estes alertas:

Present Perfect ≠ Simple Past

mustn’t ≠ don’t have to

may ≠ will

some ≠ all

most ≠ all

association ≠ causation

because + clause

because of + noun

although + clause

despite + noun/gerund

put off = postpone

call off = cancel

used to = past, normally not now

still = continues now

no longer = stopped being true

prefer X to Y

Reading: match meaning, not words

Listening: final information may correct earlier information

Writing: answer every part of the task

Speaking: develop the answer instead of stopping after one sentence

A revisão B1 está completa quando você deixa de tratar esses conteúdos como tópicos isolados e consegue usá-los juntos para compreender, inferir, explicar, comparar, resumir e comunicar ideias com autonomia intermediária.

Aula 100 — Simulado B1

Objetivos

Ao final desta aula, você deverá ser capaz de:

  • realizar um simulado integrado de proficiência em nível B1;
  • aplicar estratégias de Reading, Listening, Writing e Speaking;
  • reconhecer ideias principais, detalhes e inferências;
  • identificar sinônimos, paráfrases e relações lógico-semânticas;
  • interpretar textos jornalísticos, informativos e de divulgação científica;
  • compreender entrevistas, notícias e palestras curtas;
  • reconhecer distratores em Listening;
  • utilizar os principais conteúdos gramaticais do nível B1;
  • empregar vocabulário de educação, trabalho, ciência, saúde e sociedade;
  • produzir um texto de opinião/comparação;
  • produzir um resumo básico;
  • desenvolver respostas orais justificadas;
  • avaliar seu desempenho por área;
  • identificar erros recorrentes antes de avançar para o nível B2.

Desenvolvimento

Este simulado reúne os principais conteúdos estudados no nível B1.

A estrutura será:

Parte 1 — Reading

Parte 2 — Use of English

Parte 3 — Listening simulado por transcrição

Parte 4 — Writing

Parte 5 — Speaking

O objetivo não é apenas verificar:

grammar knowledge.

Você também deverá demonstrar capacidade de:

understand

infer

paraphrase

organize

justify

compare

summarize.

Organização sugerida

Use, se desejar, aproximadamente:

Reading — 35 minutos

Use of English — 25 minutos

Listening — 25 minutos

Writing — 40 minutos

Speaking — 15 minutos

Não consulte o gabarito antes de concluir:

as partes objetivas.

Parte 1 — Reading

Leia o texto 1.

Community Learning Hub Expands

A community education center in Brookdale will expand its evening program after receiving more applications than expected during its first year. The center currently offers free classes in English, mathematics and basic digital skills for adults.

According to the organizers, many participants work during the day and are unable to attend traditional daytime courses. For this reason, most classes begin after 6 p.m., while several weekend sessions are also available.

More than 700 adults enrolled during the first year. Organizers had originally expected around 400 participants. Because of this higher demand, the center plans to add introductory programming and workplace communication courses next semester.

Although most classes will remain free, two advanced technology courses will require a small fee to cover equipment costs. The center is also looking for additional volunteer tutors.

1. What is the main purpose of the text?

  1. To criticize adult education
  2. To report the expansion of an adult learning program
  3. To advertise only programming courses
  4. To compare universities

2. Why are most classes offered in the evening?

  1. Teachers prefer working late.
  2. Participants mainly work during the day.
  3. The building is closed in the morning.
  4. Evening classes are more expensive.

3. How many participants had organizers originally expected?

  1. About 400
  2. About 600
  3. More than 700
  4. Exactly 1,000

4. Why will new courses be introduced?

  1. Enrollment was lower than expected.
  2. Demand was higher than expected.
  3. The current subjects were canceled.
  4. The center received fewer tutors.

5. Which statement is true?

  1. Every course will remain free.
  2. All technology courses will be expensive.
  3. Two advanced courses will charge a small fee.
  4. Weekend sessions will end.

6. What does “this higher demand” refer to?

  1. The cost of equipment
  2. The number of adults enrolling
  3. The number of tutors
  4. The length of the classes

7. What can be inferred about the program?

  1. It has attracted more interest than organizers predicted.
  2. It is available only to university students.
  3. It is becoming smaller.
  4. Participants must attend every day.

Leia o texto 2.

Do Short Breaks Help Concentration?

Researchers at a university investigated whether short breaks during study sessions were associated with better concentration. A total of 240 undergraduate students participated in the experiment.

Half of the students studied continuously for 90 minutes. The others took a ten-minute walking break after 40 minutes of study. Afterward, both groups completed the same concentration task.

On average, students in the walking-break group performed slightly better. They also reported feeling less mentally tired. However, the researchers emphasized that the differences between the groups were relatively small.

The study also had several limitations. All participants were university students between the ages of 18 and 25, and the experiment took place during only one study session. Therefore, the researchers say the findings should not be generalized to all students or all learning situations.

They recommend larger studies over longer periods before stronger conclusions are made.

8. What did the researchers study?

  1. Whether students preferred walking to studying
  2. Whether short breaks were associated with concentration
  3. Whether exercise improves all university grades
  4. Whether students could walk for 90 minutes

9. How many students took a walking break?

  1. 40
  2. 90
  3. 120
  4. 240

10. What happened after the study period?

  1. Both groups completed a concentration task.
  2. Only one group took an exam.
  3. All participants went home.
  4. Students completed a physical fitness test.

11. What was one result?

  1. The walking group performed slightly better on average.
  2. The walking group performed twice as well.
  3. There was no difference of any kind.
  4. The continuous-study group performed significantly better.

12. Why should the results be interpreted cautiously?

  1. No university students were involved.
  2. The experiment lasted ten years.
  3. The sample and study conditions were limited.
  4. Researchers did not measure concentration.

13. Which statement is NOT supported by the text?

  1. The walking group reported less mental tiredness.
  2. The study involved young adults.
  3. Short walking breaks definitely improve concentration for everyone.
  4. Researchers recommend further studies.

14. The word “Therefore” introduces:

  1. an example
  2. a consequence
  3. a definition
  4. a similarity

15. Which is the best summary?

  1. Walking always improves academic performance.
  2. A study found small concentration benefits associated with a short walking break, but important limitations mean more research is needed.
  3. University students should stop studying after 40 minutes.
  4. Continuous study is dangerous.

Leia o texto 3.

Changing the Way Offices Are Used

Hybrid work has changed how some companies use office buildings. When employees work from home several days a week, organizations may need fewer individual desks than they did in the past.

As a result, some companies have replaced permanent desks with shared work areas that employees can reserve in advance. Others have created more meeting rooms and collaborative spaces because workers increasingly use office days for group activities.

These changes can reduce rental costs. However, they also create new challenges. If too many workers come to the office on the same day, there may not be enough desks available.

To address this problem, some organizations use online booking systems and encourage teams to coordinate their office schedules.

Experts say flexible offices are likely to remain common, although the most suitable arrangement depends on the type of work and the needs of employees.

16. What change has hybrid work produced?

  1. Companies always need more permanent desks.
  2. Some companies need fewer individual desks.
  3. Employees no longer use offices.
  4. All offices have closed.

17. Why have some companies created more collaborative spaces?

  1. Employees use office days more often for group activities.
  2. Meeting rooms are cheaper than desks.
  3. Employees refuse to work together.
  4. Home working has ended.

18. What is one benefit mentioned?

  1. Higher rental costs
  2. Lower rental costs
  3. Longer working hours
  4. Fewer online systems

19. What problem can shared offices create?

  1. Too many available desks
  2. Insufficient desks on busy days
  3. Employees cannot reserve spaces
  4. Offices become free

20. What solution is mentioned?

  1. Eliminating remote work
  2. Booking systems and coordinated schedules
  3. Building a new office every year
  4. Asking employees to work seven days a week

21. Which statement best reflects the final paragraph?

  1. One office model is perfect for every company.
  2. Flexible offices are expected to continue, but suitability varies.
  3. Experts believe offices will disappear.
  4. Remote work has ended permanently.

Parte 3 — Listening simulado

Para treinar esta seção, leia cada transcrição apenas uma vez antes de responder às questões correspondentes.

Listening 1 — Entrevista

Interviewer: Today we’re talking to Emma Carter, who recently opened a small bakery after working in an office for nearly ten years. Emma, had you always planned to open your own business?

Emma: Not really. I enjoyed baking, but it was only a hobby for a long time. About three years ago, I started making cakes for friends and family on weekends. Then people began asking if they could pay me to make cakes for birthdays and other events.

Interviewer: So when did you decide to leave your office job?

Emma: I thought about it for almost a year. I didn’t want to make a quick decision because I had a stable salary. Eventually, I saved enough money to cover several months of expenses, and I left the office last September.

Interviewer: What has been the biggest challenge?

Emma: Time management, definitely. I expected the baking to be the difficult part, but actually organizing orders, buying ingredients and answering messages takes a lot of time.

Interviewer: Do you regret the change?

Emma: No. I work longer hours now, but I enjoy the work much more.

  3. She owned a restaurant.

  2. Last September

  3. Buying ingredients

  3. Finding an office

  2. She prefers her old job.
  3. She enjoys her current work more.
  4. She plans to close the bakery.

Listening 2 — Notícia

Presenter: Heavy rain has caused transport problems across the Green Valley region this morning. Three major roads have been closed because of flooding, and several bus routes are operating with delays.

Train services between Northbridge and Central City were originally expected to return to normal by 10 a.m. However, transport officials now say delays may continue until approximately 1 p.m.

Residents are being advised to avoid unnecessary journeys. No serious injuries have been reported, although emergency teams helped several families leave flooded homes overnight.

Weather forecasters say the heaviest rain should end by late afternoon, but lighter rain may continue into the evening.

Listening 3 — Palestra curta

Lecturer: Today I’d like to talk about three simple strategies for improving vocabulary learning. The first is spaced review. Instead of studying a list of words once for a long period, learners review the same vocabulary several times over different days.

The second strategy is learning words in context. For example, rather than memorizing only the word “increase”, a learner might study expressions such as “increase prices”, “increase rapidly” and “an increase in demand”.

Finally, active use is important. When learners use new words in speaking or writing, they have to retrieve them from memory, which can strengthen learning.

These strategies are most effective when they are combined. In other words, reviewing vocabulary regularly, seeing it in context and actively using it can support long-term learning.

Parte 4 — Writing

Realize as duas tarefas.

Writing Task 1 — Opinião e comparação

Escreva entre:

170 e 200 palavras

sobre:

Is it better for adults to study online or in a traditional classroom?

Seu texto deve:

  • apresentar as duas opções;
  • incluir pelo menos uma semelhança;
  • apresentar vantagens e limitações;
  • usar pelo menos um comparative;
  • usar both;
  • usar however;
  • usar whereas ou while;
  • apresentar sua opinião;
  • justificar sua preferência;
  • incluir um exemplo;
  • terminar com conclusão coerente.

Writing Task 2 — Resumo

Leia:

A local council introduced a six-month free bus program on Sundays to encourage people to use public transport. During the first two months, passenger numbers were approximately 25% higher than on normal Sundays before the program began. Local businesses in the city center also reported an increase in visitors. However, operating the free service has cost more than originally expected. Council members have not yet decided whether the program will continue after the six-month trial. They say passenger data, business activity and financial costs will all be considered before a final decision is made.

Escreva um resumo entre:

55 e 75 palavras.

Seu resumo deve:

  • apresentar objetivo;
  • incluir principal resultado;
  • incluir limitação/custo;
  • mencionar que ainda não existe decisão final;
  • não incluir sua opinião.

Modelo — Writing Task 1

Both online learning and traditional classroom learning can provide adults with opportunities to develop new skills. However, the two formats offer different advantages. Online courses are usually more flexible because learners can study from different locations and may organize lessons around work or family responsibilities. For example, a person who works full-time can attend an online class in the evening without traveling to a college.

Traditional classrooms, whereas, provide more direct interaction with teachers and other students. A more natural structure is: Traditional classrooms, on the other hand, provide more direct interaction with teachers and other students, whereas online communication often depends on messages or video calls. This face-to-face contact can make it easier to ask questions and remain motivated.

In my opinion, online learning is more suitable for many adult learners because flexibility is often essential when people already have professional and family responsibilities. However, it requires good organization and independent study skills.

In conclusion, both formats can be effective, but I would choose online learning for adults who need to combine education with other commitments.

Modelo — Writing Task 2

A local council is testing free Sunday bus travel for six months in order to increase public transport use. Passenger numbers rose by about 25% during the first two months, and city-center businesses also received more visitors. However, the service has cost more than expected. The council has not decided whether to continue the program and will consider transport use, business activity and financial costs before making a final decision.

Modelo — Speaking Task 2

Both studying alone and studying in a group can be useful, but they are suitable for different situations. Studying alone allows me to work at my own pace and concentrate on the topics I find difficult. It is usually quieter and more flexible. Group study, however, gives students an opportunity to exchange ideas and explain things to each other. This can be especially helpful when a topic is difficult. Personally, I prefer studying alone for revision because I can organize my time more easily, whereas I would choose group study for discussions or collaborative activities. Overall, I think both methods are valuable, and the best choice depends on the type of task.

explicar a diferença entre Present Perfect e Simple Past;

usar Zero, First e Second Conditional;

distinguir mustn’t de don’t have to;

reconhecer Passive Voice e Reported Speech;

usar relative clauses;

escolher gerund ou infinitive em padrões frequentes;

reconhecer phrasal verbs essenciais;

identificar main idea e supporting details;

fazer inferências sem inventar informações;

reconhecer sinônimos e paráfrases;

acompanhar entrevistas, notícias e palestras curtas;

escrever um parágrafo organizado;

escrever opinião e comparação;

resumir um texto curto;

falar por pelo menos um minuto justificando uma opinião.

O objetivo final do B1 não é usar inglês perfeito. É conseguir compreender e produzir discurso conectado sobre temas familiares, explicar razões, comparar alternativas, interpretar informações menos explícitas e manter comunicação funcional com autonomia intermediária.
